name: AddEventHandler
summary: Listens for a local event.
description: Registers a callback on the current resource's local event bus. The handler is owned by the current resource generation and is discarded automatically when that generation stops or reloads; it never receives network traffic unless the event was separately registered as a network event.
example:
-- Run setup when this resource starts on the client
AddEventHandler("onClientResourceStart", function(name)
    if name ~= GetCurrentResourceName() then return end
    Open77.hud.notify("Welcome to the city")
end)

name: AddStateBagChangeHandler
summary: FiveM compatibility: watches a state-bag key with FiveM's argument list.
description: No permission. `bagName` is nil for every bag, `global`, `player:<id>`, `<kind>:<id>`, or `entity:<id>` -- the last matches any entity kind with that id. `key` may be nil for every key. The handler is called as `fn(bagName, key, value, reserved, replicated)`, where `reserved` is always nil and `replicated` always true, so a ported signature lines up. It shares the subscription index with `Open77.state.onChange`, so only this resource is touched.
example:
-- A FiveM-style watcher: react when the server changes the weather key
AddStateBagChangeHandler("weather", "global", function(bagName, key, value)
    Open77.hud.notify("Weather: " .. tostring(value))
end)

name: AllowAim
summary: Allow or block a local-player action.
description: Requires players.controls and a strict boolean. Freeze true acquires a block; Allow false acquires a block. The inverse releases only this resource VM's block, never another owner or vanilla restriction. Automatically released on resource stop, death and session teardown. Does not freeze vehicles, moving platforms or server teleports. See player-utilities.md for each native restriction and limitations.
example:
-- No aiming inside the safe zone; released again when the player leaves it
AddEventHandler("safezone:entered", function() AllowAim(false) end)
AddEventHandler("safezone:left", function() AllowAim(true) end)

name: ClearTick
summary: Cancels a tick created by `SetTick`.
description: Takes effect on the next pass: the tick body never runs again after this returns. Tick ids and timer ids come from one per-resource counter and never collide, so this is the cancellation `ClearTimeout` performs; both names exist because FiveM has both.
example:
-- Draw a marker every frame until the player reaches the point
local tick
tick = SetTick(function()
    if #(vector3(Open77.character.position()) - target) < 2.0 then
        ClearTick(tick)
        Open77.hud.notify("You made it")
    end
end)

name: ClearTimeout
summary: Cancels a timer created by `SetTimeout`.
description: Cancels a pending timeout owned by the current resource generation. It returns `false` when the id is unknown or the callback has already begun; cancelling cannot interrupt a callback that is currently running.
example:
-- The player pressed the key again before the delay ran out: cancel the pending action
local pending = SetTimeout(3000, function() openDoor() end)
RegisterKeyMapping("door_cancel", "Cancel door", "X", function()
    ClearTimeout(pending)
end)

name: CreateThread
summary: Starts a coroutine managed by the host.
description: Its body may call `Wait`, which an ordinary function cannot.
example:
-- Show a reminder every 30 seconds until the delivery is done
CreateThread(function()
    while not delivered do
        Open77.hud.notify("Deliver the package to Kabuki")
        Wait(30000)
    end
end)

name: DeleteResourceKvp
summary: FiveM-style alias for `Open77.kvp.delete`.
description: FiveM-familiar alias for `Open77.kvp.delete`. It atomically removes only the named key owned by the calling resource and reports whether that key existed.
example:
-- Forget the saved HUD position
DeleteResourceKvp("hud_position")

name: DestroySound
summary: DestroySound: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Free the engine sound when the player gets out of the car
DestroySound(engineLoop)
engineLoop = nil

name: DoesEntityExist
summary: Whether an id is live in the registry that owns that kind.
description: FiveM has one opaque handle space; Open77 has one registry per kind, so the kind is required: vehicle, npc, elevator, prop, effect, player (loot is server-only). The one-argument FiveM form cannot be answered and returns false, kind_required. Each kind answers under its own registry's permissions, so a resource that may not read that kind gets false -- call the namespace function directly to tell denied from absent. Other reasons: id_required, invalid_entity_id, unknown_entity_kind, kind_unavailable_on_client.
example:
-- The blip points at a vehicle; drop the blip if the car is gone
if not DoesEntityExist("vehicle", trackedVehicleId) then
    Open77.blips.remove(blipId)
end

name: Entity
summary: FiveM compatibility: a table carrying one entity's state bag.
description: No permission. FiveM has one entity namespace and Open77 has three registries, so the id is probed against the mirror as vehicle, then npc, then prop, and falls back to vehicle. `Open77.state.entity(kind, id)` is always unambiguous and is what a new resource should use.
example:
-- FiveM-style read of a vehicle's state bag
local owner = Entity(vehicleId).state.owner
if owner == Open77.players.localId() then print("this is my car") end

name: ExecuteCommand
summary: FiveM-style alias for `Open77.runtime.executeCommand`.
description: Resolves against the client registry only and reports whether it matched; it never forwards to the server by itself. The chat composer uses that answer to decide whether to spend a net event.
example:
-- Run a local command from a key binding
RegisterKeyMapping("toggle_hud", "Toggle HUD", "H", function()
    ExecuteCommand("hud toggle")
end)

name: GetCurrentResourceName
summary: Name of the current resource.
description: Returns the immutable manifest name of the resource whose Lua VM is executing. Use it for diagnostics and namespacing, not as a mutable display label.
example:
-- Only react to this resource's own start
AddEventHandler("onClientResourceStart", function(name)
    if name == GetCurrentResourceName() then print("started") end
end)

name: GetGameTimer
summary: Monotonic milliseconds since an arbitrary epoch.
description: The FiveM name for the clock behind `Open77.time.monotonic()`, which reports seconds. The epoch is arbitrary and is not wall clock: only the difference between two readings means anything, and the client and the server share no origin. The server has the same global. See the FiveM compatibility guide.
example:
-- A cooldown: ignore the key for 5 seconds after use
local lastUse = 0
RegisterKeyMapping("flashlight", "Flashlight", "L", function()
    if GetGameTimer() - lastUse < 5000 then return end
    lastUse = GetGameTimer()
    toggleFlashlight()
end)

name: GetHashKey
summary: TweakDBID of a record name -- not a GTA hash.
description: CRC-32/ISO-HDLC of the name in the low 32 bits, the name length in byte 4, which is what REDengine computes. This is deliberately NOT the Jenkins one-at-a-time hash FiveM returns: Open77 records are TweakDB strings, so a hash constant copied out of a FiveM resource names a GTA model and matches nothing here. The server computes the identical value.
example:
-- Compare a record name with the hash a server event carried
if GetHashKey("Vehicle.v_sport2_quadra_turbo_r") == recordHash then
    print("that is a Quadra")
end

name: GetInvokingResource
summary: Real caller of the currently executing export.
description: Returns nil outside an export callback. Use this value for service ownership instead of accepting a forgeable owner argument.
example:
-- A service export trusts the caller's real name, never an argument
exports("registerHud", function(definition)
    local owner = GetInvokingResource()
    huds[owner] = definition
    return true
end)

name: GetInvokingResourceGeneration
summary: Generation of the resource invoking the current export.
description: Returns nil outside an export callback. A changed generation lets a service retire handles left by an older VM.
example:
-- Retire handles a reloaded caller left behind
exports("open", function()
    local owner, generation = GetInvokingResource(), GetInvokingResourceGeneration()
    if generations[owner] ~= generation then
        closeAll(owner)
        generations[owner] = generation
    end
    return newHandle(owner)
end)

name: GetRegisteredCommands
summary: FiveM-style alias for `Open77.runtime.commands`.
description: Client-side. Each entry carries `name`, `resource`, `restricted` and, when the registrar declared them, `help` and `parameters` -- two fields more than FiveM's, because the composer needs them to build a completion.
example:
-- Build a help list from every client command
for _, entry in ipairs(GetRegisteredCommands()) do
    print(("/%s - %s"):format(entry.name, entry.help or ""))
end

name: GetResourceKvp
summary: FiveM-style alias for `Open77.kvp.get`.
description: FiveM-familiar alias for `Open77.kvp.get`. It returns the original stored Lua type or nil when absent and stays inside the active connection-address and calling-resource namespace.
example:
-- Restore the HUD position the player chose last time
local position = GetResourceKvp("hud_position", "top_left")

name: GetResourceState
summary: State of a resource.
description: Reads the lifecycle state currently known by the client resource host. This is a snapshot only: it does not start, stop, or wait for the target resource.
example:
-- Only use the notifications package if it is actually running
if GetResourceState("open77_notifications") == "started" then
    Open77.exports.call("open77_notifications", "show", { message = "Ready" })
end

name: GetSoundState
summary: GetSoundState: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Restart the siren loop if it has stopped playing
local state = GetSoundState(sirenId)

name: GlobalState
summary: The server-wide state bag, read-only on the client.
description: The FiveM spelling of `Open77.state.global`, mirroring what the server replicated. Reading a key the server never set, or that this client has not received yet, answers nil — check `Open77.state.ready()` before treating a nil as an absence. Writing is refused: the client never writes a bag, because a bag is shared state and a client that could write one could write another player's job or another vehicle's keys. Ask with `Open77.state.request`, which the server arbitrates and republishes.
returns: the global bag, indexable by key
example:
-- Read the round number the server replicated
CreateThread(function()
    while not Open77.state.ready() do Wait(100) end
    Open77.hud.notify("Round " .. tostring(GlobalState.round))
end)

name: IsDuplicityVersion
summary: False in the client VM, true in the server VM.
description: How one shared script branches between the two sides.
example:
-- One shared script, two sides
if IsDuplicityVersion() then
    RegisterCommand("ping", function(source) print("pong from", source) end, false)
else
    RegisterNetEvent("app:pong", function() Open77.hud.notify("pong") end)
end

Read-only, without advancing replication counters. See player-utilities.md.

end)

name: LoadResourceFile
summary: Reads a file belonging to the calling resource.
description: The FiveM spelling of `Open77.resource.readFile`, and no more powerful: the path resolves under this resource's own root, keeps the 1 MiB cap, and naming another resource returns nil, cross_resource_read_denied rather than quietly reading your own file. A traversal returns nil, invalid_resource_path. The server has the same global rooted at the resource's data/ directory, plus SaveResourceFile.
returns: file contents, or nil plus a reason

name: Player
summary: FiveM compatibility: a table carrying one player's state bag and `source`.
description: No permission. `Player(id).state` is the same bag as `Open77.state.player(id)`, read-only on the client. `source` is the id that was passed in. Present so ported code runs unchanged; new code can use either.
example:
-- FiveM-style read of a player's state bag
local job = Player(playerId).state.job
print("their job is", job)

name: RegisterCommand
summary: FiveM-style alias for `Open77.runtime.registerCommand`.
description: Client-side. The server runtime has its own `RegisterCommand` with the same handler shape but real ACL enforcement behind `restricted`; read both before porting a command that is meant to be admin-only.
example:
-- /hudpos <top_left|bottom_right>: a local client command
RegisterCommand("hudpos", function(source, args)
    if not args[1] then return end
    SetResourceKvp("hud_position", args[1])
    Open77.hud.notify("HUD position saved")
end, false)

name: RegisterKeyMapping
summary: Declares a named, rebindable action bound to a key.
description: Declares a named, rebindable action bound to a key, as an engine primitive. Requires `input.actions`. Accepts a spec table `{ id, name, key, hold, onPressed, onReleased }` or the positional form `(id, name, key, onPressed [, onReleased])`; the callback receives the mapping id, fires on the key-down edge (and key-up in hold mode), and never fires while a page owns the keyboard. Returns the effective key (the player's saved rebind, else the default). The player rebinds it from Pause -> Settings -> KEY BINDINGS, and the choice persists machine-globally across servers and relaunches. Mirrored as `Open77.input.registerKeyMapping`.
example:
-- A rebindable "open inventory" key, defaulting to I
RegisterKeyMapping("inventory_open", "Open inventory", "I", function()
    openInventory()
end)

name: RegisterNetEvent
summary: Allows an event to arrive from the server.
description: Allows an authenticated server event with this name to enter the current resource, and optionally attaches a handler in the same call. Registration is generation-scoped, requires `network.events`, and does not turn arbitrary client events into server events.
example:
-- Receive a server notification and show it natively
RegisterNetEvent("bank:deposit", function(amount)
    Open77.hud.notify(("Deposited %d eddies"):format(amount))
end)

name: RemoveEventHandler
summary: Removes a handler.
description: Removes the exact callback previously registered for the named local event. It returns `false` when that event/callback pair is not owned by the current resource generation.
example:
-- Stop listening after the tutorial step is done
local function onStep(step)
    if step == "done" then RemoveEventHandler("tutorial:step", onStep) end
end
AddEventHandler("tutorial:step", onStep)

name: RemoveStateBagChangeHandler
summary: FiveM compatibility: stops a state-bag change subscription.
description: No permission. The same function as `Open77.state.offChange`; takes the id either registration returned.
example:
-- Watch the vehicle's owner key only while the player sits in it
local sub = AddStateBagChangeHandler("owner", "vehicle:" .. vehicleId, function(_, _, value)
    print("owner is now", value)
end)
AddEventHandler("vehicle:left", function() RemoveStateBagChangeHandler(sub) end)

name: Screen2DPointTo3DSpace
summary: Unproject a normalized screen point into a world-space ray.
description: Requires world.query. x/y use normalized top-left viewport coordinates in [0,1]. maxDistance defaults to 100 metres and must be finite in [0.1,1000]. Returns origin, unit direction, endpoint position and maxDistance; this is not a collision result. Uses the active camera and checks projection consistency. Returns nil/reason if the camera or projection is unavailable. Identical global alias: Screen2DPointTo3DSpace. See screen-picking.md and context-menu.md. Requires the new screen-picking client, not the earlier .62 release.
example:
-- What is under the middle of the screen, up to 25 m away?
local ray, reason = Screen2DPointTo3DSpace(0.5, 0.5, 25)
if ray then
    local hit = Open77.world.raycast(ray.origin, ray.position, { entities = true })
    if hit and hit.hit and hit.entity then print("looking at", hit.entity.className) end
end

name: SeekSound
summary: SeekSound: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Skip the intro of the track
SeekSound(musicId, 12.5)

name: SetResourceKvp
summary: FiveM-style alias for `Open77.kvp.set`.
description: FiveM-familiar alias for `Open77.kvp.set`. It stores one typed value in the calling resource's persistent namespace for the active connection address; it cannot select another server or resource.
example:
-- Remember the player's chosen HUD position on this machine
SetResourceKvp("hud_position", "bottom_right")

name: SetSoundPosition
summary: SetSoundPosition: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Keep the boombox sound following the carried prop
SetTick(function()
    SetSoundPosition(boomboxSound, vector3(Open77.character.position()))
end)

name: SetSoundVolume
summary: SetSoundVolume: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Fade the music out over two seconds
CreateThread(function()
    for v = 10, 0, -1 do
        SetSoundVolume(musicId, v / 10)
        Wait(200)
    end
    StopSound(musicId)
end)

name: SetTick
summary: Runs a function once per host tick.
description: A scheduler task looping with an implicit `Wait(0)`: same per-frame budget, same task cap, stopped with the resource. An error inside the function is logged and the tick survives it; after five consecutive failures the tick logs `tick cancelled after 5 consecutive failures` and cancels itself. One successful pass resets the count.
returns: tick id, or nil plus invalid_tick_function / task_limit_or_stopping
example:
-- Show the prompt every frame while the player stands at the delivery point
local point = vector3(-1442.2, 127.4, 18.0)
local tick = SetTick(function()
    if #(vector3(Open77.character.position()) - point) < 2.0 then
        Open77.hud.notify("Press E to deliver", { replace = true })
    end
end)
AddEventHandler("delivery:done", function() ClearTick(tick) end)

name: SetTimeout
summary: Runs a function once, later.
description: Schedules a Lua callback after at least the requested number of milliseconds without blocking the game thread. The timer belongs to the current resource generation and is cancelled automatically on stop or hot reload.
example:
-- Hide the hint after 4 seconds
Open77.hud.notify("Press E to open the trunk")
SetTimeout(4000, function() Open77.hud.clearNotify() end)

name: StopSound
summary: StopSound: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Stop the alarm when the player leaves the building
AddEventHandler("building:left", function() StopSound(alarmId) end)

name: TriggerEvent
summary: Publishes an event to every handler in this resource's VM.
description: Dispatches an event only inside the client resource runtime. Arguments must fit the runtime's bounded script-value representation; use `TriggerServerEvent` for traffic that must cross the network.
example:
-- Tell the rest of this resource that the menu closed
TriggerEvent("shop:closed")
AddEventHandler("shop:closed", function() FreezePosition(false) end)

name: TriggerServerEvent
summary: Sends an event to the server.
description: Serializes and sends an event to the connected server with the caller's authenticated player identity. It requires `network.events`; tables must be serializable and payload limits are enforced before anything is queued.
example:
-- Ask the server to buy an item; the server decides
RegisterKeyMapping("buy_ammo", "Buy ammo", "B", function()
    TriggerServerEvent("shop:buy", "ammo_box")
end)

name: Wait
summary: Suspends the current coroutine.
description: Only usable inside a `CreateThread`.
example:
-- A three-second countdown on the HUD
CreateThread(function()
    for n = 3, 1, -1 do
        Open77.hud.notify(("Round starts in %d"):format(n), { replace = true })
        Wait(1000)
    end
end)

name: exports
summary: Declares a function callable by other resources, and proxies calls to theirs.
description: Publishes a named function from the current resource so another resource can call it through `Open77.exports.call`. The registration is tied to the current generation, so stale functions cannot survive a stop or hot reload.
example:
-- Publish a function other client resources can call
exports("isInSafeZone", function()
    return inSafeZone
end)

name: joaat
summary: Alias of `GetHashKey`; returns a TweakDBID.
description: Kept so ported code reads naturally, but it is not the Jenkins hash the name suggests -- see GetHashKey.
example:
-- FiveM habit, same value as GetHashKey: a TweakDBID, not a Jenkins hash
local id = joaat("Items.Preset_Lexington_Default")

name: print
summary: Writes to the Open77 log, prefixed with the resource name.
description: Writes a resource-prefixed line to the Open77 log. Values are converted with bounded formatting; this does not send a chat message or write into a WebUI page.
example:
-- Goes to the Open77 log, prefixed with the resource name
local x, y, z = Open77.character.position()
print(("player at %.1f, %.1f, %.1f"):format(x, y, z))

name: quat
summary: Builds a quaternion: a plain { x, y, z, w } table with three rotation methods.
description: Available in both runtimes. Deliberately minimal -- normalize (a zero quaternion becomes the identity, never NaN), mul (Hamilton product, this rotation then the other) and rotate (returns a vector3), plus unpack and table. No arithmetic operators and no #. It exists so the { x =, y =, z =, w = } orientation that Open77.effects and Open77.props already accept becomes computable; the result stays exactly that table.
example:
-- Rotate a forward offset by the player's current orientation
local rot = quat(0, 0, 0.7071, 0.7071) -- 90 degrees around z
local ahead = rot:rotate(vector3(0.0, 2.0, 0.0))

name: require
summary: Loads a local Lua module or a published dependency library into the caller's client VM.
description: Client-only Lua module loader. Loads a local module, or a published module from a declared, running dependency using `@provider` / `@provider/module`. The dependency form requires the development client update introduced with PolyZone. Dots map to folders; omit `.lua`. Code executes synchronously in the caller's VM, permissions and budget. Results are cached by resolved file per caller generation; no returned value becomes `true`. Lookup/loading failures return `nil, reason`; circular imports are rejected. Reload consumers to adopt changed library code. Unlike exports, no live Lua object crosses a VM boundary. No HTTP, native `package` loader or unrestricted filesystem access is exposed; the dedicated-server sandbox has no `require`.
returns: module value (true when no value is returned), or nil on loading failure
example:
local PZ, reason = require('@polyzone')
assert(PZ, reason)
local zone = PZ.CircleZone:Create({x=100, y=200, z=20}, 15, {name='meeting_point'})

name: vec
summary: Builds a vector of the size the arguments imply.
description: Available in both runtimes. With two, three or four numbers it builds a vector2, vector3 or vector4. With a single table it picks the size from the axes actually present: w means vector4, else z means vector3, else y means vector2 -- which makes vec(position) the short way to wrap a position returned by any existing API. A quaternion is refused, because vec makes vectors.
returns: vector2, vector3 or vector4, or nil, reason
example:
-- Wrap any position table and measure distance with #
local shop = vec(-1442.2, 127.4, 18.0)
if #(vec(Open77.character.state().position) - shop) < 3.0 then
    Open77.hud.notify("Press E to shop")
end

name: vector2
summary: Builds a 2D vector: a plain { x, y } table with vector behaviour.
description: Available in both runtimes. Same operators, swizzles and methods as vector3, minus cross, which answers nil, "cross_requires_vector3". Takes two finite numbers, or one vector or { x =, y = } table to copy.
example:
-- Screen-space distance between two points
local a, b = vector2(0.5, 0.5), vector2(0.7, 0.4)
print(#(a - b))

name: vector3
summary: Builds a 3D vector: a plain { x, y, z } table with vector behaviour.
description: Available in both runtimes, from the shared prelude scripting/lua/open77_vector.lua. Takes three finite numbers, or one vector or { x =, y =, z = } table to copy. The result IS a table with real x, y and z fields, so every API that accepts a position table accepts it unchanged and json.encode emits {"x":..,"y":..,"z":..}. Supports + - * / (by a vector, a position table or a number), unary minus, # for magnitude, == (exact, same kind only), tostring/.. as vector3(1.0, 2.0, 3.0), the swizzles .xy/.xz/.yz/.xyz/.zyx, and the methods length, lengthSquared, distance, distanceSquared, normalize (zero stays zero), dot, cross, lerp (unclamped), unpack and table. Fields are read-only except the components themselves, which Lua 5.4 cannot intercept. Operators raise; this constructor returns nil, reason. See the Vectors and quaternions guide.
example:
-- Is the player within 3 m of the shop counter?
local counter = vector3(-1442.2, 127.4, 18.0)
if #(vector3(Open77.character.position()) - counter) < 3.0 then
    Open77.hud.notify("Press E to shop", { replace = true })
end

name: vector4
summary: Builds a 4D vector: a plain { x, y, z, w } table with vector behaviour.
description: Available in both runtimes. Same operators and methods as vector3, minus cross. Its swizzles reach w, so v.xyz narrows a vector4 to a vector3. Takes four finite numbers, or one vector or { x =, y =, z =, w = } table to copy.
example:
-- A spawn point with its heading as w
local spawn = vector4(-1442.2, 127.4, 18.0, 90.0)
Open77.travel.teleport(spawn.x, spawn.y, spawn.z, spawn.w)

name: Await
summary: Waits for a promise; exactly promise:await().
description: Provided because ported code writes it this way. It needs a managed task like any await: outside one it answers nil, await_requires_scheduler_coroutine rather than parking the VM.
returns: the resolved values, or nil, reason
example:
-- A FiveM-style await of an export promise
Citizen.CreateThread(function()
    local pending = Open77.exports.call("open77_notifications", "show", { message = "Hello" })
    local result = Citizen.Await(pending)
    print(result and result.ok)
end)

name: ClearTick
summary: Alias of ClearTick.
description: Citizen holds the very same function values the bare globals do, not copies, so a ported resource may use either spelling and a stack trace names the same function.
example:
-- Same function as ClearTick, under the FiveM name
local tick = Citizen.SetTick(function() drawMarker() end)
AddEventHandler("delivery:done", function() Citizen.ClearTick(tick) end)

name: ClearTimeout
summary: Alias of ClearTimeout.
description: Citizen holds the very same function values the bare globals do, not copies, so a ported resource may use either spelling and a stack trace names the same function.
example:
-- Cancel a pending timer, FiveM spelling
local timer = Citizen.SetTimeout(5000, function() closeMenu() end)
AddEventHandler("menu:closed", function() Citizen.ClearTimeout(timer) end)

name: CreateThread
summary: Alias of CreateThread.
description: Citizen holds the very same function values the bare globals do, not copies, so a ported resource may use either spelling and a stack trace names the same function. Citizen.CreateThreadNow is deliberately absent: this scheduler starts a task on the next pass, and resuming one inline from inside a running task would reset that task's instruction counter and deadline mid-flight.
example:
-- A ported FiveM loop runs unchanged
Citizen.CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        Citizen.Wait(1000)
        print("still here")
    end
end)

name: SetTick
summary: Alias of SetTick.
description: Citizen holds the very same function values the bare globals do, not copies, so a ported resource may use either spelling and a stack trace names the same function. See SetTick for the per-frame budget and the five-consecutive-failure cancellation.
example:
-- Per-frame work, FiveM spelling
Citizen.SetTick(function()
    if Open77.input.isDown("mouse2") then showAimOverlay() end
end)

name: SetTimeout
summary: Alias of SetTimeout.
description: Citizen holds the very same function values the bare globals do, not copies, so a ported resource may use either spelling and a stack trace names the same function.
example:
-- Hide the hint after 4 seconds
Citizen.SetTimeout(4000, function() Open77.hud.clearNotify() end)

name: Trace
summary: Writes to the resource log at debug level; the same function as Open77.log.debug.
description: FiveM's trace channel, mapped onto the log this resource already writes to. It is not a separate sink and has no separate filter.
example:
-- Debug-level log line, FiveM spelling
Citizen.Trace("menu opened by key")

name: Wait
summary: Alias of Wait.
description: Citizen holds the very same function values the bare globals do, not copies, so a ported resource may use either spelling and a stack trace names the same function. Only usable inside a managed task.
example:
-- Inside any managed task
Citizen.CreateThread(function()
    Citizen.Wait(500)
    Open77.hud.notify("Half a second later")
end)

name: await
summary: Waits for a promise to settle.
description: Only usable inside a `CreateThread`.
example:
-- Wait for a notification export to answer
CreateThread(function()
    local pending = Open77.exports.call("open77_notifications", "show", { message = "Saved" })
    local result, reason = pending:await()
    if not result then print("show failed: " .. tostring(reason)) end
end)

name: next
summary: Schedules a continuation for when the promise settles.
description: Not chainable: it returns the id of the task it schedules, not a new promise, so p:next(a):next(b) does not work and sequences belong in a CreateThread with :await(). The id cancels a continuation that is still waiting. A rejection is recognised by shape -- the nil, <string reason> pair :await() returns -- which is this codebase's failure convention everywhere, so a promise deliberately resolved with a leading nil followed by a string reads as rejected.
example:
-- Fire-and-forget: run a continuation when the export answers, without a thread
local pending = Open77.exports.call("open77_notifications", "show", { message = "Saved" })
if pending then
    pending:next(function(result) print("shown", result.ok) end, function(reason) print("failed", reason) end)
end

name: reject
summary: Settles a promise you created with promise.new as failed.
description: Same shape and same refusals as resolve. A non-string reason becomes promise_rejected, because the reason has to survive as text for the awaiter's nil, reason pair to mean anything.
example:
-- Reject a promise you created when the player cancels the dialog
local answer = promise.new()
AddEventHandler("dialog:cancelled", function() answer:reject("cancelled") end)

name: resolve
summary: Settles a promise you created with promise.new, with the values the awaiter receives.
description: Only a promise this resource created can be resolved; one returned by Open77.exports.call or Open77.net.call is settled by the runtime. Settling twice answers false, promise_already_settled, and a promise whose single consumer has already taken its value answers false, promise_cancelled. On the client the values cross the same serialization boundary exports use, so one that cannot be carried is refused with false, promise_value_not_serializable rather than silently dropped.
example:
-- Resolve a promise you created when the dialog is answered
local answered = promise.new()
AddEventHandler("dialog:answered", function(yes) answered:resolve(yes) end)

name: status
summary: State of the promise, without waiting.
description: Returns the promise state without yielding the current coroutine. Use it for polling or diagnostics; `await()` remains the normal way to receive a completed export result.
example:
-- Poll a promise from a tick instead of awaiting it
SetTick(function()
    if pending and pending:status() ~= "pending" then
        print("settled:", pending:status())
        pending = nil
    end
end)

name: approveSlam
summary: Admits or refuses a pending slam activation.
description: Requires `player.abilities.project`. `allowed` must be a boolean -- there is no third answer, and a non-boolean is refused as `invalid_approval` rather than read as false. The sequence must match a pending activation on this owned request.
example:
-- The support resource admits the slam the server just accepted
RegisterNetEvent("slam:accepted", function(sequence)
    Open77.abilities.approveSlam(slamRequest, sequence, true)
end)

name: cancelSlam
summary: Cancels a slam activation, with a reason.
description: Requires `player.abilities.project`. The reason is a string of 1 to 96 characters and is required: an unexplained cancellation would leave nothing in the log to explain a slam that did not happen.
example:
-- The server refused the slam: cancel the native activation with a reason
RegisterNetEvent("slam:refused", function(sequence, reason)
    Open77.abilities.cancelSlam(slamRequest, sequence, reason or "server_refused")
end)

name: configureSlam
summary: Configures the calling resource's native Ground Slam projector.
description: Client support API requiring player.abilities.project and a running resource. options may contain ground and air booleans (at least one true), staminaManaged=true, maxDurationMs from 500 through 15000 and finite maxFallSpeed greater than zero through 60. These are adapter readiness bounds, not arbitrary motion or damage controls. Returns a configuration request handle or nil, reason; native projection acknowledgement and server admission are still required. Server creators normally use Open77.abilities.define/grant through the optional support resource. No paid implant or vanilla perk progression is changed. See ground-slam.md; a returned handle does not prove playable native movement.

name: presentSlam
summary: Projects a correlated, server-accepted Ground Slam phase for an observer.
description: Client support API requiring player.abilities.project and a running resource. Accepts a positive safe-integer playerId, a 32-hex-character activation ID, uint32 sequence greater than zero, phase, airborne boolean and elapsedMs from zero through 30000. Phases are windup, descent, contact, impact, recovery, complete, cancelled or rejected. It owns presentation only and never authorizes movement, damage or entitlement. Owner-scoped cleanup, incarnation checks and Dash/Slam pose arbitration remain native responsibilities. true means the adapter accepted the presentation request; actual rendering and sound require live observation. See ground-slam.md for the authoritative public workflow.
example:
-- Replay a remote player's slam phase the server relayed to this observer
RegisterNetEvent("slam:phase", function(playerId, activationId, sequence, phase, airborne, elapsedMs)
    Open77.abilities.presentSlam(playerId, activationId, sequence, phase, airborne, elapsedMs)
end)

name: releaseSlam
summary: Releases this resource's ground-slam ownership.
description: Requires `player.abilities.project`. Takes no arguments: the owner is the calling resource, which cannot be supplied. Resource stop releases it for you, so a reloading gamemode never leaves the slam claimed.
example:
-- The mini-game ends: give the slam projector back
AddEventHandler("minigame:ended", function()
    Open77.abilities.releaseSlam()
end)

name: requestSlam
summary: Asks the native layer to begin a slam and returns its sequence.
description: Requires `player.abilities.project`. The returned sequence identifies this activation for `approveSlam` and `cancelSlam`; it is how a late answer is stopped from acting on the wrong slam.
example:
-- The player pressed the slam key: begin the native activation and remember its sequence
RegisterKeyMapping("slam", "Ground slam", "L", function()
    local sequence = Open77.abilities.requestSlam(slamRequest)
    if sequence then pendingSlam = sequence end
end)

name: slamActivity
summary: The local character's current ground-slam activity, with its recent history.
description: Requires `player.abilities.read`. Returns `{ request, sequence, phaseSequence, impactSequence, elapsedMs, phase, mode, reason, grounded, position, contact, verticalSpeed, history }`, where `history` holds up to sixteen recent phase receipts. It is what the presenting resource replays through `presentSlam`; it is observation, not authority.
example:
-- Show the current slam phase on a debug overlay
local activity = Open77.abilities.slamActivity()
if activity then print(activity.phase, activity.verticalSpeed) end

name: slamState
summary: The phase of a ground-slam configuration request.
description: Requires `player.abilities.read`. Takes the request id `configureSlam` returned and answers the native phase plus a reason. One dispatcher serves the six slam operations, so they share identical permission, lifetime and handle checks.
example:
-- Is the projector ready before the key is enabled?
if Open77.abilities.slamState(slamRequest) == "ready" then enableSlamKey() end

name: clear
summary: Removes every world anchor owned by the calling resource.
description: Other resources are unaffected. Anchors are also cleared automatically on stop, reload, world exit, and when their page is destroyed.
example:
-- Leaving the mission removes every prompt this resource pinned
AddEventHandler("mission:ended", function()
    Open77.anchors.clear()
end)

name: create
summary: Anchors a world point, projected by the plugin on every game frame.
description:
No permission of its own: the capability is the one `Open77.camera.project` already grants ungated, with the sampling moved off the Lua tick.

Options require exactly one of `position` (a fixed world point) or `entity` (followed live, with an optional world-axis `offset`) -- passing both, or neither, is refused with `position_or_entity_required`. They also accept `tag` (`[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]`, 32 bytes), `maxDistance` (default 100.0), `minDistance` (default 0.0) and `visible` (default true).

`render` selects the delivery and is fixed for the anchor's life: `page` (the default) publishes coordinates to a WebUI page, while `card`, `ring` and `dot` are drawn natively by the plugin in the frame that presents them. `page` is REQUIRED only for `render = "page"`; a native style has nowhere to publish and needs no surface at all, though a page passed alongside one is still ownership-checked. A page this resource does not own is refused with `stale_or_unowned_page`.

Native styles take a `presentation` table: `label`, `sublabel` (192 bytes each), `key` (`card` only, 8 bytes), `color`, `accent`, `background` (`#RRGGBB` or `#RRGGBBAA`; anything else is refused as `invalid_color` / `invalid_accent` / `invalid_background`), `scale`, `thickness`, `radius` and `groundOffset` (`ring`), `progress` (`card`; negative draws no bar) and `showDistance`. The colour defaults are the OPEN//77 design tokens -- `color` `#F2F6F8`, `accent` `#22D8E2`, `background` `#0A1220F0` -- and they matter more than defaults usually do, because `presentation` is patched whole: see `Open77.anchors.update`.

The batched `open77:anchors` event a page receives is the COMPLETE set for that surface; an id that is absent is hidden, out of its distance band, behind the camera, or its entity is not streamed. Treat absence as gone rather than holding the last coordinate. Limits are 32 anchors per resource and 128 in total.
example:
-- A native "press E" card pinned above the delivery crate, visible within 30 m
local anchor, reason = Open77.anchors.create({
    render = "card",
    position = { x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.8 },
    maxDistance = 30,
    presentation = { label = "Deliver package", key = "E", accent = "#00D8FF" },
})
if not anchor then print("anchor refused: " .. reason) end

name: list
summary: Lists the calling resource's world anchors with their last projection.
description: Each snapshot carries its requested definition plus `render` (echoing its style), `resolved` (where the anchor actually was on the last frame -- for an entity anchor the live transform plus the offset, not what was registered) and `screen` (`x`, `y` normalised to [0..1] with a top-left origin, and `depth` in metres in front of the camera), `distance`, `onScreen`, and `projected`. An invisible anchor is still projected and still listed, so this stays the way to decide which of a resource's world points deserve one of its 32 slots.
returns: array of { id, tag, kind, render, entity, offset, surface, maxDistance, minDistance, visible, projected, onScreen, distance, position, resolved, screen }, or nil
example:
-- Which of our anchors is on screen and closest? That one gets the key
local best
for _, anchor in ipairs(Open77.anchors.list() or {}) do
    if anchor.onScreen and (not best or anchor.distance < best.distance) then best = anchor end
end

name: remove
summary: Removes one resource-owned world anchor.
description: Removing an unknown handle succeeds, so teardown is idempotent.
example:
-- The crate was picked up: drop its prompt
RegisterNetEvent("delivery:done", function()
    Open77.anchors.remove(crateAnchor)
end)

name: update
summary: Patches a resource-owned world anchor.
description:
Top-level fields are patched individually: only what you supply changes. **`presentation` is the exception and is patched WHOLE.** `update(handle, { presentation = { label = "Locked" } })` does not keep the colours you set at creation -- it resets `color`, `accent`, `background` and every other presentation field to its default. Always resend the complete presentation table, or keep it in a local and patch that. A prompt changes its label, its key and its hold progress on the same frame or not at all, which is why the table has one dirty flag rather than eleven.

Neither `page` nor the anchor's kind is patchable; patching a field the kind does not own -- `position` on an entity anchor, `entity` or `offset` on a position anchor -- is refused with `anchor_kind_mismatch` rather than ignored. `render` is fixed at creation and a patch carrying it is refused with `render_is_not_patchable`. Re-pointing an entity anchor at a new `entity` is supported, which is the respawn case. Ownership prevents mutation of another resource's anchor.

name: cancel
summary: Cancel the local player's RP action and pending requests.
description: Stops local presentation and queues a reliable self-cancellation request. Omitting playbackId also abandons pending starts; late acceptances are cancelled. Supply the ID from request() or sequence() in delayed callbacks so they cannot stop a replacement action. A mismatched active ID rejects with stale_playback. Resolving true means cancellation was queued (or nothing was active), not that the server has acknowledged the stop; observe onPlayerAnimationChanged for authoritative state. A player may cancel their own server-started action, never another player's action. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to true when cancellation is queued or already inactive
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, err = Open77.animations.cancel()
    if not pending then print(err); return end
    local cancelled, rejected = pending:await()
    if not cancelled then print(rejected) end
end)

name: clip
summary: Look up which RP profile owns a clip name.
description: Clip-first discovery: the counterpart of get(), for a caller that knows the animation name but not the action that carries it. Resolves to a copy of the owning profile, or nil when no shipped device's authored tree contains that clip. Clip names are case-sensitive. A name can appear in the game's 23,044-entry discovery inventory and still resolve to nil here: only the 70 clips of the twelve shipped devices are addressable. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to the owning profile table, or nil when no shipped device carries the clip
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending = Open77.animations.clip('stand__dance__02__dancing__03')
    local profile = pending and pending:await()
    if profile then print(profile.id) end -- dance
end)

name: clips
summary: List every addressable clip with the profile that owns it.
description: The closest thing this engine has to enumerating an animation dictionary. Returns one row per clip, { clip = string, profile = string }, sorted by clip name. The optional query is a case-insensitive substring matched against the clip name and the profile ID; it must be at most 128 characters. This is the complete addressable set, not a catalogue of what exists: a clip plays only because a shipped device's authored workspot tree carries it. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to an array of { clip, profile } rows
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, invalid_query if the query is too long
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local rows = Open77.animations.clips('smoke'):await()
    for _, row in ipairs(rows or {}) do print(row.profile, row.clip) end
end)

name: current
summary: The clip a body is currently playing.
description: Returns false when it is playing nothing — which is a state, not an error.
example:
-- Is the remote player's body playing an emote?
local entity = Open77.players.entity(playerId)
local clip = entity and Open77.animations.current(entity)
if clip then print("playing", clip) end

name: get
summary: Look up one RP profile without starting playback.
description: Resolves to a copy of the profile, including its default clip and exact allowed variants. Profile IDs are case-sensitive. An unknown ID resolves to nil without an error; check the second await result to distinguish a failed request from a missing profile. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to a profile table, or nil when absent
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, err = Open77.animations.get('smoke')
    if not pending then print(err); return end
    local profile, rejected = pending:await()
    if rejected then print(rejected); return end
    if profile then print(profile.clip, #profile.clips) end
end)

name: list
summary: Find synchronized RP animation profiles in the local catalogue.
description: Resolves to copied profile definitions containing id, label, category, default clip and allowed clips. The optional query is a case-insensitive substring across ID, label and category, up to 128 characters. An empty query returns all 15 profiles; no match returns an empty array. Catalogue membership and male/female rig bindings are not proof of native playback validation. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to a profile array
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, err = Open77.animations.list('social')
    if not pending then print(err); return end
    local profiles, rejected = pending:await()
    if not profiles then print(rejected); return end
    for _, profile in ipairs(profiles) do print(profile.id, profile.label) end
end)

name: play
summary: Plays a named animation on a body.
description: Does not work on the local player: their body cannot hold a workspot. Use `Open77.animations.playSelf` for that, which stands a double in for them.
example:
local ok, reason = Open77.animations.play(entityId, "emote_smoke")
if not ok then print("refused: " .. reason) end

name: playSelf
summary: Plays an emote on the local player, through a stand-in body.
description: The player's own body cannot hold a workspot, so an invisible double takes their place for the length of the clip. This is a separate call rather than `play` with the player's id because the mechanism is genuinely different.
example:
-- /sit as a purely local emote, through the stand-in body
RegisterCommand("sit", function()
    local ok, reason = Open77.animations.playSelf("emote_sit", true)
    if not ok then Open77.hud.notify("Cannot sit here: " .. reason) end
end, false)

name: request
summary: Request a synchronized RP action for the local player.
description: The server validates the named profile and returns a playback state and playbackId; acceptance does not mean the native workspot has mounted. Options are clip, durationMs and loop only. The clip must belong to the profile. loop defaults to true; omitted or zero duration is indefinite when looping. With loop=false the default is 5000 ms. A nonzero duration must be an integer from 1000 to 600000 ms. Playback temporarily uses the F7 third-person body without changing the saved camera preference. Moving, combat and unsafe player states interrupt it. Use cancel(), not the legacy local stop(entity), for synchronized actions. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to the server-accepted playback state
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected or timed out
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, err = Open77.animations.request('smoke', { loop = false, durationMs = 15000 })
    if not pending then print(err); return end
    local playback, rejected = pending:await()
    if not playback then print(rejected); return end
    print('Accepted action: ' .. playback.playbackId)
end)

name: requestClip
summary: Request a synchronized RP action for the local player by clip name.
description: The same request as request(), addressed by animation instead of by profile: the owning profile is resolved from the generated catalogue and the server re-validates it. This is the honest analogue of TaskPlayAnim -- a clip name and playback options -- and it is bounded the same way playback is. A name no shipped device carries is refused with unknown_clip before anything goes on the wire, rather than started and silently ignored by the engine. Options are durationMs and loop only; the clip is the argument. FiveM's blendIn, blendOut, upperBody, holdLastFrame and flags have no workspot equivalent and are refused by name as unsupported_option:<key>. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to the accepted playback state including playbackId
nil, unknown_clip when no shipped device carries the clip; nil, reason on rejection
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local playback, err = Open77.animations.requestClip(
        'stand__dance__02__dancing__03', { loop = true }):await()
    if not playback then print(err); return end
    print(playback.playbackId)
end)

name: sequence
summary: Request an ordered RP sequence for the local player.
description: Accepts 1–16 steps with profile, optional clip and durationMs. Each step defaults to 5000 ms, must last 1000–600000 ms, and the total cannot exceed 600000 ms. The only sequence option is loop, default false. These are server scheduling durations, not measured clip lengths. Profile changes use asynchronous workspot exit/re-entry, not guaranteed seamless blends. The result is authoritative acceptance, not a native rendering acknowledgement. Unlike the server method, this call takes no playerId. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to the server-accepted playback state
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected

name: state
summary: Read the last active RP state visible to this client.
description: Defaults to the local player, or accepts a visible player's network ID. Resolves to a copied canonical state, or nil when inactive or unavailable. It does not query arbitrary players outside the routing bucket or verify native rendering. Fields include playerId, playbackId, epoch, revision, active, steps, loop and step timing. On the client, onPlayerAnimationChanged receives this state as a Lua table; the server event instead passes JSON. Do not use a client observation to grant authoritative rewards. Declare dependency 'open77_animations' in your resource manifest. This asynchronous facade requires the service in the same downloaded resource host, not a separate bootstrap host. Await from a managed coroutine/event handler. No animations.presentation capability is required by the caller; underscore hooks are internal.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to active playback state, or nil when unavailable
nil, reason if dispatch fails; await() returns nil, reason if rejected
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, err = Open77.animations.state()
    if not pending then print(err); return end
    local state, rejected = pending:await()
    if rejected then print(rejected); return end
    if state then print(state.playbackId, state.active) end
end)

name: stop
summary: Stops whatever a body is playing and releases what was set up for it.
description: Stops the workspot animation currently managed by Open77 for the selected body and releases its native animation state. It does not claim or stop arbitrary game animations that Open77 does not own.
example:
-- Stop the emote this resource started on another body
local entity = Open77.players.entity(playerId)
if entity then Open77.animations.stop(entity) end

name: stopSelf
summary: Stops the local player's emote and removes the stand-in.
description: Ends the local-player emote created by `playSelf` and removes its stand-in body. Cleanup is idempotent and is also performed when the owning resource generation stops.
example:
-- Any movement key ends the local emote
RegisterKeyMapping("emote_stop", "Stop emote", "X", function()
    Open77.animations.stopSelf()
end)

name: apply
summary: Applies a previously captured appearance snapshot to the local player.
description: Requires `player.appearance.edit`. The runtime validates the schema, build, catalog digest, gender, option identities, choice bounds, and duplicates before touching the game.
example:
-- Restore the look the server saved for this character
RegisterNetEvent("character:appearance", function(snapshot)
    local ok, reason = Open77.appearance.apply(snapshot)
    if not ok then print("appearance not applied: " .. reason) end
end)

name: capture
summary: Captures the local player's complete validated appearance snapshot.
description: Requires `player.appearance.read`. The snapshot is bound to schema version 1, game build 2.31, a catalog digest, gender hash, and at most 256 head/body/arms options.
returns: table { schemaVersion, gameBuild, catalogDigest, gender, options }, or nil
example:
-- Save the look after the player leaves the ripperdoc
AddEventHandler("appearance:editorClosed", function()
    local snapshot = Open77.appearance.capture()
    if snapshot then TriggerServerEvent("character:saveAppearance", snapshot) end
end)

name: captureBody
summary: Capture the local native body appearance groups.
description: Requires player.appearance.read. Returns {family,groups}, with native part/name hashes and resource key pairs. This readback is for trusted projection services, not a committed character edit or visual proof. Use the selected durable identity adapter for persistence.
example:
local body, err = Open77.appearance.captureBody()
if body then print(body.family, #body.groups) else print(err) end

name: finishCommit
summary: Finishes the current appearance commit transaction.
description: Requires `player.appearance.edit`. Call after a successful apply/persistence flow so the native editor can release its commit state.
example:
-- The server confirmed the save: release the editor's commit state
RegisterNetEvent("character:appearanceSaved", function()
    Open77.appearance.finishCommit()
end)

name: isOpen
summary: Whether the local appearance editor is open.
description: Requires `player.appearance.read`; returns false when the permission or backend is unavailable.
example:
-- Hide the HUD while the editor is open
SetTick(function()
    hud.visible = not Open77.appearance.isOpen()
end)

name: open
summary: Opens the local Cyberpunk appearance editor.
description: Requires `player.appearance.edit`. The optional value may be a mode string or `{ mode = string }`; `ripperdoc` is used by default.
example:
-- Press E at the ripperdoc to open the editor
RegisterKeyMapping("ripperdoc", "Talk to the ripperdoc", "E", function()
    if nearRipperdoc then Open77.appearance.open("ripperdoc") end
end)

name: switchBodyFamily
summary: Starts a guarded body-family transition.
description: Starts a guarded transition to the requested body family and optionally resumes the native editor afterward. It requires player.appearance.edit; completion is consumed with takeBodyFamilyTransition.
example:
-- The player chose the other body family in the creator; resume the editor after
Open77.appearance.switchBodyFamily(true)

name: takeBodyFamilyTransition
summary: Consumes the pending body-family transition result.
description: Consumes the pending body-family transition result once, returning its serialized payload or nil while no result is ready. It requires player.appearance.edit.
example:
-- Poll for the transition result once it is ready
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        local result = Open77.appearance.takeBodyFamilyTransition()
        if result then print("transition finished"); break end
        Wait(250)
    end
end)

name: list
summary: Lists generic files declared by the current resource.
description: Returns the resource files declared by the current manifest. It is an allow-list view, not a directory listing, and does not grant access to undeclared files or arbitrary paths.
example:
-- Print every file this resource declared
for _, path in ipairs(Open77.assets.list()) do print(path) end

name: texture
summary: Validates a declared PNG texture for resource APIs.
description: The path must match the manifest's `files` allowlist. PNG textures are limited to 512 KiB and 512 by 512 pixels.
returns: descriptor { type, asset, mime, width, height, bytes }, or nil
example:
-- Validate the blip icon before using it
local icon, reason = Open77.assets.texture("icons/gang.png")
if icon then Open77.blips.setIcon(hqBlip, icon) else print("bad icon: " .. reason) end

name: destroy
summary: DestroySound: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Free the engine loop when the player gets out of the car
Open77.audio.destroy(engineLoop)
engineLoop = nil

name: getState
summary: GetSoundState: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Restart the siren if it stopped
local state = Open77.audio.getState(sirenId)
if state and state.status == "stopped" then Open77.audio.play(sirenId) end

name: pause
summary: PauseSound: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Pause the radio while the phone rings
AddEventHandler("phone:ringing", function()
    Open77.audio.pause(radioId)
end)

name: play
summary: PlaySound: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Resume the radio the phone call paused
AddEventHandler("phone:hungUp", function()
    Open77.audio.play(radioId)
end)

name: play2D
summary: Play2DSound: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- A UI click on every menu selection
AddEventHandler("menu:selected", function()
    Open77.audio.play2D("audio/click.wav", { volume = 0.5 })
end)

name: play3D
summary: Play3DSound: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- A ringing phone at the booth, audible within 15 m
local ring = Open77.audio.play3D("audio/ring.mp3", { x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.0 }, { maxDistance = 15, loop = true })

name: seek
summary: SeekSound: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Skip the intro of the track
Open77.audio.seek(musicId, 12.5)

name: setPosition
summary: SetSoundPosition: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Keep the boombox sound following the carried prop
SetTick(function()
    Open77.audio.setPosition(boomboxSound, vector3(Open77.character.position()))
end)

name: setVolume
summary: SetSoundVolume: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Fade the music out over two seconds
CreateThread(function()
    for v = 10, 0, -1 do
        Open77.audio.setVolume(musicId, v / 10)
        Wait(200)
    end
    Open77.audio.stop(musicId)
end)

name: stop
summary: StopSound: local package audio.
description: Requires audio.play; network=true is rejected. MP3/PCM WAV decode asynchronously off the game thread. getState reports actual decoder state and cached PCM reuse. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Stop the alarm when the player leaves the building
AddEventHandler("building:left", function()
    Open77.audio.stop(alarmId)
end)

name: attachToEntity
summary: Makes a blip follow an Open77 entity.
description: Changes an owned blip from a fixed world position to tracking a streamed Open77 entity. The entity id is ephemeral and the call requires `ui.vanilla.map`; remove or reattach the blip when its gameplay target changes.
example:
-- The delivery car's blip follows the car
local blip = Open77.blips.create({ position = car.position, sprite = "vehicle", label = "Delivery car" })
Open77.blips.attachToEntity(blip, car.entity)

name: clear
summary: Removes every blip owned by the current resource.
description: Removes every vanilla-map blip owned by the calling resource generation. Other resources' blips are left untouched, and generation teardown performs the same cleanup automatically.
example:
-- The heist is over: drop every blip this resource placed
AddEventHandler("heist:ended", function()
    Open77.blips.clear()
end)

name: clearWaypoint
summary: Clears the player's map waypoint, whoever set it.
description: Untracks the waypoint, including one the player placed themselves, which is what `DeleteWaypoint` means, and destroys the pin only when this resource owns it; another resource's pin stays registered. Clearing when there was no waypoint is a success that reports `false` as its second value, so a caller reconciling state can tell the two apart without an error. Requires `ui.vanilla.map`.
returns: whether a waypoint was actually cleared
reason on failure: permission_denied:ui.vanilla.map, waypoint_unavailable_on_this_host, wrong_thread, world_unavailable
example:
-- The taxi fare is cancelled: remove the route
local ok, wasSet = Open77.blips.clearWaypoint()
if ok and wasSet then exports.open77_chat:addMessage("Route cancelled.") end

name: create
summary: Creates a resource-owned vanilla map pin.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.map`. Provide exactly one of `position` or `entity`. Set `routable = true` on a positional blip to use Cyberpunk's trusted custom-waypoint definition; its sprite becomes `CustomPositionVariant` and `track(id)` can then start native GPS routing. The returned 64-bit generation handle is a decimal string and is cleaned up automatically when the resource stops.

params.name: options
params.type: table { position|entity, sprite?, label?, icon?, active?, visibleThroughWalls?, routable?, slot?, offset? }

name: get
summary: Reads one blip owned by the current resource.
description: Returns a read-only snapshot of one blip owned by the calling resource. The handle must still belong to the current generation; a stale or foreign id is rejected.
example:
-- Is the blip still active?
local blip = Open77.blips.get(blipId)
if blip and not blip.active then Open77.blips.setActive(blipId, true) end

name: list
summary: Lists blips owned by the current resource.
description: Lists snapshots of all vanilla-map blips owned by the calling resource generation. The returned tables are copies and changing them does not mutate the map.
example:
-- Print every blip this resource owns
for _, blip in ipairs(Open77.blips.list()) do
    print(blip.id, blip.label)
end

name: remove
summary: Removes one owned blip.
description: Deletes one blip owned by the calling resource and invalidates its handle. Removal is resource-scoped, so one package cannot erase another package's map state.
example:
-- The package was delivered: remove its map pin
RegisterNetEvent("delivery:done", function()
    Open77.blips.remove(deliveryBlip)
end)

name: setActive
summary: Activates or deactivates a vanilla mappin.
description: Updates the active/highlighted state of an owned vanilla-map blip. This changes presentation only and does not create a route or change server state.
example:
-- Highlight the shop blip only while it is open
RegisterNetEvent("shop:hours", function(open)
    Open77.blips.setActive(shopBlip, open)
end)

name: setDescription
summary: Sets the custom fullscreen-map description of an owned blip.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.map`. The description is displayed by Open77's fullscreen-map tooltip for the selected native mappin.
example:
-- A tooltip with the shop's opening hours on the fullscreen map
Open77.blips.setDescription(shopBlip, "Open 20:00 - 04:00. Cash only.")

name: setIcon
summary: Sets a declared PNG icon or restores the native sprite.
description: Accepts a path, a texture descriptor, `{ asset, size }`, or false. The native mappin remains underneath for map selection, routing, tooltips, and fallback.
example:
-- Use the resource's own PNG for the gang HQ blip
Open77.blips.setIcon(hqBlip, { asset = "icons/gang.png", size = 32 })

name: setLabel
summary: Changes the fullscreen-map tooltip title.
description: Open77 keeps the label in private script data, independent from the vanilla variant's generic title.
example:
-- Rename the blip as the job progresses
Open77.blips.setLabel(jobBlip, "Pick up the package")

name: setPosition
summary: Moves a blip to a world position.
description: Also detaches an entity-following blip.
example:
-- Move the "next checkpoint" blip as the race progresses
RegisterNetEvent("race:checkpoint", function(position)
    Open77.blips.setPosition(checkpointBlip, position)
end)

name: setRange
summary: Switches a blip off beyond a distance and back on when the player returns.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.map`. `metres` is 0..4000; `false` or `0` clears the gate. This is Open77's own distance test driving the vanilla `SetMappinActive`, not a mappin property: `gamemappinsMappinData` has no range field. It is therefore NOT FiveM's `SetBlipAsShortRange`, which hides a blip from the minimap only -- 2.31 offers no per-surface control, so out of range means off on the HUD, the minimap and the world map alike. It composes with `active` rather than overriding it. An entity-following blip is measured from the body it follows, and keeps its last state while that body is not streamed in.
example:
-- The vendor blip only shows within 300 m
Open77.blips.setRange(vendorBlip, 300)

name: setSprite
summary: Changes the vanilla mappin variant.
description: Accepts an exact 2.31 variant name, a stable alias, or an integer from 0 through 146. See `wiki/blips.md` for the complete list.
example:
-- Turn the marker red once the zone becomes dangerous
Open77.blips.setSprite(zoneBlip, "danger")

name: setTitle
summary: Sets the custom fullscreen-map title of an owned blip.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.map`. This is the semantic title alias of `setLabel`; the HUD does not permanently render it beside the icon.
example:
-- Title shown when the blip is selected on the fullscreen map
Open77.blips.setTitle(garageBlip, "Your garage")

name: setTrackingAlternative
summary: Sets another owned blip as the routing alternative.
description: Passing nil clears it. This does not force the world-map controller to start tracking.
example:
-- Route to the back entrance if the front is tracked
Open77.blips.setTrackingAlternative(frontDoorBlip, backDoorBlip)

name: setVisibleThroughWalls
summary: Changes vanilla through-wall visibility.
description: Controls whether an owned world marker remains visible when geometry occludes it. The setting affects presentation on this client only and requires `ui.vanilla.map`.
example:
-- Team-mates stay visible through buildings
Open77.blips.setVisibleThroughWalls(teamBlip, true)

name: setWaypoint
summary: Places the player's map waypoint, replacing whatever was tracked.
description: Registers a routable custom-position mappin and makes it the tracked destination, so the vanilla GPS calculates a road route to it exactly as it does for a waypoint the player set by hand. The pin is owned by the calling resource and is destroyed when that resource stops, so a crashed taxi script leaves no permanent arrow on the map. Calling it again moves the same pin rather than registering a second one. Requires `ui.vanilla.map`.
returns: reason on failure: permission_denied:ui.vanilla.map, invalid_position, waypoint_unavailable_on_this_host, too_many_blips, wrong_thread, world_unavailable
example:
-- The taxi order sets the customer's GPS to the pickup point
RegisterNetEvent("taxi:pickup", function(position)
    Open77.blips.setWaypoint(position)
end)

name: sprites
summary: Lists every usable mappin variant in the current build.
description: Returns 147 entries for Cyberpunk 2077 2.31. This metadata query does not require map mutation permission.
example:
-- Print every usable sprite name once
