for _, sprite in ipairs(Open77.blips.sprites()) do
    print(sprite.value, sprite.name)
end

name: track
summary: Selects this blip as the vanilla manually tracked destination.
description: Follows the same internal `MappinSystem` operation as selecting a pin on the fullscreen map. This changes the tracked id; native road calculation additionally requires the blip to have been created with `routable = true`. Returns `changed = false` when this blip is already tracked.
example:
-- Start GPS routing to the race start
local blip = Open77.blips.create({ position = raceStart, routable = true, label = "Street race" })
Open77.blips.track(blip)

name: untrack
summary: Safely clears manual tracking for this blip.
description: The native action is invoked only if this owned blip is currently tracked, so a resource cannot untrack a quest or another system's pin.
example:
-- Stop routing once the player arrives
RegisterNetEvent("race:arrived", function()
    Open77.blips.untrack(raceBlip)
end)

name: update
summary: Updates several properties of an owned blip.
description: A replacement mappin is registered before the previous one is removed. `position` switches to positional mode; `entity` switches to attached mode.
example:
-- Several changes in one operation
Open77.blips.update(jobBlip, { label = "Drop-off", sprite = "objective", active = true })

name: waypoint
summary: Where the player's map waypoint is, or nil when there is none.
description: Reads the vanilla waypoint, the manually tracked mappin, whoever set it: this resource, another resource, or the player right-clicking the fullscreen map. `nil` with no reason means there is simply no waypoint; `nil` WITH a reason means the question could not be asked. A GPS script has to tell those apart, because cancelling a fare is correct for only the first. Requires `ui.vanilla.map`.
returns: table { x, y, z }, or nil when no waypoint is set
reason (only on failure): permission_denied:ui.vanilla.map, waypoint_unavailable_on_this_host, native_unavailable, wrong_thread, world_unavailable
example:
-- The taxi drives to wherever the customer put their map waypoint
local to = Open77.blips.waypoint()
if to then
    TriggerServerEvent("taxi:order", to)
else
    Open77.hud.notify("Set a waypoint on the map first")
end

name: call
summary: Alias of Open77.net.call.
description: Open77.callbacks is the same four functions under a second name, for resources that prefer to read the callback surface as its own namespace. Pick one spelling per resource; the two are the same functions, not copies.
example:
-- Ask the server for the shop stock (alias of Open77.net.call)
CreateThread(function()
    local pending = Open77.callbacks.call("getStock", "ammo_box")
    local count, price = pending and pending:await()
    print(count, price)
end)

name: callAwait
summary: Alias of Open77.net.callAwait.
description: Awaits the promise, so it needs a CreateThread or another managed task.
returns: the handler's return values, or nil, reason
example:
-- The same question, awaited in one line
CreateThread(function()
    local count, price = Open77.callbacks.callAwait("getStock", "ammo_box")
    print(count, price)
end)

name: register
summary: Alias of Open77.net.register.
description: Answers a question the server asks with Open77.net.callClient. The handler receives the call's arguments and no source, because the caller is always the server.

name: unregister
summary: Alias of Open77.net.unregister.
description: Stops answering that name; a later request is refused with callback_not_found on the next frame.
example:
-- The shop UI closed: stop answering
Open77.callbacks.unregister("confirmPurchase")

name: activate
summary: Takes the view with a scripted camera, optionally blending into it.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.script`. `options.blendMs` (0..60000) interpolates from wherever the view currently is; omit it for a cut. Returns `true` and, as a SECOND value, an `Open77.Promise` that resolves when the blend completes and REJECTS with a reason if the shot is released first -- `player_died`, `resource_stopped`, `camera_superseded` and the rest. A cut settles before the call returns and hands back no promise. Refused with `camera_held_by:<resource>` when another resource has the view (never silently stolen), with `camera_unavailable` when the player is dead or a perspective transition is in flight, and with `invalid_argument` past the 250 m streaming range.
returns: true and an Open77.Promise, or false, reason
example:
-- A one-second blend into a fixed camera looking at the stage
CreateThread(function()
    local cam = Open77.camera.create({ position = vector3(-1442.2, 127.4, 20.0), lookAt = vector3(-1448.2, 96.1, 17.5) })
    local ok, blend = Open77.camera.activate(cam, { blendMs = 1000 })
    if ok and blend then blend:await() end
    Wait(5000)
    Open77.camera.deactivate({ blendMs = 1000 })
end)

name: aimRay
summary: The ray from the camera along its forward vector: what the reticle points at.
description: `Open77.camera.view()` plus `Open77.world.raycast` in one call. Unlike `Open77.inspector.target`, which answers with an entity under the crosshair or nothing, this hits empty pavement too, which is what placing a prop, a blip or a teleport target needs. `maxDistance` defaults to 200 m and is capped at 5000. Requires `world.query`. Takes the same `entities` option as `Open77.world.raycast`, adding an `entity` table naming what the reticle is actually on, which is the targeting and shot-validation question this call exists for. Without the option the result is unchanged.
returns: table { hit, position, normal, material, distance }, or nil
reason: permission_denied:world.query, invalid_distance, camera_unavailable, or the engine status
example:
local ray = Open77.camera.aimRay(100)
if ray and ray.hit then Open77.blips.create({ position = ray.position, label = "Here" }) end

name: attach
summary: Parents a scripted camera to an entity, or restores the player's own camera.
description: Attaches the Open77 camera to a game entity using the supplied local offset and rotation. Camera ownership is local to the resource generation; attaching replaces the resource's previous detached/attached camera state.
example:
-- Parent a scripted camera to the local player's body, one metre behind and above
Open77.camera.attach(camId, 0, vector3(0.0, -1.0, 1.0))

name: cameras
summary: This resource's scripted cameras, and whether it holds the view.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.script`. Owner-scoped for the camera list, like `Open77.screen.state`. `holder` is NOT owner-scoped: it names whoever has the view, including another resource, because that is the one question a `camera_held_by:` refusal leaves a caller asking. `phase` is `idle`, `blending_in`, `holding` or `blending_out`.
returns: table { held, holder, phase, activeCamera, blendRemainingMs, cameras }
example:
-- Only take the view if nobody else holds it
local cams = Open77.camera.cameras()
if cams.held and cams.holder ~= GetCurrentResourceName() then
    print("view is held by", cams.holder)
end

name: clearOrbit
summary: Releases this resource's preview orbit and framing.
description: Requires camera.preview. Clears the calling resource's preview orbit and releases preview ownership. It is a successful no-op if no preview is owned; it refuses to clear another resource's preview with camera_preview_owned.
example:
-- The wardrobe preview closes: release the orbit
AddEventHandler("wardrobe:closed", function()
    Open77.camera.clearOrbit()
end)

name: create
summary: Creates a scripted camera and returns its id.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.script`. Nothing is rendered until `activate`. Options: `position` (world vector3, required unless `attachTo`), `attachTo` (entity; `0` is the local player's body), `offset` (vector3 in the parent's frame, X right / Y forward / Z up; also accepted as `position`), `lookAt` (a world vector3 OR an entity, re-solved every frame), `rotation` (quaternion `{x,y,z,w}` or Euler degrees `{pitch,yaw,roll}`, used when there is no `lookAt`), `fov` (5..170 degrees; omit or 0 to leave the engine's field of view alone). 16 cameras per resource, 64 per client. See the Scripted cameras guide.

name: deactivate
summary: Gives the view back to the player, optionally blending out.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.script`. `options.blendMs` blends back to the player's own eyes and finishes exactly on them, so the restore writes the value already on screen. Only the holder may. Returns `true` and an `Open77.Promise` for a blended hand-back; an instant one is already finished and hands back none.
returns: true and an Open77.Promise, or false, reason
example:
-- Give the view back after the cinematic, blending over half a second
Open77.camera.deactivate({ blendMs = 500 })

name: destroy
summary: Destroys a scripted camera.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.script`. Destroying the camera you are looking through is legal and IS a release: the view comes back. Refusing would let a resource paint itself into a corner, and silently keeping the view would be worse.
example:
-- Clean up the cinematic camera when it is no longer needed
Open77.camera.destroy(cam)

name: detach
summary: Detaches the camera from the body, with an offset in the body's own space.
description: Detaches the Open77 camera from its target while retaining a controllable camera view. It does not synchronize a camera to other players and is automatically restored during resource cleanup.
example:
-- A selfie view: the player's own camera moved two metres in front of them
Open77.camera.detach(0.0, 2.0, 1.6)

name: detachFrom
summary: Un-parents a scripted camera from its entity.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.script`. NOT spelled `detach`: `Open77.camera.detach()` already means 'move the player's own camera off their eyes' and all of its arguments are optional, so there is no arity left to overload. The camera keeps the pose it had; the next `setTransform` places it.
example:
-- Stop following the car; the camera stays where it was
Open77.camera.detachFrom(cam)

name: follow
summary: Rides an entity: a camera behind it, aimed at it, both re-solved every frame.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.script`. Entity `0` is the local player's body. `options`: `distance` (metres behind, 0..100, default 4.0), `height` (metres above, -50..50, default 1.5), `side` (metres right, -50..50, default 0), `fov` (5..170 degrees; omit or 0 to leave it alone), `blendMs` (0..60000). The offsets are in the TARGET's own frame, so `distance` means behind him rather than north of him. ONE camera per resource: calling `follow` again retargets it and returns the same id, superseding the previous call's promise with `camera_superseded`. `Open77.camera.unfollow` gives the view back and destroys it. Not a new way to hold the view -- it is `create` + `lookAt` + `activate`, so every release rule on the Scripted cameras page applies unchanged. The world streams around the player's BODY, not around the lens, so a distant target renders an empty frame: move the body there first. See the Scripted cameras guide.
returns: camera id and a blend promise, or nil, reason
example:
-- A spectator camera four metres behind another player
local cam, blend = Open77.camera.follow(Open77.players.entity(targetId), { distance = 4.0, height = 1.5, blendMs = 400 })

name: lookAt
summary: Points a scripted camera at a world point or an entity.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.script`. A vector3 aims at a fixed world point; anything else is read as an entity id, and `0` is the local player's own body. The aim is re-solved EVERY frame, so a tracked entity that moves stays centred -- this is FiveM's `PointCamAtEntity`, not a snapshot. An entity that streams out holds the last aim instead of snapping the camera to the world origin.
example:
-- Keep the camera centred on the car as it drives past
Open77.camera.lookAt(cam, Open77.vehicles.get(vehicleId).entity)

name: orbit
summary: Sets this resource's preview orbit yaw on an active third-person rig.
description: Requires camera.preview. Sets a resource-owned preview orbit yaw in degrees, normalized modulo 360. The yaw must be finite. Returns false/reason if another resource owns the preview, the preview backend is unavailable, or the native operation fails. Use clearOrbit to release the owned preview.
example:
-- Rotate the wardrobe preview with the mouse wheel
RegisterKeyMapping("preview_left", "Rotate preview", "Q", function()
    previewYaw = previewYaw - 15
    Open77.camera.orbit(previewYaw)
end)

name: project
summary: Projects a world point into normalized WebUI viewport coordinates.
description: Uses REDengine's active camera projection. `(0,0)` is the top-left and `(1,1)` the bottom-right. `onScreen` is false for points behind the view or beyond the viewport.
returns: table { x, y, depth, distance, onScreen }, or nil
example:
-- Place a 2D name tag over a world position
local screen = Open77.camera.project(target)
if screen and screen.onScreen then
    nameTag.setPosition(screen.x, screen.y)
end

name: screenRay
summary: Unproject a normalized screen point into a world-space ray.
description: Requires world.query. x/y use normalized top-left viewport coordinates in [0,1]. maxDistance defaults to 100 metres and must be finite in [0.1,1000]. Returns origin, unit direction, endpoint position and maxDistance; this is not a collision result. Uses the active camera and checks projection consistency. Returns nil/reason if the camera or projection is unavailable. Identical global alias: Screen2DPointTo3DSpace. See screen-picking.md and context-menu.md. Requires the new screen-picking client, not the earlier .62 release.
example:
-- The ray under the mouse cursor, 50 m long
local cursor = Open77.input.cursor()
if cursor and cursor.inBounds then
    local ray = Open77.camera.screenRay(cursor.x, cursor.y, 50)
    if ray then print("ray ends at", ray.position.x, ray.position.y, ray.position.z) end
end

name: screenRaycast
summary: Pick a world surface/entity, with optional visible F7 self targeting.
description: Requires world.query. Same normalized coordinates and distance limits as screenRay. Optional {static=true,dynamic=true,self=false} strict boolean options; at least one of static/dynamic must be enabled. Physical world, vehicle and NPC-hitbox categories are included, not query-only player sensors. self=true with dynamic=true also picks the active visible F7 body using animated slot capsules, without enabling collision. A closer physical hit wins. This approximation returns hitSource=self_presentation, local playerId and isLocalPlayer=true, but no physical normal/material; hidden/suspended bodies are excluded. Ordinary physical hits add normal, camera distance, material, entityLookupAvailable and optional target. A miss has hit=false and position at the ray endpoint, not a surface. target distinguishes decimal-string engineEntity/local entity handles from canonical playerId, vehicleId, npcId and propId; propId is a decimal string. Never interchange these IDs. NPC records use Character.* when available. No nearest-object fallback or server authority. See screen-picking.md and context-menu.md for contracts and examples.
example:
local hit, reason = Open77.camera.screenRaycast(0.5, 0.5, 12, {self=true})
if hit and hit.hit and hit.target then
    print(hit.target.kind, hit.target.isLocalPlayer, hit.hitSource)
end

name: setFov
summary: Sets the field of view, in degrees.
description: Changes the field of view of the camera currently controlled by Open77. The value is validated by the native backend and applies only to this client's presentation.
example:
-- A wider view while driving, back to normal on foot
SetTick(function()
    Open77.camera.setFov(Open77.character.isInVehicle() and 95 or 80)
end)

name: setTransform
summary: Moves and/or turns a scripted camera.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.script`. Two forms: `setTransform(camId, position?, rotation?)` for a per-frame dolly, and `setTransform(camId, { position =, rotation =, fov = })` when the field of view changes too. Setting a rotation CLEARS a previous `lookAt` -- an explicit rotation is an explicit aim, and a stale look-at silently overriding it would be a trap. Cheap enough to call every frame.
example:
-- Dolly the camera forward a little every frame
SetTick(function()
    camZ = camZ + 0.01
    Open77.camera.setTransform(cam, vector3(-1442.2, 127.4, camZ))
end)

name: shake
summary: Shakes a scripted camera with a named preset.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.script`. Presets: `hand`, `drunk`, `explosion`, `earthquake`; an unknown name is refused rather than defaulted. `amplitude` defaults to 1.0 and is capped at 4.0, `ms` defaults to 500. Additive on top of the resolved pose, so it composes with a blend and with a look-at instead of fighting either, and it decays exactly to rest. Omit `camId` to shake the camera this resource currently holds.
example:
-- An explosion nearby shakes the current camera for a second
RegisterNetEvent("fx:explosion", function()
    Open77.camera.shake(nil, "explosion", 2.0, 1000)
end)

name: stopShake
summary: Stops a scripted camera's shake immediately.
description: Requires `camera.script`. Cancels the shake started by `Open77.camera.shake` on that camera and leaves the camera itself where it is -- it is not a deactivate, and a camera with no shake running accepts it without complaint, so a cleanup path may call it unconditionally. Refuses with `permission_denied:camera.script`, `camera_unavailable_on_this_host` when the host exposes no scripted-camera backend, `invalid_camera_id`, or `camera_not_found` for a camera this resource does not own. Shakes are released with the camera, so a resource that stops does not leave the view trembling.
example:
-- Cut the earthquake short when the player enters the bunker
Open77.camera.stopShake(cam)

name: thirdPerson
summary: Switches the view to third person.
description: Turning it off restores the view the game had before the call, rather than some default.
example:
-- A shoulder view during the fashion show, restored afterwards
AddEventHandler("show:started", function() Open77.camera.thirdPerson(true, 2.5, 1.7) end)
AddEventHandler("show:ended", function() Open77.camera.thirdPerson(false) end)

name: unfollow
summary: Ends a follow camera: blends the view back, then destroys it.
description: Client-only; requires `camera.script`. `options.blendMs` is 0..60000. Answers `false, "not_following"` when this resource has no follow camera. The camera is destroyed even when the view had already been released by something else, so a follow can never be left behind. See the Scripted cameras guide.
returns: true and a blend promise, or false, reason
example:
-- The spectated player left: blend back to our own eyes
Open77.camera.unfollow({ blendMs = 400 })

name: unproject
summary: The world ray behind a screen point.
description: Client-only and UNGATED, like `project` and `view`: it reads the camera, it does not move it. `x` and `y` are 0..1 with the origin at the TOP LEFT -- exactly the frame `Open77.camera.project` returns, which is what makes `unproject(project(p))` a round trip. Returns `{ origin, direction }` in world space, `direction` normalised.
returns: table { origin, direction }, or nil, reason
example:
-- Find what is under the centre of the screen
local ray = Open77.camera.unproject(0.5, 0.5)
if ray then
    local to = vector3(ray.origin) + vector3(ray.direction) * 30
    local hit = Open77.world.raycast(ray.origin, to)
    if hit and hit.hit then print("surface at", hit.distance, "m") end
end

name: view
summary: Where the view is: position, forward vector, field of view.
description: Returns the latest game-thread camera snapshot used by projection and presentation APIs. It is a same-client read and may return `nil, reason` while the game camera is unavailable.
example:
-- Where is the camera and which way does it face?
local view = Open77.camera.view()
if view then
    print(("camera at %.1f, %.1f, %.1f, fov %d"):format(view.position.x, view.position.y, view.position.z, view.fov))
end

name: aimState
summary: One coherent aim snapshot, with the staleness counter that makes it honest.
description: Requires `player.aim.read`. Returns `aiming`, `firing`, `weaponDrawn` and `stateSequence`. `stateSequence` rises on every observed CHANGE of the aim or reload bits; difference it across two reads to tell a live aim from a mirror that has not moved in minutes. It is evidence, never a gate -- nothing times an aim out, because a player may hold one as long as they like. `weaponDrawn` is a live check for a weapon object in the right hand: false proves empty hands, true does not say which weapon family. The read costs no raycast, advances no sequence and disturbs no ballistics.
example:
local a = Open77.character.aimState()
if a and a.aiming and a.firing then print("aimed fire") end

name: aimedEntity
summary: What the local player is aiming at, if it is a thing rather than scenery.
description: Requires **both** `player.aim.read` and `world.query`: where the player looks is about the player, what is there is a world entity read, and granting the first must not quietly hand out the second. Uses the engine's own look-at target, not a physics ray -- a physics ray answers with geometry and carries no entity reference. Returns `engineEntity`, `className`, `kind`, `family`, `position` and `distance`, plus `entity` and one of `playerId`/`vehicleId`/`npcId` when the thing is an Open77 body. `family` is the raw class family and `kind` is that refined by ownership, exactly as `Open77.camera.aimRay({ entities = true })` refines it, so a vanilla crowd ped reads `populationNpc` in both. Three outcomes, kept apart on purpose: a table, a BARE `nil` for "pointing at scenery or nothing", and `nil, reason` when the question could not be asked.
returns: table, bare nil, or nil, reason
example:
local t = Open77.character.aimedEntity()
if t and t.kind == "player" then print("aiming at player", t.playerId) end

name: animation
summary: The animation currently playing on this character.
description: Reads the current animation snapshot for an entity, or for the local player when omitted. The result is observational and can change on the next frame; it does not grant animation ownership.
example:
-- Debug overlay: show which clip the player's body is playing
SetTick(function()
    debugText.set("anim: " .. tostring(Open77.character.animation()))
end)

name: boneAliases
summary: The alias table the slot resolver uses, as data.
description: No permission: it describes the API, not a body, the way `Open77.blips.sprites()` does. Returns `{ alias, slot }` pairs -- `head` to `Head`, `pelvis`/`hips` to `Hips`, `left_hand` to `LeftHand`/`left_hand`, `right_hand` to `RightHand`/`right_hand`. `chest`, `feet` and `hands` are deliberately absent: nothing measured on a 2.31 body publishes a chest or a foot slot, and a pair of hands is not one position.
example:
-- Print the alias names bonePosition accepts
for _, pair in ipairs(Open77.character.boneAliases()) do
    print(pair.alias, "->", pair.slot)
end

name: bonePosition
summary: The world position of one of an entity's slots.
description: Requires `world.transform`. FiveM's `GetWorldPositionOfEntityBone`. `name` is a slot name the body publishes or one of the aliases `boneAliases()` lists; matching ignores case and punctuation. Anything the body does not carry is `unknown_bone`, by name, rather than a position taken from somewhere else. Read through the native `entSlotComponent.GetSlotTransform`.
returns: table { x, y, z }, or nil
example:
-- Draw a marker over a nearby player's head
local entity = Open77.players.entity(playerId)
local head = entity and Open77.character.bonePosition(entity, "head")
if head then
    Open77.markers.create({ position = { x = head.x, y = head.y, z = head.z + 0.3 }, radius = 0.2 })
end

name: bones
summary: Lists the slot names an entity actually publishes.
description: Requires `world.transform`. Cyberpunk has no `GetEntityBoneIndexByName`: what an entity publishes is `entSlotComponent.slots[].slotName`, authored per entity. So the question is inverted -- this call reports what this particular body carries, instead of handing out a vocabulary and hoping. An EMPTY array is a real answer, not a failure: most entities carry no slot component. Works on vehicles too, whose occupant slots derive from the same component.
example:
-- Which slots does this body publish?
for _, name in ipairs(Open77.character.bones() or {}) do
    print(name)
end

name: forward
summary: The unit vector an entity is facing along.
description: Requires `world.transform`. FiveM's `GetEntityForwardVector`. The same `entEntity.GetWorldForward` read `Open77.character.state().forward` answers with, so the two cannot disagree.
returns: table { x, y, z }, or nil
example:
-- A placement ghost two metres in front of the player
local me = Open77.character.state().position
local fwd = Open77.character.forward()
local spot = vector3(me.x + fwd.x * 2, me.y + fwd.y * 2, me.z)
Open77.props.create({ model = "crate.small", position = spot, collision = false })

name: frame
summary: Reads an entity's position and its own three axes, in world space.
description: Requires `world.transform`. Returns `{ position, forward, right, up }`, every axis normalised, in one engine pass. The axes are read from `entEntity.GetWorldForward/GetWorldRight/GetWorldUp` rather than rebuilt from the orientation quaternion, so `forward` is by construction the same value `Open77.character.state().forward` reports. `entity` takes the same two forms every `Open77.character` call takes.

name: groundSpeed
summary: Speed projected on the ground, without the vertical component.
description: Returns horizontal movement speed for the selected character, excluding vertical velocity. Entity ids refer to the current client stream and must not be persisted as server identity.
example:
-- A speedometer on foot, ignoring jumps and falls
SetTick(function()
    hud.speed = ("%.1f m/s"):format(Open77.character.groundSpeed())
end)

name: health
summary: Current health.
description: Reads the engine-side health visible for the selected character on this client. For replicated player gameplay rules use the server-authoritative player health APIs; this helper is a presentation snapshot, not authority.
example:
-- A low-health screen tint, from the presentation snapshot
SetTick(function()
    vignette.visible = Open77.character.health() < 30
end)

name: isAiming
summary: Whether the local player is aiming down sights.
description: Requires `player.aim.read`. Read from the player's own weapon animation graph, not from `Open77.perspective.state().aiming` -- that field has only two writers, a trigger pull and the third-person self-view's per-frame gate, and the second is skipped entirely in first person, so in FPP it reports whatever the last shot said for as long as the player does not shoot again. **The underlying bit is a latched mirror, not a poll**: it keeps its value between two pushes from the graph, so `true` alone cannot distinguish "aiming now" from "the last thing the graph ever said was aim". Use `Open77.character.aimState().stateSequence` when that distinction matters. `nil, "aim_state_unavailable"` when nothing has been observed yet.
example:
-- Show the hit marker layer only while aiming down sights
if Open77.character.isAiming() then showHitMarkers() end

name: isAlive
summary: Whether the character is alive.
description: Reports the current engine alive/dead flag for the selected character. It is useful for presentation and diagnostics but may lag the authoritative server health transition by a replication frame.
example:
-- Do not draw the HUD over the death screen
SetTick(function()
    hud.visible = Open77.character.isAlive()
end)

name: isArmed
summary: Whether a weapon is drawn.
description: Reports whether the selected character is currently considered armed by the game presentation state. It does not enumerate inventory or prove that a weapon action is server-authorized.
example:
-- The shop refuses to open while a weapon is drawn
RegisterKeyMapping("shop_open", "Open shop", "E", function()
    if Open77.character.isArmed() then return Open77.hud.notify("Holster your weapon first") end
    openShop()
end)

name: isCrouched
summary: Whether the character is crouching.
description: Reads the character's current crouch presentation flag. Omit the entity to inspect the local player; remote values exist only while that proxy is streamed.
example:
-- Sneaking makes the stealth meter fill slower
SetTick(function()
    detection = detection + (Open77.character.isCrouched() and 0.2 or 1.0)
end)

name: isDriver
summary: Whether they occupy the driver's seat.
description: Returns whether the selected character occupies the canonical driver seat of a vehicle. Use `seat()` when the exact seat and vehicle entity are also needed.
example:
-- Only the driver hears the radio station switch prompt
if Open77.character.isDriver() then Open77.hud.notify("Press R to change station") end

name: isEmoting
summary: Whether they hold a workspot (an emote is running).
description: Reports whether Open77 currently presents the character in an emote/workspot state. This is a transient local snapshot and is cleared with the owning presentation lifecycle.
example:
-- Do not start a second emote while one is running
RegisterKeyMapping("emote_wave", "Wave", "F5", function()
    if Open77.character.isEmoting() then return end
    TriggerServerEvent("emotes:play", "wave")
end)

name: isFiring
summary: Whether the local player is holding the trigger.
description: Requires `player.aim.read`. The FiveM `IsPedShooting` equivalent, read from `gameweaponAnimFeature_WeaponData` on the player's own graph -- it is the trigger being HELD, not a shot event, so it stays true across a burst and is true even when the shot is refused. Same call and same snapshot as `isAiming()`; call `aimState()` once if you want both without two reads. Nothing here reads a key or a bind: a player who fires from a script or a macro raises the same flag, because the same thing happened to the same graph.
example:
-- Screen shake while the trigger is held
SetTick(function()
    if Open77.character.isFiring() then Open77.camera.shake(nil, "hand", 0.5, 100) end
end)

name: isFrozen
summary: Whether the local body is being held still.
description: Client-only; requires `player.freeze`. True while the server's freeze bit is set OR any client resource holds a local claim -- including one that is not yours. It is **not** true merely because you are dead: `Open77.character.isAlive` answers that question, and answers it better.
example:
-- Explain why the body will not move
if Open77.character.isFrozen() then
    Open77.hud.notify("You are being held in place")
end

name: isGrounded
summary: Whether the character is touching the ground.
description: Reads the engine grounded flag for the selected character. The value is sampled from the current client frame and should not be used alone for authoritative movement validation.
example:
-- Count the time spent in the air for a stunt score
SetTick(function()
    if not Open77.character.isGrounded() then airtime = airtime + 1 end
end)

name: isInVehicle
summary: Whether the character is mounted in a vehicle.
description: Reports whether the character is mounted in a vehicle according to the current client presentation. Call `seat()` to retrieve the mounted slot and vehicle entity id.
example:
-- Show the vehicle HUD only while mounted
SetTick(function()
    vehicleHud.visible = Open77.character.isInVehicle()
end)

name: isSliding
summary: Whether the character is sliding.
description: Reads the current sliding locomotion flag for the selected character. It is an observational state and does not start or stop a slide.
example:
-- Slide under the bar to win the parkour challenge
if Open77.character.isSliding() and nearBar then TriggerServerEvent("parkour:slid") end

name: isVaulting
summary: Whether the character is vaulting.
description: Reads the current vaulting locomotion flag for the selected character. Remote values are available only while the corresponding proxy is streamed.
example:
-- Award a point per vault
local wasVaulting = false
SetTick(function()
    local vaulting = Open77.character.isVaulting()
    if vaulting and not wasVaulting then points = points + 1 end
    wasVaulting = vaulting
end)

name: offsetToWorld
summary: Turns a point in an entity's own frame into world coordinates.
description: Requires `world.transform`. FiveM's `GetOffsetFromEntityInWorldCoords`. The offset is in the entity's frame: `+y` ahead, `+x` to its right, `+z` up, which is REDengine's convention. The vector may be passed alone -- `offsetToWorld(vector3(0, 2, 0))` means two metres in front of the local player -- because a target table always carries `engineEntity` and a vector never does. Pitch and roll are in the answer for a tilted entity, because they are in the engine's axes.
returns: table { x, y, z }, or nil
example:
local ahead = Open77.character.offsetToWorld(vector3(0, 2, 0))
Open77.markers.create({ position = ahead, radius = 0.5 })

name: position
summary: The character's position.
description: Returns the character's current world-space coordinates from the game-thread snapshot. Omit the entity for the local player; do not persist a client entity id as a network identity.
example:
-- Show the player's coordinates on the HUD
SetTick(function()
    local x, y, z = Open77.character.position()
    hud.coords = ("%.1f  %.1f  %.1f"):format(x, y, z)
end)

name: seat
summary: The seat occupied in a vehicle, if any.
description: Returns the canonical seat name and the mounted vehicle's client entity id when the character is in a vehicle. A character that is not mounted returns `nil`; both values are snapshots and the entity id is valid only in the current client stream.
returns: seat name and vehicle entity id, or nil
reason when the character could not be read
example:
-- Which seat is the player in?
local seat, vehicleEntity = Open77.character.seat()
if seat then print("sitting in", seat, "of entity", vehicleEntity) end

name: setFrozen
summary: Holds the local player's body still, without a server round trip.
description:
Client-only; requires `player.freeze`. **Presentation-local**: it holds YOUR body on YOUR machine, for a menu, a progress bar or a short scripted beat where a server round trip would be felt. The server's `Open77.players.setFrozen` outranks it outright -- while the server holds you, releasing your own claim changes nothing and the second return value stays `true`.

The hold is the engine's own `GameplayRestriction.NoMovement`, the same record vanilla death applies. It stops every locomotion input -- walk, run, sprint, jump, dodge, slide, vault -- and deliberately stops nothing else: camera, chat, voice, menus, interaction prompts and damage all keep working, and you can still be killed where you stand.

The claim is keyed by your resource, so another resource's claim survives your release. Yours is dropped for you when your resource stops or reloads, when you die, and when the session ends -- a freeze whose owner is gone is the one failure this must not have. The second return value is whether the body is still held afterwards by anybody at all.
returns: effectiveFrozen, or the reason for the refusal
example:
-- Hold the body locally while the shop menu is open; the server's hold outranks ours
local ok, stillHeld = Open77.character.setFrozen(true)
AddEventHandler("shop:closed", function() Open77.character.setFrozen(false) end)

name: speed
summary: Instantaneous speed, all components.
description: Returns total character movement speed, including vertical motion, from the latest local snapshot. Use `groundSpeed()` when only horizontal locomotion is relevant.
example:
-- A crash detector: a sudden drop in speed
local last = 0
SetTick(function()
    local now = Open77.character.speed()
    if last - now > 15 then Open77.hud.notify("Ouch!") end
    last = now
end)

name: state
summary: One complete snapshot of a character.
description:
A single engine pass fills the whole record even when the caller only wanted the speed. That is deliberate: every field then describes the **same instant**, so a caller cannot see a body grounded and airborne in the same breath.

With no argument, answers about the local player. An integer is an **Open77 entity id**.

A table `{ engineEntity = n, radius? }` reads a body Open77 does **not** own -- a vanilla population ped, a traffic car -- addressed by its engine id, because it has no Open77 id to address it with. Those answers carry `source = "observed"` and `owned = false`, `id` is 0, and only what can be read straight off the object is filled in: placement, orientation and health. Locomotion, weapon and vehicle state come from Open77's own replication and are left unset rather than guessed at. The body is located among what is streamed around the local player, so `entity_not_observed` means "not in view from here", which for a vanilla ped is an ordinary outcome and not an error. There is no write counterpart: every mutator is keyed by an Open77 id and answers `npc_not_found` for one of these.

params.name: entity
params.type: entity id, or table { engineEntity, radius? }

returns: table { isPlayer, attached, id, engineId, position, orientation, forward, velocity, speed, groundSpeed, yaw, alive, health, grounded, crouched, sliding, vaulting, air, fall, landing, weapon…, inVehicle, seat, driver }
reason, when the first is nil
example:
local s = Open77.character.state()
if s.inVehicle and s.driver then
    print("driving at " .. math.floor(s.speed) .. " u/s")
end

name: weapon
summary: The equipped weapon and its state.
description: Returns the drawn weapon's recognized item id and category for the selected character. It returns `nil` when no recognized weapon is currently presented and does not expose or mutate inventory.
returns: reason when the character could not be read
example:
-- Show the weapon category in a custom HUD
local weapon = Open77.character.weapon()
hud.weapon = weapon and weapon.category or "unarmed"

name: worldToOffset
summary: Turns a world point into an entity's own frame.
description: Requires `world.transform`. The exact inverse of `offsetToWorld`: the basis is orthonormal, so its transpose is its inverse. `y > 0` means the point is in front of the entity.
returns: table { x, y, z }, or nil
example:
-- Is the marker in front of the player or behind?
local rel = Open77.character.worldToOffset(vector3(-1442.2, 127.4, 18.0))
if rel and rel.y > 0 then Open77.hud.notify("The target is ahead of you") end

name: yaw
summary: Horizontal orientation, in degrees.
description: Returns the selected character's current world yaw in degrees. The value is a presentation snapshot and should be normalized by the caller when computing angular deltas.
example:
-- A compass reading
SetTick(function()
    hud.heading = ("%d deg"):format(Open77.character.yaw() % 360)
end)

name: arm
summary: Arms the grav-chute with a gravity, descent rate and optional glide speed.
description: Requires `player.chute`. `player.chute` is its own permission rather than a member of `player.travel`, because the chute moves nobody: it rewrites the fall, and a gamemode that may teleport is not thereby a gamemode that may change gravity. Every bound is enforced in the native layer; the Lua side only refuses what Lua can get wrong first -- a missing argument, or one that is not a number.
example:
-- Arm the grav-chute when the player jumps off the tower
AddEventHandler("tower:jumped", function()
    Open77.chute.arm(2.0, 3.0, 8.0) -- gravity, descent rate, glide speed
end)

name: disarm
summary: Disarms the grav-chute.
description: Requires `player.chute`. Restores the gravity and descent the engine had before `arm`. Disarming when nothing is armed succeeds. Like `arm`, it is refused on a host with no chute backend (`chute_unavailable_on_this_host`).
example:
-- Landed: normal gravity again
AddEventHandler("tower:landed", function()
    Open77.chute.disarm()
end)

name: isArmed
summary: Whether this client last accepted an arm or a disarm.
description: Requires `player.chute`. It reports the last arm/disarm **this client accepted**, not a reading of the script side, which lags by up to one poll of the bridge loop. Treat it as bookkeeping, never as proof the player is falling slowly. Without the permission or a chute backend it answers false rather than an error.
example:
-- Show the chute icon while armed
SetTick(function()
    chuteIcon.visible = Open77.chute.isArmed()
end)

name: setText
summary: Writes UTF-8 text to the operating-system clipboard.
description: Client-only and requires `clipboard.write` on the resource whose VM performs the call. Text is limited to 256 KiB, must be valid UTF-8 and cannot contain an embedded NUL. The operation is write-only: resources cannot inspect the user's existing clipboard. A temporarily owned clipboard returns `false, clipboard_busy`; callers should let the player retry instead of polling every frame.
example:
-- /pos copies the player's coordinates for the mapper
RegisterCommand("pos", function()
    local x, y, z = Open77.character.position()
    Open77.clipboard.setText(("{ x = %.1f, y = %.1f, z = %.1f }"):format(x, y, z))
    Open77.hud.notify("Position copied")
end, false)

name: approveLegJump
summary: Answer the owned native second-jump intent with the server's decision.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project and a running resource. request is the owned native request; sequence is the positive uint32 of the pending action reported by legsActivity; allowed is a boolean. true means the matching pending native intent accepted the decision, not that a jump was consumed, displaced or rendered. Open77 buffers an eligible press for at most 750 ms, so a late grant still has to pass the native timeout and the original native predicates. Stamina is charged on server admission and is not refunded when native execution later expires. This is a trusted projection primitive, not a public server-side jump command or a security boundary against a modified client.
example:
local ok, reason = Open77.cyberware.approveLegJump(request, activity.sequence, true)
if not ok then print(reason) end

name: attackState
summary: Read local native Gorilla melee activity.
description: Requires player.cyberware.read. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant or authorize damage. Returns {sequence,holding,variant,record,chargeExpired} when a usable native Gorilla weapon is observed; unavailable/unarmed states return nil, reason. This is client observation, not authoritative charge, damage or cooldown. The platform forwards bounded intent and the server validates it.
example:
local state = Open77.cyberware.attackState()
if state then print(state.sequence, state.holding, state.chargeExpired) end

name: captureArms
summary: Capture the local native Gorilla Arms posture profiles.
description: Requires player.cyberware.read. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant or authorize damage. Returns {family,groups}; groups contain part/name hashes and key pairs. The validated adapter supplies matching holstered and drawn alternatives for male or female, not arbitrary replacement assets. Native readiness and equipment readback do not prove rendered geometry.
example:
local profile, err = Open77.cyberware.captureArms()
if not profile then print(err); return end
print(profile.family, #profile.groups)

name: configureLegs
summary: Configure the owned ready legs adapter's admission limits.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project and a running resource. request must be a ready owned request. staminaManaged=true selects suppression of the native second-jump stamina debit and requires the server pricing path; it is not a stamina cost argument. maxAirborneMs is an integer 100-10000 and maxFallSpeed a finite 0.1-30 m/s, matching the grade table. These limits only narrow native eligibility: they never change jump height, trajectory, gravity, fall damage or native collision response. Support sets them from the installed grade snapshot.
example:
local ok, reason = Open77.cyberware.configureLegs(request, true, 10000, 30.0)
if not ok then print(reason) end

name: configureLocal
summary: Configure native charge limits and stamina-override presence.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant or authorize damage. Requires the same owned ready request. options accepts nullable normalStaminaCost/chargedStaminaCost (0..300) and maxChargeMs (100..60000, default10000). Native code uses cost presence to suppress supported native attack prices; the server owns the actual costs and debits. It does not grant stamina or suppress unrelated movement costs.

name: legsActivity
summary: Read fresh native legs action and airborne state.
description: Requires player.cyberware.read. Returns {request,sequence,phase,grounded,airborneMs,verticalSpeed}. Phases are idle, pending, granted, consumed and rejected; sequence is a positive uint32 while an action is pending and can report zero when idle. This is local native observation, not an authorization and not rendered proof. A resource that does not own the native adapter should use open77_cyberware's read-only legsActivity export instead: the core method inspects only the calling VM's own owner.
example:
local activity, reason = Open77.cyberware.legsActivity()
if activity then print(activity.phase, activity.airborneMs) else print(reason) end

name: legsState
summary: Read the owned native legs projection phase.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project. request is the positive ID returned by projectLegs. Returns "pending", "ready" or "failed" plus a reason string for a validly shaped query; a malformed request returns nil, reason. "ready" means the native equipment readback matched across three bridge polls, not that a second jump was performed or rendered. Another resource cannot read this owner's private request by guessing its numeric ID.
returns: nil, reason on a malformed query
example:
local phase, reason = Open77.cyberware.legsState(request)
if phase ~= 'ready' then print(phase, reason) end

name: localState
summary: Read the native equipment projection state for an owned request.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant or authorize damage. Returns a phase string and a reason string: pending, ready or failed for the matching native request. Invalid/foreign native requests may return an empty phase plus reason; Lua permission/argument failures return nil, reason. ready describes native equipment readback, not SQL commit or visible confirmation.
returns: nil, reason on Lua validation failure
example:
local phase, reason = Open77.cyberware.localState(request)
if phase == "failed" or not phase or phase == "" then print(reason) end

name: presentArms
summary: Project or clear an owned Gorilla Arms appearance overlay.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant or authorize damage. playerId is the network player ID, including the local player for its self-view. Pass a validated captured {family,groups} profile, or false to clear. Overlay ownership survives identical replays; conflicting owners fail. Native attachment/posture work is asynchronous; true is acceptance, not visible completion.
example:
local profile, err = Open77.cyberware.captureArms()
if profile then
    local ok, reason = Open77.cyberware.presentArms(playerId, profile)
    if not ok then print(reason) end
end

name: projectLegs
summary: Queue native local double-jump legs installation or removal.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project and a running resource. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant, grant a jump or authorize damage. enabled=true equips the supported native legs cyberware (Items.BoostedTendonsRare through the native LegsCW area); false releases it. Returns an owned positive integer request ID; poll legsState(request). Readiness requires matching owned item and HasDoubleJump readback and is not rendered proof. Arms and legs have distinct native owners, requests and equipment areas, so a legs request never disturbs an installed Gorilla Arms projection. Resource stop invokes owned cleanup, which unequips only the item this adapter created.
example:
local request, reason = Open77.cyberware.projectLegs(true)
if not request then print(reason); return end
print(Open77.cyberware.legsState(request))

name: projectLocal
summary: Queue native local Gorilla equipment installation or removal.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project. Trusted native projection primitive used by open77_cyberware; it does not install a durable implant or authorize damage. enabled=true equips the supported native arms; false restores bare arms. Returns an owned positive integer request ID. Poll localState(request); queued work is neither a committed purchase nor visual proof. Resource stop releases the native owner.
example:
local request, err = Open77.cyberware.projectLocal(true)
if not request then print(err); return end
-- The platform projector correlates native readiness with the server ticket.
print(Open77.cyberware.localState(request))

name: releaseLegs
summary: Request owned native legs cleanup.
description: Requires player.cyberware.project and a running resource. Releases only the calling resource's own native legs projection and is harmless when it owns none. true acknowledges the request; completion is asynchronous. Cleanup unequips this adapter's owned item and removes an inventory copy only when this adapter created it, so a pre-existing unowned double-jump capability is left alone. Resource teardown invokes the same owned cleanup even after Lua callbacks have ended.
example:
-- The double-jump trial ended: release this resource's legs projection
AddEventHandler("trial:ended", function()
    Open77.cyberware.releaseLegs()
end)

name: call
summary: Runs the resource-owned native Dash projector operation.
description: Client support adapter; requires player.dash.project. Operations configure, state, request, approve, cancel, activity, release and present are bounded and generation-scoped. Server creators use the separate server Open77.dash define/grant/revoke API documented in dash.md. Native permits and correlated phases are not proof of rendered movement. Arbitrary speed, distance, effect IDs and stamina settings are unavailable. Multiplayer acceptance is pending.
example:
-- The support resource forwards a server-accepted dash phase to the native projector
RegisterNetEvent("dash:phase", function(...)
    Open77.dash.call("present", ...)
end)

name: item
summary: Looks up an `Items.*` clothing or item record in the game's live TweakDB.
description: No permission required; this is static game data. **The client ships no catalogue**: it is inside Cyberpunk 2077, so it reads the real database and gets the display name in the player's own language for zero shipped bytes. `source` is `tweakdb` here and `catalogue` on the server, which answers the same call from a reduced shipped table. `recordClass` -- the record's runtime RTTI class -- is always present once the lookup succeeds and is the honest local answer to FiveM's `GetEntityModel`; every other field is best effort, and an **absent field means the engine did not expose it**, not that the record lacks it. A `record` is a TweakDB string, never a Jenkins hash. Fails with `record_unknown`, `record_wrong_kind`, `invalid_record` or `tweakdb_unavailable`. See [Game data catalogues](data-catalogues.md).
returns: { record, kind, recordClass, tweakDbId, source, ... }, or nil
example:
-- Show the localized name of a clothing item in the shop
local info = Open77.data.item("Items.Cap_01_basic_01")
if info then print(info.displayName or info.record) end

name: localize
summary: Resolves a localisation key to the text the player would actually see.
description: No permission required. Accepts `LocKey#12345`, a bare numeric key -- so a `localeKey` read off a server catalogue row can be passed straight in -- or a secondary key string. The FiveM `GetLabelText` equivalent. Fails with `localization_unavailable` when the engine declines the key; the server refuses this call outright, because the locale tables only exist inside the game. See [Game data catalogues](data-catalogues.md).
example:
-- Turn a locale key from a server catalogue row into the player's language
print(Open77.data.localize("LocKey#12345"))

name: npc
summary: Looks up a `Character.*` NPC record in the game's live TweakDB.
description: No permission required; this is static game data. **The client ships no catalogue**: it is inside Cyberpunk 2077, so it reads the real database and gets the display name in the player's own language for zero shipped bytes. `source` is `tweakdb` here and `catalogue` on the server, which answers the same call from a reduced shipped table. `recordClass` -- the record's runtime RTTI class -- is always present once the lookup succeeds and is the honest local answer to FiveM's `GetEntityModel`; every other field is best effort, and an **absent field means the engine did not expose it**, not that the record lacks it. A `record` is a TweakDB string, never a Jenkins hash. Fails with `record_unknown`, `record_wrong_kind`, `invalid_record` or `tweakdb_unavailable`. See [Game data catalogues](data-catalogues.md).
returns: { record, kind, recordClass, tweakDbId, source, ... }, or nil
example:
-- Check that a record exists before asking the server to spawn it
if Open77.data.npc("Character.Judy") then TriggerServerEvent("npcs:spawn", "Character.Judy") end

name: vehicle
summary: Looks up a `Vehicle.*` record in the game's live TweakDB.
description: No permission required; this is static game data. **The client ships no catalogue**: it is inside Cyberpunk 2077, so it reads the real database and gets the display name in the player's own language for zero shipped bytes. `source` is `tweakdb` here and `catalogue` on the server, which answers the same call from a reduced shipped table. `recordClass` -- the record's runtime RTTI class -- is always present once the lookup succeeds and is the honest local answer to FiveM's `GetEntityModel`; every other field is best effort, and an **absent field means the engine did not expose it**, not that the record lacks it. A `record` is a TweakDB string, never a Jenkins hash. Fails with `record_unknown`, `record_wrong_kind`, `invalid_record` or `tweakdb_unavailable`. See [Game data catalogues](data-catalogues.md).
returns: { record, kind, recordClass, tweakDbId, source, ... }, or nil
example:
-- The dealership lists a car with its real display name and class
local car = Open77.data.vehicle("Vehicle.v_sport2_quadra_turbo_r")
if car then print(car.displayName, car.classLabel, car.seats) end

name: weapon
summary: Looks up an `Items.*` weapon record in the game's live TweakDB.
description: No permission required; this is static game data. **The client ships no catalogue**: it is inside Cyberpunk 2077, so it reads the real database and gets the display name in the player's own language for zero shipped bytes. `source` is `tweakdb` here and `catalogue` on the server, which answers the same call from a reduced shipped table. `recordClass` -- the record's runtime RTTI class -- is always present once the lookup succeeds and is the honest local answer to FiveM's `GetEntityModel`; every other field is best effort, and an **absent field means the engine did not expose it**, not that the record lacks it. A `record` is a TweakDB string, never a Jenkins hash. Fails with `record_unknown`, `record_wrong_kind`, `invalid_record` or `tweakdb_unavailable`. See [Game data catalogues](data-catalogues.md).
returns: { record, kind, recordClass, tweakDbId, source, ... }, or nil
example:
-- Show a weapon's name in the shop UI
local gun = Open77.data.weapon("Items.Preset_Lexington_Default")
if gun then print(gun.displayName or gun.record) end

name: command
summary: Runs one registered native laboratory command directly.
description: Requires `debug.runtime` and the trusted `open77_debug` owner. Input is limited to 4096 bytes and unknown commands are not forwarded to the server.
returns: true and command result on success
example:
-- The trusted debug resource runs a lab command
local ok, result = Open77.debug.command("population.restore")
print(ok, result)

name: eval
summary: Compiles and executes a bounded text-only Lua chunk in the privileged debug VM.
description: Requires `debug.runtime` and the trusted `open77_debug` owner. Source is limited to 32 KiB, the optional chunk label to 64 bytes, returned values to 16 and result text to 8 KiB. The ordinary memory, instruction and frame-time quotas remain active.
returns: true and bounded result text on success
example:
-- The trusted debug resource evaluates a snippet in the privileged VM
local ok, text = Open77.debug.eval("return Open77.character.state().position.x", "probe")
print(ok, text)

name: redscript
summary: Queues one bounded command through the REDscript debug bridge.
description: Requires `debug.runtime` and the trusted `open77_debug` owner. The opaque command is limited to 4096 bytes and executes from a genuine REDscript frame.
returns: true and bridge result on success
example:
-- The trusted debug resource queues a REDscript bridge command
Open77.debug.redscript("perspective.state")

name: clear
summary: Remove one tag's debug geometry, or every batch the calling resource drew.
description: With a tag, removes that batch; with no argument, removes every batch this resource owns. It never touches another resource's drawings, and it cannot fail: clearing a tag that was never set is a no-op. The runtime does the same on stop and reload, so calling it is only needed to take a drawing down early, before its `ttl` would.
example:
-- Hide the safe-zone outline the moment the admin closes the editor
RegisterCommand("safezone_hide", function()
    Open77.debugDraw.clear("safezone")
end)

-- Or drop everything this resource has drawn
AddEventHandler("onResourceStop", function(name)
    if name == GetCurrentResourceName() then Open77.debugDraw.clear() end
end)

name: set
summary: Draw resource-owned debug lines and triangles in the world under a tag, replacing that tag atomically.
description:
The overlay PolyZone's editor and `debug` zones use. `tag` (1..96 characters) names a batch owned by the calling resource; setting it again replaces the whole batch. `geometry` is `{ lines = { { a = {x,y,z}, b = {x,y,z}, color = "#RRGGBB" | "#RRGGBBAA" }, ... }, triangles = { { a, b, c, color }, ... }, ttl?, maxDistance?, thickness? }`. Limits: 512 lines and 256 triangles per batch, 32 tags per resource, 128 batches in total, 8192 input vertices in total; coordinates finite and within +/-1,000,000; `ttl` 0.05..10 s (the batch expires on its own, so a resource that stops drawing leaves nothing behind), `maxDistance` 1..5000 m, `thickness` 0.5..8 px. Requires `world.debug`.

Everything a resource drew is released when it stops or reloads. Fails with `invalid_debug_tag`, `invalid_debug_geometry`, `invalid_debug_options`, `invalid_debug_primitives`, `invalid_debug_point`, `invalid_debug_color`, `debug_geometry_quota` or `debug_geometry_unavailable`.

name: aimed
summary: The streamed door currently under the crosshair.
description: Requires `world.doors`. The returned `id` is an opaque 64-bit REDengine identity encoded as a string; never convert it to a Lua number. A successful discovery also makes that door addressable by `state` and the command functions while it remains streamed.
returns: reason when the first is nil
example:
local door, reason = Open77.doors.aimed()
if door then
    print(door.id, door.open, door.locked, door.distance)
end

name: aimedAny
summary: Reads the entity currently under the crosshair even when it is not a controllable Door.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Unlike `aimed`, this controller-agnostic probe accepts static and scenery door meshes. It always provides identity and placement when targeting succeeds; open, locked, and sealed state is populated only when the entity exposes a door controller.
example:
-- Sink the scenery door the player is looking at, even without a controller
RegisterKeyMapping("door_probe", "Probe door", "K", function()
    local door = Open77.doors.aimedAny()
    if door then print(door.class, door.name, door.open) end
end)

name: available
summary: Whether the client door backend is available.
description: This capability check does not discover or stream a door. Door operations require the `world.doors` permission.
example:
-- Skip the door features entirely on a host without the backend
if not Open77.doors.available() then
    print("door backend unavailable, /lockpick disabled")
    return
end

name: clearInteractionPolicy
summary: Removes this resource's interaction policy for a door.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Other resources' policies are unaffected.
example:
-- The heist is over: the vault door goes back to its vanilla behaviour
AddEventHandler("heist:ended", function()
    Open77.doors.clearInteractionPolicy(vaultDoorId)
end)

name: close
summary: Closes a door.
description: Alias of `setOpen(door, false, force)`. Requires `world.doors`; application is asynchronous.
example:
-- Close the garage door behind the car
Open77.doors.close(garageDoorId)

name: closest
summary: The closest streamed door around the local player.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Uses the same 0.5 to 100 metre player-centered query as `near`.
returns: reason when the first is nil
example:
-- Press E to toggle the nearest door within 3 m
RegisterKeyMapping("door_toggle", "Open or close door", "E", function()
    local door = Open77.doors.closest(3.0)
    if not door then return end
    Open77.doors.setOpen(door.id, not door.open)
end)

name: grantKey
summary: Grants an entity an opening token for a door.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Uses the door controller's native token mechanism rather than a parallel Open77 key list. This grants authorization but does not lock or deny an otherwise usable door; access enforcement belongs to `setInteractionAllowed`.
example:
-- Give the local player's body a token for the apartment door
Open77.doors.grantKey(apartmentDoorId, Open77.players.entity(Open77.players.localId()))

name: hasKey
summary: Whether an entity holds an opening token for a door.
description: Requires `world.doors`.
returns: reason when the first is nil
example:
-- Only holders of a token get the "unlock" prompt
local me = Open77.players.entity(Open77.players.localId())
if Open77.doors.hasKey(doorId, me) then
    Open77.hud.notify("Press E to unlock", { replace = true })
end

name: holders
summary: The entities holding an opening token for a door.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Holder IDs are opaque strings for the same precision reason as door IDs. Tokens are vanilla authorization data, not a global lock rule: an unlocked interactive door remains usable with no token. Combine `hasKey` with `setInteractionAllowed` when implementing an ox_doorlock-style policy.
returns: array of opaque entity ids, or nil
reason when the first is nil
example:
-- Debug: who holds a token for this door?
for _, holder in ipairs(Open77.doors.holders(doorId) or {}) do
    print("token holder", holder)
end

name: lock
summary: Locks a door.
description: Alias of `setLocked(door, true, force)`.
example:
-- Lock the shop door when closing time comes
RegisterNetEvent("shop:closed", function()
    Open77.doors.lock(shopDoorId)
end)

name: near
summary: All streamed doors around the local player.
description: Requires `world.doors`. The radius is centered on the player and must be between 0.5 and 100 metres. Results are sorted nearest first and register each door for later ID-based operations.
returns: array of door snapshots, or nil
reason when the first is nil
example:
-- List every door within 10 m, nearest first
for _, door in ipairs(Open77.doors.near(10) or {}) do
    print(door.name, door.distance, door.locked and "locked" or "unlocked")
end

name: open
summary: Opens a door.
description: Alias of `setOpen(door, true, force)`. Requires `world.doors`; application is asynchronous.
example:
-- The server approved the lockpick: open the door
RegisterNetEvent("lockpick:success", function(doorId)
    Open77.doors.open(doorId, true)
end)

name: reset
summary: Resets a door to its configured default state.
description: Requires `world.doors`; queues the vanilla `ResetDoorState` event.
example:
-- Put the door back to its authored default when the mission ends
Open77.doors.reset(missionDoorId)

name: revokeKey
summary: Revokes an entity's opening token for a door.
description: Requires `world.doors`.
example:
-- The tenant moved out: take the token back
Open77.doors.revokeKey(apartmentDoorId, tenantEntity)

name: seal
summary: Seals a door.
description: Alias of `setSealed(door, true, force)`.
example:
-- Seal the vault after the alarm
Open77.doors.seal(vaultDoorId, true)

name: setAutomaticClose
summary: Enables or disables a door's automatic closing behavior.
description: Requires `world.doors`; queues the vanilla `SetCloseItself` event.
example:
-- The garage door stays open until closed by a script
Open77.doors.setAutomaticClose(garageDoorId, false)

name: setInteractionAllowed
summary: Pre-declares whether vanilla interaction may open a door.
description: Requires `world.doors`. The decision is synchronous when the game interacts with the door. Policies are owned by the resource, all active policies must allow, and they are removed automatically on stop/reload. `open77:doorInteract` is an observational event with `(doorId, activatorId, "true"|"false")`; it is too late to change that interaction.
example:
Open77.doors.setInteractionAllowed(doorId, playerHasAccess)
AddEventHandler("open77:doorInteract", function(door, activator, allowed)
    print(door, activator, allowed)
end)

name: setLocked
summary: Sets whether a door is locked.
description: Requires `world.doors`. `force` uses the vanilla quest-authority action; application is asynchronous.
example:
-- Lock or unlock the door from a server decision
RegisterNetEvent("doors:setLocked", function(doorId, locked)
    Open77.doors.setLocked(doorId, locked)
end)

name: setOpen
summary: Sets whether a door is open.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Success means the REDscript action was accepted; application is asynchronous and may take up to 200 ms. `force` uses the vanilla quest-authority action.
example:
-- Toggle a door and wait for the asynchronous application
CreateThread(function()
    Open77.doors.setOpen(doorId, true)
    Wait(250)
    local door = Open77.doors.state(doorId)
    print("open now:", door and door.open)
end)

name: setSealed
summary: Sets whether a door is sealed.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Sealing is distinct from locking. `force` uses the vanilla quest-authority action.
example:
-- Unseal the bunker once the code is entered
Open77.doors.setSealed(bunkerDoorId, false, true)

name: setState
summary: Sets a door state by name.
description: Accepted states: `open`, `closed`, `locked`, `unlocked`, `sealed`, `unsealed`. Requires `world.doors`; `force` selects the quest-authority action.
example:
-- One call with the state as a word from the server
RegisterNetEvent("doors:setState", function(doorId, state)
    Open77.doors.setState(doorId, state) -- "open", "closed", "locked", ...
end)

name: sink
summary: Moves a static or scenery door below the floor.
description: Requires `world.doors`. This is a visual removal fallback for geometry that has no DoorControllerPS and therefore cannot be opened normally. Depth must be greater than zero and no more than 100 metres; the default is 3 metres.
example:
-- A static door with no controller blocks the mission route: drop it into the floor
local door = Open77.doors.aimedAny()
if door and not door.controller then Open77.doors.sink(door.id, 3.0) end

name: state
summary: A live snapshot of a streamed door.
description: Requires `world.doors`. Reads the live `DoorControllerPS`, never a fabricated default from the save record. Returns `door_not_streamed` after the entity unloads. Snapshot fields include `id`, `class`, `name`, `position`, `distance`, `open`, `closed`, `locked`, `sealed`, `busy`, `playerAuthorised`, `automaticClose`, toggle capabilities, shutter/lift flags, type/sides and opening speed/time.
returns: reason when the first is nil
example:
-- Show the lock state of the nearest door on the HUD
local door = Open77.doors.closest(3.0)
if door then
    local live = Open77.doors.state(door.id)
    if live then Open77.hud.notify(live.locked and "Locked" or "Unlocked", { replace = true }) end
end

name: unlock
summary: Unlocks a door.
description: Alias of `setLocked(door, false, force)`.
example:
-- The player bought the key: unlock the door
RegisterNetEvent("doors:keyBought", function(doorId)
    Open77.doors.unlock(doorId)
end)

name: unseal
summary: Unseals a door.
description: Alias of `setSealed(door, false, force)`.
example:
-- The alarm is reset: unseal the vault
Open77.doors.unseal(vaultDoorId)

name: all
summary: Lists every replicated elevator state visible to the client.
description: Requires `elevators.read`; returns an empty array when the capability or backend is unavailable.
example:
-- Show every managed elevator's floor on a debug overlay
for _, lift in ipairs(Open77.elevators.all()) do
    print(("elevator %d at floor %d (%s)"):format(lift.id, lift.activeFloor, lift.phase))
end

name: get
summary: Reads one replicated elevator by Open77 ID.
description: Requires `elevators.read`. Elevator IDs are server-assigned and should be kept unchanged.
returns: table { id, revision, bucket, engineEntity, activeFloor, originFloor, targetFloor, floorCount, travelMs, remainingMs, flags, phase, position, streamed, applied }, or nil
example:
-- Is the lift the player called still moving?
local lift = Open77.elevators.get(elevatorId)
if lift and lift.remainingMs > 0 then
    Open77.hud.notify(("Arriving in %d s"):format(math.ceil(lift.remainingMs / 1000)), { replace = true })
end

name: nearby
summary: Discovers streamed native elevators around the local player.
description: Requires `elevators.read`. Radius must be between 1 and 300 metres. Results distinguish unmanaged engine lifts from elevators already adopted by Open77.
returns: array of { engineEntity, controllerEntity, position, distance, managed, floorCount, activeFloor, id }
example:
-- Find an adopted lift within 10 m to offer the call prompt
for _, lift in ipairs(Open77.elevators.nearby(10)) do
    if lift.managed then Open77.hud.notify("Press E to call the elevator", { replace = true }) end
end

name: request
summary: Submits a floor request to the authoritative server.
description: Requires `elevators.request`. `action` is normally `call` or `goto`; the server validates the ID, floor, player bucket, range, state and policy.
example:
-- Press E to call the nearest managed lift to the ground floor
RegisterKeyMapping("elevator_call", "Call elevator", "E", function()
    for _, lift in ipairs(Open77.elevators.nearby(5)) do
        if lift.managed then Open77.elevators.request(lift.id, 0, "call"); break end
    end
end)

name: getTime
summary: Lit l'horloge REDengine locale.
description: Primitive interne protégée par `world.environment`. Retourne un snapshot atomique de l'heure appliquée et de l'état de pause. Dans une session normale, utilisez l'export `open77_weather.getState` plutôt que cette valeur de projection.
returns: table { day, hour, minute, second, totalSeconds, frozen }, ou nil
example:
-- Show the game clock on the HUD (the client projection of the server's time)
SetTick(function()
    local t = Open77.environment.getTime()
    if t then hud.clock = ("%02d:%02d"):format(t.hour, t.minute) end
end)

name: isWeatherFrozen
summary: Indique si la météo automatique vanilla est neutralisée.
description: Demande `world.environment`.
example:
-- Debug: is vanilla weather neutralised on this client?
print("weather frozen:", Open77.environment.isWeatherFrozen())

name: setTime
summary: Projette une heure serveur dans REDengine.
description: Demande `world.environment`. `open77_weather` est normalement le seul propriétaire de cette permission. REDengine choisit la prochaine occurrence de l'heure demandée ; le package officiel filtre donc les petits reculs réseau pour éviter un saut d'un jour.
returns: true en cas de succès, sinon false
example:
-- A local projection primitive (normally only open77_weather holds this permission)
Open77.environment.setTime(22, 30)

name: setTimeFrozen
summary: Fige ou libère uniquement l'horloge du jeu.
description: Ne fige pas la simulation. Demande `world.environment`; utilisé par la projection serveur pour neutraliser la vitesse vanilla.
returns: true en cas de succès, sinon false
example:
-- Stop only the clock on this client (the projection layer's job, not a gamemode's)
Open77.environment.setTimeFrozen(true)

name: setWeather
summary: Applique un preset météo REDengine.
description: Primitive interne demandant `world.environment`. Le second retour `applied=false` est aussi possible en cas de succès si le preset était déjà actif.
returns: true en cas de succès, sinon false
applied si succès, sinon raison du refus
example:
-- Local projection of a preset over 20 seconds (normally only open77_weather calls it)
local ok, applied = Open77.environment.setWeather("rain", 20)

name: setWeatherFrozen
summary: Désactive ou réactive le contrôleur météo automatique vanilla.
description: Demande `world.environment`. Figer conserve le preset courant et laisse le serveur décider du prochain événement.
returns: true en cas de succès, sinon false
example:
-- Keep the vanilla controller from overriding the server's sky
Open77.environment.setWeatherFrozen(true)

name: apply
summary: Applies a table of local equipment slot values.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.edit. Returns true on accepted native mutation, or nil, reason; acceptance is not rendered completion. Values are record strings or false to clear. Options: allowRestricted=false and replace=false. With replace=false omitted slots are preserved; replace=true also clears omitted slots. Worn-set mutations run sequentially and may partially apply before an error; this is not an atomic transaction.

name: attached
summary: Reads the item actually attached at a local slot.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Returns a record string or false when no item is attached. Attachment alone does not prove the expected garment appearance has settled.
returns: record or false, or nil, reason
example:
-- Is the helmet really on the body yet?
local worn = Open77.equipment.attached("Head")
print(worn or "bare head")

name: equip
summary: Equips a record in the local worn set.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.edit. Returns true on accepted native mutation, or nil, reason; acceptance is not rendered completion. Call equip(record[, slot][, options]); omitted slot is inferred by the native record adapter. options.allowRestricted defaults false. Read registry/attached/visualSettled separately when completion matters.
example:
-- The wardrobe menu: put on the selected cap
RegisterNetEvent("wardrobe:pick", function(record)
    local ok, reason = Open77.equipment.equip(record)
    if not ok then Open77.hud.notify("Cannot wear that: " .. reason) end
end)

name: family
summary: Reads the local equipment body family.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Returns the native adapter body-family name, used to filter compatible records.
example:
-- Only list records this body can wear
local family = Open77.equipment.family()
local records = Open77.equipment.records({ slot = "Head", family = family })

name: info
summary: Looks up metadata for one equipment record.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. The record name is 1..160 bytes. Result fields: record, tweakDbId, slot, attachmentSlot, catalogScope, supportsMale, supportsFemale, defaultSelectable and nonvisual. This lookup does not equip the item.
example:
-- Show which slot an item goes into before offering it
local info = Open77.equipment.info("Items.Cap_01_basic_01")
if info then print(info.slot, info.supportsMale, info.supportsFemale) end

name: records
summary: Lists equipment records with optional slot and body-family filters.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Options: slot, family="male" or "female", restricted=false and limit=200 (positive integer, capped at 2000). restricted=true includes records not default-selectable; it does not grant mutation permission. Results use the same metadata shape as info().
example:
-- Fill the shop's hat list
for _, item in ipairs(Open77.equipment.records({ slot = "Head", limit = 50 }) or {}) do
    print(item.record)
end

name: registry
summary: Reads the local worn equipment slot registry.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Returns a table keyed by slot: record strings or false for empty slots. Registry state is separate from the attached item and its settled visual appearance.
example:
-- Save the current outfit so it can be restored after a respawn
local outfit = Open77.equipment.registry()
if outfit then SetResourceKvp("outfit", json.encode(outfit)) end

name: slots
summary: Lists the supported clothing slot names and attachment slots.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Returns nine {name, attachmentSlot} entries: Head, Face, InnerChest, OuterChest, Legs, Feet, Outfit, UnderwearTop and UnderwearBottom.
example:
-- Build the wardrobe tabs from the slot list
for _, slot in ipairs(Open77.equipment.slots() or {}) do
    print(slot.name, slot.attachmentSlot)
end

name: tags
summary: Reads native tags associated with a local equipment slot.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Returns an array of tag strings for the current wearer and slot.
example:
-- Does the worn jacket carry a faction tag?
for _, tag in ipairs(Open77.equipment.tags("OuterChest") or {}) do
    if tag == "Maelstrom" then print("wearing gang colours") end
end

name: unequip
summary: Removes equipment from a local worn slot.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.edit. Returns true on accepted native mutation, or nil, reason; acceptance is not rendered completion. Does not delete the inventory item. Read native visual readiness separately.
example:
-- Take the hat off when entering the church
AddEventHandler("church:entered", function()
    Open77.equipment.unequip("Head")
end)

name: visualSettled
summary: Checks native visual readiness for an expected clothing slot value.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. expected must be a record string or false.
