Reads registry/outfit visibility and actual attachment/appearance readiness; false means not yet settled, whereas nil, reason indicates an error. This native readback is not screenshot proof.
example:
-- Wait until the new jacket is visibly on before taking the screenshot
CreateThread(function()
    Open77.equipment.equip("Items.Jacket_01_basic_01", "OuterChest")
    while not Open77.equipment.visualSettled("OuterChest", "Items.Jacket_01_basic_01") do Wait(100) end
    takePhoto()
end)

name: emit
summary: Publishes an event in this resource's VM; the same function as TriggerEvent.
description: Emits an event on the resource-local client bus and invokes matching local handlers. It never sends a packet; use the network event API for server communication.
example:
-- Tell the rest of this resource that the shop closed
Open77.events.emit("shop:closed")

name: off
summary: Removes a handler registered with `on`.
description: Unregisters a local event handler id previously returned by `on`/`AddEventHandler`. The id is the only argument -- there is no event name parameter. Handler ids are owned by a resource generation and cannot remove another resource's callback.
example:
-- Listen for the first "ready" only
local handler
handler = Open77.events.on("hud:ready", function()
    print("HUD ready")
    Open77.events.off(handler)
end)

name: on
summary: Listens for a local event.
description: Same as the `AddEventHandler` global. Events emitted by the plugin — `open77:pauseKey`, `open77:menuStateChanged`, `open77:inspector:on` — arrive here.
example:
-- React to the plugin's own menu-state event
Open77.events.on("open77:menuStateChanged", function(state)
    print("menu open:", state.open)
end)

name: call
summary: Calls a function exported by another resource, asynchronously.
description: Schedules another running client resource's exported function and returns a generation-bound Promise. Arguments and results must be serializable; unavailable resources, missing exports, stale generations and scheduler saturation are returned immediately as `nil, reason`.

name: callSync
summary: Calls a function exported by another resource, inline on this thread.
description: The non-sugar form of exports.resource:name(...). Runs the callee in its own VM before returning and yields its values directly. RAISES on failure instead of returning nil, reason — the one place Open77 departs from its own convention, so that ported FiveM code behaves the same; use pcall to handle failure. The callee must not yield (export_yielded), gets its own instruction budget (export_budget_exhausted fails only that call), and chains are capped at 8 frames (export_recursion_limit). Arguments and results are copied, never shared. A resource may call its own export.
example:
-- The export name is in a variable: the non-sugar synchronous form
local ok, fuel = pcall(Open77.exports.callSync, "open77_fuel", exportName, vehicleId)
if ok then print("fuel", fuel) end

name: clear
summary: Requests cleanup of the calling resource's hacking presentation.
description: Client-only; requires player.hacking.project. Clears only presentation owned by the calling resource and is harmless when it owns none. Resource stop invokes the same owned cleanup automatically. true acknowledges the cleanup request, not native completion; the native script retains its bounded expiry fallback if the bridge cannot accept a clear command. This does not cancel an authoritative upload, purge a status, refund costs or undo committed damage. Use the server hacking APIs for gameplay state changes.
example:
-- The hack minigame closes: drop this resource's HUD presentation
AddEventHandler("hackui:closed", function()
    Open77.hacking.clear()
end)

name: clearNativeStatus
summary: Releases this resource's owned native hacking statuses.
description: Client-only; requires player.hacking.status. An omitted kind clears every status the calling resource holds; passing "blind" or "weapon_jam" clears only that slot, and any other value is refused with invalid_kind. It never clears another resource's slot and is harmless when the caller owns none. true acknowledges the clear request, not native completion; the adapter retains its bounded expiry, death, vehicle, workspot and session guards. This does not cancel an authoritative upload or undo committed damage.
example:
-- The server cured the blindness early: release just that slot
RegisterNetEvent("hack:cured", function(kind)
    Open77.hacking.clearNativeStatus(kind) -- "blind" or "weapon_jam"
end)

name: nativeStatus
summary: Applies a bounded native hacking status -- blind or weapon jam -- to the local player.
description: Client-only; requires `player.hacking.status`, a server-driven projection primitive a player resource should not hold by default (distinct from the HUD-only `player.hacking.project`). `kind` is `blind` (Reboot Optics) or `weapon_jam` (Weapon Glitch); `durationMs` is 1..3600000 and the client clamps it to the kind's cap (15 s). One independent slot per kind, owned by the calling resource: a second call on the same kind replaces this resource's own slot and cannot touch another resource's. The adapter releases on the deadline, on death, vehicle entry, workspot, session change and resource stop; the server's deadline stays the authority and this only presents it. Returns the request id, not proof of a rendered effect.
returns: reason: permission_denied:player.hacking.status, resource_not_running, hacking_status_backend_unavailable, invalid_kind, invalid_duration
example:
-- The server says we were hit by Reboot Optics: blind the local player for 5 s
RegisterNetEvent("hack:blinded", function()
    Open77.hacking.nativeStatus("blind", 5000)
end)

name: nativeStatusState
summary: Reads the bounded native hacking status slots and their counters.
description: Client-only; requires player.hacking.status. Returns one sub-table per held kind, keyed by kind (blind, weapon_jam), each carrying kind, phase, owner, reason, request, grantedMs, remainingMs, elapsedMs, releaseOverdue and applied, plus the totals applications, refusals, releases and watchdogRemovals. Slots are independent, one per kind, and the client clamps each duration to that kind's cap. applied is adapter state, not proof of a rendered effect; the server's deadline is the authority and the client only presents it.
example:
local state, reason = Open77.hacking.nativeStatusState()
if state and state.blind then print(state.blind.phase, state.blind.remainingMs) end

name: observe
summary: Reads a streamed multiplayer target's position, camera angle and local visibility for real-time selection.
description: Client-only; requires world.query. playerId is a positive integer network player ID. Returns streamed=true, visible, distance in metres, angle in radians and position={x,y,z}; no engine pointer or entity handle is exposed. The target must have an attached, presentation-ready remote body. Native selection checks camera-to-chest distance from 0.8 through 80 metres; peers outside the 0.35-radian selection cone return visible=false without a physics query. Within the cone, a failed native raycast returns nil, reason. This is local selection evidence only: it does not authorize a target, start an upload or prove server visibility. The server separately validates identity, life, range, policy and challenged visibility. It does not enter the vanilla scanner or slow game time. See the Hacking and counterplay guide for the public server workflow.
example:
local target, reason = Open77.hacking.observe(2)
if target and target.visible then
  print(('Target %.1f m away, angle %.3f rad'):format(target.distance, target.angle))
end

name: present
summary: Queues this resource's native hacking warning, progress or outcome presentation.
description: Client-only; requires player.hacking.project and a running resource. options contains actionId (integer 1..9007199254740991), phase (targeting, incoming, upload, block, purge, impact or cancel) and finite progress (0..1). actionId correlates presentation; it is not a damage authorization. Ownership comes from the calling resource. A different resource's active 1.5-second presentation lease refuses admission; refresh a continuing presentation periodically. The native adapter uses the vanilla progress HUD and sound cues while preserving other native HUD ownership. true means queued, not rendered or acoustically proven: the native script may refuse or defer a busy HUD. The official hacking resource supplies an incoming-warning fallback. This API does not execute a vanilla quickhack, apply native damage or change movement/camera controls. Resource stop requests owned cleanup; native presentation also has body/session and expiry guards.
returns: true when queued, or nil, reason
example:
local queued, reason = Open77.hacking.present({actionId=123, phase='incoming', progress=.25})
-- Queued admission is not proof that the HUD or audio was rendered.

name: clearNotify
summary: Empties one vanilla notification channel.
description: Client-only; requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. The channel is "ingame" (default) or "menu". There is one vanilla slot per channel, so this clears whatever is in it, whoever put it there.
example:
-- Clear the vanilla toast slot when the prompt no longer applies
AddEventHandler("delivery:done", function()
    Open77.hud.clearNotify("ingame")
end)

name: components
summary: Lists the supported stock HUD component names.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. Returns the thirteen canonical names suitable for `setVisible`, `isVisible`, or a complete custom-HUD replacement loop. The `all` selector is not listed: it is a selector, not a component.
returns: array of canonical component names, or nil
example:
-- Hide every stock component except the minimap
for _, name in ipairs(Open77.hud.components() or {}) do
    if name ~= "minimap" then Open77.hud.setVisible(name, false) end
end

name: help
summary: Vanilla on-screen help text. UNSUPPORTED on this build.
description: Client-only; requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. Validates its arguments (duration 100..60000 ms) and then refuses with `unsupported_channel` without entering engine code. The global behind it, MPDisplayOnscreenMessage, belongs to Cyberpunk's dormant multiplayer HUD and closed the process with an access violation when invoked on 2.31. The name stays bound so a resource written against it keeps working the day the channel is real; today, use Open77.hud.notify.
example:
-- Unsupported on 2.31: always false, "unsupported_channel". Use Open77.hud.notify instead.
local ok, reason = Open77.hud.help("HOLD F", 2000)
if not ok then Open77.hud.notify("Hold F to open the trunk") end

name: isVisible
summary: Reads the effective visibility of one stock HUD component.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. The result already combines hide claims from every resource. Names are case-insensitive and aliases such as `map`, `time`, `hp`, `ammo`, `weaponAmmo`, `speed`, `quest`, `vision`, `toasts`, `reticle` and `hub` are accepted. The selector `all` answers true only when every component is visible.
example:
-- Draw our own health bar only when the stock one is hidden
if Open77.hud.isVisible("health") == false then drawCustomHealthBar() end

name: log
summary: Adds one line to Cyberpunk's activity log.
description: Client-only; requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. Calls `gameActivityLogSystem.AddLog`. Confirmed working on 2.31.
example:
-- A line in Cyberpunk's activity log when a contract is accepted
RegisterNetEvent("jobs:accepted", function(title)
    Open77.hud.log("Contract accepted: " .. title)
end)

name: menu
summary: Queues a vanilla menu notification preset.
description: Client-only; requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. A menu preset carries its own localized title and therefore takes no text. Accepts vendor_not_enough_money, not_enough_money, inventory_action_blocked, crafting_not_enough_materials, upgrade_level_too_low, no_perk_points, perks_locked, perks_max_level, no_attribute_points, in_combat, in_combat_explicit, crafting_quickhack, crafting_ammo_cap, player_level_too_low, inventory_full, face_unequip_blocked, tutorial_unequip_blocked and no_junk. Only visible while the menu layer that owns the queue is mounted.
example:
-- The player cannot afford the item: the vanilla "not enough money" preset
RegisterNetEvent("shop:tooPoor", function()
    Open77.hud.menu("not_enough_money")
end)

name: notify
summary: Queues Cyberpunk's own five-second side notification.
description: Client-only; requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. Writes to the real vanilla pipeline (`UIInGameNotificationEvent`), not to a WebUI surface, so it looks native and needs no resource dependency. Options: `replace` (replace what is on screen instead of queueing) and `preset` (one of generic, action_blocked, combat_blocked, cant_save_action, cant_save_combat, cant_save_quest, cant_save_death, save_slots_full, save_space_full, photo_mode_disabled, sandevistan_in_call, expansion_installed). Text is required unless a preset is given, since a preset carries its own localized title. The five-second duration is the engine's and cannot be changed. Hiding the `vanillaNotifications` HUD component hides this stack, including your own toasts.
example:
-- A native five-second toast when the bounty is paid
RegisterNetEvent("bounty:paid", function(amount)
    Open77.hud.notify(("BOUNTY CLAIMED: %d eddies"):format(amount))
end)

name: setVisible
summary: Hides or restores one stock HUD component for this resource.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. Passing `false` adds this resource's hide claim; passing `true` releases only its own claim. Another resource may still keep the component hidden. Claims are released automatically when the resource stops or reloads. Canonical components are `minimap`, `compass`, `clock`, `health`, `stamina`, `weapon`, `speedometer`, `questTracker`, `phone`, `scanner`, `vanillaNotifications`, `crosshair` and `hubMenu`; the selector `all` claims or releases every one of them at once. Names are case-insensitive. `scanner` also refuses scanner activation, because an invisible scanner would still hold aim snap and the movement restriction.
example:
-- Hide the minimap during the race; release only our own claim afterwards
AddEventHandler("race:started", function() Open77.hud.setVisible("minimap", false) end)
AddEventHandler("race:finished", function() Open77.hud.setVisible("minimap", true) end)

name: state
summary: Returns the complete effective stock-HUD visibility snapshot.
description: Requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. Keys always use canonical component names and values are booleans after all resources' claims have been combined. The `all` selector is not a component and never appears here.
returns: table keyed by canonical component name, or nil
example:
-- Debug: print the effective visibility of every component
for name, visible in pairs(Open77.hud.state() or {}) do print(name, visible) end

name: subtitle
summary: Vanilla narration subtitle. UNSUPPORTED on this build.
description: Client-only; requires `ui.vanilla.hud`. Same story as Open77.hud.help: validated, then refused with `unsupported_channel`. MPDisplayNarrationEventEntry comes from the same dormant CPO group and is deliberately never invoked.
example:
-- Unsupported on 2.31: always false, "unsupported_channel". Use Open77.hud.notify instead.
local ok, reason = Open77.hud.subtitle("...", 3000)
if not ok then Open77.hud.notify("Dispatch: all units respond") end

name: axis
summary: Reads one analogue control: a stick, a trigger, the cursor or a cumulative counter.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Sticks (`padLeftStickX/Y`, `padRightStickX/Y`, also spelled `leftStickX` and so on) return -1..1 with XInput's own dead zone removed and the remainder rescaled, so a stick at rest reads exactly 0 and a stick at the rim exactly 1; stick Y is positive UP. Triggers (`padLeftTrigger`, `padRightTrigger`) return 0..1. `mouseX` and `mouseY` are the cursor, identical to `Open77.input.cursor()`. `mouseWheel`, `mouseWheelX`, `mouseDeltaX` and `mouseDeltaY` are CUMULATIVE counters since the client started -- difference two samples to get what happened between them. They are deliberately not consumed on read: a consume-on-read wheel would give each of two resources part of the same scroll. A missing pad answers `nil, "gamepad_not_connected"` rather than a silent zero, because a zero cannot be told from a stick held at centre. A button name answers `nil, "control_is_a_button"`. Gamepad reads are zero while the game window is not in the foreground.
example:
local turn = Open77.input.axis("padRightStickX") or 0
local before = Open77.input.axis("mouseWheel") or 0
Wait(100)
local scrolled = (Open77.input.axis("mouseWheel") or 0) - before

name: blockAll
summary: Takes the player's whole gameplay control stream, sparing named exceptions.
description: Requires `input.blockAll`, a separate permission from `input.actions` because it is a different blast radius. Consumes the entire gameplay action stream on the player puppet and asserts every blockable lever, minus `except`. Call with `{ except = { "Movement" } }` or nothing to acquire, `false` to release this resource's claim. Chat and voice keep working -- they run on focused browser input, not on the gameplay action stream -- so a blocked player can still say so. Vanilla menus are NOT closed or prevented: menu shortcuts arrive on a different controller alongside the pause menu, which must stay reachable, so block `Map` and `Hub` explicitly. `except` names vocabulary actions, never raw engine actions, and is validated in full before anything is taken.
returns: reason: permission_denied:input.blockAll, invalid_action_arguments, unknown_action, action_not_blockable, action_already_enforced, action_blocking_unavailable_on_this_host
example:
-- A cutscene: take every gameplay control except looking around
Open77.input.blockAll({ except = { "Movement" } })
AddEventHandler("cutscene:ended", function() Open77.input.blockAll(false) end)

name: blockableActions
summary: The actions that can really be blocked on this build, with mechanism and confidence.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Returns an array of `{ action, mechanism, confidence, note }`. `mechanism` is one of `stream`, `action`, `restriction`, `condition`, `flow`, `native`. `confidence` is `proven`, `measured` or `inferred` -- reported rather than hidden, so a lever reasoned from the engine's shape is distinguishable from one observed working in a live session. Read this instead of hard-coding action names.
returns: array of { action, mechanism, confidence, note }, otherwise nil
example:
-- Only block what this build can really block
for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.input.blockableActions() or {}) do
    print(entry.action, entry.mechanism, entry.confidence)
end

name: blocks
summary: Who currently holds which input blocks.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Returns `{ actions = { { action, owners } }, blockAll = { { owner, except } } }`. This is how an admin or debug resource proves a claim really came back: the failure this API most has to avoid is a player left unable to act by a resource that stopped without tidying up.
example:
-- Debug: who is holding a block right now?
local blocks = Open77.input.blocks()
for _, row in ipairs(blocks and blocks.actions or {}) do
    print(row.action, table.concat(row.owners, ", "))
end

name: cursor
summary: Read the OS cursor relative to the foreground game window.
description: Requires input.actions. Returns normalized x/y, pixelX/pixelY, client-area width/height, inBounds and captured. captured is true when any WebUI owns keyboard or cursor input. The coordinates may fall outside [0,1]; check inBounds. Returns nil, game_not_focused on focus loss, or a cursor/viewport availability reason. Does not show, capture or unlock the mouse: use an owned WebUI page with setFocus. WebUI uses its own virtual pointer; for exact WebUI clicks pass event.clientX/innerWidth and event.clientY/innerHeight to screenRaycast instead. See screen-picking.md.
example:
local cursor, reason = Open77.input.cursor()
if cursor and cursor.inBounds then print(cursor.x, cursor.y) end

name: devices
summary: Lists the mouse and gamepad controls, and whether this machine can answer for each.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Each row is `{ name, device, kind, available, reason }`: `device` is `mouse` or `gamepad`, `kind` is `button` or `axis`, and `name` is the canonical spelling to pass to `isDown` or `axis` (aliases resolve but are not listed twice). A control this machine cannot answer for is present and marked `available = false` with a reason -- an unplugged pad is `gamepad_not_connected` -- rather than omitted, so a resource discovers the gap instead of finding out from an axis that silently reads zero. Keyboard keys are not listed: their vocabulary belongs to `isDown` and `registerKeyMapping`. Same honesty contract as `Open77.input.blockableActions()`.
returns: array of control tables, or nil, reason
example:
for _, c in ipairs(Open77.input.devices() or {}) do
    if not c.available then print(c.name, c.reason) end
end

name: isActionBlocked
summary: Reads whether one curated action is blocked right now, for anyone.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Effective state, combining every resource's claims and any standing `blockAll` -- not the caller's own claim, so a resource that released its block still reads true while another resource holds one. Actions Open77 enforces unconditionally read as blocked; `Scanner` and `Quickhack` follow the multiplayer policy, `PhotoMode` is always blocked.
example:
-- Do not draw the map hint if the map is blocked
if not Open77.input.isActionBlocked("Map") then
    Open77.hud.notify("Press M to open the map")
end

name: isCaptured
summary: Whether another WebUI currently owns keyboard input.
description: Contextual actions should become inert while this is true so chat and menu typing cannot activate gameplay.
example:
-- A held key does nothing while the player is typing in chat
SetTick(function()
    if Open77.input.isCaptured() then return end
    if Open77.input.isDown("mouse2") then showAimOverlay() end
end)

name: isDown
summary: Whether a key, mouse button or gamepad button is currently held.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Keys: A-Z, 0-9, F1-F12, SPACE, ENTER/RETURN, TAB, SHIFT, CTRL/CONTROL, ALT, CAPSLOCK, BACKSPACE, INSERT, DELETE, HOME, END, PAGEUP/PAGEDOWN and arrows. Mouse: mouse1/mouseLeft, mouse2/mouseRight, mouse3/mouseMiddle, mouse4, mouse5. Gamepad: padA/B/X/Y, padUp/Down/Left/Right, padStart, padBack, padLeftShoulder (padLB), padRightShoulder (padRB), padLeftThumb, padRightThumb. Names are case-insensitive; `Open77.input.devices()` lists what this machine can actually answer for. These are PHYSICAL device reads -- they do not know the player's bindings and do not know whether the game is currently consuming the control, which makes them the `GetDisabledControlNormal` flavour rather than the enabled one. An unplugged pad answers `false, "gamepad_not_connected"`; an axis name answers `false, "control_is_an_axis"`. Prefer a press edge or a hold timer over firing every frame.
returns: reason when the control, the device or the permission is refused
example:
if Open77.input.isDown("mouse2") and not Open77.input.isCaptured() then
    showAimOverlay()
end

name: keyFor
summary: The effective key of one of this resource's own mappings.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Returns the effective key (the player's rebind if any, otherwise the registered default) for a mapping id owned by the calling resource, or nil when no such mapping exists.
returns: key string, or nil when the id is not registered by this resource
example:
-- Show the real key in the prompt, even after the player rebound it
Open77.hud.notify(("Press %s to open the inventory"):format(Open77.input.keyFor("inventory_open") or "I"))

name: mappings
summary: Every registered key mapping across all running resources.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Returns an array of `{ resource, id, name, key, defaultKey, hold, rebound }` records for the rebinding UI. Only serialisable metadata is exposed; the callbacks stay in their owning resource.
example:
-- A settings page listing every rebindable action
for _, mapping in ipairs(Open77.input.mappings()) do
    print(mapping.resource, mapping.name, mapping.key, mapping.rebound and "(rebound)" or "")
end

name: pointer
summary: Where the pointer is, as 0..1 across the rendered image -- the overlay's own pointer when a WebUI holds the cursor.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Returns `x, y, source`. Unlike `Open77.input.cursor`, which samples the OS cursor against the game window and answers with a table, this reads the WebUI's VIRTUAL pointer whenever a surface owns the cursor (`source = "overlay"`) -- Cyberpunk keeps recentring the Win32 cursor while it owns the camera, so the OS position says nothing about where the drawn pointer is -- and falls back to the OS cursor otherwise (`source = "system"`). The origin is the TOP LEFT and the units are fractions of the image -- the same frame `Open77.camera.project` answers in and `Open77.camera.unproject` consumes, so hit-testing a projected world point is a subtraction rather than a conversion. It is a ratio and not pixels on purpose: a client-rect read and the engine's back-buffer size disagree on a display with DPI scaling, so every pixel answer would need a qualifier the caller cannot see. `source` is `overlay` when a WebUI surface owns the pointer -- Open77's own virtual cursor, the one CEF and the drawn pointer share -- or `system` when the OS cursor is the only answer. During ordinary gameplay Cyberpunk recentres the OS cursor every frame, so `system` reads near 0.5, 0.5; that is where the cursor is, not a failed read.
returns: x, y, source, or nil, reason
example:
-- Where is the pointer over the image right now?
local x, y, source = Open77.input.pointer()
if x then print(("%.3f %.3f (%s)"):format(x, y, source)) end

name: rebind
summary: Sets and persists a new key for any mapping.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Rebinds the mapping identified by `resource` and `id` to `key` (same key vocabulary as `Open77.input.isDown`), persists it machine-globally, and raises `open77:keybinds:changed`. Used by the pause KEY BINDINGS tab.
example:
-- A settings page rebinds another resource's action
Open77.input.rebind("myinventory", "inventory_open", "TAB")

name: registerKeyMapping
summary: Declares a named, rebindable action bound to a key (twin of the RegisterKeyMapping global).
description: Requires `input.actions`. Accepts a spec table `{ id, name, key (or defaultKey), hold, onPressed, onReleased }` or the positional form `(id, name, key, onPressed [, onReleased])`. The engine owns the registry and the per-frame dispatch; the callback receives the mapping id and never fires while a page owns the keyboard. `onPressed` fires on the key-down edge; with `hold` (or a positional release callback) `onReleased` fires on key-up. Re-registering an id replaces the entry but keeps the player's saved rebind. Ids are letters/numbers/`_.:-`, up to 64 chars; names up to 96. Up to 64 mappings per resource.
returns: effective key (the saved rebind, else the default)
example:
-- A hold-to-talk push key with press and release callbacks
Open77.input.registerKeyMapping({
    id = "radio_ptt",
    name = "Radio push-to-talk",
    key = "CAPSLOCK",
    hold = true,
    onPressed = function() TriggerServerEvent("radio:talk", true) end,
    onReleased = function() TriggerServerEvent("radio:talk", false) end,
})

name: reset
summary: Restores a mapping to its registered default key.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Drops any saved override for the mapping identified by `resource` and `id`, restores the default key, persists the change, and raises `open77:keybinds:changed`.
example:
-- "Reset to default" button on the settings page
Open77.input.reset("myinventory", "inventory_open")

name: setActionBlocked
summary: Blocks or releases one curated input action for the calling resource.
description: Requires `input.actions`. The vocabulary is curated rather than an engine enum dump, because Cyberpunk has no single input-blocking lever: five unrelated mechanisms serve five families of action and a large minority of actions cannot be refused at all. Blockable today: `Movement`, `Map`, `Hub`, `FastTravel`, `Attack`. An action outside the vocabulary is refused with `unknown_action`; one this engine cannot refuse with `action_not_blockable`; one Open77 already blocks unconditionally (`PhotoMode`, `Scanner`, `Quickhack`, `CallVehicle`, `Journal`) with `action_already_enforced`. Nothing is accepted and silently ignored. Claims are owned by the calling resource: two resources may block the same action, `blocked=false` removes only the caller's claim, and everything a resource holds is released when it stops. See `wiki/input-blocking.md` and `docs/research/input-action-blocking.md`.
returns: reason: permission_denied:input.actions, invalid_action_arguments, unknown_action, action_not_blockable, action_already_enforced, action_blocking_unavailable_on_this_host
example:
-- No fast travel during the race
AddEventHandler("race:started", function() Open77.input.setActionBlocked("FastTravel", true) end)
AddEventHandler("race:finished", function() Open77.input.setActionBlocked("FastTravel", false) end)

name: setNativeActionBlocked
summary: Blocks or restores one vanilla input action by its engine name.
description: Requires input.actions. Accepts exactly (actionName, blockedBoolean); supports OpenMapMenu and WeaponWheel. Applies or removes the calling resource's claim, returning boolean/reason. A block remains while any resource claims it; stop/reload/disconnect automatically releases that owner's claims. WeaponWheel prevents native radial entry and cancels an already-open weapon wheel without selecting an item. It does not remap ALT, block other radial menus or disable SwitchItem. Acquire before the activation key is pressed. Other action names return unsupported_native_action. This is not a general-purpose arbitrary native input blocker.
example:
-- A custom weapon wheel replaces the vanilla one
Open77.input.setNativeActionBlocked("WeaponWheel", true)

name: unregisterKeyMapping
summary: Removes a key mapping this resource declared.
description: Requires `input.actions`. Frees the mapping's callbacks and raises `open77:keybinds:changed`. Only affects mappings owned by the calling resource.
returns: boolean: true when a mapping was removed
example:
-- The job ends: its key goes away
Open77.input.unregisterKeyMapping("job_cancel")

name: enable
summary: Turns the permanent aim ray on or off.
description: Turning it off also clears the outline: the outline belongs to the session that asked for it and must not outlive it.
returns: reason, when the first is nil
example:
-- Turn the permanent aim ray on while the admin tool is open
AddEventHandler("admin:opened", function() Open77.inspector.enable(true) end)
AddEventHandler("admin:closed", function() Open77.inspector.enable(false) end)

name: outline
summary: Outlines the aimed object, independently of the ray.
description: Lets a caller read the target without painting the world. The outline uses `entRenderHighlightEvent`, the same event focus mode and scanning already use.
returns: reason, when the first is nil
example:
-- Highlight what the player aims at, without the ray overlay
Open77.inspector.outline(true)

name: target
summary: What the aim ray is currently pointing at.
description:
Reads a snapshot, never a probe. The ray has to be cast on the game thread, and the plugin refreshes it at 10 Hz, so calling this costs nothing and cannot land a raycast on the wrong thread.

Always returns a table when a game is present. `valid` separates "nothing in view" from "no game" — the latter returns `nil, reason`.
returns: table { valid, engineId, class, name, kind, position, distance }
reason, when the first is nil
example:
local t = Open77.inspector.target()
if t and t.valid then
    print(t.kind, t.name, t.distance)   --> door  Door  1.38
end

name: decode
summary: Parses a JSON string.
description: Parses JSON into Open77's bounded Lua value model. Invalid JSON returns `nil, "invalid_json"`; decoded objects and arrays contain only supported scalar/table values.
example:
-- Parse a config file shipped with the resource
local text = Open77.resource.readFile("config.json")
local config, reason = Open77.json.decode(text or "")
if not config then print("bad config: " .. tostring(reason)) end

name: encode
summary: Serialises a Lua value to JSON.
description: Serializes a supported Lua value to JSON using the same bounded representation used by events, exports and WebUI. Functions, userdata, cycles and unsupported table shapes return `nil, reason`.
example:
-- Save a table as a string in the kvp store
Open77.kvp.set("hud_layout", Open77.json.encode({ x = 0.1, y = 0.9 }))

name: clear
summary: Clears this resource's keys matching a prefix.
description: Atomically removes every key matching an optional prefix from the calling resource's current-server store and returns the removal count. An empty prefix clears only that resource namespace.
example:
-- Reset every saved setting of this resource on this server
RegisterCommand("resetsettings", function()
    local removed = Open77.kvp.clear()
    Open77.hud.notify(("Cleared %d settings"):format(removed or 0))
end, false)

name: compareAndSet
summary: Atomically changes a key when its typed value matches.
description: Atomically replaces a key only when its typed value exactly matches the expected value. Nil expected means the key must be absent; nil replacement deletes after a successful comparison.
example:
-- Only mark the tutorial done if it was still pending
Open77.kvp.compareAndSet("tutorial", "pending", "done")

name: delete
summary: Deletes one persistent key.
description: Atomically deletes one key from the current resource store and returns whether it existed. Deleting a missing key succeeds with false.
returns: true when removed, false when absent
example:
-- Forget the saved HUD layout
Open77.kvp.delete("hud_layout")

name: find
summary: Finds typed entries by sorted key prefix.
description: Performs a sorted prefix search in the current resource store and returns bounded `{key, value, type}` records. The default result limit is 256 and the hard limit is 4096.
returns: array of { key, value, type }, or nil
example:
-- List every saved radio favourite with its value
for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.kvp.find("radio:") or {}) do
    print(entry.key, entry.value, entry.type)
end

name: get
summary: Reads one typed persistent value.
description: Reads a typed value from the current connection-address and resource namespace. Missing keys return the optional default (or nil) and are distinct from storage errors, which return `nil, reason`.
example:
-- Remember the last radio station across sessions on this server
local station = Open77.kvp.get("radio:last", "night_fm")

name: has
summary: Checks whether a persistent key exists.
description: Checks whether a key exists in the calling resource's current-server store without exposing its value or any other resource namespace.
example:
-- Show the tutorial only the first time
if not Open77.kvp.has("tutorial_seen") then
    showTutorial()
    Open77.kvp.set("tutorial_seen", true)
end

name: increment
summary: Atomically increments a numeric key.
description: Atomically creates or increments a numeric key. Integer arithmetic remains 64-bit and rejects overflow; mixed/floating arithmetic rejects non-finite results.
example:
-- Count how many times the player opened the map
local opens = Open77.kvp.increment("map_opens", 1)

name: keys
summary: Lists sorted keys matching a prefix.
description: Returns only the sorted keys matching an optional prefix in the current resource store. It is a bounded index query and cannot enumerate another package or connection address.
example:
-- Which settings has the player customised?
for _, key in ipairs(Open77.kvp.keys("setting:") or {}) do print(key) end

name: set
summary: Persists one typed value for this server address and resource.
description: Atomically persists a string, signed integer, finite number or boolean under the current connection address and resource. Keys/values and the 1 MiB resource quota are validated before the old file is replaced.
example:
-- Save the chosen HUD position on this machine, for this server
Open77.kvp.set("hud_position", "bottom_right")

name: setIfAbsent
summary: Stores a value only when its key is missing.
description: Redis-style SETNX for the current resource namespace: atomically stores the typed value only when the key is missing and reports whether insertion occurred.
example:
-- Default settings on first run only
Open77.kvp.setIfAbsent("hud_scale", 1.0)

name: stats
summary: Returns this resource store's usage and quotas.
description: Returns this resource's entry/byte usage and enforced quotas together with the active address/resource scope. It exposes no keys or usage belonging to other resources.
example:
-- Warn before the resource's store fills up
local stats = Open77.kvp.stats()
if stats and stats.bytes > stats.maximumBytes * 0.9 then print("kvp store nearly full") end

name: debug
summary: Writes a debug line to this resource's client log.
description: No permission. The line is written with the calling resource's name, so `red4ext/logs/open77-*.log` always says which resource spoke. Unlike its server namesake, the client honours the level. It takes one value, converted to text.
example:
-- Verbose tracing that only shows at debug level
Open77.log.debug(("menu opened at %.1f"):format(Open77.time.monotonic()))

name: error
summary: Writes an error line to this resource's client log.
description: No permission. Same resource-prefixed client log as `Open77.log.debug`, at the error level. It only logs: it does not raise, abort the handler or stop the resource.
example:
-- A refused call is logged, not raised
local ok, reason = Open77.blips.create({ position = spot })
if not ok then Open77.log.error("blip refused: " .. tostring(reason)) end

name: info
summary: Writes an informational line to this resource's client log.
description: No permission. Same resource-prefixed client log as `Open77.log.debug`, at the informational level.
example:
-- Normal lifecycle lines
Open77.log.info("HUD started")

name: warn
summary: Writes a warning line to this resource's client log.
description: No permission. Same resource-prefixed client log as `Open77.log.debug`, at the warning level.
example:
-- Something unexpected but survivable
Open77.log.warn("notifications package missing, falling back to the vanilla toast")

name: acceptPickup
summary: Applique localement un pickup déjà accepté par le serveur.
description: API interne appelée uniquement après `open77:loot:pickupResult`. Elle projette l'objet dans l'inventaire REDengine local; l'inventaire persistant reste une responsabilité serveur.
example:
-- Reserved for open77_loot: apply a pickup the server already accepted
-- (a gameplay resource listens to open77:loot:result instead)
Open77.loot.acceptPickup(dropId, "Items.money", 200)

name: clear
summary: Supprime toutes les projections locales et leurs prompts.
description: Clears the client-side native loot projection when the caller has `world.loot`. This is intended for the authoritative loot replication package during snapshot replacement; ordinary gameplay resources should request server-owned changes instead.
example:
-- The replication package wipes the projection before applying a fresh snapshot
Open77.loot.clear()

name: remove
summary: Retire une projection locale de loot.
description: Removes one replicated native loot entity from this client's projection and requires `world.loot`. It does not by itself delete the server record, so gameplay code should normally use the authoritative loot package API.
example:
-- Reserved for open77_loot: drop the local projection of a removed server drop
Open77.loot.remove(dropId)

name: requestPickup
summary: Demande au serveur de ramasser un drop.
description: Le serveur contrôle l'existence, le routing bucket et la distance calculée depuis son dernier snapshot du joueur.
returns: true si la requête réseau est partie
example:
-- Press E on the nearest drop to ask the server for it; the answer arrives on open77:loot:result
RegisterKeyMapping("loot_pickup", "Pick up", "E", function()
    if nearestDropId then Open77.loot.requestPickup(nearestDropId) end
end)
AddEventHandler("open77:loot:result", function(id, accepted, reason)
    if not accepted then Open77.hud.notify("Pickup refused: " .. tostring(reason)) end
end)

name: setAuthorityEnabled
summary: Active ou désactive la projection de loot autoritaire.
description: Réservé à `open77_loot`. Quand il est actif, les choix, conteneurs et drops vanilla sont neutralisés et les objets physiques deviennent de simples représentations du registre serveur.
example:
-- Reserved for open77_loot: turn vanilla loot off and project the server registry
Open77.loot.setAuthorityEnabled(true)

name: upsert
summary: Crée ou met à jour la projection locale d'un drop serveur.
description: API interne de réplication. Demande la permission `world.loot`; un script gameplay ne doit pas inventer un drop côté client.

params.name: drop
params.type: table { id, item, quantity, position, radius, label, model, revision }

example:
-- Reserved for open77_loot: project a server drop locally
Open77.loot.upsert({ id = 42, item = "Items.money", quantity = 200, position = { x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.0 },
    radius = 2, label = "Eddies", revision = 1 })

name: cancelPick
summary: Cancels this resource's outstanding native map request.
description: Requires map.control. Returns true or false, reason. The requester receives open77:map:pointPicked with status='cancelled' when a picker was active. Resource shutdown also releases its UI ownership without delivering events to its replacement instance.
example:
-- ESC cancels the pending "choose a destination" picker
RegisterKeyMapping("taxi_cancel", "Cancel destination", "BACKSPACE", function()
    Open77.map.cancelPick()
end)

name: close
summary: Closes a map session opened by this resource.
description: Requires map.control. Returns true on accepted closure, otherwise false, reason. Cannot close a user-opened map or another resource's map. Closure is asynchronous. A pending picker is cancelled.
example:
-- Close the map this resource opened once the destination is chosen
AddEventHandler("open77:map:pointPicked", function(result)
    if result.status == "selected" then Open77.map.close() end
end)

name: getSelectedMarker
summary: Reads the marker highlighted in the vanilla map.
description: Requires map.read. Returns a marker table or nil. kind distinguishes waypoint, quest, poi, resource and unknown. Selection is not the same as the player's waypoint; highlighting a marker does not change navigation.
example:
-- Read what the player highlighted on the map
local marker = Open77.map.getSelectedMarker()
if marker then print(marker.kind, marker.position.x, marker.position.y) end

name: getWaypoint
summary: Reads the player's manual vanilla waypoint.
description: Returns nil (without an error) when no player waypoint is tracked. Quest, POI and Open77 resource markers are excluded. Requires map.read. The result has a string id, kind='waypoint', source='player', position={x,y,z} and revision. Errors return nil, reason; map_unavailable means the world snapshot is unavailable or stale.
example:
-- Send the player's manual waypoint to the server as the taxi destination
local waypoint = Open77.map.getWaypoint()
if waypoint then TriggerServerEvent("taxi:order", waypoint.position) end

name: isOpen
summary: Checks whether the vanilla world map is open.
description: Requires map.read. Returns a boolean, or nil, reason when map state is unavailable. Uses native map controller lifecycle callbacks.
example:
-- Pause the HUD timer while the map is open
SetTick(function()
    if not Open77.map.isOpen() then timer = timer + 1 end
end)

name: open
summary: Opens the vanilla map, optionally focused on a world location.
description: Requires map.control. options.position={x,y,z} optionally focuses the map. Returns requestId, or nil, reason. Acceptance is asynchronous; observe open77:map:opened or open77:map:requestFailed. Respects game UI restrictions and exclusive ownership; map_busy means another map session exists.
example:
-- Open the map focused on the meeting point
Open77.map.open({ position = { x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.0 } })

name: pickPoint
summary: Lets the player select a native map point without travel.
description: Requires map.control. Optional position={x,y,z} and timeoutMilliseconds (1000..300000, default 60000). Returns requestId or nil, reason. open77:map:pointPicked is delivered only to the requesting resource, with requestId, status, position and marker. Use the vanilla waypoint gesture to select. Fast travel, taxi confirmation and Open77 admin map teleport are suppressed during the picker.
example:
-- Let the player pick a taxi destination on the map, one minute to decide
local requestId = Open77.map.pickPoint({ timeoutMilliseconds = 60000 })
AddEventHandler("open77:map:pointPicked", function(result)
    if result.requestId ~= requestId then return end
    if result.status == "selected" then TriggerServerEvent("taxi:order", result.position) end
end)

name: state
summary: Reads a coherent native map snapshot.
description: Requires map.read. Returns open, picking, waypoint, selectedMarker, revision and sampleAgeMs, or nil, reason. Read this on resource startup before subscribing to change events; no historical placement event is synthesized.
example:
-- Read the whole map state once at startup, before subscribing to events
local map = Open77.map.state()
if map and map.waypoint then print("waypoint already set at", map.waypoint.position.x) end

name: clear
summary: Removes every 3D marker owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.markers`; other resources are unaffected.
example:
-- The race is over: remove every checkpoint marker
AddEventHandler("race:finished", function()
    Open77.markers.clear()
end)

name: create
summary: Creates a resource-owned 3D world marker.
description: Requires `world.markers`. Options require `position` and accept `shape`, `style`, `radius`, `maxDistance`, `minDistance`, and `visible`. The returned decimal-string handle preserves its full 64-bit identity.
example:
-- A cylinder marker at the delivery point, visible within 80 m
local marker = Open77.markers.create({
    position = { x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.0 },
    shape = "cylinder",
    radius = 1.5,
    maxDistance = 80,
})

name: list
summary: Lists the calling resource's 3D markers.
description: Requires `world.markers`. Each snapshot includes its requested definition and whether the native renderer currently presents it.
returns: array of { id, shape, style, radius, maxDistance, minDistance, visible, rendered, position }, or nil
example:
-- Debug: are our markers actually rendered?
for _, marker in ipairs(Open77.markers.list() or {}) do
    print(marker.id, marker.rendered)
end

name: remove
summary: Removes one resource-owned 3D marker.
description: Requires `world.markers`.
example:
-- The player reached the checkpoint: remove its marker
Open77.markers.remove(checkpointMarker)

name: update
summary: Patches a resource-owned 3D marker.
description: Requires `world.markers`. Only supplied fields are changed, and ownership prevents mutation of another resource's marker.
example:
-- Move the marker to the next checkpoint
RegisterNetEvent("race:checkpoint", function(position)
    Open77.markers.update(checkpointMarker, { position = position })
end)

name: knockdown
summary: Queue an owned native reaction on an exact local body.
description: Requires player.motion.project. entity is a local registry handle (1 for the owner), not a network player ID. Direction is normalized; distance is0..6 m and the local owner must be alive, ready, on foot and grounded. Returns an owned request ID. Owner phase starts pending, then active after two valid consecutive native-down observations within1.5s. Remote projection starts its native action immediately. No damage, teleport or server authority is granted.
example:
local request, err = Open77.motion.knockdown(1, 0, 1, 0)
if not request then print(err); return end
print(Open77.motion.state(request))

name: state
summary: Read the phase of this resource's native reaction.
description: Requires player.motion.project. Phases include pending, active and recovering; an expired/unknown/foreign ID returns nil, reason. active is a native PSM observation for the owner, not proof of physical displacement or the observer rendering. The support resource waits for active before acknowledging server motion.
example:
local phase, err = Open77.motion.state(request)
if not phase then print(err) else print(phase) end

name: stop
summary: Request cleanup of this resource's native reaction.
description: Requires player.motion.project. Pending cancellation is latched so cleanup retries cannot later activate it. Cancellation removes the owned status/action but may leave native momentum and get-up in progress. It does not instantly freeze velocity, revive a player, or cancel another resource's request.
example:
-- Cancel this resource's knockdown reaction early
local ok, err = Open77.motion.stop(request)
if not ok then print(err) end

name: lock
summary: Applies a bounded local movement lock -- freeze, cripple or heavy cripple -- to the local player.
description: Client-only; requires `player.movement.lock`, a server-driven projection primitive a player resource should not hold by default. `kind` is `freeze` (no movement), `cripple` (slow) or `cripple_heavy`; `durationMs` is 1..3600000 and the adapter clamps it to its own cap. One slot, owned by the calling resource; a later call replaces this resource's own lock and never another's. The adapter releases on the deadline, on death, vehicle entry, workspot, session change and resource stop -- `lockState` exposes the watchdog that removes a lock whose owner never released it. Returns the request id; the server's deadline stays the authority. For a server-authoritative freeze use `Open77.players.setFrozen` on the server instead.
returns: reason: permission_denied:player.movement.lock, resource_not_running, movement_backend_unavailable, invalid_kind, invalid_duration
example:
-- A "cripple" status from the server: the player walks slowly for five seconds
RegisterNetEvent("hack:crippled", function()
    Open77.movement.lock("cripple", 5000)
end)

name: lockState
summary: Reads the current client movement-lock slot and its lifecycle counters.
description: Client-only; requires player.movement.lock. Returns phase, kind, owner, reason, request, grantedMs, remainingMs, elapsedMs, locks, refusals, releases, watchdogRemovals, releaseOverdue and locked. phase is the adapter's own state, not proof of a rendered input restriction, and the server's deadline remains the authority. releaseOverdue and watchdogRemovals expose the bounded watchdog that removes a lock whose owner never released it.
example:
local state, reason = Open77.movement.lockState()
if state then print(state.phase, state.kind, state.remainingMs) else print(reason) end

name: unlock
summary: Releases this resource's owned client movement lock.
description: Client-only; requires player.movement.lock. Releases only a lock the calling resource owns and is harmless when it owns none. It cannot lift another resource's lock. true acknowledges the release request; the native adapter also releases on its own deadline and on death, vehicle entry, workspot, session change and resource stop. Releasing does not undo damage, cancel an authoritative hack or refund a status; use the server hacking APIs for gameplay state.
example:
-- The cripple status ended early: release this resource's lock
RegisterNetEvent("hack:cured", function()
    Open77.movement.unlock()
end)

name: clear
summary: Removes every nameplate override owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates`; other owners are unaffected.
example:
-- Leaving the arena: drop every plate override this resource set
AddEventHandler("arena:left", function()
    Open77.nameplates.clear()
end)

name: remove
summary: Removes the calling resource's nameplate override for one player.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates`.
example:
-- The player left the team: back to the default plate
RegisterNetEvent("team:left", function(playerId)
    Open77.nameplates.remove(playerId)
end)

name: render
summary: Draws remote-player nameplates natively, with no WebUI surface at all.
description:
Requires `ui.nameplates`. `stream` had already taken Lua off the per-frame path, and plates still trailed the world: what was left is the CEF chain itself -- IPC, a page repaint on the page's own timer, an offscreen raster, a shared-texture handoff, then the composite -- and every stage buffers. `render(true)` draws the plate in the frame that presents it, from a projection taken on that same frame, so there is nothing left to buffer and no page to create.

Guard the call rather than invoking it bare: a client older than the native drawer has no `render` at all, and indexing nil takes the whole resource down instead of falling back. `Open77.nameplates.render ~= nil and Open77.nameplates.render(true)` is the shipped form, with `stream(page)` and then a `Wait(33)` poll loop as the two fallbacks.

`render(false)` stops it. The drawer is released on stop, reload and world exit anyway, but asking explicitly is what keeps a reload from leaving one frame painted. `Open77.nameplates.set` gains `showDistance` on this path; `label`, `color` and `maxDistance` apply to every path.
returns: true when the plugin is drawing them, otherwise false
example:
-- Let the plugin draw the plates natively (guarded for older clients)
if Open77.nameplates.render then
    Open77.nameplates.render(true)
end

name: set
summary: Creates or updates the calling resource's nameplate override for a remote player.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates`. Options accept `label`, `color`, `maxDistance`, and `visible`. Overrides are owner-scoped and cleaned up with the resource.
example:
-- Team-mates get a blue plate visible from further away
RegisterNetEvent("team:joined", function(playerId, name)
    Open77.nameplates.set(playerId, { label = "[TEAM] " .. name, color = "#3399FF", maxDistance = 60 })
end)

name: setTalking
summary: Shows or clears the native speaker icon on one remote player's nameplate.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates`. Talking assertions are owner-scoped and automatically released on stop; several voice/HUD resources may assert the same player without racing. The integrated voice package drives this from authenticated native talker state.
example:
-- Show the speaker icon while the voice package reports the player talking
for _, talker in ipairs(Open77.voice.talkers() or {}) do
    Open77.nameplates.setTalking(talker.playerId, talker.speaking == true)
end

name: snapshot
summary: Returns the currently rendered remote-player nameplates.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates`. Screen coordinates and distance describe the most recent presentation snapshot.
returns: array of { id, label, color, x, y, distance }, or nil
example:
-- Draw a health bar under each rendered plate
for _, plate in ipairs(Open77.nameplates.snapshot() or {}) do
    healthBars.place(plate.id, plate.x, plate.y + 0.02)
end

name: stopStream
summary: Stops the calling resource's native nameplate stream.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates`. Stopping a stream that does not exist succeeds, so teardown is idempotent. The stream is also dropped automatically on stop, reload, world exit, and when its page is destroyed.
example:
-- Stop streaming plates when the HUD page is closed
AddEventHandler("hud:closed", function()
    Open77.nameplates.stopStream()
end)

name: stream
summary: Streams the native nameplate projection to a page, once per game frame.
description: Requires `ui.nameplates` and a WebUI page this resource owns. The projection was always native and always correct; relaying it from a Lua timer is what made plates lag and freeze. This publishes the same `nameplates:update` event with the same `{ players = { { id, label, color, x, y, distance } } }` payload, so an existing page needs no change and the resource can delete its `Wait(33)` loop. An identical frame is not re-sent.
example:
-- Feed the native plate projection to this resource's HUD page every frame
Open77.nameplates.stream(hudPage)

name: call
summary: Asks the server a question and returns a promise for the answer.
description: Requires network.events. The name alone targets the handler this same resource registered on the server; the table form { resource = "other", name = "x", timeout = ms } targets another resource or sets a deadline (default 10000 ms, range 100..120000). Resolves with the handler's return values, or rejects with a reason such as callback_not_found, callback_timeout or callback_target_stopped. Up to 29 arguments and 48 KiB per frame; 256 questions open per resource. Open77.net.callAwait(...) is the same call followed by :await(), for use inside a CreateThread. Aliased as Open77.callbacks.call. See the Network callbacks guide.
example:
-- Ask the server for the stock and price of an item
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, reason = Open77.net.call("getStock", "medkit")
    if not pending then return print(reason) end
    local count, price = pending:await()
    print(count, price)
end)

name: callAwait
summary: Asks the server a question and waits for the answer.
description: Requires network.events. Open77.net.call followed by :await() on the promise it returns, so it must run inside a CreateThread or another managed task; outside one the await answers nil, await_requires_scheduler_coroutine instead of blocking the frame. Same targeting, timeouts, limits and failure reasons as Open77.net.call. Defined by the client's callback prelude rather than by a native. Aliased as Open77.callbacks.callAwait. See the Network callbacks guide.
returns: the handler's return values, or nil, reason

name: emitServer
summary: Sends an event to the server.
description: Alias of `TriggerServerEvent`: sends a bounded, serializable event payload to the authenticated server session. The current resource must declare `network.events`.
example:
-- Namespaced spelling of TriggerServerEvent
Open77.net.emitServer("shop:buy", { item = "ammo_box" })

name: on
summary: Listens for an event coming from the server.
description: Registers an authenticated incoming server event and its callback for the current resource generation. It is the namespaced equivalent of `RegisterNetEvent` and requires `network.events`.
example:
-- Namespaced spelling of RegisterNetEvent
Open77.net.on("bank:deposit", function(amount)
    Open77.hud.notify(("Deposited %d eddies"):format(amount))
end)

name: register
summary: Answers a callback the server sends with Open77.net.callClient.
description: Requires network.events. The handler receives the call's arguments (the caller is always the server, so there is no source) and its return values become the answer; raising rejects the caller's promise with the error text. Callback names are per resource: the server reaches this handler by naming this resource. Up to 256 names and 256 in-flight calls per resource; stopping the resource answers what it was still serving with callback_target_stopped. Aliased as Open77.callbacks.register. See the Network callbacks guide.

name: unregister
summary: Stops answering a callback name registered with Open77.net.register.
description: Requires network.events. A later request for that name is refused with callback_not_found on the next frame rather than waiting for a timeout. Aliased as Open77.callbacks.unregister.
example:
-- Stop answering the server's question once the dialog is gone
Open77.net.unregister("confirmPurchase")

name: catalog
summary: The catalog as of the last refresh.
description: Reads a snapshot: refreshing is asynchronous, so call `refresh`, then `catalog` a beat later.
example:
-- The server browser reads the catalog a beat after refreshing it
CreateThread(function()
    Open77.network.refresh()
    Wait(1000)
    local catalog = Open77.network.catalog()
    for _, server in ipairs(catalog.servers or {}) do print(server.name) end
end)

name: connect
summary: Joins an Open77 server.
description: Starts a connection to the supplied Open77 server endpoint using the current identity and resource pipeline. It requires `network.client`; success means the request was accepted, while connection progress and errors are observed through `status()`.
returns: true when the request is accepted
example:
-- The trusted server browser joins the selected server
Open77.network.connect("play.example.net:11778", "V")

name: disconnect
summary: Leaves the current server.
description: Requests an orderly disconnect with an optional diagnostic reason. It returns after queuing teardown; the session phase in `status()` is the authoritative view of when cleanup has completed.
example:
-- A "Leave server" entry in a custom pause menu
RegisterNetEvent("pause:leave", function()
    Open77.network.disconnect()
end)

name: identity
summary: Reads the local Master-backed identity profile state.
description: Returns the durable user id, current display name, registration state, and asynchronous update phase. The private key is never exposed. This bridge exists for the trusted local server browser; server-downloaded resources should use the verified player APIs instead.
returns: table { phase, generation, userId, displayName, error, registered }, or nil
example:
-- The trusted browser shows the player's display name
local identity = Open77.network.identity()
if identity then print("playing as", identity.displayName) end

name: identityUpdate
summary: Requests a signed username update from the Master.
description: Queues the HTTP enrollment on the networking worker and returns immediately. Poll `identity()` until the matching generation becomes `ready` or `failed`. The backend is deliberately available only to the trusted system server-browser resource and refuses updates during a live session.
example:
-- The trusted browser asks the master for a new display name
Open77.network.identityUpdate(masterUrl, "V_from_Watson")

name: refresh
summary: Asks the directory for the server catalog again.
description: Starts a master-server catalog refresh for the supplied URL and requires `network.client`. The call only accepts the request; use `catalog()` to inspect generation, phase, HTTP status, body and error.
example:
-- Refresh the server list when the browser opens
Open77.network.refresh()

name: status
summary: State of the network session.
description: Returns the current client session snapshot: phase, endpoint, authenticated player identity, routing bucket, rates, server time, ping and downloaded resource-set metadata. Reading it does not initiate a connection or wait for a phase change.
returns: table { phase, endpoint, playerId, routingBucket, ping, error }
example:
-- Show the ping on the HUD
SetTick(function()
    local session = Open77.network.status()
    if session then hud.ping = session.ping end
end)

name: all
summary: Lists the NPCs this client can see, Open77-owned and optionally vanilla.
description:
With no argument this is the server-owned set in this client's interest set, unchanged: every row has an `id` the server agrees with, and `source` is `"open77"`. Canonical creation, tasks, health and removal are server-only; see [NPCs](npcs.md).

`includeForeign = true` additionally lists the **vanilla population peds** standing around the local player. Those rows are deliberately a different shape -- `source = "population"`, `kind = "populationNpc"`, no `id`, no `health`, no `bucket` -- because nothing replicates them. They are here so a targeting resource can see the whole world, not so anything can be commanded. The extra reach costs a world query and its own permission, `npcs.foreign`, and is refused by name without it.
returns: array of NPC snapshots (owned) and population rows, or nil
example:
for _, row in ipairs(Open77.npcs.all({ includeForeign = true, radius = 25 })) do
    if row.source == "open77" then print("ours", row.id)
    else print("scenery", row.engineEntity) end
end

name: currentTask
summary: Returns the canonical active task ID for an NPC.
description: Returns the last Open77 NPC task snapshot currently presented for a network NPC. It requires `npcs.read`; task state is ephemeral and can disappear when the NPC leaves the streaming set.
example:
-- Debug: which task is this NPC presenting?
print("task", Open77.npcs.currentTask(npcId))

name: entity
summary: Returns the ephemeral local Open77 entity handle for an NPC projection.
description: Returns nil before readiness and after stream-out. Never cache this handle across lifecycle changes.
example:
-- Read a server NPC's body through its entity handle
local entity = Open77.npcs.entity(npcId)
if entity then print(Open77.character.state(entity).position.x) end

name: get
summary: Reads one server-owned NPC currently known by this client.
description: Read-only and guarded by npcs.read. The snapshot includes the exact Character record; template is the legacy alias or 'record' for direct spawns. The local entity handle is generation-checked and becomes invalid after stream-out. Observe onNpcReady/onNpcSpawnFailed for asynchronous projection readiness; see wiki/npcs.md.
example:
-- Show the NPC's record name over its head
local npc = Open77.npcs.get(npcId)
if npc then Open77.hud.notify(npc.record) end

name: isStreamedIn
summary: Whether an NPC projection is attached and ready locally.
description: Reports whether a network NPC currently has a live client proxy in this player's streaming scope. It does not request streaming or prove that the server NPC record no longer exists.
example:
-- Only draw the marker when the NPC has a body on this client
if Open77.npcs.isStreamedIn(npcId) then drawMarker(npcId) end

name: applyPolicy
summary: Applies a third-person policy received from the server.
description: `disabled`, `allowed`, `default` or `forced`, with the pinned perspective for `forced` (a pin with nothing pinned is refused rather than quietly becoming first person). Requires the `perspective.policy` permission -- not because it exposes anything, since all of this is client-local presentation, but because it is the one call that can take the choice away from the player. It deliberately cannot express the bridge's fifth value, `lab`, which disengages the arbiter entirely: a server able to reach that could leave a client with nothing governing the camera. The bundled `open77_perspective` resource is the intended caller, on receipt of `open77:perspective:policy`.
example:
-- The bundled perspective resource applies what the server decided
RegisterNetEvent("perspective:policy", function(policy, perspective)
    Open77.perspective.applyPolicy(policy, perspective)
end)

name: get
summary: Returns the perspective actually in force.
description: `fpp` or `tps`, read from the committed camera owner rather than from the request -- intention is not evidence, which is the same rule `camera.state` had to learn. An engine-owned view (a vehicle camera, a cutscene) reads `fpp`, because that is what the player sees; `Open77.perspective.state().camera` keeps the distinction.
example:
-- Adjust the crosshair for the view actually in force
SetTick(function()
    crosshair.big = Open77.perspective.get() == "tps"
end)

name: set
summary: Asks the perspective arbiter for first or third person.
description: Records the local player's standing request. It is a REQUEST, not a switch: `Api::PerspectiveArbiter` owns the six ownership values -- camera, body, input, weapon, effects, audio -- and moves them together, and every world state (vehicle, workspot, death, photo mode, an unaccounted-for camera) outranks the player. A server policy outranks them too, and a request the policy refuses is still stored, so that lifting a `forced` pin returns the player to what they wanted rather than dropping them somewhere arbitrary; that refusal is reported as `refused_by_policy`. Accepts `fpp`/`first`/`1` and `tps`/`tpp`/`third`/`3`. Never reach past this to `Open77.camera.thirdPerson`: that moves one of the six owners and leaves five behind, which is the split state the arbiter exists to prevent.
example:
-- Third person on foot when the player joins; the arbiter still decides
AddEventHandler("onClientResourceStart", function(name)
    if name == GetCurrentResourceName() then Open77.perspective.set("tps") end
end)

name: state
summary: Reports the whole perspective decision.
description: Returns `mode`, `requested`, `requestExpressed`, `policy`, `forced`, `allowed`, `engaged`, `available`, `settled`, `transition`, `reason`, `rule`, `tier`, the six owners (`camera`, `body`, `input`, `weapon`, `effects`, `audio`) and `violations`. `allowed` is false under a `disabled` or `forced` policy -- the moment a UI should grey its control out. `violations` counts the ticks on which the arbiter caught itself drawing two bodies or two weapons. A pure read, and unlike the `perspective.state` bridge command it works during a live session.
example:
-- Grey out the "toggle view" button when the server forbids it
local state = Open77.perspective.state()
toggleButton.enabled = state and state.allowed

name: toggle
summary: Flips the standing request and returns the new mode.
description: Flips the REQUEST, not the effective view. Sitting in a vehicle the view is first person whatever the preference says, and flipping the effective value would leave a player pressing the key twice to change anything once they got out. The one exception is a player who has never expressed a preference: there the effective view is inverted, so the first press of a fresh session cannot land on the perspective already in force and appear to do nothing.
example:
-- V flips between first and third person
RegisterKeyMapping("toggle_view", "Toggle view", "V", function()
    local mode = Open77.perspective.toggle()
    if mode then Open77.hud.notify(mode == "tps" and "Third person" or "First person") end
end)

name: close
summary: Closes Cyberpunk's native photo mode.
description: Calls the native photo-mode deactivation routine. The operation is idempotent when photo mode is already inactive.
example:
-- Leave photo mode when the round starts
RegisterNetEvent("arena:roundStarted", function()
    Open77.photoMode.close()
end)

name: isActive
summary: Reports whether REDengine photo mode is active.
description: Reads `gamePhotoModeSystem::IsPhotoModeActive`; it reports engine state rather than remembering the last Lua request.
example:
-- Hide the custom HUD while photo mode is up
SetTick(function()
    hud.visible = not Open77.photoMode.isActive()
end)

name: open
summary: Opens Cyberpunk's native photo mode.
description: This is the sole supported activation path while Open77 is loaded. The native plugin refuses the stock keyboard/controller activation entry, then this call invokes the retained original REDengine implementation directly. It is idempotent when already active; REDengine can still refuse contexts in which photo mode is unavailable.
example:
-- A key owned by this resource opens photo mode (the stock shortcut is disabled)
RegisterKeyMapping("photo", "Photo mode", "F8", function()
    local ok, reason = Open77.photoMode.open()
    if not ok then Open77.hud.notify("Photo mode unavailable: " .. reason) end
end)

name: setEnabled
summary: Opens or closes the native photo mode.
description: Equivalent to `open()` for true and `close()` for false. This controls one client-local engine state and is not a resource-owned lease.
example:
-- A photo-mode toggle key owned by this resource
RegisterKeyMapping("photo", "Photo mode", "F8", function()
    Open77.photoMode.setEnabled(not Open77.photoMode.isActive())
end)

name: accept
summary: Queue acceptance of the local player's offered invitation.
description: Declare dependency 'open77_player_interactions >=1.0.0'. This is an asynchronous resource-export facade: call from a managed coroutine and await the Promise; nil plus reason indicates dispatch/rejection. No presentation capability is required for consumers. Resolving a request ID means queued, not accepted by the server. Observe onPlayerInteractionResult or result(requestId), then lifecycle state events.
returns: Open77.Promise resolving to request ID; nil, reason on rejection
example:
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, err = Open77.playerInteractions.accept(interactionId)
    if not pending then print(err); return end
    local value, rejected = pending:await()
    if rejected then print(rejected); return end
    print(value)
end)

name: all
summary: Lists every player this client currently knows about, ascending by player id.
description: No permission. STREAMING-SCOPED, not the server roster: it holds the players this client has been told about and can draw, so a player the server counts as connected can legitimately be absent. Anything that must be true of the whole session asks the server. The local player is included, matching FiveM's GetActivePlayers. A player who is connected but has no body is still listed; pass `{ streamed = true }` to keep only the ones with a body, which is the NetworkIsPlayerActive filter.
example:
-- How many players does this client currently see with a body?
local visible = Open77.players.all({ streamed = true })
Open77.hud.notify(("%d players around you"):format(#visible - 1)) -- minus yourself

name: allHealthStates
summary: Lists all replicated player health snapshots known to the client.
description: Requires `players.life.read`; returns an empty array when unavailable.
example:
-- Show a low-health warning icon over every wounded player nearby
for _, health in ipairs(Open77.players.allHealthStates()) do
    if health.health < health.maxHealth * 0.25 then
        markWounded(health.playerId)
    end
end

name: allLifeStates
summary: Lists all replicated canonical player life states known to the client.
description: Requires `players.life.read`; returns an empty array when unavailable.
example:
-- Count how many players around are down
local down = 0
for _, life in ipairs(Open77.players.allLifeStates()) do
    if life.phase ~= "alive" then down = down + 1 end
end

name: allowAim
summary: Allow or block a local-player action.
description: Requires players.controls and a strict boolean. Freeze true acquires a block; Allow false acquires a block. The inverse releases only this resource VM's block, never another owner or vanilla restriction. Automatically released on resource stop, death and session teardown. Does not freeze vehicles, moving platforms or server teleports. See player-utilities.md for each native restriction and limitations.
example:
-- No aiming inside the safe zone; released again when the player leaves it
AddEventHandler("safezone:entered", function() Open77.players.allowAim(false) end)
AddEventHandler("safezone:left", function() Open77.players.allowAim(true) end)

name: closest
summary: The nearest player with a body.
description: No permission. `Open77.players.nearby` reduced to its first entry, with the same options plus an optional `radius` (unbounded without one). Returns `nil, "no_player_in_range"` when nobody qualifies, which is deliberately distinct from `nearby`'s empty table.
returns: { playerId, entity, distance, position, name, isLocal }
example:
-- Press E to trade with the nearest player within 3 m
RegisterKeyMapping("trade", "Trade", "E", function()
    local other = Open77.players.closest({ radius = 3.0 })
    if not other then return Open77.hud.notify("Nobody close enough") end
    TriggerServerEvent("trade:request", other.playerId)
end)

name: entity
summary: The entity id of one player's body.
description: No permission. Feed the result to any Open77 entity API, `Open77.character.state(entity)` first among them. The local player's body is the reserved entity id `0` that every entity API reads as "me", which is a value, not a failure. Reasons: `player_not_streamed` (known, no body right now), `unknown_player`, `invalid_player`. Cache the player id, never the entity id: a proxy body is destroyed and recreated on death, re-dress and world transition.
example:
-- Read another player's body state through their entity id
local entity = Open77.players.entity(playerId)
if entity then
    local state = Open77.character.state(entity)
    print(state.position.x, state.position.y, state.position.z)
end

name: fromEntity
summary: Which player wears a given body.
description: No permission. The inverse of `Open77.players.entity`, for turning a raycast or a proximity hit back into a player id. Accepts the entity as an integer or as the decimal string form. Entity `0` resolves to the local player. Returns `nil, "unknown_entity"` for an id that is not a live player body right now, which is what a cached id becomes after its body is retired.
example:
-- The raycast hit a body: which player is it?
local hit = Open77.world.raycast(from, to, { entities = true })
if hit and hit.entity then
    local playerId = Open77.players.fromEntity(hit.entity.engineEntity)
    if playerId then Open77.hud.notify("You are looking at player " .. playerId) end
end

    local hp = Open77.players.getHealthState()
    if hp then healthBar.set(hp.health / hp.maxHealth, hp.armor) end
end)

False means absent from this client's active bucket snapshot; it is not a cross-bucket global query or proof that native pixels are rendered. There is intentionally no client setter. See holocall-eyes.md.

    if death and death.killer then

end)

end)

summary: Whether a player is canonically dead or awaiting revive/respawn.
description: Requires `players.life.read`. Omit `playerId` for the local player. Unknown or unavailable states return false.
example:
-- Hide the HUD while the local player is dead
SetTick(function()
    Open77.hud.setVisible("all", not Open77.players.isDead())
end)

summary: Native underwater swimming state.
description: Requires players.read. Omit playerId to query the local network player. Remote players must be streamed and presentation-ready; swimming/diving are local-only and return nil, state_not_replicated remotely. Unavailable is not false. Read-only, without advancing replication counters. See player-utilities.md.
example:
-- Warn about the oxygen the moment the player goes under
SetTick(function()
    if Open77.players.isDiving() then Open77.hud.notify("Watch your oxygen", { replace = true }) end
end)

Read-only, without advancing replication counters. See player-utilities.md.

RegisterKeyMapping("car_radio", "Car radio", "R", function()

Read-only, without advancing replication counters. See player-utilities.md.

Remote players must be streamed and presentation-ready; swimming/diving are local-only and return nil, state_not_replicated remotely. Unavailable is not false. Read-only, without advancing replication counters. See player-utilities.md.

description: Requires players.read. Omit playerId to query the local network player. Remote players must be streamed and presentation-ready; swimming/diving are local-only and return nil, state_not_replicated remotely. Unavailable is not false. Read-only, without advancing replication counters. See player-utilities.md.

-- Play a grunt sound on a vault
local wasVaulting = false
