    local vaulting = Open77.players.isVaulting()

name: local
summary: The local player's id; keyword-named alias of `localId`.
description: No permission. Identical function value to `Open77.players.localId`. `local` is reserved in Lua, so this name only parses through the bracket form `Open77.players["local"]()`; prefer `localId`.
example:
-- Reachable only through the bracket form; prefer localId
local me = Open77.players["local"]()

name: localId
summary: The local player's id.
description: No permission. Returns `nil, "no_session"` while not connected. Registered under `local` as well, for the FiveM-parity spelling, but `local` is a Lua keyword: `Open77.players.local()` is a syntax error and the name is only reachable as `Open77.players["local"]()`. Same function value.
example:
-- Skip yourself when listing nearby players
local me = Open77.players.localId()
for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.players.nearby(20)) do
    if entry.playerId ~= me then print(entry.name, entry.distance) end
end

name: nearby
summary: Players with a body within `radius`, nearest first.
description: No permission. Centred on the local player unless `origin` is given; ties broken by player id so the order does not flicker. Each entry is `{ playerId, entity, distance, position, name, isLocal }`, where `position` is a plain x/y/z table and therefore already a vector3. Players without a body are skipped, having no position; use `all()` to see that they exist. Empty table when nobody qualifies. Reasons: `invalid_radius`, `invalid_origin`, `invalid_limit`, `no_session`, `no_local_position` (connected with no body, so no centre - pass `origin` to ask anyway).
returns: array of { playerId, entity, distance, position, name, isLocal }
example:
-- Everyone within 20 m, nearest first
for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.players.nearby(20)) do
    print(("%s is %.1f m away"):format(entry.name, entry.distance))
end

name: resetControls
summary: Release every player-control block owned by the calling resource VM.
description: Requires players.controls. Does not remove other resources' blocks or expose vanilla restriction state. See player-utilities.md.
example:
-- The mini-game ends: release every block this resource holds
AddEventHandler("minigame:ended", function()
    Open77.players.resetControls()
end)

name: setEnabled
summary: Turns NCPD dispatch on or off for this client.
description: `TogglePreventionSystem`, the nearest equivalent of `SetDispatchServiceActive`. This is the session's own switch and is **not** the three block flags `VehicleSpawnPolicy` owns and drives from world population suppression; this call deliberately never touches those, so the two cannot fight. Reaches the engine through the REDscript command queue, never a native call: all 276 methods on `PreventionSystem` are scripted, and invoking one from C++ without a script frame terminates the process. A `true` return therefore means *queued*, not applied; `Open77.prevention.state()` reports whether the script loop later acknowledged it. Requires `world.prevention`. A server that sets policy through `Open77.players.setWanted` reaches this same surface through the `open77_prevention` resource; a client resource calling it directly is overriding that.
example:
-- The server turned dispatch off for this instance
RegisterNetEvent("world:dispatch", function(enabled)
    Open77.prevention.setEnabled(enabled)
end)

name: setMaxWanted
summary: Sets the ceiling the wanted level resets to, 0 to 5.
description: `SetMinMaxResetHeatLevels(0, level, false)`. The floor stays at 0 deliberately: a nonzero minimum would strand a session at a heat it could never clear. Reaches the engine through the REDscript command queue, never a native call: all 276 methods on `PreventionSystem` are scripted, and invoking one from C++ without a script frame terminates the process. A `true` return therefore means *queued*, not applied; `Open77.prevention.state()` reports whether the script loop later acknowledged it. Requires `world.prevention`. A server that sets policy through `Open77.players.setWanted` reaches this same surface through the `open77_prevention` resource; a client resource calling it directly is overriding that.
example:
-- The VIP zone caps heat at two stars on this client
Open77.prevention.setMaxWanted(2)

name: setWanted
summary: Sets this client's NCPD wanted level, 0 to 5.
description: The wanted level is **world state on this client**, not player state: nothing in the engine's wanted surface takes a target, the heat stage is a scalar on a singleton `PreventionSystem`, and every consumer reads one global `UI_WantedBar`. The NCPD units it summons are this client's own - not Open77 entities, not replicated, invisible to every other player. `0` clears it. Raising it above 0 while world population suppression is active is refused with `population_suppressed` rather than silently doing nothing: the spawn policy is holding `SetSystemLock`/`SetBlockOnFootSpawn`/`SetBlockVehicleSpawn` on in that state, so the stage would change and no unit would ever arrive. Clearing to 0 is always allowed. Reaches the engine through the REDscript command queue, never a native call: all 276 methods on `PreventionSystem` are scripted, and invoking one from C++ without a script frame terminates the process. A `true` return therefore means *queued*, not applied; `Open77.prevention.state()` reports whether the script loop later acknowledged it. Requires `world.prevention`. A server that sets policy through `Open77.players.setWanted` reaches this same surface through the `open77_prevention` resource; a client resource calling it directly is overriding that.
returns: reason: permission_denied:world.prevention, invalid_wanted_level, population_suppressed, script_bridge_unavailable, script_queue_full
example:
-- Clear the local heat after the bribe
local ok, reason = Open77.prevention.setWanted(0)
if not ok then print("wanted not cleared: " .. reason) end

name: state
summary: What was last requested of the prevention system, and whether the script loop acknowledged it.
description: **Never an engine reading.** There is no value channel back from REDscript, only a per-command acknowledgement, so this reports a request record and the field names say so: `requestedLevel`, `requestedMaxLevel`, `requestedEnabled`, plus `levelAcknowledged`, `maxLevelAcknowledged` and `enabledAcknowledged`. An acknowledgement means the script loop found `PreventionSystem` and ran the call; it does not mean the engine honoured it. `scriptAttached` is false until the REDscript loop has polled at least once - anything queued before that is waiting, not lost. `populationSuppressed` says whether the spawn policy is currently holding police off, which is why a `setWanted` raise would be refused. Requires `world.prevention`.
returns: table { scriptAttached, populationSuppressed, requestedLevel, requestedMaxLevel, requestedEnabled, levelAcknowledged, maxLevelAcknowledged, enabledAcknowledged }, or nil
example:
-- Did the script loop acknowledge the last request?
local state = Open77.prevention.state()
if state and not state.levelAcknowledged then print("wanted level still pending") end

name: attach
summary: Attach a resource-owned local prop to a rendered bone or vehicle.
description: Binding fields: parentType ('player' or 'vehicle'), parentId (canonical network ID, not an engine handle), bone (named slot, empty for root), offset {x,y,z} in metres (each ±20), rotation {x,y,z} in degrees (each ±360, local Z-Y-X composition). Unknown fields and non-finite numbers reject. Missing streamed parents are hidden, then rebound when available. See attachments.md. Requires world.props. This changes only this client's prop, not server authority. Physics uses a visual-only attachment host; arbitrary mesh paths without that host are refused.
example:
-- A local placement ghost held in the player's hand
Open77.props.attach(localPropId, { parentType = "player", parentId = Open77.players.localId(), bone = "RightHand" })

name: bones
summary: List available named attachment slots on a streamed parent.
description: Requires world.props. Returns sorted names from the current native slot components, not all skeleton bones. Parent IDs are canonical player/vehicle IDs. Empty array means unavailable or no slots; it does not establish that a different body/model supports a requested slot.
example:
local slots, err = Open77.props.bones('player', playerId)
if slots then for _, slot in ipairs(slots) do print(slot) end end

name: clear
summary: Removes every local prop this resource created.
description: Called automatically when the resource stops or reloads, so a reloading gamemode never leaves orphaned decorations behind. It never touches another resource's props, nor server-owned ones.
example:
-- Leaving build mode removes every placement ghost
AddEventHandler("build:exit", function()
    Open77.props.clear()
end)

name: create
summary: Creates a local, decorative prop owned by this resource.
description: Requires `world.props`. This is the **client** meaning of the name: the prop is never replicated and never visible to anyone else -- a placement ghost, a build cursor, a preview being dragged. It is charged against this resource's quota and released when the resource stops. The identically-named *server* function mints an authoritative, replicated prop instead; the two `Open77` tables are different objects on different machines.

params.name: options
params.type: table { model, position, yaw?, scale?, appearance?, kind?, physics?, collision?, visible?, light? }

name: detach
summary: Detach a resource-owned local prop.
description: Requires world.props. Restores an independent host at the last locally rendered pose. Does not detach a server-owned network prop. Calling the server API is required for a replicated release.
example:
-- Drop the local ghost prop where it is
Open77.props.detach(localPropId)

name: list
summary: Local props this resource owns, with what the renderer did with each.
description: Each entry carries the model, kind, physics, transform, scale, the back-end that drew it, and whether it rendered or failed. Scoped to the caller: it deliberately excludes server-owned props, which belong to the session rather than to any resource, so asking a resource-scoped question about them would return an empty table and read as "no props" rather than "wrong question". Use the `open77_props` resource's `all` export for those.
example:
-- Did every local prop actually render?
for _, prop in ipairs(Open77.props.list()) do
    if not prop.rendered then print("prop failed to render:", prop.model) end
end

name: nearest
summary: Finds the nearest local prop owned by this resource.
description: Requires `world.props`. Searches only the calling resource's local prop set, using a 10 metre default radius. A non-positive or non-finite radius is rejected; use `list` when an unbounded set is intended.
returns: prop snapshot and distance, or nil
example:
-- Press E on the nearest of this resource's ghosts to confirm the placement
RegisterKeyMapping("build_confirm", "Confirm placement", "E", function()
    local prop, distance = Open77.props.nearest(Open77.character.state().position, 3)
    if prop then TriggerServerEvent("build:confirm", prop.model, prop.position) end
end)

name: project
summary: Upserts a server-owned prop into the world, keyed by the server id.
description: What the bundled `open77_props` projection resource drives; not the way a gamemode places objects. Because the native layer is keyed by the server's own id, a prop that only moved is transformed in place rather than destroyed and rebuilt, which is what stops it visibly popping. Projected props are owned by the session, survive a resource reload, and are not charged against any resource's quota.
example:
-- The projection resource shows a server prop under the server's own id
RegisterNetEvent("props:sync", function(serverId, definition)
    Open77.props.project(serverId, definition)
end)

name: remove
summary: Removes a local prop this resource owns.
description: Removing a prop that is already gone succeeds: the caller asked for it not to be there, and it is not there. Another resource's prop answers `owned_by_another_resource`.
example:
-- The player cancelled the placement: remove the ghost
Open77.props.remove(ghostId)

name: setTransform
summary: Moves a local prop to a position and yaw.
description: The one mutation the engine accepts on a live entity, so it never respawns and never pops. Scale is deliberately not part of it: scale is read when the render proxy is built, so it goes through `update` and costs a respawn.
example:
-- Drag the placement ghost to wherever the reticle points
SetTick(function()
    local ray = Open77.camera.aimRay(20)
    if ray and ray.hit then Open77.props.setTransform(ghostId, { position = ray.position }) end
end)

name: unproject
summary: Stops projecting one server-owned prop.
description: Succeeds when the prop is already absent: the server is saying stop showing something, and it is not being shown.
example:
-- The server removed the prop: stop showing it
RegisterNetEvent("props:removed", function(serverId)
    Open77.props.unproject(serverId)
end)

name: unprojectAll
summary: Stops projecting every server-owned prop.
description: Used on disconnect and when the projection resource restarts, so a stale world never survives into a new session.
example:
-- Leaving the server: nothing stale survives into the next session
AddEventHandler("session:disconnected", function()
    Open77.props.unprojectAll()
end)

name: update
summary: Patches a local prop this resource owns.
description: Only the fields present in the patch are taken. Changing anything the render proxy reads when it is built -- model, scale, kind, physics, collision, visibility or the light parameters -- respawns the underlying entity rather than mutating it, because the engine offers no in-place path for those. Use `setTransform` to move a prop without that cost.
example:
-- The player chose a bigger crate: scale respawns the ghost
Open77.props.update(ghostId, { scale = 1.5 })

name: setBody
summary: Project a captured body onto a network player proxy.
description: Requires puppets.present. playerId is a network player ID; body={family,groups}, or false to clear the remote body. Uses asynchronous native dressing; true means acceptance, not a fully rendered proxy. Use the appearance service to distribute authoritative records and preserve wardrobe ownership.
example:
local ok, err = Open77.puppets.setBody(playerId, capturedBody)
if not ok then print(err) end

name: setSlot
summary: Project one remote equipment-slot override.
description: Requires puppets.present. playerId is a network player ID. record is a TweakDB record string (up to160 bytes), false for explicitly empty, or nil for the native default. Do not confuse nil and false when restoring a clothing snapshot. Native dressing is asynchronous; this is not durable inventory ownership.
example:
local ok, err = Open77.puppets.setSlot(playerId, "OuterChest", false)
if not ok then print(err) end

name: setWardrobe
summary: Project a remote wardrobe snapshot.
description: Requires puppets.present. snapshot={active=integer,outfits={[outfitId]={[slot]=recordOrFalse}}}. false means an explicitly empty slot. Network player IDs and native wardrobe IDs are different namespaces. This is asynchronous presentation; the server wardrobe service remains the durable source of truth.
example:
local ok, err = Open77.puppets.setWardrobe(playerId, wardrobeSnapshot)
if not ok then print(err) end

name: generation
summary: Generation number, incremented on every reload.
description: With no argument, returns the current resource generation. Pass a resource name to inspect that resource, or receive nil when it is missing.
example:
-- Tag a deferred callback with the generation so a reload can ignore it
local generation = Open77.resource.generation()
SetTimeout(5000, function()
    if Open77.resource.generation() ~= generation then return end
    print("still the same VM")
end)

name: hasPermission
summary: Whether the resource holds this permission.
description: Checks whether the current resource manifest grants an exact Open77 capability. It is a read-only convenience check; native APIs still enforce their own permission and must handle refusal results.
example:
-- Only offer the map feature if the manifest granted it
if Open77.resource.hasPermission("ui.vanilla.map") then
    Open77.blips.create({ position = shop, label = "Shop" })
end

name: name
summary: Name of the current resource.
description: Returns the current resource's immutable manifest name. This is equivalent to `GetCurrentResourceName()` and remains stable for the lifetime of the resource definition.
example:
-- Prefix log lines with the resource name
print(("[%s] loaded"):format(Open77.resource.name()))

name: readFile
summary: Reads a file from the resource, within its declared allowlist.
description: Reads a file declared by the current resource manifest through a safe relative path. Undeclared files, traversal, oversized content and host filesystem paths are rejected.

name: readPackedFile
summary: Reads a file another resource declared, as base64.
description: Requires `resources.files.read`, which only the bundled audio service holds: every other resource reads its own files with `Open77.resource.readFile`, and a resource holding this one can read any **declared** file of any resource, which is why the grant is visible in the manifest. Only files listed in the named resource's `files` entry are reachable -- scripts, the manifest itself and anything merely present on disk are not, so a resource author publishes deliberately rather than by accident. The 1 MiB ceiling is `readFile`'s; base64 of that is 1.37 MiB, which still clears the 2 MiB JSON limit a `page:send` payload rides, and base64 rather than raw bytes because a raw audio file is not valid UTF-8 and the encoder would refuse the whole event. Refusals: `permission_denied:resources.files.read`, `invalid_resource_path`, `resource_not_found`, `file_not_declared`, `file_too_large`.
example:
-- The audio service reads a declared sound file from another resource, as base64
local base64, reason = Open77.resource.readPackedFile("myradio", "sounds/jingle.mp3")

name: state
summary: State of a resource.
description: Returns the lifecycle state known for a resource name, or for the current resource when omitted. It is an immediate snapshot and does not wait for dependencies or mutate lifecycle state.
example:
-- Only talk to the notifications package if it is running
if Open77.resource.state("open77_notifications") == "started" then
    Open77.exports.call("open77_notifications", "show", { message = "Ready" })
end

name: version
summary: Version declared in `open77.lua`.
description: Returns the version string declared by the current resource manifest. It is package metadata and is unrelated to the Open77 runtime or Lua interpreter version.
example:
-- Show the version in a debug line
print(("running %s %s"):format(Open77.resource.name(), Open77.resource.version()))

name: commands
summary: Every client command registered across every running resource.
description: Client-only. Returns an array of `{ name, resource, restricted, help?, parameters? }`. Only serialisable metadata crosses; handlers stay in their owner's state, exactly as `Open77.input.mappings` does for key binds. This is what the chat composer reads to merge client commands into its completion list -- it skips the restricted ones, which cannot run. `GetRegisteredCommands` is the same function under the FiveM name.
example:
-- Build a "/help" list from every client command
for _, command in ipairs(Open77.runtime.commands()) do
    print("/" .. command.name, command.help or "")
end

name: executeCommand
summary: Runs a command line against the CLIENT command registry only.
description: Client-only. Accepts a raw line with or without a leading `/`, tokenised exactly as the chat composer tokenises it: `\` escapes, `"` and `'` quote, 32 arguments, 4096 bytes. The handler is scheduled, never called inline, so one resource's command cannot run inside another's C frame. `false, unknown_command` is the signal to forward the line to the server and is not an error; `command_restricted`, `empty_command`, `unterminated_quote`, `trailing_escape`, `too_many_arguments`, `command_line_too_long` and `command_task_limit` are. First match wins in resource-name order. Unlike FiveM's `ExecuteCommand` this never forwards to the server by itself -- the caller decides.
returns: true when a client command claimed the line, otherwise false
example:
-- Run a client command from a key; forward to the server when no client command matched
RegisterKeyMapping("quick_cmd", "Quick command", "F4", function()
    local ok, reason = Open77.runtime.executeCommand("hud toggle")
    if not ok and reason == "unknown_command" then TriggerServerEvent("chat:command", "hud toggle") end
end)

name: luaVersion
summary: Embedded Lua version.
description: Returns the embedded Lua interpreter version used by this resource VM. Use it for diagnostics or compatibility checks, not to infer the Open77 build version.
example:
-- Log the interpreter version once
print("Lua", Open77.runtime.luaVersion())

name: registerCommand
summary: Registers a client-side slash command in this resource's VM.
description: Client-only; no permission. The handler is `(source, args, raw)` with `source` always 0, because on the client there is no other party to attribute a command to. The optional third argument `restricted` is honoured by REFUSING: such a command is registered and listed but declines to run with `command_restricted`, because the client has no ACL and cannot answer an authority question -- an admin-only action belongs on the server. The optional fourth argument `{ help, parameters }` is merged into the chat composer's completions (8 parameters, 240 bytes each). Names accept `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]` up to 64 bytes, the same set the server's `RegisterCommand` accepts; a leading `/` is stripped. Re-registering a name inside one VM replaces the handler. 128 commands per resource. `RegisterCommand` is the same function under the FiveM name.
example:
-- A local command with chat completion metadata
Open77.runtime.registerCommand("hudscale", function(source, args)
    hud.scale = tonumber(args[1]) or 1.0
end, false, { help = "Scale the HUD", parameters = { { name = "factor", help = "0.5 to 2" } } })

name: unregisterCommand
summary: Withdraws a client command this resource registered.
description: Client-only. The registry is per VM: a resource can only withdraw its own command, and asking for another's answers `false, command_not_found`. Stopping a resource withdraws all of its commands.
example:
-- Withdraw the command when the feature is disabled
Open77.runtime.unregisterCommand("hudscale")

name: version
summary: Open77 version.
description: Returns the Open77 scripting runtime version exposed to resources. This describes the host API and is distinct from both the resource manifest version and game build.
example:
-- Refuse to run on an older runtime
print("Open77 runtime", Open77.runtime.version())

name: cancel
summary: Cancels an owned native transition and restores the image immediately.
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. Ownership includes resource generation and host instance. Never clears a native game fade that has taken over. Emits open77:screen:cancelled with reason=requested on success.
example:
-- The player pressed ESC: abort the fade and restore the image now
Open77.screen.cancel(fadeId)

name: catalog
summary: Lists supported native screen transition presets and backend availability.
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. Current preset is fade, with backend=native_quest_fade, available, color, maxDurationMs, maxHoldMs and maxTimeoutMs. Availability verifies this executable's guarded native entry, not whether a world is ready or another fade is busy. Glitch remains unsupported.
example:
-- Check the fade backend is available before relying on it
local presets = Open77.screen.catalog()
if presets and presets.fade and presets.fade.available then print("fade ready") end

name: fadeIn
summary: Returns the image for this resource's active native fade.
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. options.durationMs is 0..10000 (default 500). Returns true and, as a second value, an Open77.Promise that resolves when the image is back. Can reverse an outgoing fade; does not extend the safety deadline. Rejects another owner, stale generation or an already-running return. open77:screen:finished marks the same boundary.
example:
-- Bring the image back after the teleport landed
CreateThread(function()
    local ok, back = Open77.screen.fadeIn(fadeId, { durationMs = 800 })
    if back then back:await() end
    Open77.hud.notify("Welcome to the garage")
end)

name: fadeOut
summary: Applies a native black or color-tinted quest fade (colored rendering is engine-controlled).
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. Returns an owned string ID and, as a SECOND value, an Open77.Promise that resolves with the state table when the screen is actually covered and rejects with the transition's reason if it ends first. Options: durationMs (0..10000, default 500), color={r,g,b,a=255}, timeoutMs (1000..60000, default at least 15000). Resource cleanup and a bounded real-time deadline restore the image, and both fail the promise rather than leave a caller waiting. See the Native screen transitions guide.
example:
-- Fade to black, teleport, fade back
CreateThread(function()
    local id, covered = Open77.screen.fadeOut({ durationMs = 400 })
    if not id then return end
    covered:await()
    Open77.travel.teleportAndSettle({ x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.0 }):await()
    Open77.screen.fadeIn(id, { durationMs = 400 })
end)

name: isFaded
summary: Is the screen covered right now, whoever covered it.
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. UNOWNED: true when the engine's own fade manager reports a completed outgoing fade, whether this resource, another resource, the server relay or a vanilla quest/loading fade caused it. Read it before fading out so a spawn or teleport does not stack a second fade on a screen that is already black. Answers nil, reason rather than a confident false when the guarded backend is unavailable or the call is off the game thread.
example:
-- Do not stack a second fade on a screen that is already black
if not Open77.screen.isFaded() then
    Open77.screen.fadeOut({ durationMs = 300 })
end

name: nativeState
summary: The engine's own fade state, unowned.
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. Returns faded, fading, out, busy, ready and remainingMs read straight from the native fade manager with no owner filter -- the detailed form of isFaded(). fading separates 'on its way to black' from 'already black'. Engine truth, not an estimate, and not a GPU presentation fence.
example:
-- Wait until the engine reports the screen fully black
CreateThread(function()
    repeat Wait(50) until (Open77.screen.nativeState() or {}).faded
    print("black now")
end)

name: state
summary: Reads this resource generation's active or recent native transition.
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. OWNER-SCOPED: it answers for this resource generation's own transition and nothing else -- isFaded() and nativeState() read a fade someone else owns. Returns id, generation, phase, reason, backend, timing, automatic, elapsedMs, remainingMs, timeoutMs, black and color. remainingMs is the native fade timer, not hold time; native-state completion is not a GPU fence or streaming-complete signal. History is bounded to 64 global entries and removed on resource release.
example:
-- Is our own fade still running?
local state = Open77.screen.state(fadeId)
if state then print(state.phase, state.remainingMs) end

name: transition
summary: Runs a native fade, bounded hold and return sequence.
description: Client-only; requires screen.effects. Supported preset: fade. Returns an owned string ID and, as a second value, an Open77.Promise that resolves when the whole sequence has finished. Options: durationMs=500, holdMs=250, fadeInMs=500, timeoutMs and opaque RGB color. Durations are integer milliseconds; hold is 0..30000, fades 0..10000. Only one active owner; vanilla requests retain priority. No teleport or network mutation. Glitch is not yet a supported preset.
example:
-- A complete fade-hold-return in one call, for a scene change
CreateThread(function()
    local id, done = Open77.screen.transition("fade", { durationMs = 500, holdMs = 1000, fadeInMs = 500 })
    if done then done:await() end
end)

name: characterBootstrap
summary: Reads the current character-bootstrap state.
description: Returns the current client-local character bootstrap projection as phase, body family, error and generation. The table is a snapshot; polling it does not advance the transaction.
example:
-- A custom character-creation flow watches the bootstrap phase
local bootstrap = Open77.session.characterBootstrap()
if bootstrap then print("bootstrap phase:", bootstrap.phase, "family:", bootstrap.bodyFamily) end

name: failCharacterBootstrap
summary: Marks character bootstrap as failed.
description: Marks the active client-local character bootstrap as failed with an optional bounded diagnostic reason. It requires player.appearance.edit and does not disconnect the network session.
example:
-- The creator was cancelled: mark the bootstrap as failed with a reason
Open77.session.failCharacterBootstrap("player_cancelled")

name: isMenuOpen
summary: Whether any modal layer -- Open77's or the game's -- owns the screen.
description: Requires `session.menus`. True when a gameplay loop should stop reading input: an Open77 WebUI surface holding the keyboard, any vanilla menu scenario, photo mode, the appearance mirror, the pre-game character creator, or the Open77 developer console. It is the same disjunction the window procedure already uses to route the escape key, extended by photo mode and the console, so the read cannot disagree with the behaviour the player sees. **What it cannot see**: the vanilla half is fed by the gameplay idle scenario's wrappers, so a screen that does not pass through that scenario -- radial and hub wheels, pre-game menus other than the creator -- never reports itself. A resource that needs certainty about its own modal should still track its own and compare `menuState().overlayResource`. Pairs with the `open77:menuStateChanged` event, which is raised from the same snapshot.
example:
CreateThread(function()
  while true do
    Wait(0)
    if not Open77.session.isMenuOpen() then pollGameplayInput() end
  end
end)

name: isPauseMenuOpen
summary: Whether the VANILLA pause menu is on screen.
description: Requires `session.menus`. The FiveM `IsPauseMenuActive` equivalent, and it means the pause menu specifically -- not the inventory, the map, the journal or the death screen, which `isMenuOpen()` covers. Read from the scenario name the script bridge already carries (`MenuScenario_PauseMenu`). On a server whose own pause resource has taken over, the vanilla menu never opens and this stays false while the Open77 overlay is up; `isMenuOpen()` is the question that covers both, and `menuState().overlayResource` names which resource has the screen.
example:
-- Pause the custom HUD timer while the vanilla pause menu is up
SetTick(function()
    if not Open77.session.isPauseMenuOpen() then timer = timer + 1 end
end)

name: launcherContext
summary: What the launcher told this game process at boot.
description: Returns a table { connectEndpoint, master, serverId, modsDigest, launched } read once from the environment the OPEN//77 launcher sets when it starts the game (OP77_CONNECT, OP77_CONNECT_MASTER, OP77_WORLD_SERVER, OP77_WORLD_MODS_DIGEST), every value validated against a strict alphabet. All strings are empty and `launched` is false when the game was started without the launcher (Steam, GOG, a shortcut): that is a state, not an error. `modsDigest` is the SHA-256 of the required-mod set the launcher installed for the world it booted into, the same digest the master relays as `requiredModsDigest` in the catalogue, so the shell can decide whether this boot can join a world without a relaunch. Returns nil plus a reason only when no game backend is attached.
example:
-- Was the game started by the launcher, and for which server?
local ctx = Open77.session.launcherContext()
if ctx and ctx.launched then print("launched for server", ctx.serverId) end

name: loadPristine
summary: Loads the local development world from Open77's bundled pristine save.
description: No network session is armed by this operation.
example:
-- A development helper: load the bundled pristine world without connecting
RegisterCommand("devworld", function()
    Open77.session.loadPristine()
end, false)

name: loadScreen
summary: Describes the connected server's declared loading screen.
description: Returns availability and the server name so the trusted shell can choose the verified server page or its built-in fallback. This function does not create the WebUI surface; the shell uses `WebUI.create({ loadScreen = true })` for that.
example:
-- The trusted shell decides between the server's page and the fallback
local screen = Open77.session.loadScreen()
if screen.available then print("loading screen from", screen.server) end

name: menuState
summary: Every modal layer at once, sampled in one instant.
description: Requires `session.menus`. Returns `open`, `pauseMenu`, `vanillaMenu`, `scenario`, `overlay`, `overlayResource`, `photoMode`, `appearanceEditor`, `characterCreator`, `console` and `source`. One call rather than several because the answer a script wants is the disjunction, and a caller assembling it from separate reads would sample them at different instants and could see it half-true. `source` names the highest-priority layer in the same order the escape key is routed: `overlay`, `creator`, `vanilla`, `photoMode`, `appearance`, `console`, `none`. `scenario` is the vanilla scenario name, empty during gameplay. This is also the payload of `open77:menuStateChanged(open, pauseMenu, source, scenario)`, deliberately: the event and the read describe the same snapshot. The event is an EDGE and is not synthesised at startup -- read this once when your resource starts.
example:
AddEventHandler("open77:menuStateChanged", function(open, pause, source)
    if open == "1" then pauseLoop(source) else resumeLoop() end
end)
local now = Open77.session.menuState()
if now and now.open then pauseLoop(now.source) end

name: openSettings
summary: Opens the game's own settings screen without exposing the pause menu.
description: Requests the client-side Open77 settings interface. It only changes local presentation and does not modify server configuration or another player's settings.
example:
-- A "Settings" entry in a custom pause menu
RegisterNetEvent("pause:settings", function()
    Open77.session.openSettings()
end)

name: quitGame
summary: Exits Cyberpunk 2077 to the desktop.
description: The vanilla exit path, reached through the script bridge rather than by terminating the process: the request is ENQUEUED and runs inside the script frame the bridge loop already owns, because a native call into script without a frame kills the process outright. Fails with `script_bridge_not_attached` before the bridge is up, `queue_full` if the bridge queue is saturated, and `game_unavailable_on_this_host` on a host with no game backend. Intended for the trusted pause surface -- `open77_pause` is the only caller -- and not for gameplay code: quitting a session is `Open77.network.disconnect`, which walks the engine back to the main menu instead of closing the game.
example:
-- The "Quit to desktop" entry of a custom pause surface
local ok, reason = Open77.session.quitGame()
if not ok then print("quit refused: " .. reason) end

name: relaunchViaLauncher
summary: Hands the player to the launcher for a world this boot cannot serve.
description: Opens `open77://connect?server=<serverId>&endpoint=<host:port>&relaunch=<pid>` through the OS protocol handler the OPEN//77 launcher registers. The launcher waits for this process to exit, installs the world's required mods into its profile and starts the game again with an auto-connect to the endpoint. Nothing here terminates the game: the caller quits (Open77.session.quitGame) once this returned true, so a missing launcher is reported instead of leaving the player at the desktop. Both arguments are validated (a GUID-shaped server id, a host:port endpoint) and only that one scheme and query shape can ever be launched, so a resource cannot turn this into a generic open-URL or run-program primitive. Returns true, or false plus a reason: invalid_server_id, invalid_endpoint, launcher_not_registered (no handler for the open77 scheme on this machine), launcher_launch_failed:<code>.
example:
-- This boot lacks the world's mods: hand over to the launcher, then quit
if Open77.session.relaunchViaLauncher(serverId, "play.example.net:27015") then
    Open77.session.quitGame()
end

name: requestCharacterCreator
summary: Requests the native character creator.
description: Requests the native character creator for the active bootstrap transaction. It requires player.appearance.edit and returns a stable failure when the game backend cannot accept the request.
example:
-- Open the native character creator for a brand-new character
Open77.session.requestCharacterCreator()

name: resetCharacterBootstrap
summary: Resets the local character-bootstrap transaction.
description: Clears the client-local character bootstrap transaction so a fresh bootstrap can begin. It does not delete a server character or change another player's state.
example:
-- Start the character bootstrap again after a failure
Open77.session.resetCharacterBootstrap()

name: resolveCharacterBootstrap
summary: Completes bootstrap with a selected body family.
description: Completes the active bootstrap with the validated female or male body family. It requires player.appearance.edit and only updates the local bootstrap backend.
example:
-- The player picked a body family in a custom menu
Open77.session.resolveCharacterBootstrap("female")

name: setMenuReady
summary: Declares that this resource is able to serve the pause menu.
description: The escape key is only intercepted while this is true. A resource that fails to start therefore leaves the game's own menu reachable, rather than stranding the player with none.
example:
-- Only intercept ESC once the pause page is really up
AddEventHandler("pause:pageReady", function()
    Open77.session.setMenuReady(true)
end)

name: takeCharacterCreatorResult
summary: Consumes the pending character-creator result.
description: Consumes the pending native character-creator result once and returns its serialized payload, or nil when no result is ready. It requires player.appearance.edit.
example:
-- Poll for the creator's result once it closes
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        local result = Open77.session.takeCharacterCreatorResult()
        if result then TriggerServerEvent("character:created", result); break end
        Wait(500)
    end
end)

name: request
summary: Asks the script bridge to list the variables of a group.
description: Asynchronous: request, then read with `values` a beat later.
example:
-- Ask for the graphics group, then read it a beat later
CreateThread(function()
    Open77.settings.request("graphics")
    Wait(250)
    for _, v in ipairs(Open77.settings.values()) do print(v.name, v.value) end
end)

name: set
summary: Writes a settings variable.
description: Submits one local Open77 setting change through the settings backend. The key, value type and published bounds are validated; use `values()` to read the resulting projection.
example:
-- Write one setting from a custom settings page
Open77.settings.set("audio", "master_volume", 80)

name: values
summary: The variables as the script last reported them.
description: Returns a snapshot of the settings currently published by the client backend. The returned table is a copy and modifying it does not apply changes.
returns: table of { name, value, minimum, maximum, step }
example:
-- Fill a settings page from the last reported values
for _, v in ipairs(Open77.settings.values()) do
    print(("%s = %d (%d..%d)"):format(v.name, v.value, v.minimum, v.maximum))
end

name: clear
summary: Stops every SFX owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`; VFX and other resource owners are unaffected.
example:
-- Stop every sound this resource plays when the mini-game ends
AddEventHandler("minigame:ended", function() Open77.sfx.clear() end)

name: list
summary: Lists active SFX owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`.
returns: array of { id, kind, name, entity, remaining }, or nil
example:
-- Debug: which sounds are still playing?
for _, sfx in ipairs(Open77.sfx.list() or {}) do print(sfx.id, sfx.name, sfx.remaining) end

name: play
summary: Starts resource-owned spatial audio on an entity.
description: Requires `world.effects`. Options accept `entity`, `emitter`, `tag`, `seekTime`, `duration`, and `unique`; omitting `entity` uses the local player.
example:
-- A Wwise event on the local player when the hack lands
RegisterNetEvent("hack:hit", function()
    Open77.sfx.play("ui_hacking_access_denied", { duration = 2 })
end)

name: play2d
summary: Plays a non-spatialised (2D) Wwise event -- the frontend door.
description: Client-only; requires `world.effects`. `Open77.sfx.play` posts the sound at an entity, so it always comes from somewhere in the world; a user-interface click comes from nowhere. This posts through `gameGameAudioSystem::Play` with no entity and no emitter, the same call vanilla scripts make for menu sounds. Returns `true` rather than a handle: a frontend one-shot has no emitter to address a stop to, so it is untracked, unstoppable and consumes no effect quota. There is no `volume` and no `pitch` option here or on `play` -- REDengine's audio events carry neither field; the only float in the surface is a bank-authored Wwise RTPC, not a gain. Use `open77_sound` when you need to control loudness or pitch.
example:
-- A menu click that comes from nowhere
AddEventHandler("menu:selected", function()
    Open77.sfx.play2d("ui_menu_onpress")
end)

name: stop
summary: Stops one SFX handle owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`. REDengine stops audio by event name, so identical simultaneous events on one entity may share stop behavior.
example:
-- Stop the alarm loop on the car
local alarm = Open77.sfx.play("v_car_alarm", { entity = carEntity })
AddEventHandler("alarm:off", function() Open77.sfx.stop(alarm) end)

name: entity
summary: The replicated state bag of one vehicle, NPC or prop, read-only.
description: No permission. Accepts `(kind, id)` or `{ kind = , id = }`, where kind is `vehicle`, `npc` or `prop`. The mirror only holds entities this client is streaming.
example:
-- Read a car's replicated fuel level set by the server
local fuel = Open77.state.entity("vehicle", vehicleId).fuel
if fuel then hud.fuel = fuel end

name: localPlayer
summary: The local player's own replicated state bag.
description: No permission. Resolved from the live session on every call, so it answers `no_session` before a session exists and `network_unavailable` on a host that does not replicate. `LocalPlayer.state` is the FiveM spelling of the same thing.
example:
-- Show the local player's job on the HUD
local me = Open77.state.localPlayer()
if me and me.job then hud.job = me.job.name end

name: offChange
summary: Stops a state-bag change subscription.
description: No permission. Takes the id returned by `Open77.state.onChange` or by `AddStateBagChangeHandler`.
example:
-- Stop watching the round key when the match is over
local sub = Open77.state.onChange("global", "round", function(_, _, value) hud.round = value end)
AddEventHandler("arena:matchOver", function() Open77.state.offChange(sub) end)

name: onChange
summary: Watches state-bag changes matching a selector and a key.
description: No permission. The selector is a bag handle, a `{ kind = , id = }` table, a bare kind string, or nil for every bag; the key is a key name or nil for every key. The handler runs at a tick boundary as `fn(selector, key, value, previous)`. Subscriptions die with the resource instance.
example:
-- React when the server changes this player's job
Open77.state.onChange({ kind = "player", id = Open77.players.localId() }, "job", function(selector, key, value, previous)
    Open77.hud.notify("New job: " .. tostring(value and value.name))
end)

name: player
summary: The replicated state bag of one player, read-only.
description: No permission. Accepts a player id as a number or its decimal string. A bag this client is not entitled to reads as empty rather than erroring, so a read is always safe.
example:
-- Is the player in front of us a cop?
local job = Open77.state.player(otherId).job
if job and job.name == "police" then print("that is a cop") end

name: ready
summary: Asks the server to resend every state bag this client may see.
description: Requires `network.events`. Rarely needed: the host asks for a resync itself whenever the server session changes, and the mirror survives a resource restart because it lives in the host rather than in a VM. Use it after a deliberate local reset.
returns: true when the request was sent, otherwise false
example:
-- After a deliberate local reset, ask for every bag again
Open77.state.ready()

name: request
summary: Asks the server to change one state-bag key.
description: Requires `network.events`. An acknowledgement of the SEND, never of the outcome: the server runs the owning resource's validator and republishes, so the mirror only moves when the delta comes back. Refused with `not_requestable` unless a server resource opted the key in. Requests are coalesced per key and leave as one net event at most four times a second -- that is what keeps a naive per-keystroke caller from tripping the transport's 32-inbound-events-per-second disconnect.
returns: true when queued for sending, otherwise false
reason: permission_denied:network.events, invalid_state_selector, invalid_state_key, state_value_not_serializable, state_value_too_large, state_request_rate_limit
example:
-- Ask the server to change the player's radio frequency (the server validates it)
RegisterNetEvent("radio:tune", function(frequency)
    Open77.state.request({ kind = "player", id = Open77.players.localId() }, "radioFrequency", frequency)
end)

name: get
summary: Reads the canonical health and stamina state for one player.
description: Requires `players.stats.read` (or the legacy `players.life.read`). Omit `playerId` for the local player. Returns the same combined shape as the server API, including both point pools, maximums, fractions, regeneration flags/rates, armor, god mode, damage attribution and revisions. Client resources cannot mutate these server-owned values.
example:
-- A custom HUD reads both pools of the local player
SetTick(function()
    local stats = Open77.stats.get()
    if stats then hud.set(stats.health.fraction, stats.stamina.fraction) end
end)

name: getHealth
summary: Reads one player's canonical health pool.
description: Requires `players.stats.read` (or `players.life.read`). Omit `playerId` for the local player. The table contains `value/current`, `maximum/max`, `fraction`, `percentage`, `regenEnabled`, `regenPerSecond` and `regenerating`.
example:
-- Flash the screen when health drops under 25 %
local hp = Open77.stats.getHealth()
if hp and hp.fraction < 0.25 then flashRed() end

name: getStamina
summary: Reads one player's canonical stamina pool.
description: Requires `players.stats.read` (or `players.life.read`). Omit `playerId` for the local player. The table contains `value/current`, `maximum/max`, `fraction`, `percentage`, `regenEnabled`, `regenPerSecond` and `regenerating`.
example:
-- Grey out the sprint icon when stamina is empty
local stamina = Open77.stats.getStamina()
sprintIcon.enabled = stamina and stamina.value > 0

name: health
summary: Alias of `Open77.stats.getHealth`.
description: Reads the replicated server-owned health pool. This alias has exactly the same permission, optional player id and return shape as `getHealth`.
example:
-- Short spelling: another player's health on the scoreboard
local hp = Open77.stats.health(playerId)
if hp then print(("%d %%"):format(hp.percentage)) end

name: stamina
summary: Alias of `Open77.stats.getStamina`.
description: Reads the replicated server-owned stamina pool. This alias has exactly the same permission, optional player id and return shape as `getStamina`.
example:
-- Short spelling: is the player too tired to climb?
local stamina = Open77.stats.stamina()
if stamina and stamina.fraction < 0.1 then Open77.hud.notify("Too tired to climb") end

name: monotonic
summary: Monotonic clock, in seconds.
description: Never goes backwards, unlike wall-clock time: this is the one to measure a duration with. Multiply by 1000 only when an API explicitly expects milliseconds.
example:
-- Measure how long the menu stayed open
local openedAt = Open77.time.monotonic()
AddEventHandler("menu:closed", function()
    print(("menu open for %.1f s"):format(Open77.time.monotonic() - openedAt))
end)

name: beginSettle
summary: Raw half of teleportAndSettle: issues the teleport and returns a settle ticket.
description: Requires `player.travel`. Prefer `Open77.travel.teleportAndSettle`, which wraps this and `settleStatus` in a promise. `timeoutMs` is clamped to 1000..30000, default 12000.
example:
-- The raw form: teleport, then poll the ticket yourself
local ticket = Open77.travel.beginSettle(-1442.2, 127.4, 18.0, 90.0)
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        local status = Open77.travel.settleStatus(ticket)
        if not status or status.state ~= "pending" then print("settle:", status and status.state); break end
        Wait(100)
    end
end)

name: cancelSettle
summary: Stops the live settle session.
description: Requires `player.travel`. The body stays wherever it is; only the watch stops, and its promise rejects with `settle_cancelled`.
example:
-- The player pressed ESC during the fade: stop watching the move
Open77.travel.cancelSettle(ticket)

name: isMapPick
summary: Whether the world-map double-click travel gesture is armed.
description: Returns whether this client has the world-map double-click travel gesture armed. It requires `player.travel` and reports false when the permission or native bridge is unavailable. This is only local input state: it neither teleports the player nor bypasses the ACL check performed by the server command that consumes a picked point.
example:
-- Show the "double-click the map to travel" hint only while the gesture is armed
if Open77.travel.isMapPick() then
    Open77.hud.notify("Double-click the map to travel there")
end

name: isNoclip
summary: Whether local-player noclip is currently active.
description: Returns false without `player.travel` or when the backend is unavailable.
example:
-- Hide the speedometer while flying around in noclip
SetTick(function()
    speedometer.visible = not Open77.travel.isNoclip()
end)

name: setMapPick
summary: Arms or disarms the world-map double-click travel gesture.
description: Requires `player.travel`. This only lets the local map publish a picked world point; it moves nobody and does not bypass the ACL-checked server command that consumes the point.
example:
-- An admin resource arms map-pick travel when the server says the player may
RegisterNetEvent("admin:mapTravel", function(allowed)
    Open77.travel.setMapPick(allowed)
end)

name: setNoclip
summary: Enables or disables native noclip for the local player.
description: Requires `player.travel`. Multiplayer deployments should expose this only behind an ACL-checked server command.
example:
-- Toggle noclip, only after the server approved the admin command
RegisterNetEvent("admin:noclip", function(enabled)
    Open77.travel.setNoclip(enabled)
    Open77.hud.notify(enabled and "Noclip on" or "Noclip off")
end)

name: setNoclipSpeed
summary: Sets the local noclip movement speed.
description: Requires `player.travel`; the value must be finite and is validated by the native backend.
example:
-- Faster noclip while SHIFT is held
SetTick(function()
    if Open77.travel.isNoclip() then
        Open77.travel.setNoclipSpeed(Open77.input.isDown("SHIFT") and 40 or 10)
    end
end)

name: settleStatus
summary: Reads the state of a settle ticket.
description: Requires `player.travel`. Returns `{ state, reason, x, y, z, attempts, pins, elapsedMs }` where `state` is `pending`, `settled`, `near`, `failed` or `idle`; `nil, unknown_settle_ticket` for a ticket that is neither the live session nor the last one to finish.
example:
-- Is the body really standing at the destination yet?
local status = Open77.travel.settleStatus(ticket)
if status and status.state == "settled" then Open77.hud.notify("Arrived") end

name: teleport
summary: Teleports the local player directly to a world transform.
description: Requires `player.travel`. One queued engine request: it returns before the body has moved and knows nothing about streaming, so a destination whose floor is not resident yet drops the player through it and the engine's fall-under-world failsafe silently returns them to the save's spawn. Use `Open77.travel.teleportAndSettle` for a move that has to be believed, or `Open77.players.teleport` when the server decides. The server respawn transaction is NOT a general move: it refuses unless the player is already dead.
example:
-- A quick local move to the garage (no confirmation that the floor was loaded)
RegisterCommand("garage", function()
    Open77.travel.teleport(-1442.2, 127.4, 18.0, 90.0)
end, false)

name: teleportAndSettle
summary: Teleports the local player and resolves when the body is really standing there.
description: Requires `player.travel`. Returns a Promise, or `nil, reason` when the teleport itself was refused. Resolves with `{ state, x, y, z, attempts, pins, elapsedMs }`, where `state` is `settled` (grounded on the point for three consecutive frames) or `near` (on the point but never reported grounded inside the 1.5 s window -- a mark on a prop, or a very slow stream-in). Rejects with `settle_timeout`, `settle_superseded`, `settle_cancelled`, or the reason the teleport refused. There is no streaming query anywhere in the engine surface, so this is the empirical answer: while the body sinks through a floor that has not streamed in, the teleport is re-issued every 250 ms, which resets the fall before the engine's own fall-under-world failsafe can drag the player to the save's spawn. One local player means one session, so a second call supersedes the first.
example:
-- Move to the garage and only then show the menu
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, reason = Open77.travel.teleportAndSettle({ x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.0 }, 90.0)
    if not pending then return Open77.hud.notify("Teleport refused: " .. reason) end
    local landed, err = pending:await()
    if landed then openGarageMenu() else Open77.hud.notify("Could not settle: " .. err) end
end)

name: adoptable
summary: Every engine-spawned vehicle near the player that the server does not own.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. This is the only read on either side that can see a car REDengine spawned: `Open77.vehicles.get`, `nearby`, `closest` and `aimed` all answer from the replicated registry, which is why `aimed()` reports `unknown_entity` when the player is plainly looking at a traffic car. Options are `radius` (default 25, at most 200) and `limit` (default 8, at most 32); a bare number is read as the radius. Nearest first. Each entry carries `engineEntity` (a fixed `0x` string, because a REDengine entity hash does not survive a Lua number), `record`, `recordId`, `adoptable`, `position`, `orientation`, `distance`, `speed`, `speedKph`, `health`, `engineOn`, `locked`, `destroyed`, `doors`, `windows`, `tires`, `brokenGlass`, `brokenLights` and `detachedParts` -- everything the server's `Open77.vehicles.adopt` reads, spelled the same, so an entry can be handed over untouched. `adoptable` is false, and `record` empty, when the car's TweakDBID is not in the shipped reverse table: a shipping build keeps no id-to-name table and `gamedataVehicle_Record` has no `Name` accessor, so the 1376 known 2.31 records are carried and anything else reports its raw id and nothing more. `world_query_layout_unknown` means the targeting part layout has not been proven yet this session -- a precondition shared with the interaction prompts, and reported rather than answered with an empty list, because "the query cannot run" and "there is no car here" need opposite fixes.
example:
-- Car theft: propose the nearest street car to the server when the key is pressed
RegisterKeyMapping("steal_car", "Steal the nearest car", "G", function()
    local cars = Open77.vehicles.adoptable({ radius = 6, limit = 1 })
    if not cars or not cars[1] then return Open77.hud.notify("No car close enough") end
    TriggerServerEvent("garage:adopt", cars[1])
end)

name: aimed
summary: The replicated vehicle the local player is looking at.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. One `gametargetingTargetingSystem.GetLookAtObject` probe, right now, mapped through the replica table -- not the permanent inspector ray, which answers nothing unless some resource turned it on. Returns the full vehicle snapshot. `unknown_entity` is the interesting failure and it is COMMON: the player really is looking at a car, and that car is vanilla traffic no server resource created. It does not mean 'nothing is there'.
example:
-- Show the id of the server vehicle the player is looking at
RegisterKeyMapping("inspect_car", "Inspect vehicle", "K", function()
    local car, reason = Open77.vehicles.aimed()
    if not car then return Open77.hud.notify(reason == "unknown_entity" and "That is vanilla traffic" or "Look at a vehicle") end
    Open77.hud.notify(("Vehicle #%d %s"):format(car.id, car.record))
end)

name: all
summary: Lists every vehicle currently streamed to this client.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Returns an empty array when permission or the projection backend is unavailable. Every entry has the exact shape returned by `Open77.vehicles.get`; server vehicles outside the client's streaming interest set are intentionally absent.
example:
-- Draw a blip on every server vehicle streamed to this client
for _, car in ipairs(Open77.vehicles.all()) do
    Open77.blips.create({ position = car.position, label = car.record })
end

name: clearAllPerformance
summary: Drops every performance ceiling, instance and record class alike.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. Intended for a gamemode teardown so a stopped resource cannot leave cars governed.
example:
-- The race resource stops: no car stays governed
AddEventHandler("onClientResourceStop", function(name)
    if name == GetCurrentResourceName() then Open77.vehicles.clearAllPerformance() end
end)

name: clearPerformance
summary: Removes one vehicle's performance ceiling.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. The vehicle falls back to its record class profile, then the default, then to untouched native behaviour.
example:
-- The player left the slow zone: lift the cap on their car
AddEventHandler("slowzone:left", function()
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
    if seat then Open77.vehicles.clearPerformance(seat.vehicleId) end
end)

name: clearPerformanceClass
summary: Removes a TweakDB record's performance ceiling.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. Vehicles of that record fall back to the default profile, then to untouched native behaviour.
example:
-- Rebalance: the Quadra is no longer capped
Open77.vehicles.clearPerformanceClass("Vehicle.v_sport2_quadra_turbo_r")

name: closest
summary: The nearest replicated vehicle.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. A bare number is the radius, which is the spelling almost every caller wants; the table form takes the same options as `nearby` plus `radius`, and without one the search is unbounded. `no_vehicle_in_range` is a real answer, not an error. **Only server-spawned vehicles are in the registry.** A player standing next to a vanilla traffic car is standing next to something REDengine population spawned on their own client: it has no canonical id and this call cannot see it. Adopting vanilla traffic is a separate capability that does not exist yet. This is the call an RP resource reaches for first, so read that paragraph twice: `closest()` answering a car forty metres away while the player leans on a taxi is the expected behaviour, not a bug.
returns: reason: permission_denied:vehicles.read, invalid_radius, no_vehicle_in_range, no_session, no_local_position
example:
-- Press E near a server vehicle to ask the server to unlock it
RegisterKeyMapping("unlock_car", "Unlock nearby car", "E", function()
    local car, reason = Open77.vehicles.closest(5.0)
    if not car then return end -- no_vehicle_in_range is a normal answer
    TriggerServerEvent("keys:unlock", car.id)
end)

name: describeAdoptable
summary: The same description for one named engine-spawned chassis.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Takes the `engineEntity` string an `adoptable()` entry carries (a plain integer id also works). `already_managed` means the server already owns that car and it is not a candidate; `vehicle_not_found` means it is not within eighty metres of the player, which is as far as this read looks.
example:
-- Re-describe one chassis right before proposing it, so the position is fresh
local description, reason = Open77.vehicles.describeAdoptable(engineEntity)
if description then TriggerServerEvent("garage:adopt", description) end

name: fromEntity
summary: The replicated vehicle wearing an entity id.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Accepts either id a vehicle carries: the Open77 `entity` (what `Open77.players.entity` and a raycast hand back) or the REDengine `engineEntity`. Returns the full snapshot, so `fromEntity(entity).id` is the round trip from a world query to a canonical vehicle id.
example:
-- Turn a raycast hit into a canonical vehicle id
local hit = Open77.world.raycast(from, to, { entities = true })
if hit and hit.entity and hit.entity.kind == "vehicle" then
    local car = Open77.vehicles.fromEntity(hit.entity.engineEntity)
    if car then print("looking at vehicle", car.id) end
end

name: get
summary: Reads one streamed server-owned vehicle.
description: Client read-only API requiring `vehicles.read`. The snapshot contains durable state (`health`, flags, the derived `locked` boolean, six door bits, four open-window bits, tyre/glass/light masks, detached panels and the 30-cell body grid), authority and occupants including durable seat-policy flags, an ephemeral generation-checked local entity handle, plus the replicated transform and the latest drivetrain and wheel telemetry. The transform is `position` (a plain `{ x, y, z }`, which is what an Open77 vector3 is), `orientation` as `{ x, y, z, w }`, and `heading`/`yaw` -- one value under both names, in degrees, extracted from the full quaternion so a car on a slope reports the heading it is actually facing, and matching the server vehicle read exactly. Both come from the latest replicated motion when one exists and from the canonical create otherwise, so a proximity query answers for a car whose REDengine projection has not attached yet. `speed` is metres per second, the unit every Open77 read uses, and `speedKph` is the same number converted once because performance ceilings and speed limits are authored in km/h. Open windows and broken glass are separate states. Creation, repair, authoritative seat assignment and arbitrary mutation are server-only; the complete server surface is documented in `wiki/vehicles.md`.
returns: table { id, record, entity, engineEntity, revision, physicsOwner, authorityEpoch, flags, locked, health, position, orientation, heading, yaw, doors, windows, tires, bodyDamage, brokenGlass, brokenLights, detachedParts, damage, speed, speedKph, rpm, rpmMax, throttle, brake, steering, wheelRotation, suspensionLongitudinal, suspensionTransversal, burnout, gear, onGround, reversing, streamed, locallyOwned, occupants }, or nil
example:
-- A dashboard: speed and health of the car the player is driving
SetTick(function()
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
    if not seat then return end
    local car = Open77.vehicles.get(seat.vehicleId)
    if car then dashboard.set(car.speedKph, car.health) end
end)

name: getActiveWeapons
summary: Lists the attached weapons selected by the driver.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Uses captured selection for the local driver and replicated selection for observers. Unknown selection returns nil, weapon_state_unavailable; a known empty selection returns an empty table.
returns: Array of weapon tables, or nil, reason
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local weapons, reason = Open77.vehicles.getActiveWeapons(seat.vehicleId)
if not weapons then print(reason); return end
for _, weapon in ipairs(weapons) do
    print("Selected mount", weapon.index, weapon.type)
end
-- An empty array means known selection with no active attached weapons.

name: getPaint
summary: Reads replicated authoritative paint for one streamed vehicle.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Returns the separate `applied` flag plus primary and secondary keyed RGB tables. It returns `nil` while the vehicle is unknown or not streamed; the value is read-only on the client.
returns: table { applied, primary, secondary }, or nil
example:
local paint = Open77.vehicles.getPaint(vehicleId)
if paint and paint.applied then print(paint.primary.r, paint.primary.g, paint.primary.b) end

name: getPlayerSeat
summary: Reads a replicated player's canonical vehicle-seat assignment.
description: Client read-only API requiring `vehicles.read`. Omitting `playerId` selects the local player. The result includes `playerId`, `vehicleId`, canonical `seat`, numeric `flags`, `entering`, `exiting`, `forcedEntry`, `exitLocked`, `forcedExit`, plus the current local projection's `streamed` state and ephemeral `entity` handle. It returns nil when no assignment is currently replicated.
example:
-- Is the local player driving right now?
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if seat and seat.seat == "seat_front_left" then
    Open77.hud.notify("You are the driver")
end

name: getWeapon
summary: Reads one weapon mount by its stable one-based index.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. The index comes from weapon.index, not weaponId or slotId. An unattached declared mount is returned with attached=false; invalid indices are rejected.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local weapons = Open77.vehicles.getWeapons(seat.vehicleId)
if not weapons or not weapons[1] then return end
local weapon, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeapon(seat.vehicleId, weapons[1].index)
if not weapon then print(reason); return end
print(weapon.index, weapon.attached, weapon.active)

name: getWeaponAim
summary: Reads the Basilisk's captured or replicated turret inputs.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Returns yaw, pitch and source. These are graph angles in degrees relative to the chassis, not a world aim ray. Other models or unavailable state return nil, weapon_aim_unavailable.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local aim, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeaponAim(seat.vehicleId)
if not aim then print(reason); return end
print(aim.yaw, aim.pitch, aim.source) -- degrees relative to the chassis

name: getWeaponAmmo
summary: Reads available native ammunition counters for a mounted weapon.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Returns available, source, optional magazine/capacity/total/reserve. Ammunition is native-local-driver only; observer counters are not replicated and are omitted, never invented as zero. Counters do not establish whether a mounted weapon has infinite ammo or can fire.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local weapons = Open77.vehicles.getWeapons(seat.vehicleId)
if not weapons or not weapons[1] then return end
local ammo, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeaponAmmo(seat.vehicleId, weapons[1].index)
if not ammo then print(reason); return end
if ammo.available and ammo.magazine ~= nil then
    print(ammo.magazine, ammo.capacity)
else
    print("--", ammo.source) -- e.g. not_replicated for a passenger
end

name: getWeaponCount
summary: Counts weapon objects attached to a streamed vehicle.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Returns actual attached count, not declaredCount or activeCount. Zero means a known streamed vehicle with no resolved weapon objects.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local count, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeaponCount(seat.vehicleId)
if count == nil then print(reason); return end
print("Attached weapons:", count) -- zero is valid

name: getWeaponModel
summary: Reads the weapon mounts declared by a vehicle model.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. This is a TweakDB declaration, not proof that all weapons are attached in an appearance. Returns record, hasWeaponMounts, declaredCount and mounts.
example:
local model, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeaponModel("Vehicle.v_militech_basilisk")
if not model then print(reason); return end
print(model.record, model.declaredCount)
for _, mount in ipairs(model.mounts) do
    print(mount.index, mount.record, mount.slot, mount.type)
end

name: getWeaponState
summary: Reads one coherent mounted-weapon snapshot.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Uses a canonical network vehicle ID. Includes declared mounts, attached/active counts, selection mask, local-driver flag and available native ammo/heat. Local reads are cached for at most 100 ms.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if seat then
    local state, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeaponState(seat.vehicleId)
    if state then print(state.attachedCount, state.activeCount) end
end

name: getWeaponType
summary: Reads a mounted weapon's stable category.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Categories: machine_gun, cannon, missile, countermeasure, unknown. Native itemType, when available, is a separate field in getWeapon.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local weapons = Open77.vehicles.getWeapons(seat.vehicleId)
if not weapons or not weapons[1] then return end
local category, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeaponType(seat.vehicleId, weapons[1].index)
if not category then print(reason); return end
print(category) -- machine_gun, cannon, missile, countermeasure or unknown

name: getWeapons
summary: Lists the weapon objects actually attached to a streamed vehicle.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. The returned array is dense but each weapon.index preserves its one-based position in the model mount list. Do not use the array position as the mount index.
returns: Array of weapon tables, or nil, reason
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local weapons, reason = Open77.vehicles.getWeapons(seat.vehicleId)
if not weapons then print(reason); return end
for _, weapon in ipairs(weapons) do
    print(weapon.index, weapon.type, weapon.slot)
end

name: honk
summary: Alias of `Open77.vehicles.triggerHorn`.
description: Requires `vehicles.control` and local physics ownership. Duration is bounded to 100..2000 ms and defaults to 250 ms.
example:
-- Honk the car the player is simulating
RegisterKeyMapping("horn", "Horn", "H", function()
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
    if seat then Open77.vehicles.honk(seat.vehicleId, 400) end
end)

name: isArmed
summary: Checks whether a streamed vehicle actually has attached weapons.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Counts resolved weapon objects, not the model's inherited mount declarations. An unstreamed vehicle returns nil, vehicle_not_streamed.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local armed, reason = Open77.vehicles.isArmed(seat.vehicleId)
if armed == nil then print(reason); return end
print(armed and "Attached weapons found" or "No attached weapons")

name: isDoorOpen
summary: Reads a canonical vehicle door, trunk, or hood state.
description: Client read-only API requiring `vehicles.read`. Accepts index 0..5, a standard camelCase/snake_case name, or a `Open77.vehicles.doors` constant. This reads the replicated reversible opening mask.
returns: boolean, or nil when denied, unavailable, or unknown
example:
-- Warn the driver when the trunk is open while moving
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if seat and Open77.vehicles.isDoorOpen(seat.vehicleId, "trunk") then
    Open77.hud.notify("Trunk is open")
end

name: isLocked
summary: Reads a vehicle's replicated entry-lock state.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Returns the durable server-authoritative lock for a streamed vehicle. This is the vehicle entry lock, not the per-occupant exit lock and not the client-side grid control lock.
returns: boolean, or nil when the vehicle is unknown
example:
-- Show a lock icon on the nearest car
local car = Open77.vehicles.closest(5.0)
if car then
    Open77.hud.notify(Open77.vehicles.isLocked(car.id) and "Locked" or "Unlocked", { replace = true })
end

name: isPlayerExitLocked
summary: Reports the replicated exit-lock policy for a player.
description: Client read-only API requiring `vehicles.read`. Omitting `playerId` selects the local player. Returns nil when the player has no replicated seat assignment; otherwise returns the canonical `exitLocked` boolean.
example:
-- Tell the player why F does nothing
if Open77.vehicles.isPlayerExitLocked() then
    Open77.hud.notify("You cannot leave this vehicle")
end

name: isWeaponActive
summary: Checks whether the driver selected a particular attached mount.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. Selection is not a firing event or a guarantee of native mesh deployment. Unknown selection is an explicit error.
example:
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if not seat then return end
local weapons = Open77.vehicles.getWeapons(seat.vehicleId)
if not weapons or not weapons[1] then return end
local active, reason = Open77.vehicles.isWeaponActive(seat.vehicleId, weapons[1].index)
if active == nil then print(reason); return end
print(active and "Selected" or "Not selected") -- not a firing flag

name: isWindowOpen
summary: Reads a canonical openable side-window state.
description: Client read-only API requiring `vehicles.read`. Windows use indexes 0..3 and names `frontLeft`, `frontRight`, `backLeft`, and `backRight`. This does not report shattered glass; inspect `brokenGlass` or `damage.glass` in the vehicle snapshot for that.
returns: boolean, or nil when denied, unavailable, or unknown
example:
-- Rain sound is louder with the driver's window open
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if seat and Open77.vehicles.isWindowOpen(seat.vehicleId, "frontLeft") then
    SetSoundVolume(rainLoop, 1.0)
end

name: modelHasWeaponMounts
summary: Checks whether a vehicle model declares any weapon mounts.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Client-side, synchronous and read-only. A valid unarmed model returns false; an unknown model returns nil. Inherited mounts do not guarantee a usable armed vehicle.
example:
local declared, reason = Open77.vehicles.modelHasWeaponMounts("Vehicle.v_militech_basilisk")
if declared == nil then print(reason); return end
print(declared and "Model declares mounts" or "No declared mounts")
-- Declarations alone do not prove weapons are attached to a live vehicle.

name: nearby
summary: Every replicated vehicle within a radius, nearest first.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Centred on the local player unless `origin` is given. `streamed = true` keeps only the ones with a REDengine projection, `occupied` filters on whether anyone is aboard, `limit` caps the list. Ties are broken by vehicle id so the order does not flicker between frames. Each entry is `{ id, entity, engineEntity, record, distance, streamed, locked, occupants, position }`, and `position` is a plain `{ x, y, z }` -- which is what an Open77 vector3 is, so `#(a.position - b.position)` works on it without a conversion. **Only server-spawned vehicles are in the registry.** A player standing next to a vanilla traffic car is standing next to something REDengine population spawned on their own client: it has no canonical id and this call cannot see it. Adopting vanilla traffic is a separate capability that does not exist yet.
returns: reason: permission_denied:vehicles.read, invalid_radius, invalid_origin, invalid_limit, no_session, no_local_position
example:
-- List the server vehicles within 30 m, nearest first
for _, car in ipairs(Open77.vehicles.nearby(30, { limit = 5 })) do
    print(("#%d %s at %.1f m, %d aboard"):format(car.id, car.record, car.distance, car.occupants))
end

name: occupantInSeat
summary: Which player is in one seat of a replicated vehicle.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. The `GetPedInVehicleSeat` of FiveM, answering an Open77 player id. A plain `nil` means the seat is free; a `nil` with a reason means the question could not be answered.
example:
-- Who is sitting next to the driver?
local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
if seat then
    local passenger = Open77.vehicles.occupantInSeat(seat.vehicleId, "frontPassenger")
    if passenger then print("passenger is player", passenger) end
end

name: ratedTopSpeed
summary: Gearing rating of a vehicle's TweakDB record, in km/h.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Returns the speed at which the record's top gear reaches its rated maximum engine RPM, reached through `vehEngineData`. Use it to rank a roster and to pick a ceiling no car has to be slowed much to meet. It is **not** the measured terminal velocity, which torque and aerodynamic drag carry higher. Returns `nil` when the record cannot be resolved.
example:
-- Pick a fair race cap: 10 km/h under the slowest car in the roster
local cap = math.huge
for _, record in ipairs(roster) do
    cap = math.min(cap, Open77.vehicles.ratedTopSpeed(record) or cap)
end
Open77.vehicles.setPerformanceClass(roster[1], { topSpeedKph = cap - 10 })

name: releaseAdopted
summary: Hands one engine-spawned chassis back to the population system.
description: Requires `vehicles.adopt`, which is its own permission because this deletes something from the local world rather than reading it. It is the second half of adoption and must run ONLY after the server has accepted the proposal: the canonical vehicle replaces this car, and removing it first deletes a traffic car for nothing.
