Removal goes through `gameIPopulationSystem::RemoveEntity`, the asynchronous teardown path the world sanitizer already runs every second in production -- never `entEntity.Dispose` or any of the lifecycle functions the debug bridge blocks, which tear an object down while save and AI systems still hold references. `not_offered` means this chassis was not returned by an `adoptable()` or `describeAdoptable()` call in the last minute: an engine entity id is just a number, so being offered is the capability, and without that rule a resource could name an NPC or a door. `managed_vehicle` refuses a car the server owns, `player_mounted` refuses the one the player is sitting in, and a chassis the engine already removed answers true, because the caller wanted it gone and it is.
example:
-- The server accepted the proposal: hand the vanilla chassis back
RegisterNetEvent("garage:adopted", function(engineEntity, vehicleId)
    Open77.vehicles.releaseAdopted(engineEntity)
    Open77.hud.notify(("Vehicle #%d is yours"):format(vehicleId))
end)

name: seatFree
summary: Whether one seat of a replicated vehicle is free.
description: Requires `vehicles.read`. Read from the replicated occupancy ledger, so it agrees with the server's own answer rather than with the local projection. An occupant whose entry animation is still running counts as present: the seat is reserved and a second entry into it is refused.
example:
-- Only offer the "enter as passenger" prompt when the seat is free
local car = Open77.vehicles.closest(4.0)
if car and Open77.vehicles.seatFree(car.id, "frontPassenger") then
    Open77.hud.notify("Press E to get in", { replace = true })
end

name: setControlLock
summary: Locks or releases a stopped vehicle's driving inputs.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. While locked, the native drive update consumes zero acceleration, zero brake/reverse and no burnout. Releasing restores REDengine's current input snapshot on the next frame; the API never teleports or clamps velocity. Use it for authoritative starting grids after the vehicle is stationary. Like the performance governor, this is client-side gamemode enforcement, not an anti-cheat boundary.
example:
-- Starting grid: freeze the inputs, then release them on GO
RegisterNetEvent("race:grid", function(vehicleId)
    Open77.vehicles.setControlLock(vehicleId, true)
end)
RegisterNetEvent("race:go", function(vehicleId)
    Open77.vehicles.setControlLock(vehicleId, false)
end)

name: setFrozen
summary: Freezes or wakes a vehicle's native chassis physics.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. Disables the verified REDengine vehicle physics group without changing the authority lease, player-controlled state or mounted workspot. Unlike `setControlLock`, this stops inertia, gravity and external impulses without teleporting the vehicle. Releasing restores the mask and calls the native physics wake-up path. Pair both calls for a starting grid: lock inputs then freeze; on GO thaw then unlock inputs. Unknown or not-yet-streamed vehicles fail so the resource can retry.
example:
-- Starting grid: lock the inputs and freeze the chassis until GO
RegisterNetEvent("race:grid", function(vehicleId)
    Open77.vehicles.setControlLock(vehicleId, true)
    Open77.vehicles.setFrozen(vehicleId, true)
end)
RegisterNetEvent("race:go", function(vehicleId)
    Open77.vehicles.setFrozen(vehicleId, false)
    Open77.vehicles.setControlLock(vehicleId, false)
end)

name: setPerformance
summary: Caps one vehicle's top speed and pickup on this client.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. Cyberpunk 2077 2.31 has no speed setter, so the ceiling is applied by withdrawing driver throttle where the drive update reads it, tapered across a band so the top of the acceleration curve flattens instead of hitting a wall. The profile table takes `topSpeedKph` (0 leaves the top end alone), `taperKph` (default 12, values under 3 are refused because a narrower band makes the limiter hunt) and `accelerationScale` in (0, 1]. Precedence is instance, then record class, then default. **This is balance, not anti-cheat**: the client that simulates the vehicle applies it, and a modified client can decline to. Cleared automatically on despawn. This is the client-local form and it still works unchanged; the server-authoritative form is `Open77.vehicles.setPerformance` on the server, which takes the same three numbers, replicates them to every viewer and does not need the client to cooperate in deciding them. The two are separate policies over the same native governor, which resolves instance, then record class, then default -- so a client-local instance profile on the same vehicle takes precedence over the replicated one.
example:
-- A 60 km/h limit inside the city centre, applied to the car the player drives
AddEventHandler("citycentre:entered", function()
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat()
    if seat then Open77.vehicles.setPerformance(seat.vehicleId, { topSpeedKph = 60, taperKph = 10 }) end
end)

name: setPerformanceClass
summary: Caps every present and future vehicle spawned from one TweakDB record.
description: Requires `vehicles.performance`. This is the shape a roster wants: name the cars offered and the ceiling they share once, rather than tracking instances. Same profile table as `setPerformance`. A record class is overridden by an explicit per-instance profile.

name: taskPlayerEnterVehicle
summary: Presents an authorized replicated occupant with the staged entry path.
description: Requires `vehicles.presentation` and an already-authorized occupancy tuple. Uses the guarded door/workspot presentation for a live remote entry and retains a bounded instant-warp fallback. This is presentation only and never grants a seat or changes physics authority.
example:
-- Play the door animation for a remote player whose seat the server already granted
RegisterNetEvent("garage:showEntry", function(playerId, vehicleId, seat)
    Open77.vehicles.taskPlayerEnterVehicle(playerId, vehicleId, seat)
end)

name: triggerHorn
summary: Sounds the horn of a locally simulated vehicle.
description: Requires `vehicles.control`. The vehicle must be streamed and this client must be its current physics owner. Duration is bounded to 100..2000 ms. For an arbitrary vehicle, call the authoritative server API so it can route the request to the current owner.
example:
-- Double honk from the car this client simulates
CreateThread(function()
    Open77.vehicles.triggerHorn(vehicleId, 200)
    Wait(400)
    Open77.vehicles.triggerHorn(vehicleId, 200)
end)

name: warpPlayerIntoVehicle
summary: Presents a replicated player instantly in an authoritative vehicle seat.
description: Requires `vehicles.presentation`. This is the client meaning of the name: a guarded visual operation for an existing server-owned vehicle and occupancy assignment. It does not claim the seat or physics authority. The exact `(player, vehicle, seat)` tuple must already exist in the replicated ledger or the call fails with `occupancy_mismatch`. The server runtime exposes an identically named authoritative assignment API; the two Lua states are distinct.
example:
-- Instantly show a remote occupant in the seat the server assigned
RegisterNetEvent("garage:showWarp", function(playerId, vehicleId, seat)
    Open77.vehicles.warpPlayerIntoVehicle(playerId, vehicleId, seat)
end)

name: attach
summary: Attach an owned world effect to a local native body slot.
description: Requires world.effects. effectId and entity are local handles; slot is a nonempty native slot name up to128 bytes. anchor defaults to body; weaponRight uses the supported equipped weapon anchor. Missing body/slot/weapon is a refusal, not permission to bind an unrelated target. True is native attachment acceptance, not visual proof.
example:
local entity, err = Open77.vfx.resolveTarget({kind="player",id=tostring(playerId)})
if not entity then print(err); return end
local ok, reason = Open77.vfx.attach(effectId, entity, "RightHand", "body")
if not ok then print(reason) end

name: catalog
summary: Returns the curated stable world-VFX aliases and cooked paths.
description: Catalog access does not start an effect. Raw cooked paths remain build-dependent even when present.
returns: table mapping alias to effect path, or nil
example:
-- Print every alias this client can play
for alias, path in pairs(Open77.vfx.catalog() or {}) do print(alias, path) end

name: clear
summary: Stops every VFX owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`; SFX and other resource owners are unaffected.
example:
-- The fireworks show is over
AddEventHandler("fireworks:ended", function()
    Open77.vfx.clear()
end)

name: list
summary: Lists active VFX owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`.
returns: array of { id, kind, name, entity, remaining }, or nil
example:
-- Debug: which effects does this resource still own?
for _, fx in ipairs(Open77.vfx.list() or {}) do print(fx.id, fx.name, fx.remaining) end

name: play
summary: Starts a resource-owned world VFX at a fixed transform.
description: Requires `world.effects`. `options` requires `position` and accepts `orientation`, `duration`, and `ignoreTimeDilation`. The effect is released automatically with its owner.
example:
-- Local smoke at the campfire for 30 seconds
Open77.vfx.play("smoke.exterior", { position = { x = -1460.2, y = 99.9, z = 14.8 }, duration = 30 })

name: playEntity
summary: Starts a resource-owned authored VFX on an entity.
description: Requires `world.effects`. Options accept `entity`, `instance`, `persistOnDetach`, `breakAllLoops`, `breakAllOnDestroy`, and `duration`; omitting `entity` targets the local player.
example:
-- Sparks on the local player's body when a hack lands
RegisterNetEvent("hack:hit", function()
    Open77.vfx.playEntity("sparks.burst.small", { duration = 2 })
end)

name: resolveTarget
summary: Resolve a typed network target to its currently streamed local handle.
description: Requires world.effects. Accepts {kind="player"|"npc"|"vehicle"|"prop",id=decimalStringOrInteger}. Returns a decimal string local registry handle (local player resolves to1), or nil, reason such as target_not_streamed. Re-resolve after stream/body changes; never send this local handle over the network.
example:
local handle, err = Open77.vfx.resolveTarget({kind="player",id=tostring(playerId)})
if handle then print(handle) else print(err) end

name: screen
summary: Plays one of Cyberpunk's full-screen post-process effects on the local view.
description: Client-only; requires `vfx.screen`, which is deliberately NOT `world.effects` -- covering somebody's eyes is a different power from putting smoke in a street. `name` must be an alias from `Open77.vfx.screenCatalog()`; anything else, including the engine's own effect name, is refused with `unsupported_screen_effect` and never forwarded, because an unknown authored effect name is a SILENT no-op in the engine. `options.strength` (0..1, default 1.0) picks among the tiers the game authored for the `drunk`, `drugged` and `health` families and is ignored by single-tier aliases: 2.31 has no continuous amount channel. `options.duration` is seconds, 0..600; 0 holds until stopped. The handle is an ordinary effect handle -- `Open77.vfx.stop`, `list` and `clear` all work on it. See the Effects guide.
example:
-- The player drank too much: medium drunk wobble for 30 seconds
Open77.vfx.screen("drunk", { strength = 0.5, duration = 30 })

name: screenCatalog
summary: The curated screen-effect aliases and the engine effect name behind each.
description: Client-only and ungated, like `Open77.vfx.catalog`: knowing the vocabulary is not the power, playing it is. Returns `{ [alias] = engineEffectName }`. Tiered families appear as their tiers (`drunk.light`, `drunk.medium`, `drunk.heavy`), never as the bare family name -- the family is an input convenience for `strength`, the tiers are what exists. See the Effects guide.
returns: table of alias to engine effect name
example:
-- Check an alias before using it
local aliases = Open77.vfx.screenCatalog()
if aliases["drunk.heavy"] then print("heavy drunk available") end

name: setParameter
summary: Set a scalar parameter on an owned native world effect.
description: Requires world.effects. Parameter name is nonempty, at most128 bytes and contains no NUL; value must be finite. The native graph must actually expose the requested parameter. Acceptance does not guarantee visible change and does not modify authoritative gameplay.
example:
-- Only use a parameter authored by your chosen effect graph.
local ok, err = Open77.vfx.setParameter(effectId, parameterName, 0.5)
if not ok then print(err) end

name: stop
summary: Stops one VFX handle owned by the calling resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`.
example:
-- Stop the smoke when the fire is put out
local smoke = Open77.vfx.play("smoke.exterior", { position = campfire })
AddEventHandler("fire:extinguished", function() Open77.vfx.stop(smoke) end)

name: update
summary: Move an owned native world effect.
description: Requires world.effects. options.position is a finite{x,y,z}; optional orientation{x,y,z,w} must be a nonzero quaternion and is normalized. Updates an existing owned world effect, not the registry target or TTL; use server attached effects for replicated lifetime.
example:
local ok, err = Open77.vfx.update(effectId, {position={x=0,y=0,z=1}})
if not ok then print(err) end

name: devices
summary: Enumerates active native voice endpoints.
description: Requires `voice.client`. `flow` is `input`, `output`, or `all`; the empty endpoint id represents the current Windows communications default.
returns: array of { id, name, flow, default, selected, available }, or nil
example:
-- Fill the settings dropdown with the microphones this machine has
for _, device in ipairs(Open77.voice.devices("input") or {}) do
    print(device.id, device.name, device.selected and "(selected)" or "")
end

name: getLipSyncStatus
summary: Reads native mouth-presentation policy and tracked-player counts.
description: Requires voice.client. Fields: enabled, sessionActive, mode=audio_envelope, trackedPlayers, availablePlayers, activePlayers. Not phoneme recognition.
example:
local state, reason = Open77.voice.getLipSyncStatus()
if state then print(state.mode, state.activePlayers) else print(reason) end

name: getPlayerLipSyncState
summary: Reads a player's current facial binding and smoothed voice envelope.
description: Requires voice.client. Fields: playerId, entity, isLocal, enabled, available, active, level (0..1), reason. Unstreamed/custom unsupported heads report unavailable without changing the body animation.
example:
local state, reason = Open77.voice.getPlayerLipSyncState(42)
if state then print(state.available, state.level, state.reason) else print(reason) end

name: selectDevice
summary: Selects a microphone or voice output endpoint.
description: Requires `voice.client`. `flow` is `input` or `output`; an empty id follows the Windows communications default.
example:
-- The player picked a microphone in the settings page
RegisterNetEvent("settings:microphone", function(endpointId)
    Open77.voice.selectDevice("input", endpointId)
end)

name: setCaptureEnabled
summary: Enables or disables native microphone capture.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Capture alone does not select recipients or bypass PTT/server policy.
example:
-- A "mute microphone" toggle key
local muted = false
RegisterKeyMapping("voice_mute", "Mute microphone", "M", function()
    muted = not muted
    Open77.voice.setCaptureEnabled(not muted)
    Open77.hud.notify(muted and "Microphone muted" or "Microphone on")
end)

name: setChannelVolume
summary: Sets local gain for a voice route/channel.
description: Requires `voice.client`. The native engine retains it for current and future streams using that route id.
example:
-- Turn the radio channel down while driving
Open77.voice.setChannelVolume("ncpd_dispatch", 0.5)

name: setInputVolume
summary: Sets microphone gain.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Gain is clamped before the native capture frame is metered and encoded; the pause package persists it per server.
example:
-- A microphone gain slider (0..2)
RegisterNetEvent("settings:micGain", function(gain)
    Open77.voice.setInputVolume(gain)
end)

name: setLipSyncEnabled
summary: Enables or suppresses local voice-driven mouth presentation.
description: Requires voice.client. False adds this resource's global suppression; true removes only its own suppression. Resource stop/reload/failure releases it. Does not mute audio. See the Voice lipsync guide for setup and client-build requirements.
example:
-- The helmet hides the face: no mouth animation while it is on
AddEventHandler("helmet:on", function() Open77.voice.setLipSyncEnabled(false) end)
AddEventHandler("helmet:off", function() Open77.voice.setLipSyncEnabled(true) end)

name: setMicrophoneTest
summary: Enables local microphone loopback.
description: Requires `voice.client`. This is a bounded local monitor and does not transmit by itself.
example:
-- The "test your microphone" button in the settings page
Open77.voice.setMicrophoneTest(true)
SetTimeout(5000, function() Open77.voice.setMicrophoneTest(false) end)

name: setOutputVolume
summary: Sets the global remote-voice gain.
description: Requires `voice.client`. This is local rendering policy and does not affect what any other listener hears.
example:
-- Halve everybody's voice during the cutscene
Open77.voice.setOutputVolume(0.5)
AddEventHandler("cutscene:ended", function() Open77.voice.setOutputVolume(1.0) end)

name: setPlayerBlocked
summary: Locally blocks or unblocks one remote talker.
description: This affects only local playback. Use the server mute/deaf APIs for authoritative policy.
example:
-- A local block from the scoreboard's "mute" button
RegisterNetEvent("scoreboard:blockVoice", function(playerId, blocked)
    Open77.voice.setPlayerBlocked(playerId, blocked)
end)

name: setPlayerLipSyncEnabled
summary: Enables or suppresses voice-driven lipsync for one network player.
description: Requires voice.client. Positive network player ID, not entity ID. True cannot override another resource's suppression or a global suppression. Per-player policies reset across sessions.
example:
local ok, reason = Open77.voice.setPlayerLipSyncEnabled(42, false)
if not ok then print(reason) end

name: setPlayerVolume
summary: Sets one remote player's local playback gain.
description: Requires `voice.client`. The preference is applied to the native jitter/render path only; it cannot change server reachability.
example:
-- Turn one loud player down locally
Open77.voice.setPlayerVolume(playerId, 0.4)

name: setProximityDistance
summary: Requests a personal proximity-voice reach.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Queues a reliable request only; the authenticated server clamps it to the advertised minimum/maximum and republishes the canonical value in `status().proximityDistance`. Proximity remains permanently enabled unless server policy disables it; this method cannot change enabled, mute, deaf, buckets, memberships, or recipients.
returns: true when queued or already canonical, otherwise false
example:
-- Whisper and shout keys change how far the player is heard
RegisterKeyMapping("voice_whisper", "Whisper", "PAGEDOWN", function() Open77.voice.setProximityDistance(3) end)
RegisterKeyMapping("voice_shout", "Shout", "PAGEUP", function() Open77.voice.setProximityDistance(40) end)

name: setTransmitting
summary: Sets PTT state and requested route intent.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Intent may be `proximity`, `channels`, `channel:<id>`, or `all`. `channels` selects up to four authorized speakable memberships and `all` adds proximity. The server still validates every recipient and membership.

name: setVoiceActivation
summary: Enables VAD and sets its normalized threshold.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Threshold `0` is most sensitive and `1` least sensitive. The native gate uses a short hangover, emits an explicit talkspurt end, and sends no silent talkspurt frames; held PTT may still use bounded Opus DTX.
example:
-- Voice activation instead of push-to-talk, medium sensitivity
Open77.voice.setVoiceActivation(true, 0.4)

name: status
summary: Returns one native voice capture/render snapshot.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Includes device ids, gains, input/output levels, PTT/VAD state, packet counters, active talker count, backend states, and the local canonical proximity reach. `proximityDistance` is server-confirmed; `requestedProximityDistance` and `proximityRequestPending` describe an in-flight request. The server-advertised default/minimum/maximum bounds are read-only. It never includes audio payloads.
example:
-- A microphone level meter on the HUD
SetTick(function()
    local voice = Open77.voice.status()
    if voice then micMeter.set(voice.inputLevel) end
end)

name: talkers
summary: Lists native remote-talker playback state.
description: Requires `voice.client`. Each entry contains player id, speaking/level state, local volume/block preference, and authorized active routes.
returns: array of talker snapshots, or nil
example:
-- Show a speaker icon over everyone who is talking
for _, talker in ipairs(Open77.voice.talkers() or {}) do
    if talker.speaking then showSpeakerIcon(talker.playerId) end
end

name: activate
summary: Activates a native outfit or returns to the worn set.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.edit. Returns true on accepted native mutation, or nil, reason; acceptance is not rendered completion. Pass an outfit index; false, nil or omitted disables the active outfit. Activation does not itself prove all garment visuals have settled.
example:
-- Switch to outfit slot 2 from the wardrobe menu
Open77.wardrobe.activate(2)

name: active
summary: Reads the active native outfit index.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Returns the outfit index or false when no outfit is active; false is not an error.
returns: index or false, or nil, reason
example:
-- Highlight the active outfit in the wardrobe menu
local index = Open77.wardrobe.active()
if index then print("wearing outfit", index) else print("no outfit active") end

name: outfit
summary: Returns slot operations bound to a native outfit index.
description: Client-only; requires player.equipment.read. Failures return nil, reason. Index must be an integer from 0 through 6. The result contains index and bound registry(), equip(record[, slot][, options]), unequip(slot), hide(slot) and apply(slots[, options]) functions; call them with dot syntax. registry requires read permission; mutations separately require player.equipment.edit. hide marks an outfit slot hidden, while unequip removes its override. apply false marks a hidden slot, and replace controls preservation of omitted overrides. Editing does not automatically activate the outfit.
example:
-- Edit outfit 1 without activating it
local outfit = Open77.wardrobe.outfit(1)
if outfit then
    outfit.equip("Items.Cap_01_basic_01", "Head")
    outfit.hide("Face")
end

name: activate
summary: Alias of `Open77.weapons.setActive`.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`; see `setActive` for template placement and asynchronous completion semantics.
example:
-- Draw slot 1 when the round starts
RegisterNetEvent("arena:roundStarted", function()
    Open77.weapons.activate(1)
end)

name: all
summary: Alias of `Open77.weapons.snapshot`.
description: Requires `player.weapons.read`; results arrive asynchronously as slot-state events followed by completion.
example:
-- Same as snapshot: ask for every slot's verified state
Open77.weapons.all()
AddEventHandler("open77:weapons:state", function(requestId, slot, record)
    print("slot", slot, record ~= "" and record or "empty")
end)

name: assign
summary: Assigns an exact TweakDB weapon template to a standard loadout slot.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`. `slot` is 1..3. Options are `active` (default false) and `addToInventory` (default true). The return value only confirms that the validated request was queued; listen for `open77:weapons:completed` for the state verified by REDscript.
example:
-- A pistol in slot 1, drawn immediately
local request, reason = Open77.weapons.assign("Items.Preset_Lexington_Default", 1, { active = true })
if not request then print("assign refused: " .. reason) end

name: holster
summary: Holsters the currently drawn right-hand weapon.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`. Loadout assignments and the selected equipment-area item are unchanged; completion reports whether the right-hand slot became empty.
example:
-- Entering the shop holsters the weapon
AddEventHandler("shop:entered", function()
    Open77.weapons.holster()
end)

name: remove
summary: Removes the weapon assigned to one standard slot.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`. This unequips the item but does not delete it from inventory. The empty slot is verified asynchronously.
example:
-- The round is over: empty slot 1
Open77.weapons.remove(1)

name: setActive
summary: Selects and draws a standard weapon by slot or TweakDB template.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`. A numeric target must already contain a weapon. A template target reuses an assigned instance or equips it first; options accept fallback `slot` 1..3 and `addToInventory` (default true). Completion is asynchronous through `open77:weapons:completed`.
example:
-- The 2 key draws whatever is in slot 2
RegisterKeyMapping("weapon_slot_2", "Weapon slot 2", "2", function()
    Open77.weapons.setActive(2)
end)

name: setAmmo
summary: Sets exact spare and/or loaded ammunition for a weapon slot.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`. `amounts` accepts integer `reserve` and `magazine` counts plus optional `activate`. At least one count is required; omitted counts are preserved. The operation verifies the shared ammo total, spare reserve, magazine, and live capacity asynchronously through `open77:weapons:completed`.
example:
-- Refill the pistol: full magazine plus 60 spare rounds
Open77.weapons.setAmmo(1, { magazine = 12, reserve = 60 })

name: slots
summary: Lists the three supported standard weapon slots.
description: Requires `player.weapons.read`. Slot numbers are one-based and deliberately exclude QuickSlot grenades, WeaponHeavy items, and ArmsCW cyberware.
example:
-- Print the standard slots this API manages
for _, slot in ipairs(Open77.weapons.slots() or {}) do print("slot", slot) end

name: snapshot
summary: Requests the verified state of every standard weapon slot.
description: Requires `player.weapons.read`. Emits one `open77:weapons:state` event per available slot and then `open77:weapons:completed`. TweakDB IDs remain opaque hexadecimal strings and are the presence authority; `record` may be empty for items equipped outside this API because shipping builds do not retain every reverse TweakDB name.
example:
-- Ask for the verified state, then read it from the events
Open77.weapons.snapshot()
AddEventHandler("open77:weapons:state", function(requestId, slot, record, tweakDbId, active, drawn)
    print(slot, record, active, drawn)
end)

name: unequip
summary: Alias of `Open77.weapons.remove`.
description: Requires `player.weapons.edit`; the inventory instance is retained.
example:
-- Confiscate slot 3 (alias of remove)
Open77.weapons.unequip(3)

name: create
summary: Creates a web surface.
description:
**Creation is asynchronous.** A `show()` issued right after `create` loses the race against the `visible` flag the request carried, and the surface then never paints at all. So a surface meant to stay up is created with `visible = true`, and the page shows or hides its own content.

Valid layers: `hud`, `menu`, `modal`, `system` (needs the `webui.system` permission), `debug`.

name: default
summary: The surface declared by `web_ui_page` in the manifest.
description: Returns the auto-created WebUI page declared by `web_ui_page` in the current manifest. It returns `nil, reason` when the resource has no live default page; the handle is generation-owned and becomes stale after destroy or reload.
example:
-- Use the page declared by web_ui_page in the manifest
local page = Open77.webui.default()
if page then page:send("hello", { name = "V" }) end

name: clearDeviceInteraction
summary: Drops this resource's device-interaction policy for one target.
description: Removes the calling resource's policy for that engine entity or class name, which is not the same as setDeviceInteractionEnabled(target, true): an explicit allow is still a policy this resource holds, while a cleared key is one it no longer has an opinion about. Another resource's refusal on the same target is untouched either way -- every active policy must allow for an interaction to happen. Clearing a key that was never set is not an error, so a resource that tidies up on every path can do so unconditionally. Requires the world.devices permission.

params.name: target
params.type: integer engine entity id, or string class name / 0x id

example:
-- The custom vending menu closes: give the vanilla prompt back
AddEventHandler("vending:closed", function()
    Open77.world.clearDeviceInteraction("VendingMachine")
end)

name: deviceInteractionEnabled
summary: Whether a vanilla device prompt is currently allowed, across every resource.
description: The EFFECTIVE verdict, combining every running resource's policies -- not the calling resource's own claim. A resource that released its policy still reads false while another resource holds one, exactly as Open77.input.isActionBlocked answers for every holder. The same target spelling as setDeviceInteractionEnabled; a decimal id and its 0x form resolve to the same device. Requires the world.devices permission, deliberately the same string as the write: a resource that may not change a policy has no business enumerating what other resources set.

params.name: target
params.type: integer engine entity id, or string class name / 0x id

example:
-- Before drawing our own prompt, check nobody else already refused the device
if Open77.world.deviceInteractionEnabled(machine.engineEntity) then
    Open77.hud.notify("Press E to hack the machine", { replace = true })
end

name: deviceInteractionPolicies
summary: Every standing device-interaction policy and who holds it.
description: One row per policy: owner (the resource that set it), enabled, and exactly one of engineEntity or className. Ordered by owner then by key. This is how an admin resource proves a claim really came back, the same role Open77.input.blocks() plays for input claims. Requires the world.devices permission.
returns: array of { owner, engineEntity | className, enabled }, or nil
example:
-- Debug: list who blocked which device
for _, policy in ipairs(Open77.world.deviceInteractionPolicies() or {}) do
    print(policy.owner, policy.className or policy.engineEntity, policy.enabled)
end

name: district
summary: The district the local player is standing in.
description: Reads the engine's own district for the player: `Watson`, `Dogtown`, `Arroyo`, and a finer `subDistrict` such as `ClairesGarage` where one is authored. The names are the `gamedataDistrict` enum's, so they are stable identifiers rather than display text; `localized` carries the record's own display name. `position` is optional and is accepted only when it is the local player's own position (within 25 m); any other position is refused with `position_not_local`. That is not a limitation of Open77: Cyberpunk resolves a district by trigger volume, the volume fires when the PLAYER crosses it, and the geometry is baked sector data with no getter, so nothing in the engine maps an arbitrary coordinate to a district and a guessed answer would be worse than a refusal. There is deliberately no `Open77.world.street`: the engine has no street layer, only street names painted onto sign meshes as UI text, so no coordinate has a street. To learn another player's district, listen for `open77:districtChanged` on their client and send it to the server. Requires `world.query`.

params.name: position
params.type: table { x, y, z } (the local player's own)

returns: table { district, subDistrict?, localized? } -- subDistrict is absent, not empty, when there is none, or nil
reason: permission_denied:world.query, invalid_position, position_not_local, district_unavailable, world_unavailable_on_this_host
example:
-- Show the district name when the player crosses into a new one
local last
SetTick(function()
    local place = Open77.world.district()
    if place and place.district ~= last then
        last = place.district
        Open77.hud.notify("Now entering " .. (place.localized or place.district))
    end
end)

name: entityGeometry
summary: Position, facing, orientation and loaded mesh bounds of one entity, for geometry built on top of it.
description:
The engine-side read PolyZone's entity zones are built on. Takes an engine entity id (a number, the `engineEntity` a `nearby` or raycast row carries) or a typed reference `{ kind = "player" | "vehicle" | "npc" | "entity", id = <Open77 id> }`, and answers `{ attached, entity, position, forward, orientation = {x, y, z, w}, bounds?, head?, damage? }`. `bounds` is `{ min, max, source = "loaded_mesh_bounds" }` in world space and is only present while the mesh is streamed in; `head` (puppets) and `damage` (`{ health, revision, attacker?, weapon?, isMelee }`) are likewise omitted rather than fabricated when the engine has nothing to say. Requires `world.query`.

Fails with `invalid_entity_kind`, `invalid_entity_id`, `entity_geometry_unavailable`, or the entity resolver's own reason when the id names nothing attached.
returns: table { attached, entity, position, forward, orientation, bounds?, head?, damage? }, or nil
example:
-- Is the local player inside the footprint of the nearest car?
local hits = Open77.world.nearby(15, "other")
for _, hit in ipairs(hits or {}) do
    if hit.family == "vehicle" then
        local geometry = Open77.world.entityGeometry(hit.engineEntity)
        if geometry and geometry.bounds then
            local x, y = Open77.character.position()
            local b = geometry.bounds
            if x >= b.min.x and x <= b.max.x and y >= b.min.y and y <= b.max.y then
                Open77.hud.notify("Step away from the " .. hit.className)
            end
        end
        break
    end
end

name: groundZ
summary: Height of the static ground below a point, by a downward ray.
description: Casts a `Static`-only ray straight down from `(x, y, fromZ)` over one kilometre and returns the Z of the first surface. Static only on purpose: a parked car or a body is not the ground. The default start height clears every rooftop in Night City. Returns nil when nothing was hit (open water, outside the world). Requires `world.query`.
returns: z (number), or nil when nothing is below
example:
-- Place a marker on the ground under a map-picked point
local z = Open77.world.groundZ(-1442.2, 127.4)
if z then
    Open77.markers.create({ position = { x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = z }, radius = 1.0 })
end

name: nearby
summary: Every object within a radius of the local player, nearest first.
description:
Exposes `Api::WorldQuery::Around`, the engine's own targeting search. It is centred on the local player because the search takes a source object, not a point: to look around somewhere else, stand there. `filter` narrows the object classes: a name, a list of names or a raw mask. Names: `player`, `puppet`, `sensor`, `device`, `other` (classes), `friendly`, `hostile`, `neutral`, `alive`, `dead`, `turnedOn`, `turnedOff`, `quickHackable` (attitude and state bits, which widen a search rather than narrow it). Requires `world.query`.

Every row answers two separate questions. **What is it** -- `kind`, from the same classifier the raycast row uses, refined by ownership: an Open77-owned body is `npc`, a vanilla crowd body is `populationNpc`, an Open77 car is `vehicle` and a traffic car is `trafficVehicle`. `family` is the unrefined answer (`npc`, `vehicle`, `device`, `door`, `player`, `weapon`, `item`, `object`, `unknown`) for a caller that means "is this a ped at all".

**Whose is it** -- exactly one of `playerId`, `vehicleId` or `npcId` when Open77 owns the entity, and none of the three when it does not. A row with no identity is local scenery: nothing replicates it, every client sees a different one, and it can be gone next frame. `Open77.character.state({ engineEntity = row.engineEntity })` reads such a body, read-only.

params.name: filter
params.type: string | table of strings | number mask

returns: array of table { engineEntity, entity identity (playerId | vehicleId | npcId), kind, family, className, position { x, y, z }, distance }

name: nearest
summary: The closest object within a radius of the local player, or nil.
description: Same search, same filter vocabulary and the same row shape as `Open77.world.nearby` -- including `kind`, `family` and the single owner identity -- returning only the first hit. Requires `world.query`.

params.name: filter
params.type: string | table of strings | number mask

returns: table { engineEntity, entity identity (playerId | vehicleId | npcId), kind, family, className, position { x, y, z }, distance }, or nil
example:
-- Press E on the nearest device (ATM, vending machine, terminal) within 3 m
RegisterKeyMapping("use_device", "Use device", "E", function()
    local device = Open77.world.nearest(3, "device")
    if device then TriggerServerEvent("devices:use", device.className, device.engineEntity) end
end)

name: population
summary: The ambient population policy the server set for this client's routing bucket.
description:
Read-only, and there is no client setter on purpose: density is a server-load decision that has to be the same for every client in a bucket, so there is nothing here to race the server with. `Open77.world.setPopulation` on the server is the write side.

`crowd` is a genuine fraction of the vanilla pedestrian density and is applied as one. `traffic` is reported as sent but the engine offers no vehicle density modifier on 2.31, so any value above zero means vanilla traffic -- `trafficGranularity` says `binary` and `crowdGranularity` says `continuous` rather than letting a caller assume otherwise. `applied` is what the engine did with the policy (`Ok`, or a refusal name): a policy can arrive and be refused, and a caller comparing its own numbers against the street needs to see that. Requires `world.query`.

Fails with `no_population_policy` until a server has sent one. That is a different answer from empty streets and must not be read as one.
returns: table { bucket, crowd, traffic, police, revision, applied, crowdGranularity, trafficGranularity }, or nil
example:
-- Tell the player when they are in an empty instance
local policy = Open77.world.population()
if policy and policy.crowd == 0 and policy.traffic == 0 then
    Open77.hud.notify("Private instance: no crowd, no traffic")
end

name: raycast
summary: Traces a physics ray between two world points and returns the nearest blocking surface.
description: Runs `gameSpatialQueriesSystem::SyncRaycastByCollisionGroup`, the same native the combat and camera code use, against the `Static` and `Dynamic` collision groups and keeps the nearer hit. `options` may disable either group (`{ static = true, dynamic = false }`). The result is what the engine's trace publishes: position, surface normal, material name and distance. With `options.entities = true` it also carries `entity` when the ray stopped on an object rather than on world geometry: `engineEntity`, `className`, `kind`, `position`, `distance`, and one of `playerId`, `vehicleId` or `npcId` when Open77 owns the thing. Without that option the returned table is unchanged, so existing resources are unaffected. The entity is not read out of the trace, which carries none: the object standing at the hit point is found with the same object search `Open77.world.nearest` uses, so the search is centred on the local player and a hit more than 250 m away cannot be attributed. A hit on a wall, a road or a railing has no entity at all, which is the ordinary answer and not an error. Synchronous, on the game thread; requires the `world.query` permission.
returns: table { hit, position { x, y, z }, normal { x, y, z }, material, distance, entity? } (position, normal, material and distance only when hit is true; entity only when options.entities is set AND the ray stopped on an object), or nil
reason: permission_denied:world.query, invalid_from, invalid_to, ray_entities_unavailable_on_this_host, world_unavailable_on_this_host, or the engine status
example:
-- Is there a wall between the player and the target point?
local from = Open77.character.state().position
local hit = Open77.world.raycast(from, target)
if hit and hit.hit and hit.distance < #(vector3(target) - vector3(from)) then
    print("blocked by", hit.material, "at", hit.distance, "m")
end

name: safeAreasEnabled
summary: Whether the vanilla safe-area marking is currently in effect.
description: Reads the effective safe-area state across every resource that claimed it through `Open77.world.setSafeAreas`: true when the staged interiors behave as vanilla (walk-only, weapons holstered), false while at least one running resource holds the marking off. Requires the `world.safeareas` permission. Returns nil plus a reason when the permission is missing or no game backend is attached.
example:
-- Warn the player before they draw a weapon in a bar
if Open77.world.safeAreasEnabled() then
    Open77.hud.notify("Weapons are holstered in this area")
end

name: setDeviceInteractionEnabled
summary: Turns a vanilla device prompt off, so a resource can put its own there.
description: I3. Cyberpunk has no per-device interactive flag a mod can write, so this wraps the one scripted choke point every device controller passes through: ScriptableDeviceComponentPS::DetermineInteractionState, which is declared on gameDeviceComponentPS, overridden exactly once on the scriptable device PS, and otherwise only on ScriptedPuppetPS, which is not a device. GetActions is overridden by some sixty controller subclasses and is therefore useless as a single gate. When a policy refuses, the wrapper publishes an EMPTY choice set through the class's own PushChoicesToInteractionComponent -- the same call vanilla makes for a device with no valid actions -- so the engine clears the prompt on the layer it chose itself. A second wrapper on InteractiveDevice::OnInteractionUsed refuses the use as well, so a policy that says off means off even if a scene or a subclass reaches the action another way. target is either an engine entity id -- exactly what Open77.world.nearby reports as engineEntity, decimal or 0x -- or a device class name, matched case-insensitively against BOTH names the engine has for a device: the object class (VendingMachine) and the controller persistent state (VendingMachineControllerPS), because the caller reads the first and the hook runs on the second. A class name accepts letters, digits and underscore only: a typo must not become a wildcard that disables half the city. The claim is per resource and additive in the refusing direction -- every active policy must allow an interaction for it to happen -- and everything a resource holds is released when it stops, reloads or crashes. Deliberately NOT under world.query, which is the read gate on nearby: this is a write that changes what the player can do with the world. It does not touch quickhacks, does not power a device down, and is presentation policy on one client rather than authority. Refusals: permission_denied:world.devices, device_backend_unavailable, invalid_device_target, invalid_device_state (a missing or non-boolean second argument is refused rather than read as 'disable'), device_policy_limit.

params.name: target
params.type: integer engine entity id, or string class name / 0x id

example:
-- Replace every ATM's vanilla prompt with the server's banking menu
Open77.world.setDeviceInteractionEnabled("ATM", false)

name: setSafeAreas
summary: Turns the vanilla safe-area marking of staged interiors on or off for this session.
description: Vanilla marks a handful of interiors (the Afterlife, Lizzie's, Clouds) as staged, walk-only, weapons-holstered space. `setSafeAreas(false)` takes that marking off for the duration of the session, which is what makes a lobby staged in the Afterlife playable rather than a walking simulator. The claim is cooperative and owner-scoped: safe areas return once every claiming resource has released (or stopped), never because one resource asked. Requires the `world.safeareas` permission. Returns true plus the effective state across every owner, so a caller can see that another resource still holds safe areas off; false plus a reason on failure (permission_denied:world.safeareas, safe_area_backend_unavailable, invalid_safe_area_argument).
returns: effective state across owners, or reason on failure
example:
-- The deathmatch lobby is staged in the Afterlife: make it playable
AddEventHandler("onClientResourceStart", function(name)
    if name == GetCurrentResourceName() then Open77.world.setSafeAreas(false) end
end)

name: bounds
summary: The zone's bounding volume: a planar centre and radius plus an optional height band.
description: Available in both runtimes, from the shared prelude scripting/lua/open77_zones.lua. Exactly the shape of the one squared comparison a poll loop wants per zone per tick, and of the radius a server roster scan wants. `minZ` and `maxZ` are nil when the zone is unbounded on that side, which only a polygon with no declared height range can be. This is what makes a polygon affordable: a zone the player is not standing in is rejected by its bounds for about the cost of a sphere (1.25 us against 1.2 us, measured in the client host), so cost tracks the zones that actually overlap the player rather than the number registered.

params.name: zone
params.type: table (a definition, or a value from Open77.zones.normalize)

returns: table { x, y, z, radius, minZ, maxZ } (minZ and maxZ may be nil), or nil, reason
reason: the same tokens as Open77.zones.contains
example:
local b = assert(Open77.zones.bounds(turf))
print(("turf spans %.1f m around %.1f, %.1f"):format(b.radius, b.x, b.y))

name: contains
summary: Is a point inside a zone? The one containment implementation both runtimes share.
description: Available in both runtimes, from the shared prelude scripting/lua/open77_zones.lua. The client poller and the server's Open77.zones.playersIn both call this, which is the point: a client and a server that disagreed at a boundary would leave a place a player can stand where the prompt appears but the grant is refused, or worse the other way round. Shapes: omit `shape` for the cylinder that shipped (planar `radius` around `position` plus a `maxHeight` band, default 6 m); `sphere` is a true 3-D ball and refuses `maxHeight`; `box` takes `position`, `size` (FULL extents) and `rotation` in degrees about the vertical axis; `poly` (alias `polygon`) takes `points` (3..512 planar vertices, concave allowed) with optional `minZ`/`maxZ` -- absent means unbounded on that side; `combo` takes `zones`, nested up to 4 deep. Every shape is CLOSED: a point on an edge, a face or a vertex is inside. `point` is a vector3 or any { x =, y =, z = } table. `options` may carry `grace` (metres to expand the zone outward, with rounded corners -- the server's tolerance for a replicated position, and the client's hysteresis band), `origin` ({ x, y, z } where the zone's anchor actually is right now, which is how an entity-attached zone is tested) and `rotation` (degrees, the zone's heading right now). A definition carrying `attach` REQUIRES `origin`, because resolving an entity is not something pure geometry may do. `false` always means outside and never 'could not tell'. Pure: it reads no world and holds no state. See the Proximity zones guide.

params.name: zone
params.type: table (a definition, or a value from Open77.zones.normalize)

returns: reason: invalid_definition, unknown_shape, invalid_position, invalid_radius, invalid_max_height, max_height_unsupported, invalid_size, invalid_rotation, invalid_points, too_many_points, degenerate_polygon, invalid_height_range, invalid_zones, too_many_zones, zone_nesting_too_deep, invalid_attach, invalid_point, invalid_options, invalid_grace, invalid_origin, origin_required

name: normalize
summary: Validates a zone definition once and precomputes everything a containment test needs.
description: Available in both runtimes, from the shared prelude scripting/lua/open77_zones.lua. Returns a prepared zone -- a plain table, so it still survives json.encode and pairs -- carrying the validated shape, its bounding volume and the derived values a test would otherwise recompute. Open77.zones.contains accepts either form, but on a raw definition it has to redo this work on every single call: measured in the client host, a 32-vertex polygon costs about 9.5 us prepared and roughly eight times that unprepared, because the vertex list is rebuilt and the shoelace area re-run before the test can start. Normalize once, keep the result, test many. Shapes: omit `shape` for the cylinder that shipped (planar `radius` around `position` plus a `maxHeight` band, default 6 m); `sphere` is a true 3-D ball and refuses `maxHeight`; `box` takes `position`, `size` (FULL extents) and `rotation` in degrees about the vertical axis; `poly` (alias `polygon`) takes `points` (3..512 planar vertices, concave allowed) with optional `minZ`/`maxZ` -- absent means unbounded on that side; `combo` takes `zones`, nested up to 4 deep. Every shape is CLOSED: a point on an edge, a face or a vertex is inside.
returns: reason: the same tokens as Open77.zones.contains
example:
local shop = assert(Open77.zones.normalize({ shape = "box",
    position = { x = -1460.2, y = 99.9, z = 14.8 },
    size = { x = 12.0, y = 6.0, z = 4.0 }, rotation = 37.0 }))
print(shop.shape, shop.bounds.radius)

name: destroy
summary: Destroys the surface.
description: Destroys this resource-owned browser surface, removes all of its Lua event handlers and invalidates the page handle. Resource teardown performs the same cleanup automatically.
example:
-- Tear the menu surface down when the player leaves the shop
AddEventHandler("shop:left", function()
    if page then page:destroy(); page = nil end
end)

name: hasFocus
summary: Check whether this resource-owned page currently owns keyboard or cursor focus.
description: Call page:hasFocus(). Reads actual focus ownership and presentation availability without changing either. Returns false if another surface owns focus or this surface cannot present. Only accepts a live page handle owned by the calling resource. Combine with setFocus(false,false), hide and resource-scoped control cleanup when closing a modal. See screen-picking.md and the generic open77_contextmenu package.
example:
page:show()
page:setFocus(true, true)
print(page:hasFocus())
page:setFocus(false, false)
page:hide()

name: hide
summary: Hides the surface.
description: Makes the owned browser surface invisible without destroying its document or handlers. Visibility is client-local and can be restored with `show()`.
example:
-- Hide the HUD page during the cutscene, keeping its document alive
AddEventHandler("cutscene:started", function() page:hide() end)
AddEventHandler("cutscene:ended", function() page:show() end)

name: id
summary: Numeric id of the surface.
description: Returns the opaque client-local surface id for diagnostics and host integration. It is not a network id and must not be persisted across page destruction or resource reload.
example:
-- Log the surface id for a bug report
print("hud surface id", page:id())

name: off
summary: Removes a handler registered with `on`.
description: Removes one WebUI callback id previously returned by `page:on`. The id is the only argument -- there is no event name parameter. It must belong to this page and the current resource generation.
example:
-- Stop listening to the page's "buy" event after checkout
local handler = page:on("buy", function(payload) buy(payload.item) end)
AddEventHandler("shop:checkout", function() page:off(handler) end)

name: on
summary: Listens for an event the page raised with `Open77.emit`.
description: Registers a Lua callback for an event emitted by this page's JavaScript bridge. Event names and handler counts are bounded, and the registration is automatically removed with the page or resource generation.
example:
-- The page's JavaScript called Open77.emit("buy", { item = "ammo" })
page:on("buy", function(payload)
    TriggerServerEvent("shop:buy", payload.item)
end)

name: reply
summary: Answers an `invoke` call made by the page.
description: Completes a pending JavaScript request identified by its request id with a JSON-serializable Lua value. The payload is the SECOND argument and the success flag the third: `page:reply(requestId, { accepted = true })` resolves the promise, and a third argument of `false` rejects it. Success defaults to true when omitted. The payload is positional and cannot be skipped -- an absent third argument fails with `invalid_webui_reply`, though an explicit `nil` is accepted. Request ids are page-local and invalid or unsupported payloads are rejected.
example:
-- Answer an invoke() from the page with the player's balance
page:on("getBalance", function(payload, requestId)
    page:reply(requestId, { balance = balance })
end)

name: send
summary: Sends an event to the page.
description: Sends a named event and JSON-serializable payload from Lua to this page's JavaScript runtime. This is local UI IPC, not a network event, and both event names and payloads are bounded.
example:
-- Push the new balance to the page
RegisterNetEvent("bank:balance", function(amount)
    page:send("balance", { amount = amount })
end)

name: setFocus
summary: Gives the surface focus, cursor and keyboard separately.
description: The FIRST argument is keyboard capture, not a general `focused` flag, and the second is the cursor: `page:setFocus(true, true)` takes both, `page:setFocus(false, true)` takes only the mouse. Keyboard capture is asked for separately so a page can take the mouse without depriving the game of the movement keys. The optional third argument keeps game input alive while the page holds focus and requires `webui.keep_input`; without that permission it fails with `permission_denied:webui.keep_input`.
example:
-- Open the menu: take the mouse, leave the keyboard to the game
page:show()
page:setFocus(false, true)

name: show
summary: Shows the surface.
description: Avoid calling this right after `create` — see the race described in `Open77.webui.create`.
example:
-- Show the menu surface (created hidden) when the key is pressed
RegisterKeyMapping("shop_menu", "Shop menu", "F3", function()
    page:show()
    page:setFocus(true, true)
end)

name: new
summary: Creates a promise this resource settles itself.
description: The same Open77.Promise object Open77.exports.call and Open77.net.call return, so the runtime has one promise type rather than two: resolve, reject, next, await and status all work on it. On the client a pending promise has a single consumer -- the first await or next woken by a settle takes the value and the promise then reports cancelled -- while on the server it keeps its value and can be awaited repeatedly. Code that awaits once is portable across both. See the FiveM compatibility guide.
example:
-- A promise resolved by an event, awaited by a thread
local answered = promise.new()
AddEventHandler("dialog:answered", function(yes) answered:resolve(yes) end)
CreateThread(function()
    local yes = answered:await()
    print("player said", yes)
end)

name: AddEventHandler
summary: Listens for an event in this resource; the same function as Open77.events.on.
description: No permission. One handler list serves three sources: this VM's TriggerLocalEvent, the host-wide bus, and the platform's own lifecycle events (onResourceStart, onPlayerReady, playerDropped), so a resource listens for its own and the platform's events the same way. Handlers run as managed tasks and may Wait. The limit is 2,048 handlers per resource; beyond it registration raises `handler quota exceeded`. Returns the id RemoveEventHandler takes.
example:
-- React to a player leaving: save their money before the session is gone
AddEventHandler("onPlayerDisconnected", function(playerId, reason)
    local key = "money:" .. (Open77.players.identifier(playerId) or "")
    Open77.kvp.set(key, wallet[playerId] or 0)
    wallet[playerId] = nil
end)

name: AddStateBagChangeHandler
summary: Subscribes to bag changes, FiveM style.
description: Wraps `Open77.state.onChange` in the FiveM signature. `key` may be a key name, or nil or `"*"` for every key. `bagName` may be nil for every bag, `"global"`, `"player:<id>"`, `"<kind>:<id>"`, or `"entity:<id>"`, which matches any entity kind carrying that id. The handler receives `(bagName, key, value, reserved, replicated)`; `reserved` is always nil and `replicated` always true, so a ported signature lines up. It runs at a tick boundary rather than inside the write, so it may Wait. Only subscribed resources are touched: the filter is on the host side, so one resource's interest in a key does not marshal that key into every other resource.

summary: `floorCount`.
description: `floorCount`. Constants are in `Open77.elevators.flags`. Low-level aliases are `AdoptElevator`,

name: AttachEffect
summary: `world.effects`;
description: `world.effects`; decimal effect ID or nil/reason. Prefer `Open77.effects.attach`.

name: BanPlayer
summary: `Open77.players.ban` and `BanPlayer` resolve the player's authenticated device identity, submit a
description: `Open77.players.ban` and `BanPlayer` resolve the player's authenticated device identity, submit a

name: CancelEvent
summary: Server only. Vetoes the cancellable event this handler is running under.
description: Meaningful only inside a handler reached by TriggerCancellableEvent; anywhere else it answers false, not_in_cancellable_event rather than raising. The flag is shared by every resource in the dispatch, so the first cancel wins and the remaining handlers still run and can read it.
example:
-- A chat filter: veto any message containing a banned word
AddEventHandler("chatMessage", function(source, name, text)
    if text:lower():find("badword", 1, true) then
        CancelEvent()
        Open77.chat.send(source, "That word is not allowed here.")
    end
end)

description: `AttachProp`, `DetachProp`, `RemoveProp`, `GetProp`, `GetProps`, and `ClearProps`. The namespaced API supplies validation and structured

name: ClearTick
summary: Cancels a tick created by SetTick.
description: Answers false for an id that is not a live tick. Cancellation goes through a flag rather than ClearTimeout because a tick pass pulls every due task out of the queue before resuming any of them, and a task cancelled by id while it is already in that batch would be put back. The flag is read at the top of the loop, so the body never runs again after this returns.
example:
-- Count down on every tick until the round starts, then stop the tick
local tick
tick = SetTick(function()
    if GetGameTimer() >= roundStartAt then
        ClearTick(tick)
        startRound()
    end
end)

name: ClearTimeout
summary: Cancels a timer created by SetTimeout.
description: Drops the task before it runs. An id that has already fired, or was never issued, is ignored rather than raising.
example:
-- The bomb defusal: cancel the explosion timer when the bomb is defused
local fuse = SetTimeout(30000, function() detonate() end)
RegisterNetEvent("bomb:defused", function()
    ClearTimeout(fuse)
    Open77.chat.broadcast("Bomb defused!")
end)

name: CreateThread
summary: Starts a coroutine this resource's scheduler manages.
description: Its body may Wait, which an ordinary function cannot. Returns the task id. A resource may hold 1,024 scheduled tasks at once and raises `task quota exceeded` beyond that; stopping the resource drops every task it owns. Command, event and callback handlers already run as managed tasks, so they may Wait without a CreateThread of their own.
example:
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        Wait(60000)
        print("still here")
    end
end)

summary: DestroySound: server-authoritative network package audio.
description: Requires audio.network; network=false is rejected. Server owns the timeline, handles and bucket/optional-target audience. Clients cannot request broadcasts directly. getState reports intended playback, not decoder acknowledgement. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. name: DoesEntityExist
summary: Whether an id is live in the registry that owns that kind.
description: FiveM has one opaque handle space; Open77 has one registry per kind, so the kind has to be named: vehicle, npc, prop, loot, effect, elevator or player. The one-argument FiveM form cannot be answered and is refused with false, kind_required rather than guessed at. Each kind is answered by the registry that already owns it, under that registry's permissions, so a resource that may not read vehicles gets false -- the same answer an absent id gets. Call the namespace function directly when you need to tell denied from absent. Other reasons: id_required, invalid_entity_id, unknown_entity_kind.
example:
-- The tow job stored a vehicle id an hour ago; is the car still there?
if not DoesEntityExist("vehicle", job.vehicleId) then
    Open77.chat.send(job.playerId, "The car you were towing is gone.")
    return
end

summary: Addresses one entity's state bag, FiveM style.
description: `Entity(id).state` is `Open77.state.entity(kind, id)` with the kind resolved by looking the id up in the vehicle, NPC and prop registries in turn. name: GetConvar
summary: Reads a convar as a string, or the caller's default.
description: A COMPATIBILITY SHIM for ported code, not the mechanism to reach for when writing something new -- see `Open77.tunables`, which is typed, range-checked, validated on every write, retunable from the Warden panel while the server runs, persisted across a restart, and scoped to the declaring resource. Resolution order: an in-memory `SetConvar` override, then the `convars` block of `server.jsonc`, then **this resource's own declared tunables by exact key**, then the default. That third step is how a port migrates to the better mechanism one key at a time. Never raises: an unset convar answers the default. Names are case-insensitive.
example:
-- A FiveM port reads its config the way it always did
local webhook = GetConvar("myshop_webhook", "")
if webhook == "" then print("myshop_webhook is not set") end

name: GetConvarBool
summary: Reads a convar as a boolean, or the caller's default.
description: `true`, `1`, `yes` and `on` are true; `false`, `0`, `no` and `off` are false; anything else is not a boolean and the default stands. The same vocabulary the console's tunable parser accepts, so an operator does not have to remember two.
example:
-- Turn PvP on from the server config: "myserver_pvp": "true"
local pvp = GetConvarBool("myserver_pvp", false)
Open77.combat.setFriendlyFire(pvp)

name: GetConvarInt
summary: Reads a convar as an integer, or the caller's default.
description: Never raises. A value that is not a whole number answers the default rather than failing -- a ported script reads a convar that may simply not be set, and a strict parse would turn a missing setting into a crash on the first frame.
example:
-- The starting money of a new player, from the convars block
local startingMoney = GetConvarInt("myserver_starting_money", 500)

name: GetHashKey
summary: TweakDBID of a record name -- not a Jenkins hash.
description: CRC-32/ISO-HDLC of the name in the low 32 bits with the name length in byte 4, which is what REDengine computes and the only hash that resolves to anything in this game. It is deliberately NOT the Jenkins one-at-a-time hash FiveM's GetHashKey returns, so a hash constant copied out of a FiveM resource names a GTA model and matches nothing here: port the string, not the number. Non-string input answers nil, invalid_argument. The client computes the identical value, and results are memoised up to 1,024 names per resource.
example:
-- Compare a record name with a TweakDBID a client sent (never a FiveM/Jenkins hash)
if GetHashKey("Vehicle.v_sport2_quadra_turbo_r") == recordHash then print("a Quadra") end

description: Recognised types, matched case-insensitively: open77 and userId both give the account GUID, name the display name, fingerprint the SHA-256 of the identity public key. Anything else answers nil, unknown_identifier_type, and a non-string type answers nil, invalid_identifier_type. The value is bare, without the "type:" prefix GetPlayerIdentifiers puts on it.

name: GetPlayerIdentifiers
summary: Every identifier of a connected player, in FiveM's array-of-strings shape.
description: Each entry is "type:value" -- open77:<account guid>, name:<display name>, fingerprint:<sha-256> -- so `for _, id in ipairs(GetPlayerIdentifiers(source))` ports unchanged. Entries the session does not carry are left out rather than emitted empty, and a player id that names nobody answers nil, player_not_found. There is no steam, license or discord entry: Open77 has one account identity, and inventing the others would let ported code believe it had verified something.
returns: array of strings, or nil, player_not_found
example:
-- A FiveM whitelist loop runs unchanged
for _, id in ipairs(GetPlayerIdentifiers(source)) do
    if id:sub(1, 7) == "open77:" then print("account", id:sub(8)) end
end

name: PauseSound
summary: PauseSound: server-authoritative network package audio.
description: Requires audio.network; network=false is rejected. Server owns the timeline, handles and bucket/optional-target audience. Clients cannot request broadcasts directly. getState reports intended playback, not decoder acknowledgement. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Intermission: pause the concert stream for everyone
PauseSound(concertId)

name: PerformHttpRequest
summary: Performs an outbound HTTP request, off the tick thread.
description: Requires http.request, and the server must have enabled the bridge with a host allow-list. The request leaves the tick thread at once and the callback runs on this resource's own scheduler with (status, body, headers, err); status is 0 when the exchange did not complete and err then names the reason. method defaults to GET; body may be a string or a table, which is JSON-encoded for you, up to 256 KiB. A request refused before it leaves answers false, reason and still calls the callback with status 0. Namespaced as Open77.http.request.
example:
-- Post a Discord webhook when a player is banned
PerformHttpRequest("https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...", function(status, body)
    if status ~= 204 then print("webhook failed", status) end
end, "POST", { content = "Player banned: " .. name }, { ["Content-Type"] = "application/json" })

name: Player
summary: Addresses one player's state bag, FiveM style.
description: `Player(id).state` is `Open77.state.player(id)`, and `Player(id).source` answers the id back, so a ported script that passes a player object around keeps working. An unknown id still returns a handle: the bag is created on first write and dies when the player disconnects. The bag reaches every player who can see that player, which is the roster of their routing bucket, so it is not a private channel.
example:
-- FiveM-style write of a player's state bag
Player(source).state.cuffed = true

name: RegisterCommand
summary: Registers a command usable from the server console and from chat.
description: No permission to register. The handler receives (source, args, raw), where source is the player id or 0 for the console, args is the packed argument list and raw is the untouched line. Names are 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `:` or `-`, matched case-insensitively; registering one twice raises `duplicate command`. With restricted = true the caller must hold the ACL entry command.<name> -- see Identity and ACL.

name: RegisterNetEvent
summary: Registers a handler for an authenticated client event; the same function as Open77.net.on.
description: Requires network.events. During the handler the global `source` is set from the authenticated connection and never from the client's payload -- that is the whole difference from AddEventHandler. Called with the name alone it only marks the name as reachable from a client and registers nothing. Such a handler also receives host-wide bus events, so one that acts on authority must validate `source` rather than assume it. Events carry at most 32 arguments in a 48 KiB envelope.
returns: handler id, or true when only the name is declared
example:
-- The client asks to buy an item; `source` is the authenticated buyer
RegisterNetEvent("shop:buy", function(itemId)
    local price = prices[itemId]
    if not price then return end
    if takeMoney(source, price) then
        Open77.chat.send(source, "Purchased " .. itemId)
    end
end)

name: SetConvar
summary: Records a server-wide, in-memory convar override.
description: Server-wide, not per resource -- `SetConvar` here is visible to `GetConvar` in another resource, which is what the FiveM code being ported assumes and is exactly why a convar is a poor place for anything two resources might both want to own. **In memory only**: the value is gone on the next restart and the `convars` block of `server.jsonc` comes back. Making it durable would mean writing to the operator's tracked configuration file from Lua. Booleans and numbers are coerced to their string form. 512 overrides, 4096-byte values, names `[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]` up to 128 bytes.
example:
-- Toggle a server-wide flag other resources read with GetConvar
RegisterCommand("maintenance", function(source, args)
    SetConvar("myserver_maintenance", args[1] == "on")
end, true)

name: SetTick
summary: Runs a function once per server tick.
description: A scheduler task looping with an implicit Wait(0), so it is bounded by the same budget and counted against the same 1,024-task quota as a CreateThread loop. The difference is the pcall: an error inside the function is logged and the tick survives it, up to five *consecutive* failures, after which the tick cancels itself rather than filling the log for the rest of the session. One successful pass resets the count. Answers nil, invalid_tick_function for a non-function and nil, task_limit_or_stopping when no task slot is available.
example:
-- Check the zone every tick; the tick survives an occasional error
SetTick(function()
    for _, playerId in ipairs(Open77.players.inBucket(0)) do
        checkZone(playerId)
    end
end)

name: SetTimeout
summary: Runs a function once, later.
description: Schedules a managed task due after the delay, so the body may Wait. Counts against the same 1,024-task budget as CreateThread. Returns the timer id ClearTimeout takes.
example:
-- Respawn the player 8 seconds after they died
AddEventHandler("onPlayerLifeStateChanged", function(playerId, revision, phase)
    if phase == "dead" then
        SetTimeout(8000, function()
            Open77.players.respawn(playerId, { position = hospital })
        end)
    end
end)

name: TriggerCancellableEvent
summary: Server only. Publishes a host-wide event handlers may veto, and returns a verdict handle.
description: Only events published this way can be cancelled; an ordinary TriggerEvent ignores CancelEvent(). Handlers run inline during the host drain, in resource-name order then registration order, so Wait() is not available inside one. Every handler still runs after a veto (FiveM semantics) and a later one reads the flag with WasEventCanceled(). The handle settles one tick later: verdict:await() answers true when a handler cancelled, verdict:canceled() answers nil plus status while pending, verdict:status() answers pending, settled or unknown. An unread verdict is forgotten 30 s after it settles. Same caps and reserved list as TriggerEvent.
example:
-- Let other resources veto a purchase before it happens
RegisterNetEvent("shop:buy", function(itemId)
    local buyer = source
    local verdict = TriggerCancellableEvent("shop:beforeBuy", buyer, itemId)
    if verdict and verdict:await() then return end -- somebody said no
    sell(buyer, itemId)
end)
