name: TriggerEvent
summary: Publishes an event host-wide: every running resource that handles the name receives it.
description: No permission, to publish or to receive. Delivery is queued and never re-entrant: publishing appends to the host's queue, the host drains it at the next tick boundary and pushes the event into each VM in resource-name order, so one resource's error cannot abort the fan-out. Arguments cross by value through the export marshaller -- 32 values, 4,096 nodes, depth 16, 48 KiB -- and functions, userdata, cyclic tables and non-finite numbers are refused. `source` is not propagated, so a publisher that wants receivers to know which player caused the event passes the id as an argument. Platform event names are refused with reserved_event. The client function of this name is local to its own VM; this one is the bus. Failure tokens: invalid_event_name, reserved_event, resource_stopping, resource_preparing, event_argument_limit, event_payload_not_serializable, event_queue_limit.
example:
-- Announce a robbery to every resource on the server; source is passed by hand
TriggerEvent("bank:robbed", source, amount)

name: TriggerLocalEvent
summary: Server only. Fires an event in this resource's VM and nowhere else.
description: The behaviour server TriggerEvent had before the host-wide bus: no marshalling, no reserved-name filter, no host round trip. Use it for a resource's own internal signalling, and wherever a fixture must simulate a host lifecycle event inside its own VM.
example:
-- Internal signalling that never leaves this resource
TriggerLocalEvent("shop:restocked", "ammo", 200)
AddEventHandler("shop:restocked", function(item, count)
    print(item, "restocked to", count)
end)

name: TriggerVehicleHorn
summary: `ResetVehiclePaint`, `SetVehicleLocked`, `TriggerVehicleHorn`, `SetVehicleTransform`, `RemoveVehicle`, `GetVehicle`, `GetVehicles`,
description: `ResetVehiclePaint`, `SetVehicleLocked`, `TriggerVehicleHorn`, `SetVehicleTransform`, `RemoveVehicle`, `GetVehicle`, `GetVehicles`,

name: UpdateEffect
summary: Low-level aliases are `PlayEffect`, `CreateEffect`, `UpdateEffect`, `RemoveEffect`,
description: Low-level aliases are `PlayEffect`, `CreateEffect`, `UpdateEffect`, `RemoveEffect`,

name: UpdateLootDrop
summary: and `ttlMs`.
description: and `ttlMs`. Low-level aliases are `CreateLootDrop`, `UpdateLootDrop`, `RemoveLootDrop`,

name: UpdateNpc
summary: Low-level aliases are `CreateNpc`, `UpdateNpc`, `SetNpcTransform`, `SetNpcBucket`, `RemoveNpc`,
description: Low-level aliases are `CreateNpc`, `UpdateNpc`, `SetNpcTransform`, `SetNpcBucket`, `RemoveNpc`,

name: UpdateProp
summary: Low-level aliases are `CreateProp`, `UpdateProp`, `SetPropTransform`, `SetPropBucket`,
description: Low-level aliases are `CreateProp`, `UpdateProp`, `SetPropTransform`, `SetPropBucket`,

name: UpdateVehicleState
summary: Low-level aliases are `CreateVehicle`, `UpdateVehicleState`, `SetVehiclePaint`,
description: Low-level aliases are `CreateVehicle`, `UpdateVehicleState`, `SetVehiclePaint`,

name: VehicleDrivingCommand
summary: `world.vehicles`;
description: `world.vehicles`; driving-state table or nil/reason (state may be nil when absent). Prefer [vehicle AI methods](vehicle-ai.md).

name: Wait
summary: Suspends the current managed coroutine.
description: Usable inside a CreateThread, a command handler, an event handler, a callback handler or an export body -- anywhere the scheduler owns the coroutine. Accepts 0 to 86,400,000 ms and raises `invalid wait` outside that range. Cancellable event handlers are the one exception: they run inline during the host drain, where a yield would outlive the verdict, so Wait is not available there.
example:
-- A countdown in chat, one line per second
CreateThread(function()
    for n = 5, 1, -1 do
        Open77.chat.broadcast(("Starting in %d..."):format(n))
        Wait(1000)
    end
    Open77.chat.broadcast("Go!")
end)

name: WasEventCanceled
summary: Server only. Whether the cancellable event being dispatched has already been vetoed.
description: True only inside a cancellable dispatch some handler has cancelled, in this resource or an earlier one. False everywhere else, including inside an ordinary event handler and at top level.
example:
-- Log which messages another resource's filter already rejected
AddEventHandler("chatMessage", function(source, name, text)
    if WasEventCanceled() then
        print(("filtered message from %s: %s"):format(name, text))
    end
end)

name: joaat
summary: Alias of GetHashKey; returns a TweakDBID.
description: The same function value under the name ported code uses. Kept so that code reads naturally, but it is not the Jenkins hash the name promises -- see GetHashKey before copying any hash constant across.
example:
-- FiveM habit, same value as GetHashKey: a TweakDBID, not a Jenkins hash
local id = joaat("Vehicle.v_sport2_quadra_turbo_r")

name: quat
summary: Builds a quaternion: a plain { x, y, z, w } table with three rotation methods.
description: Available in both runtimes. Deliberately minimal -- normalize (a zero quaternion becomes the identity, never NaN), mul (Hamilton product, this rotation then the other) and rotate (returns a vector3), plus unpack and table. No arithmetic operators and no #. It exists so the { x =, y =, z =, w = } orientation that Open77.effects and Open77.props already accept becomes computable; the result stays exactly that table. Identical on both runtimes by construction: one file, scripting/lua/open77_vector.lua, is embedded by the client build and by the server assembly, so the semantics cannot drift.
example:
-- Rotate a spawn offset by a 90-degree yaw
local yaw90 = quat(0, 0, 0.7071, 0.7071)
local offset = yaw90:rotate(vector3(2.0, 0.0, 0.0)) -- now points along +y

name: vec
summary: Builds a vector of the size the arguments imply.
description: Available in both runtimes. With two, three or four numbers it builds a vector2, vector3 or vector4. With a single table it picks the size from the axes actually present: w means vector4, else z means vector3, else y means vector2 -- which makes vec(position) the short way to wrap a position returned by any existing API. A quaternion is refused, because vec makes vectors. Identical on both runtimes by construction: one file, scripting/lua/open77_vector.lua, is embedded by the client build and by the server assembly, so the semantics cannot drift.
returns: vector2, vector3 or vector4, or nil, reason
example:
-- Wrap a position any API returned, then measure a distance with #
local me = vec(Open77.players.position(source))
if #(me - vec(-1442.2, 127.4, 18.0)) < 10.0 then print("at the garage") end

name: vector2
summary: Builds a 2D vector: a plain { x, y } table with vector behaviour.
description: Available in both runtimes. Same operators, swizzles and methods as vector3, minus cross, which answers nil, "cross_requires_vector3". Takes two finite numbers, or one vector or { x =, y = } table to copy. Identical on both runtimes by construction: one file, scripting/lua/open77_vector.lua, is embedded by the client build and by the server assembly, so the semantics cannot drift.
example:
-- Distance on the map, ignoring height
local a = vector2(-1442.2, 127.4)
local b = vector2(-1448.2, 96.1)
print(("%.1f m apart on the map"):format(#(a - b)))

name: vector3
summary: Builds a 3D vector: a plain { x, y, z } table with vector behaviour.
description: Available in both runtimes, from the shared prelude scripting/lua/open77_vector.lua. Takes three finite numbers, or one vector or { x =, y =, z = } table to copy. The result IS a table with real x, y and z fields, so every API that accepts a position table accepts it unchanged and json.encode emits {"x":..,"y":..,"z":..}. Supports + - * / (by a vector, a position table or a number), unary minus, # for magnitude, == (exact, same kind only), tostring/.. as vector3(1.0, 2.0, 3.0), the swizzles .xy/.xz/.yz/.xyz/.zyx, and the methods length, lengthSquared, distance, distanceSquared, normalize (zero stays zero), dot, cross, lerp (unclamped), unpack and table. Fields are read-only except the components themselves, which Lua 5.4 cannot intercept. Operators raise; this constructor returns nil, reason. See the Vectors and quaternions guide. Identical on both runtimes by construction: one file, scripting/lua/open77_vector.lua, is embedded by the client build and by the server assembly, so the semantics cannot drift.
example:
-- Is the player within 10 m of the garage?
local garage = vector3(-1442.2, 127.4, 18.0)
local me = vector3(Open77.players.position(source))
if #(me - garage) < 10.0 then print("at the garage") end

name: vector4
summary: Builds a 4D vector: a plain { x, y, z, w } table with vector behaviour.
description: Available in both runtimes. Same operators and methods as vector3, minus cross. Its swizzles reach w, so v.xyz narrows a vector4 to a vector3. Takes four finite numbers, or one vector or { x =, y =, z =, w = } table to copy. Identical on both runtimes by construction: one file, scripting/lua/open77_vector.lua, is embedded by the client build and by the server assembly, so the semantics cannot drift.
example:
-- Carry a spawn point and its heading in one value
local spawn = vector4(-1442.2, 127.4, 18.0, 90.0)
Open77.players.respawn(playerId, { position = spawn.xyz, heading = spawn.w })

name: Await
summary: Waits for a promise; exactly promise:await().
description: Provided because ported code writes it this way. Anything that is not a promise answers nil, invalid_promise instead of raising, and the await itself needs a managed task: outside one it answers nil, await_requires_scheduler_coroutine rather than parking the tick.
returns: the resolved values, or nil, reason
example:
-- Await a server export promise, FiveM spelling
Citizen.CreateThread(function()
    local pending = Open77.exports.call("bank", "balance", playerId)
    local balance = Citizen.Await(pending)
    print("balance", balance)
end)

name: ClearTick
summary: Alias of ClearTick.
description: Citizen holds the very same function values the bare globals do, not copies, so a ported resource may use either spelling and a stack trace names the same function.
example:
-- Same function as ClearTick, FiveM spelling
local tick = Citizen.SetTick(function() checkZones() end)
AddEventHandler("event:ended", function() Citizen.ClearTick(tick) end)

name: ClearTimeout
summary: Alias of ClearTimeout.
description: Citizen holds the very same function values the bare globals do, not copies, so a ported resource may use either spelling and a stack trace names the same function.
example:
-- Cancel the round timer when everyone left
local timer = Citizen.SetTimeout(60000, function() endRound() end)
AddEventHandler("arena:empty", function() Citizen.ClearTimeout(timer) end)

name: CreateThread
summary: Alias of CreateThread.
description: Citizen holds the very same function values the bare globals do, not copies, so a ported resource may use either spelling and a stack trace names the same function. Citizen.CreateThreadNow is deliberately absent: this scheduler starts a task on the next pass, and resuming one inline from inside a running task would reset that task's instruction counter and deadline mid-flight.
example:
-- A ported FiveM server loop runs unchanged
Citizen.CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        Citizen.Wait(60000)
        saveEverything()
    end
end)

name: SetTick
summary: Alias of SetTick.
description: Citizen holds the very same function values the bare globals do, not copies, so a ported resource may use either spelling and a stack trace names the same function. See SetTick for the task budget and the five-consecutive-failure cancellation.
example:
-- Per-tick work, FiveM spelling
Citizen.SetTick(function()
    for _, playerId in ipairs(Open77.players.all()) do checkZone(playerId) end
end)

name: SetTimeout
summary: Alias of SetTimeout.
description: Citizen holds the very same function values the bare globals do, not copies, so a ported resource may use either spelling and a stack trace names the same function.
example:
-- Respawn 8 seconds after death, FiveM spelling
Citizen.SetTimeout(8000, function() Open77.players.respawn(playerId, { position = hospital }) end)

name: Trace
summary: Writes to the resource log at debug level; the same function as Open77.log.debug.
description: FiveM's trace channel, mapped onto the log this resource already writes to. It is not a separate sink and has no separate filter.
example:
-- Debug-level log line, FiveM spelling
Citizen.Trace("player", source, "bought", itemId)

name: Wait
summary: Alias of Wait.
description: Citizen holds the very same function values the bare globals do, not copies, so a ported resource may use either spelling and a stack trace names the same function. Only usable inside a managed task, and never inside a cancellable event handler, which runs inline during the host drain.
example:
-- A countdown in chat
Citizen.CreateThread(function()
    for n = 3, 1, -1 do
        Open77.chat.broadcast(("%d..."):format(n))
        Citizen.Wait(1000)
    end
end)

name: await
summary: Waits for the event to have been offered to every resource, then answers the verdict.
description: Settles one tick after publication. Needs a managed coroutine -- a CreateThread, a command or an event handler -- and answers false, await_requires_scheduler_coroutine outside one rather than blocking the server tick.
returns: true when a handler cancelled, false otherwise
false, reason outside a managed coroutine
example:
local verdict = TriggerCancellableEvent("chatMessage", source, name, text)
if verdict ~= nil and verdict:await() then return end

name: canceled
summary: The verdict itself, once it has settled.
description: Answers nil plus the status while the event is still in flight, so a caller that must not yield can poll instead of awaiting. True means some handler, in this resource or another, called CancelEvent.
example:
-- Poll the verdict from a tick instead of awaiting it
local verdict = TriggerCancellableEvent("shop:beforeBuy", source, itemId)
SetTick(function()
    local cancelled = verdict and verdict:canceled()
    if cancelled ~= nil then
        if not cancelled then sell(source, itemId) end
        verdict = nil
    end
end)

name: status
summary: Whether the verdict has settled, without waiting.
description: `pending` while the host is still offering the event to the other resources, `settled` once every running resource has been given it, `unknown` when the handle has been released or has expired. A verdict nobody reads is forgotten 30 seconds after it settles.
example:
-- Is the verdict in yet?
local verdict = TriggerCancellableEvent("shop:beforeBuy", source, itemId)
print(verdict and verdict:status()) -- "pending" until the next tick

name: await
summary: Waits for the promise to settle and returns its values.
description: Needs a managed coroutine; outside one it answers nil, await_requires_scheduler_coroutine instead of blocking the server tick. Returns the callee's values on success and nil, reason on rejection, so a caller never has to pcall it.
returns: the resolved values, or nil, reason
example:
-- Await a bank export from another resource
CreateThread(function()
    local pending = Open77.exports.call("bank", "balance", playerId)
    local balance, reason = pending and pending:await()
    print(balance or reason)
end)

name: next
summary: Schedules a continuation for when the promise settles.
description: Not chainable: it returns the id of the task it schedules, not a new promise, so p:next(a):next(b) does not work and sequences belong in a CreateThread with :await(). A rejection is recognised by shape -- the nil, <string reason> pair :await() returns for one -- which is this codebase's failure convention everywhere, so a promise deliberately resolved with a leading nil followed by a string reads as rejected. Answers nil, invalid_promise_handler for a non-function and nil, task_limit_or_stopping when no task slot is available.
example:
-- Continue when the client answers, without a thread
local pending = Open77.net.callClient(playerId, "confirmPurchase", "ammo_box", 50)
if pending then
    pending:next(function(confirmed) if confirmed then sell(playerId, "ammo_box") end end)
end

name: reject
summary: Settles a promise you created with promise.new as failed.
description: Same shape and same refusals as resolve. A non-string reason becomes promise_rejected, because the reason has to survive as text for the awaiter's nil, reason pair to mean anything.
example:
-- A promise this resource created is rejected when the timer runs out
local answer = promise.new()
SetTimeout(10000, function() answer:reject("timeout") end)

name: resolve
summary: Settles a promise you created with promise.new, with the values the awaiter receives.
description: Only a promise this resource created can be settled by hand: one returned by Open77.exports.call or Open77.net.callClient answers false, promise_not_local, and settling twice answers false, promise_already_settled. Values are passed through untouched on the server, where the client copies them across a serialization boundary.
example:
-- Resolve a promise you created when the database answers
local ready = promise.new()
Open77.database.ready(function() ready:resolve(true) end)
CreateThread(function() print("db ready:", ready:await()) end)

name: status
summary: State of the promise, without waiting.
description: The one handle type covers both an export call and a question asked of a client, so the same four states describe either.
example:
-- Poll a client question from a tick
SetTick(function()
    if pending and pending:status() ~= "pending" then
        print("answered:", pending:status())
        pending = nil
    end
end)

name: cancel
summary: Cancels this resource's in-flight ability action, keeping the entitlement.
description: Requires `players.abilities.manage`. Use it to interrupt a slam in progress without taking the ability away; `revoke` does both.
example:
-- Entering a safe zone interrupts a slam in progress but keeps the ability
RegisterNetEvent("safezone:entered", function()
    Open77.abilities.cancel(source)
end)

name: current
summary: The player's current ability projection snapshot.
description: Requires `players.abilities.read`. Reports what the server believes the client is projecting, which is admission state rather than proof of a rendered animation.
example:
-- Is the player mid-slam?
local snapshot = Open77.abilities.current(playerId)
if snapshot and snapshot.active then print("slam phase", snapshot.phase) end

name: define
summary: Registers a server-owned ability definition for this resource.
description: Requires `players.abilities.define`. The definition names the ability and its native parameters; grants later refer to it by id. Definitions belong to the declaring resource, so a reload republishes them. See the [ground slam guide](ground-slam.md) for the definition fields and the projection contract.

name: grant
summary: Grants a defined ability to one player.
description: Requires `players.abilities.manage`. Acceptance is entitlement, not rendering: native projection on the target client can still be pending when this returns. Only the granting resource may revoke or cancel it.
example:
-- Give the ability to whoever buys the implant
RegisterNetEvent("shop:buySlam", function()
    local result, reason = Open77.abilities.grant(source, "myserver.quake")
    if not result then Open77.chat.send(source, "Not granted: " .. reason) end
end)

name: revoke
summary: Removes this resource's ability grant from a player and cancels its action.
description: Requires `players.abilities.manage`. Scoped to the calling resource: another resource's grant on the same player is untouched. Resource stop revokes automatically.
example:
-- Take the ability away when the player is arrested
Open77.abilities.revoke(playerId)

name: allow
summary: Adds an identity to the built-in whitelist.
description: Requires `players.access`. The optional label is operator-facing text shown beside the entry in the console and the admin panel; it is not an identity.
example:
-- /whitelist add <userId> <label>
RegisterCommand("whitelist-add", function(source, args)
    Open77.access.allow(args[1], table.concat(args, " ", 2))
end, true)

name: ban
summary: Bans an identity on the built-in list and disconnects them if they are online.
description: Requires `players.access`. `seconds` nil or 0 makes the ban permanent. `name` is the display name recorded with the entry, so a later reader knows who was banned without resolving the identity again. Unlike `Open77.players.ban`, this writes the *server's own* list rather than submitting a device ban to the master.
example:
-- A one-day local ban from an in-game command
RegisterCommand("tempban", function(source, args)
    local target = tonumber(args[1])
    local identity = target and Open77.players.identity(target)
    if identity then Open77.access.ban(identity.userId, table.concat(args, " ", 2), 86400, identity.name) end
end, true)

name: disallow
summary: Takes an identity off the built-in whitelist.
description: Requires `players.access`. It does not disconnect a player who is already in: combine it with `Open77.players.kick` when that is the intent.
example:
-- Remove from the whitelist and kick if they are online
Open77.access.disallow(userId)
for _, playerId in ipairs(Open77.players.all()) do
    if Open77.players.identifier(playerId) == userId then Open77.players.kick(playerId, "Whitelist removed.") end
end

name: isAllowed
summary: Whether an identity is on the built-in whitelist.
description: Requires `players.access`. Reads the built-in list only; it does not consider a resource's own gate logic in `onPlayerConnecting`.
example:
-- Show a "VIP" tag in chat for whitelisted players
if Open77.access.isAllowed(userId) then name = "[VIP] " .. name end

name: isBanned
summary: Whether an identity is on the built-in ban list.
description: Requires `players.access`. An expired temporary ban reads as not banned.
example:
-- Refuse a friend invite to a banned account
if Open77.access.isBanned(friendUserId) then
    return Open77.chat.send(source, "That account is banned here.")
end

name: setWhitelist
summary: Turns the built-in whitelist on or off.
description: Requires `players.access`. While it is on, only identities returned by `status().whitelist` are admitted. The switch is persisted by the host, so it survives a resource reload and a restart.
example:
-- Lock the server to the whitelist during the event
RegisterCommand("private", function(source, args)
    Open77.access.setWhitelist(args[1] == "on")
end, true)

name: status
summary: The server's built-in whitelist and ban list.
description: Requires `players.access`. Returns `{ whitelistEnabled, whitelist = { { userId, label, addedAt, addedBy } }, bans = { { userId, name, reason, bannedAt, expiresAt?, bannedBy } } }` -- the same door list the console and Warden read and write, so a gamemode and an operator never disagree about who is allowed in.
example:
-- /bans: list the current bans
RegisterCommand("bans", function(source)
    local status = Open77.access.status()
    for _, ban in ipairs(status and status.bans or {}) do
        Open77.chat.send(source, ("%s: %s"):format(ban.name, ban.reason))
    end
end, true)

name: unban
summary: Lifts a ban on the built-in list.
description: Requires `players.access`. Lifting a ban does not re-add the identity to the whitelist, which is a separate list.
example:
-- /unban <userId>
RegisterCommand("unban", function(source, args)
    if args[1] then Open77.access.unban(args[1]) end
end, true)

name: addRole
summary: Puts a user in an ACL role at runtime.
description: FiveM's `add_principal`. Requires `acl.grant:<pattern>`, and the check is on the role's **entire reach**, not on its name: every permission behind it must be inside the scope or the call is refused `role_exceeds_scope`. Without that rule a resource scoped to `job.police.*` would collect `command.*` by adding the operator's `moderator` role, which is the same escalation arriving one indirection later. The role may be one this resource defined with `definePermission` or one the operator defined in `acl.jsonc`. Idempotent. Shows up in `Open77.acl.roles`. Publishes `onAclChanged`.
returns: reason: role_exceeds_scope, role_not_defined, role_reserved, operator_principal, permission_denied:acl.grant, scope_not_delegable, invalid_user_id, invalid_role, runtime_acl_limit, acl_persistence_failed
example:
-- Promote a player to the "cop" role defined by this resource (needs acl.grant:job.police.*)
RegisterCommand("hire-cop", function(source, args)
    local identity = Open77.players.identity(tonumber(args[1]))
    if identity then Open77.acl.addRole(identity.userId, "cop") end
end, true)

name: definePermission
summary: Defines, retunes or deletes what a runtime ACL role may do.
description: FiveM's `add_ace` against a group. Requires the **second** capability, `acl.define:<pattern>`, because retuning a role changes the rights of everyone holding it at once and retroactively -- a resource that may promote people should not also decide what the promotion is worth. Every permission, and every permission the role *currently* holds, must be inside that scope. Passing nil or an empty list deletes the role and takes it off every subject holding it, rather than leaving a name that resolves to nothing. A role the operator defined in `acl.jsonc` is theirs: `role_defined_by_operator`. `owner` and `admin` are reserved. Publishes `onAclChanged`.

params.name: permissions
params.type: array of string, or nil to delete

returns: reason: permission_denied:acl.define, scope_not_delegable, permission_not_delegable, role_defined_by_operator, role_reserved, not_defined, invalid_role, invalid_permission, runtime_acl_limit, acl_persistence_failed
example:
-- Define what a cop may do (needs acl.define:job.police.*)
Open77.acl.definePermission("cop", { "job.police.arrest", "job.police.fine" })

name: grant
summary: Grants one permission to a user id at runtime, persisted.
description: Native-parity A12, FiveM's `add_ace`. Requires a scoped `acl.grant:<pattern>` in the manifest; there is no bare `acl.grant`, and `acl.grant:*` is not a wildcard scope but is dropped, leaving `scope_not_delegable`. The permission must fall inside one of the declared patterns or the call is refused `permission_not_delegable` -- that scope is the whole answer to whether a resource may grant a right it does not itself hold. The subject is a **master-issued userId**, the string `Open77.players.identity(playerId).userId` answers, never a playerId: a grant outlives the session that earned it. Writes to `acl.runtime.jsonc`, the machine-owned sibling of `acl.jsonc`, atomically through a temporary; the operator's own document is never touched and can never be reduced by this call. Takes effect on the very next `isAllowed`, with no reload. Idempotent. Publishes `onAclChanged`. See the [ACL guide](server-acl.md).
returns: reason: permission_denied:acl.grant, scope_not_delegable, permission_not_delegable, operator_principal, invalid_user_id, invalid_permission, runtime_acl_limit, acl_persistence_failed, acl_unavailable
example:
-- A single right for one account, persisted across sessions
local identity = Open77.players.identity(playerId)
Open77.acl.grant(identity.userId, "job.police.arrest")

name: grants
summary: What the runtime overlay holds for one user id.
description: Requires the existing `acl.read`. Answers `{ permissions = {}, roles = {} }`, with empty tables for a subject that has no runtime grant. It reports **only** what the resource layer granted at runtime and never a principal from the operator's `acl.jsonc`, so it widens nothing a per-permission `isAllowed` could not already answer. For the effective answer, which unions both layers, call `Open77.acl.isAllowed`.
example:
-- What did this resource layer give the player?
local grants = Open77.acl.grants(userId)
if grants then print(#grants.permissions, "permissions,", #grants.roles, "roles") end

name: isAllowed
summary: Whether a principal holds an ACL right on this server.
description: The same access-control list the console and restricted commands consult, exposed so a resource can make its own authorization decision with the operator's configuration rather than a hard-coded admin list. `RegisterCommand(name, handler, true)` already checks `command.<name>` through it.
example:
-- Only cops may use /arrest
RegisterCommand("arrest", function(source, args)
    if not Open77.acl.isAllowed(source, "job.police.arrest") then
        return Open77.chat.send(source, "You are not a cop.")
    end
    arrest(source, tonumber(args[1]))
end, false)

name: removeRole
summary: Takes a user out of a role the runtime put them in.
description: The same scope and the same `role_exceeds_scope` check as `addRole`. Removes only from the runtime overlay: a role assigned by the operator's own principal answers `operator_grant`, and one nobody assigned answers `not_granted`. Publishes `onAclChanged`.
returns: reason: operator_grant, not_granted, role_exceeds_scope, role_not_defined, permission_denied:acl.grant, scope_not_delegable, operator_principal, invalid_user_id, invalid_role, acl_persistence_failed
example:
-- Fired from the police
Open77.acl.removeRole(userId, "cop")

name: revoke
summary: Takes back a runtime permission grant.
description: FiveM's `remove_ace`. Same `acl.grant:<pattern>` scope and the same refusals as `grant`, so a resource cannot strip a right it could not have handed out -- which is what stops one resource tampering with another's job model. It removes only from the runtime overlay: a permission the operator wrote into `acl.jsonc` answers `operator_grant` rather than appearing to work, and one nobody granted answers `not_granted`. Publishes `onAclChanged`.
returns: reason: operator_grant, not_granted, permission_denied:acl.grant, scope_not_delegable, permission_not_delegable, operator_principal, invalid_user_id, invalid_permission, acl_persistence_failed
example:
-- Take a single right back
Open77.acl.revoke(userId, "job.police.arrest")

name: roles
summary: The ACL roles a principal holds.
description: Reads the server's configured role assignments. Roles are operator configuration, not player state: a resource should treat them as a policy input and still validate the gameplay preconditions of whatever it is about to do.
example:
-- Greet admins differently
AddEventHandler("onPlayerReady", function(playerId)
    for _, role in ipairs(Open77.acl.roles(playerId)) do
        if role == "admin" then Open77.chat.send(playerId, "Welcome back, admin.") end
    end
end)

name: clip
summary: Look up which RP profile owns a clip name.
description: Clip-first discovery, the counterpart of get(). Returns the owning profile table, or nil when no shipped device's authored tree carries that clip. Requires no capability, like list() and get(). Clip names are case-sensitive. An absent result is the answer, not an error: a name can appear in the game's discovery inventory and still be unaddressable here. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.
returns: Profile table, or nil when no shipped device carries the clip
example:
local profile = Open77.animations.clip('stand__dance__02__dancing__03')
print(profile and profile.id) -- dance

name: clips
summary: List every addressable clip with the profile that owns it.
description: The nearest equivalent this engine offers to enumerating an animation dictionary, and the discovery step before playClip(). Returns one row per clip, { clip = string, profile = string }, ordered by clip name. The optional query is a case-insensitive substring matched against both the clip name and the profile ID, at most 128 characters. Requires no capability. This is the complete addressable set, not a catalogue of what the game contains. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.
returns: nil, invalid_query when the query exceeds 128 characters
example:
for _, row in ipairs(Open77.animations.clips('dance') or {}) do
    print(row.profile, row.clip)
end

name: current
summary: Read a player's authoritative active RP playback state.
description: Requires players.animations.read. Returns the active state synchronously, or nil without an error when inactive. Fields include epoch, revision, playerId, playbackId, active, bucket, steps, loop, startedAtMs, serverTimeMs, cycle, step, elapsedMs and remainingMs. Timestamps are monotonic server time and step/cycle indices are zero-based. clientRequestId is internal correlation, not a cancellation token. State proves scheduling, not that a native clip rendered. Unlike client current(entity), this does not return a raw clip name. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.
returns: Active playback state, or nil when inactive
example:
local state, err = Open77.animations.current(playerId)
if err then print(err); return end
if state then print(state.playbackId, state.step, state.elapsedMs) end

name: get
summary: Read the definition and allowed clips of one RP profile.
description: No capability is required. Looks up an exact, case-sensitive profile ID such as smoke or phone. Returns nil without an error for an unknown profile. Use the returned clip and clips fields to construct a valid playback request instead of passing arbitrary game animation names. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.
returns: Profile table, or nil when absent
example:
local profile, err = Open77.animations.get('smoke')
if err then print(err); return end
if profile then print(profile.clip, #profile.clips) end

name: list
summary: Search the authoritative RP profile catalogue.
description: No capability is required. Returns profile definitions synchronously, not a Promise. Search is a case-insensitive substring across ID, label and category; the maximum query length is 128 characters. Empty search returns all 15 profiles and no match returns an empty array. Definitions include clip variants and rig metadata, which must not be mistaken for proof of native rendering. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.
example:
local profiles, err = Open77.animations.list('social')
if not profiles then print(err); return end
for _, profile in ipairs(profiles) do print(profile.id, profile.label) end

name: play
summary: Start a server-owned, synchronized RP action on a player.
description: Requires players.animations.control. The player must be ready, alive, on foot and have a known position. The calling resource VM generation owns the action; another resource cannot replace it. Options are clip, durationMs and loop only. loop defaults to true; omitted/zero duration is indefinite when looping. With loop=false the default is 5000 ms. Nonzero durations are integers from 1000 to 600000 ms; variants must belong to the profile. Returns authoritative acceptance, not proof of native mounting. The local view temporarily uses third person. Unlike the legacy client play(entity, rawClip), this method replicates a curated profile. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.

name: playClip
summary: Start a synchronized RP action on a player, addressed by clip name.
description: Requires players.animations.control and the same readiness, ownership and duration rules as play(); only the addressing differs. The owning profile is resolved from the generated catalogue, so the caller names the animation rather than the action that carries it. This is the closest honest analogue of FiveM's TaskPlayAnim. It is not 'play any clip': Cyberpunk plays a named clip only through a workspot bound into a device entity at asset-build time, so the addressable set is the 70 clips of the twelve shipped devices. A name outside it -- including a name from the 23,044-entry discovery inventory -- is refused with unknown_clip rather than started and ignored by the engine. Options are durationMs and loop only. blendIn, blendOut, upperBody, holdLastFrame, flags, dict and playbackRate are refused by name as unsupported_option:<key>, because an author porting a TaskPlayAnim call has to be able to see which concept is missing rather than assume a bad value. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.
returns: nil, unknown_clip | unsupported_option:<key> | invalid_duration | any play() rejection
example:
-- open77.lua: permission 'players.animations.control'
local playback, err = Open77.animations.playClip(
    playerId, 'stand__dance__02__dancing__03', { durationMs = 15000, loop = false })
if not playback then print(err); return end
print(playback.playbackId)

name: sequence
summary: Schedule a server-owned sequence of RP profiles for a player.
description: Requires players.animations.control and the same readiness and ownership checks as play(). Accepts 1–16 steps with profile, optional clip and durationMs. Each step defaults to 5000 ms and must last at least 1000 ms; the total cannot exceed 600000 ms. The only sequence option is loop, default false. Durations schedule server transitions and are not measured native clip lengths. Profile switches require workspot exit/re-entry and may not blend seamlessly. Server resource stop, player death, vehicle entry, movement or bucket changes cancel the action. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.

name: stop
summary: Stop an RP action owned by the calling server resource.
description: Requires players.animations.control. Omitting playbackId stops the current action owned by this VM generation; an action owned by another resource is refused. Pass the recorded ID in delayed callbacks so an old timer cannot stop a newer action: stale IDs return stale_playback. Stopping an already inactive player succeeds. The authoritative onPlayerAnimationChanged event carries the player ID string and JSON state string; native detachment may finish asynchronously on clients. This is not the client-local stop(entity) method. Provided directly by the server runtime; no animation resource export dependency is needed for this server call.
returns: true on success, including already inactive
example:
local playback, err = Open77.animations.play(playerId, 'smoke')
if not playback then print(err); return end
SetTimeout(10000, function()
    local stopped, reason = Open77.animations.stop(playerId, playback.playbackId)
    if not stopped then print(reason) end
end)

name: apply
summary: Restores a saved appearance snapshot on a player, without the client asking.
description: Asynchronous, and relayed exactly like `Open77.clothing`: the addressed client owns the REDengine player object, so the server asks and the client answers. Requires `players.appearance.relay` in the manifest AND `network.events`; the request is relayed to the official `open77_appearance` client package. Returns a request id prefixed with the resource name and an `appearance` segment, so an appearance answer can never complete a clothing or weapon request and only this resource's VM can match the completion. Listen for the resource-local `open77:appearance:relayCompleted` event with `playerId, requestId, operation, accepted, reason, result`; an unanswered request completes with `request_timeout` after ten seconds rather than leaving the caller waiting. The client refuses while its appearance is busy (`appearance_busy` -- an editor, the character creator or a fitting-room preview is open), before the player is in the world (`player_not_ready`) or after a failed restore (`appearance_restore_failed`). `players.appearance.relay` is a permission of its own, not a corner of `player.appearance.edit` (which is a client-side grant over the local player) or of clothing (garments a player can see and take off): a snapshot is the output of the character creator and the closest thing the platform holds to a likeness of the person playing. Nothing here writes a snapshot to a log. The snapshot must be the table `capture` returned. It does not reach the native layer behind `open77_appearance`'s back: it becomes that player's new appearance **record** -- the server's word about what they wear -- and the resource's ordinary reconciliation puts it on the body. That is the same road a stored appearance takes at world entry, so a relayed face survives death, a bucket change and a reload instead of being quietly undone by the next reconcile. It does **not** change the body family: a different family is a player *reload*, not an appearance change, and a snapshot whose gender disagrees with the body on the player is refused with `body_family_mismatch`. The platform's stored appearance row is not written -- a resource that wants the change to outlive the session owns that persistence itself. Completion is the client's acceptance, reported once the player is observed wearing the snapshot; `apply_timeout` means the record was set but the body had not settled in eight seconds, and `appearance_superseded` means a newer apply replaced it.
example:
-- Restore a saved look on a player who just spawned
RegisterNetEvent("character:loaded", function()
    local snapshot = savedLooks[Open77.players.identifier(source)]
    if snapshot then Open77.appearance.apply(source, snapshot) end
end)

name: capture
summary: Asks a player's client for its current appearance snapshot.
description: Asynchronous, and relayed exactly like `Open77.clothing`: the addressed client owns the REDengine player object, so the server asks and the client answers. Requires `players.appearance.relay` in the manifest AND `network.events`; the request is relayed to the official `open77_appearance` client package. Returns a request id prefixed with the resource name and an `appearance` segment, so an appearance answer can never complete a clothing or weapon request and only this resource's VM can match the completion. Listen for the resource-local `open77:appearance:relayCompleted` event with `playerId, requestId, operation, accepted, reason, result`; an unanswered request completes with `request_timeout` after ten seconds rather than leaving the caller waiting. The client refuses while its appearance is busy (`appearance_busy` -- an editor, the character creator or a fitting-room preview is open), before the player is in the world (`player_not_ready`) or after a failed restore (`appearance_restore_failed`). `players.appearance.relay` is a permission of its own, not a corner of `player.appearance.edit` (which is a client-side grant over the local player) or of clothing (garments a player can see and take off): a snapshot is the output of the character creator and the closest thing the platform holds to a likeness of the person playing. Nothing here writes a snapshot to a log. The result is `{ snapshot, family, revision, characterKey }`, where `snapshot` is the network form -- schema version, game build, catalogue digest, gender and the option identities and values -- with the editor's local metadata (editable/active/censored) stripped. It is the same shape `apply` takes, so a capture can be stored and handed straight back later.
example:
-- Ask the client for its look and store the answer
Open77.appearance.capture(playerId)
AddEventHandler("open77:appearance:relayCompleted", function(playerId, requestId, operation, accepted, reason, result)
    if operation == "capture" and accepted then savedLooks[Open77.players.identifier(playerId)] = result end
end)

name: destroy
summary: DestroySound: server-authoritative network package audio.
description: Requires audio.network; network=false is rejected. Server owns the timeline, handles and bucket/optional-target audience. Clients cannot request broadcasts directly. getState reports intended playback, not decoder acknowledgement. Assets must be declared in the resource manifest files; absolute paths, URLs and traversal are rejected. Handles are scoped to the creating resource VM; stop rewinds, pause preserves position, seek uses seconds, destroy releases permanently. Volume 0..1, range <=1000m. Network loops require actual duration. See package-audio.md for options, lifecycle, quotas and errors.
example:
-- Release the network handle
Open77.audio.destroy(concertId)

name: callClient
summary: Alias of Open77.net.callClient.
description: Asks one client a question and returns an Open77.Promise, or nil, reason when the request is refused before it leaves.
example:
-- Ask one client to confirm a purchase (alias of Open77.net.callClient)
CreateThread(function()
    local pending = Open77.callbacks.callClient(source, "confirmPurchase", "ammo_box", 50)
    local confirmed = pending and pending:await()
    if confirmed then sell(source, "ammo_box") end
end)

name: callClientAwait
summary: Alias of Open77.net.callClientAwait.
description: Awaits the promise, so it needs a CreateThread or another managed task.
returns: the client handler's return values, or nil, reason
example:
-- The same question, awaited in one line
CreateThread(function()
    local confirmed = Open77.callbacks.callClientAwait(source, "confirmPurchase", "ammo_box", 50)
    if confirmed then sell(source, "ammo_box") end
end)

name: register
summary: Alias of Open77.net.register.
description: Open77.callbacks is the same four callback functions under a second name, for resources that prefer to read the callback surface as its own namespace. Pick one spelling per resource; these are the same functions, not copies.
example:
-- Answer a client's question with the authenticated source (alias of Open77.net.register)
Open77.callbacks.register("getStock", function(source, item)
    return stock[item] or 0, prices[item]
end)

name: unregister
summary: Alias of Open77.net.unregister.
description: Stops answering that name; a later request is refused with callback_not_found on the next frame.
example:
-- The shop closed for the night: stop answering
Open77.callbacks.unregister("getStock")

name: addSuggestion
summary: Publishes one slash-command suggestion to a player's chat.
description: Facade over `chat:addSuggestion`. `target` is a playerId or -1 for everyone; `command` is the command text (for example "/tow"), `help` a one-line description, `parameters` a list of { name, help } tables. The suggestion list is also what the admin menu harvests.

name: addSuggestions
summary: Publishes a list of slash-command suggestions at once.
description: Facade over `chat:addSuggestions`. The list is an array of { command, help, parameters } tables. Usually sent from a `chat:ready` handler, when a player's chat UI comes up.

name: broadcast
summary: Sends a chat message to every player.
description: Exactly `Open77.chat.send(-1, message)`. Same asynchrony and same ordering caveat.
example:
-- The round is starting in 30 seconds
Open77.chat.broadcast("Round starts in 30 seconds!")

name: clear
summary: Clears a player's local chat history.
description: Facade over `chat:clear`. Presentation only -- it empties what that client is showing and deletes nothing on the server.
example:
-- Clear the chat of everyone in the arena at round start
for _, playerId in ipairs(Open77.players.inBucket(ARENA_BUCKET)) do
    Open77.chat.clear(playerId)
end

name: onMessage
summary: Observes every chat message the authority accepted.
description: Subscribes to `chat:message`, so the handler receives (playerId, playerName, text) AFTER the cancellable `chatMessage` veto has settled. It is therefore the wrong place to refuse a message: to do that, AddEventHandler('chatMessage', ...) and call CancelEvent(). Returns the handler id for RemoveEventHandler.
example:
-- Log every accepted chat line to the server console
Open77.chat.onMessage(function(playerId, playerName, text)
    print(("[chat] %s (%d): %s"):format(playerName, playerId, text))
end)

name: removeSuggestion
summary: Withdraws one slash-command suggestion.
description: Facade over `chat:removeSuggestion`. Use it when a command stops being available to that player rather than leaving a suggestion that will be refused.
example:
-- The player left the police job: /arrest disappears from their autocomplete
Open77.chat.removeSuggestion(playerId, "/arrest")

name: send
summary: Sends a chat message to one player, or to everyone with -1.
description: A thin facade over `chat:addMessage` on the host-wide event bus; `open77_chat` remains the only chat authority and does the actual push to clients. `message` is a plain string or the full table the chat UI renders ({ type, author, text, playerId, color = { r, g, b } }). Grants nothing: the facade never reaches a client itself, so it needs no `network.events`. Delivery is asynchronous -- it lands on the next tick boundary -- and two sends in the same tick arrive in the opposite order, because the resource scheduler collects ready tasks back to front. Put a `Wait(0)` between lines that must read in order. With no chat authority running the call still returns true, since the bus cannot tell a publisher that nobody listened.

name: clear
summary: Asks a player's client to empty every clothing slot.
description: Asynchronous, same relay and completion contract as the other clothing calls.
example:
-- Prison intake: strip every clothing slot
Open77.clothing.clear(prisonerId)

name: equip
summary: Asks a player's client to equip one clothing record.
description: Asynchronous. The calling resource must declare `network.events`; the request is relayed to the official `open77_equipment` client package. Returns a request id prefixed with the resource name -- only this resource's VM can match the completion. Listen for the resource-local `open77:clothing:completed` event with `playerId, requestId, operation, accepted, reason, result`; an unanswered request completes with `request_timeout` after ten seconds. Completion is acceptance by the client relay, not proof that other observers see the change.
example:
-- Give the new officer the uniform jacket
RegisterNetEvent("police:onDuty", function()
    Open77.clothing.equip(source, "Items.Jacket_01_basic_01")
end)

name: requestSnapshot
summary: Asks a player's client for its current clothing state.
description: Asynchronous. The completion event's `result` carries rows with `slot`, `attachmentSlot`, `equipped` and an optional `record`/`tweakDbId`. This is a read of the client's live registry, so it is the honest answer to "what is actually on them" after a write has settled.
example:
-- Ask the client what it really wears, and read the completion
Open77.clothing.requestSnapshot(playerId)
AddEventHandler("open77:clothing:completed", function(playerId, requestId, operation, accepted, reason, result)
    if operation == "snapshot" and accepted then print(json.encode(result)) end
end)

name: set
summary: Applies a whole slot-to-record wardrobe to a player in one request.
description: Asynchronous, same relay and completion contract. `wardrobe` maps slot to record, for example `{ outer_chest = "Items.Jacket_01_basic_01" }`; `false` empties a slot and an omitted slot is left unchanged. An active wardrobe outfit on the client can hide what this equips.

name: unequip
summary: Asks a player's client to empty one clothing slot.
description: Asynchronous, same relay, same completion event and ten-second timeout as `equip`. Slot names follow the relay's equipment registry.
example:
-- Confiscate the helmet
Open77.clothing.unequip(playerId, "head")

name: createScope
summary: Enable scoped PvP for an explicit ready roster.
description: Requires combat.scope.control. definition={bucket,players={...}} accepts2..32 unique positive player IDs currently combat-capable in that bucket; a player belongs to at most one scope. Limits64 scopes globally/8 per resource. Scope can permit PvP while global PvP is off but keeps team, life, invulnerability and Lua veto rules. Stop/disconnect/bucket changes remove ownership/participants. Creator must enforce opt-in; no automatic team or bucket change occurs.
example:
local scope, err = Open77.combat.createScope({bucket=arenaBucket,players={firstPlayer,secondPlayer}})
if not scope then print(err); return end
-- Retain scope for teardown.

name: offDamage
summary: Removes a previously installed damage arbiter.
description: Requires `combat.config`. Pass the value `onDamage` returned. Removing a handler that is not installed is a no-op.
example:
-- The "double damage" event is over: remove the arbiter
local arbiter = Open77.combat.onDamage(function(event) return event.amount * 2 end)
AddEventHandler("event:ended", function()
    Open77.combat.offDamage(arbiter)
end)

name: onDamage
summary: Installs a synchronous damage arbiter and returns it.
description: Requires `combat.config`. The handler receives one event table `{ victim, attacker, amount, attackKind, bodyPart, weaponTdbId, distance }` for every candidate damage application. Returning `false` cancels the damage and the first refusal wins; returning a number rewrites the amount for the arbiters that follow; anything else leaves it alone. Handlers run inside a `pcall`, so one that raises is skipped rather than dropping the hit. Keep the body short: this runs on the server tick, in the damage path.
returns: the handler, so it can be stored for offDamage

name: removeScope
summary: Remove this resource's scoped PvP permission.
description: Requires combat.scope.control. Accepts the32-character scope ID returned by createScope. Does not alter global PvP or revive/teleport participants. Missing or foreign scopes fail; ordinary combat policy applies after removal.
example:
-- The duel is over: drop the scoped PvP permission
AddEventHandler("duel:ended", function()
    local ok, err = Open77.combat.removeScope(duelScope)
    if not ok then print(err) end
end)

name: setDamageMultiplier
summary: Scales every damage application on the server.
description: Requires `combat.config`. Range 0 to 100; `0` makes the server effectively damage-free without touching god mode. Applied before the headshot, weapon and kind multipliers.
example:
-- /dmg <factor>: an admin halves or doubles all damage for the round
RegisterCommand("dmg", function(source, args)
    local factor = tonumber(args[1])
    if factor then Open77.combat.setDamageMultiplier(factor) end
end, true)

name: setFriendlyFire
summary: Enables or disables global player-versus-player damage.
description: Requires `combat.config`. Players carrying the same nonzero team remain protected even when friendly fire is on, so a team mode does not have to arbitrate every hit itself. For a duel between two named players while global PvP stays off, use `createScope` instead.
example:
-- PvP is on everywhere on this server
Open77.combat.setFriendlyFire(true)

name: setHeadshotMultiplier
summary: Scales damage from hits on the head.
description: Requires `combat.config`. Range 0 to 100. Combines with the global multiplier rather than replacing it.
example:
-- A "one in the head" round: headshots do five times the damage
Open77.combat.setHeadshotMultiplier(5)

name: setKindDamageMultiplier
summary: Overrides the damage of one attack kind.
description: Requires `combat.config`. Kinds are `ranged`, `melee` and `explosion`, range 0 to 100. Useful for a melee-only round without removing weapons from anyone.
example:
-- Fists-only round: guns and explosions do nothing, melee does double
Open77.combat.setKindDamageMultiplier("ranged", 0)
Open77.combat.setKindDamageMultiplier("explosion", 0)
Open77.combat.setKindDamageMultiplier("melee", 2)

name: setTeam
summary: Assigns a player to a combat team.
description: Requires `combat.config`. Team ids are non-negative; `0` means no team. Two players on the same nonzero team never damage each other, whatever the friendly-fire setting.
example:
-- Split the arena players into two teams; team-mates cannot hurt each other
for i, playerId in ipairs(Open77.players.inBucket(ARENA_BUCKET)) do
    Open77.combat.setTeam(playerId, (i % 2) + 1)
end

name: setWeaponDamageMultiplier
summary: Overrides the damage of one weapon record.
description: Requires `combat.config`. Range 0 to 100, keyed by the weapon's TweakDB id, so a single gun can be tuned without rebalancing everything.
example:
-- The Lexington is a training pistol here: a quarter of its damage
Open77.combat.setWeaponDamageMultiplier("Items.Preset_Lexington_Default", 0.25)

name: get
summary: Namespaced spelling of `GetConvar`.
description: The same function value.
example:
-- Namespaced spelling of GetConvar
local webhook = Open77.convars.get("myshop_webhook", "")

name: getBool
summary: Namespaced spelling of `GetConvarBool`.
description: The same function value.
example:
-- Namespaced spelling of GetConvarBool
Open77.combat.setFriendlyFire(Open77.convars.getBool("myserver_pvp", false))

name: getInt
summary: Namespaced spelling of `GetConvarInt`.
description: The same function value.
example:
-- Namespaced spelling of GetConvarInt
local startingMoney = Open77.convars.getInt("myserver_starting_money", 500)

name: set
summary: Namespaced spelling of `SetConvar`.
description: The same function value.
example:
-- Namespaced spelling of SetConvar
Open77.convars.set("myserver_maintenance", true)

name: activity
summary: Read fresh authoritative Gorilla charge activity.
description: Requires players.cyberware.read. Returns {player,incarnation,sequence,armed,holding,charged,chargeExpired,holdAt,elapsedMs,remainingMs,maxChargeMs,definition,grade}. Null for unavailable/stale (over1500ms) body/implant activity. Values drive presentation, not an extra permission to commit damage. Hold expiry latches until release/new swing.
example:
local activity = Open77.cyberware.activity(playerId)
if activity and activity.holding then print(activity.remainingMs) end

name: bind
summary: Bind the authenticated player to a server-selected durable character.
description: Requires players.cyberware.identity. The user UUID comes from the connection; only the character key is supplied. Identity ownership is exclusive to a resource. Starts asynchronous database/native restoration; success is not readiness. Prefer the shipped appearance identity adapter and never accept an unvalidated client-selected character key.
example:
-- In a trusted identity adapter after server-side character selection:
local result, err = Open77.cyberware.bind(playerId, "default")
if not result then print(err) end

name: cancel
summary: Cancel an owned installation/removal before durable commit.
description: Requires players.cyberware.manage. Supply the ticket from the same resource's operation. Native staging is rolled back; an already submitted storage transaction returns operation_committing and completes normally. Never refund irrevocably until the correlated operation outcome is known.
example:
local result, err = Open77.cyberware.cancel(playerId, ticket)
if not result then print(err) end

name: current
summary: Read the ready durable implant record.
description: Requires players.cyberware.read. Returned synchronously, not a Promise. Record fields are revision, arms and operationId; arms includes instanceId, definition, definitionVersion, profile, slot and the committed grade snapshot. Returns nil while loading/projecting/failed. An empty arms value means no installed implant. Temporary arena overlays do not overwrite this record. A ready record does not imply its definition provider is running.
returns: record table, or nil when not ready
example:
local record, err = Open77.cyberware.current(playerId)
if record then print(record.revision, record.arms and record.arms.definition) elseif err then print(err) end

name: define
summary: Register resource-owned Gorilla Arms grades.
description: Requires players.cyberware.define. definition={id,version,slot="arms",profile="gorilla_arms",grades={...}}. IDs use1..96 ASCII alphanumeric/_.:- characters; version positive;1..32 unique grades. Required grade fields: id,normalDamage/chargedDamage(0..300),knockbackMeters(0..6),cooldownMs(100..600000),chargeMs(100..10000). Optional normalKnockbackMeters defaults to35% of charged, maxChargeMs defaults10000 and must be>=chargeMs and<=60000; nullable normalStaminaCost/chargedStaminaCost0..300 retain native price when omitted. nonlethal/cosmetic defaultfalse; blockDamageMultiplier0..1 default0 and blockAngleDegrees0..180 default45. Stop unregisters the provider and disables its grants without deleting paid records.

name: effective
summary: Read the ready implant including an active temporary loadout.
description: Requires players.cyberware.read. Returned synchronously, not a Promise. Record fields are revision, arms and operationId; arms includes instanceId, definition, definitionVersion, profile, slot and the committed grade snapshot. An active lease overlays arms; durable revision/operationId retain their base meaning. Pending/restoring projections return nil. Use current() for paid storage identity and effective() for ready presentation/gameplay loadout.
example:
local record = Open77.cyberware.effective(playerId)
if record and record.arms then print(record.arms.grade.id) end

name: install
summary: Stage a durable Gorilla Arms installation.
description: Requires players.cyberware.manage. options requires expectedRevision and operationId. Compare-and-swap and receipt storage are atomic; reuse the same ID/contents on retries. Native projection occurs before commit. Completion is asynchronous via onCyberwareOperationCompleted(playerId,ticket,encodedResult), correlated by ticket; retain the pending operation until final outcome. Rejected/failed work restores the prior paid record. Server makers own consent, costs and progression.
returns: {ok=true,ticket=string,...}; ticket may be absent on a completed idempotent replay
example:
local record = Open77.cyberware.current(playerId)
if not record then return end
local operationId, err = Open77.cyberware.newOperationId()
if not operationId then print(err); return end
local result, rejected = Open77.cyberware.install(playerId, "myrp.gorilla", "training", {
 expectedRevision=record.revision,operationId=operationId
})
if not result then print(rejected) else print(result.ticket) end

name: lease
summary: Stage a temporary implant without overwriting paid state.
description: Requires players.cyberware.temporary. options.durationMs is1000..300000, default300000. Requires a ready bound character and registered definition/grade. pending→active only after native acknowledgement. Wait for the matching onCyberwareLeaseChanged state before admitting PvP. Owner stop, body/bucket change, expiry or disconnect releases the overlay; native restoration remains asynchronous.
example:
local result, err = Open77.cyberware.lease(playerId, "myrp.gorilla", "training", {durationMs=60000})
if not result then print(err); return end
-- Keep result.lease; wait for its matching active event before PvP.

name: leaseState
summary: Read a temporary loadout lease and restoration phase.
description: Requires players.cyberware.read. Returns {id,player,phase,definition,grade,expiresAt,ticket,reason}, or nil when none exists. Phases pending/active/restoring/failed; ended is an event state, then the read becomes nil. expiresAt is server-monotonic milliseconds. Wait for nil AND current() ready before another lease.
example:
local state = Open77.cyberware.leaseState(playerId)
if state then print(state.id, state.phase) end

name: newOperationId
summary: Create an operation ID to retain across durable retries.
description: Requires players.cyberware.manage. Returns a32-character GUID string. Store it with the pending operation and reuse the same ID, expectedRevision and contents when retrying; generating a new ID per retry loses receipt idempotency. This does not start a transaction.
example:
local operationId, err = Open77.cyberware.newOperationId()
if not operationId then print(err); return end
-- Persist operationId with the intended mutation before submitting it.

name: releaseLease
summary: Release this resource's temporary loadout and restore paid arms.
description: Requires players.cyberware.temporary. Works during pending/active; repeated restoration requests return the same ticket. Lease id and resource owner must match. An ended event due to body loss alone is not proof of native paid restoration: wait for no lease and a ready current record.
example:
local result, err = Open77.cyberware.releaseLease(playerId, leaseId)
if not result then print(err) end

name: remove
summary: Stage a durable Gorilla Arms removal.
description: Requires players.cyberware.manage. options requires expectedRevision and operationId. Compare-and-swap and receipt storage are atomic; reuse the same ID/contents on retries. Native projection occurs before commit. Completion is asynchronous via onCyberwareOperationCompleted(playerId,ticket,encodedResult), correlated by ticket; retain the pending operation until final outcome. Rejected/failed work restores the prior paid record. Server makers own consent, costs and progression.
returns: {ok=true,ticket=string,...}; ticket may be absent on a completed idempotent replay
example:
local record = Open77.cyberware.current(playerId)
if not record then return end
local operationId, err = Open77.cyberware.newOperationId()
if not operationId then print(err); return end
local result, rejected = Open77.cyberware.remove(playerId, {
 expectedRevision=record.revision,operationId=operationId
})
if not result then print(rejected) else print(result.ticket) end

name: unbind
summary: Release this resource's character binding and runtime grants.
description: Requires players.cyberware.identity. Does not delete durable implants. Stops current projection/temporary ownership and prevents stale acknowledgements from restoring the old grant. Another owner cannot unbind the character.
example:
-- The character logged out: release the binding and its runtime grants
AddEventHandler("onPlayerDisconnected", function(playerId)
    Open77.cyberware.unbind(playerId)
end)

name: cancel
summary: Cancels a player's active Dash by its activation id.
description: Requires `players.dash.manage`. Cancellation keeps bounded server movement ownership during native recovery, until the correlated native-exit acknowledgement or a 1500 ms deadline; `current().phase` reports `recovering` in that window. The charge and stamina spent on acceptance are not refunded.
example:
-- The player entered a safe zone mid-dash
RegisterNetEvent("safezone:entered", function()
    local activity = Open77.dash.current(source)
    if activity and activity.activation then Open77.dash.cancel(source, activity.activation) end
end)

name: capabilities
summary: Reports the supported Dash profile and implementation limits.
description: Requires `players.dash.read`. The one `profile` (`dash`), the configuration bounds `define` enforces, the presentation presets and the movement model. Read it to build a definition editor rather than hard-coding the table in [Dash / Air Dash](dash.md).
example:
-- Read the bounds before building a definition editor
local caps = Open77.dash.capabilities()
if caps then print(caps.profile) end

name: current
summary: Reads a player's Dash activity and projection state.
description: Requires `players.dash.read`. Answers `{ projection, charges, cooldownUntil, nextChargeAt, airUsed, activation, phase, ownedByCaller }` -- times in server monotonic milliseconds -- or `nil` when the player holds no Dash. `ownedByCaller` is server-derived and stays accurate across projection restarts; a definition id or revision alone is not proof of ownership.
returns: activity table, or nil when absent
example:
-- Only present the dash key once the projection is ready
local activity = Open77.dash.current(playerId)
if activity and activity.projection.status == "ready" then
    TriggerClientEvent("dash:ready", playerId)
end

name: define
summary: Registers an immutable, versioned Dash definition owned by this resource.
description: Requires `players.dash.define`. `definition` is `{ id, version, profile = "dash", config }`; `config` takes `inputKey`, `allowGround`, `allowAir`, `requireDoubleJump`, `movementProfile = "native"`, `presentation` (`native` | `silent` | `none`), `staminaCost` (0..300), `cooldownMs` (300..600000), `maxCharges` (1..3), `chargeRegenMs`, `landingRearmMs` (150..1000), `maxAirborneMs` (100..10000) and `maxFallSpeed` (0.1..30). Speed, distance and immunity are not configurable. Ownership comes from the resource, never from a supplied owner name. See [Dash / Air Dash](dash.md).
example:
assert(Open77.dash.define({ id = "myserver.air_dash", version = 1, profile = "dash",
  config = { inputKey = "ctrl", allowGround = false, allowAir = true, staminaCost = 20,
    cooldownMs = 700, maxCharges = 1, chargeRegenMs = 2500, maxFallSpeed = 30 } }))

name: grant
summary: Grants a player this resource's Dash capability and starts its native projection.
description: Requires `players.dash.manage`. A success means pending native work, not a usable Dash: read `current(player).projection.status == "ready"` before presenting it. Grants require the authenticated cyberware character binding and an alive, ready, unmounted body. They are session capabilities -- no implant is purchased or replaced -- and cooldown or charge debt survives revoke and regrant within the session.
example:
-- The player bought the dash implant
RegisterNetEvent("shop:buyDash", function()
    local result, reason = Open77.dash.grant(source, "myserver.dash")
    if not result then Open77.chat.send(source, "Not granted: " .. reason) end
end)

name: revoke
summary: Removes this resource's Dash grant from a player.
description: Requires `players.dash.manage`. Only the calling resource's capability is removed; another resource's grant and every installed implant stay. Charge and cooldown debt are retained for the session.
example:
-- Arrested: no more dashing
Open77.dash.revoke(playerId)

name: item
summary: Looks up an `Items.*` clothing or item record in the shipped 2.31 catalogue.
description: No permission required; this is static game data. A `record` is a **TweakDB string**, never a Jenkins hash -- the same choice the `Citizen` alias layer's `GetHashKey` already made, and a resource ported from FiveM must expect it. The server answers from a reduced catalogue embedded in the host and parsed lazily on first use; a **client** answers the same call from the live TweakDB, in the player's own language. Read `source` to tell them apart: `catalogue` here, `tweakdb` there. A field that could only be derived says so -- `seatsSource` of `class` on a vehicle means the seat count came from the chassis class in the record name, because no repository source holds a real one. An unknown record fails with `record_unknown`. See [Game data catalogues](data-catalogues.md).
returns: { record, kind, source, build, ... }, or nil
example:
-- Validate a shop entry against the shipped catalogue at startup
for _, entry in ipairs(shopItems) do
    assert(Open77.data.item(entry.record), "unknown item " .. entry.record)
end

name: localize
summary: Refused on the server: localisation only exists inside the game.
description: Always answers `nil, "localization_client_only"`. The locale tables live in the game's own resources, which a dedicated server does not have, and handing back the key would let it pass for a translation. Send the row's `localeKey` to a client and call `Open77.data.localize` there. See [Game data catalogues](data-catalogues.md).
example:
-- Always refused on the server: send the key to the client instead
local text, reason = Open77.data.localize("LocKey#12345") -- nil, "localization_client_only"
TriggerClientEvent("ui:localize", playerId, "LocKey#12345")

name: npc
summary: Looks up an NPC entity template path in the shipped 2.31 catalogue.
description: No permission required; this is static game data. A `record` is a **TweakDB string**, never a Jenkins hash -- the same choice the `Citizen` alias layer's `GetHashKey` already made, and a resource ported from FiveM must expect it. The server answers from a reduced catalogue embedded in the host and parsed lazily on first use; a **client** answers the same call from the live TweakDB, in the player's own language. Read `source` to tell them apart: `catalogue` here, `tweakdb` there. A field that could only be derived says so -- `seatsSource` of `class` on a vehicle means the seat count came from the chassis class in the record name, because no repository source holds a real one. An unknown record fails with `record_unknown`. See [Game data catalogues](data-catalogues.md).
returns: { record, kind, source, build, ... }, or nil
example:
-- Check a spawn request against the catalogue before creating the NPC
local info = Open77.data.npc(record)
if not info then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Unknown character record.") end

name: vehicle
summary: Looks up a `Vehicle.*` record in the shipped 2.31 catalogue.
description: No permission required; this is static game data. A `record` is a **TweakDB string**, never a Jenkins hash -- the same choice the `Citizen` alias layer's `GetHashKey` already made, and a resource ported from FiveM must expect it. The server answers from a reduced catalogue embedded in the host and parsed lazily on first use; a **client** answers the same call from the live TweakDB, in the player's own language. Read `source` to tell them apart: `catalogue` here, `tweakdb` there. A field that could only be derived says so -- `seatsSource` of `class` on a vehicle means the seat count came from the chassis class in the record name, because no repository source holds a real one. An unknown record fails with `record_unknown`. See [Game data catalogues](data-catalogues.md).
returns: { record, kind, source, build, ... }, or nil
example:
-- The dealership only sells records the catalogue knows, and prices by class
local car = Open77.data.vehicle("Vehicle.v_sport2_quadra_turbo_r")
if car then print(car.classLabel, car.seats) end

name: weapon
summary: Looks up an `Items.*` weapon record in the shipped 2.31 catalogue.
description: No permission required; this is static game data. A `record` is a **TweakDB string**, never a Jenkins hash -- the same choice the `Citizen` alias layer's `GetHashKey` already made, and a resource ported from FiveM must expect it. The server answers from a reduced catalogue embedded in the host and parsed lazily on first use; a **client** answers the same call from the live TweakDB, in the player's own language. Read `source` to tell them apart: `catalogue` here, `tweakdb` there. A field that could only be derived says so -- `seatsSource` of `class` on a vehicle means the seat count came from the chassis class in the record name, because no repository source holds a real one. An unknown record fails with `record_unknown`. See [Game data catalogues](data-catalogues.md).
returns: { record, kind, source, build, ... }, or nil
example:
-- Refuse an unknown weapon record before giving it to the player
if not Open77.data.weapon(record) then return Open77.chat.send(source, "No such weapon.") end

name: insert
summary: Runs an INSERT and returns the inserted id.
description: Requires `database.access`. Same callback and `.await` forms as `query`.
example:
-- Create the player's row on first join and keep the id
CreateThread(function()
    local id = Open77.database.insert.await("INSERT INTO players (identifier, name) VALUES (?, ?)", { identifier, name })
    print("new player row", id)
end)

name: isReady
summary: Whether the database has answered yet.
description: Requires `database.access`. `true` once the host's probe has opened a connection and got an answer out of it; otherwise `false` and the reason -- `database_connecting` while the first connection is still being attempted, `database_unreachable` for a database that is configured but not answering (still retried), `database_unavailable` for a server that has no database bridge at all, and `permission_denied:database.access` for a resource that may not query one. Readiness is one-way: a later outage surfaces as a failing request, not as un-readiness, because every request already reports its own failure.
example:
-- Refuse the shop until the database answers
RegisterCommand("shop", function(source)
    local ready, reason = Open77.database.isReady()
    if not ready then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Shop unavailable: " .. reason) end
    openShop(source)
end, false)

name: prepare
summary: Alias of `Open77.database.query`.
description: Requires `database.access`. Present for oxmysql compatibility: `prepare` and `query` are the same function, so an ported resource that calls one behaves exactly as one that calls the other.
example:
-- oxmysql-style code works unchanged (await needs a managed task: a thread, a command or an event handler)
RegisterCommand("mycars", function(source)
    local rows = Open77.database.prepare.await("SELECT plate FROM vehicles WHERE owner = ?", { Open77.players.identifier(source) })
    Open77.chat.send(source, ("You own %d cars"):format(#rows))
end, false)

name: query
summary: Runs a SQL query and returns every row.
description: Requires `database.access`. `Open77.database` and the global `MySQL` are the same oxmysql-compatible table. Two forms: pass a callback, or use `Open77.database.query.await(sql, params?)` from a managed coroutine. Either way the continuation resumes on the owning resource's scheduler, never on the database worker, so the rest of the resource's state is safe to touch. `prepare` is an alias.
example:
-- Every car the player owns
CreateThread(function()
    local rows = Open77.database.query.await("SELECT plate, props FROM vehicles WHERE owner = ?", { identifier })
    for _, row in ipairs(rows) do print(row.plate) end
end)

name: rawExecute
summary: Alias of `Open77.database.update`.
description: Requires `database.access`. Present for oxmysql compatibility; it is the same function as `update`, not a way around parameter binding.
example:
-- oxmysql-style code works unchanged
RegisterNetEvent("garage:sell", function(plate)
    Open77.database.rawExecute.await("DELETE FROM vehicles WHERE plate = ? AND owner = ?", { plate, Open77.players.identifier(source) })
end)

name: ready
summary: Runs a handler once the database is reachable, or refuses when it never will be.
description: Requires `database.access`. oxmysql's boot gate: register schema creation or a migration here rather than racing it against the first connection. `ready` distinguishes three states a boolean would hide. A server with **no database configured** answers `false, "database_unavailable"` and the handler never runs -- the connection it would promise will never come. A database still connecting, or configured but **not answering**, queues the handler and keeps polling, so one that comes up late still fires. And a handler registered **after** readiness runs anyway, on the next tick, so a resource never has to ask whether it missed the moment. Handlers always run on this resource's own scheduler, never on the database worker. Refusals: `invalid_argument`, `database_unavailable`, `permission_denied:database.access`.
returns: true when the handler was run or queued, or false

name: scalar
summary: Runs a SQL query and returns one value.
description: Requires `database.access`. The first column of the first row -- a count, a sum, an id. Same callback and `.await` forms as `query`.
example:
-- One value: the player's money
RegisterCommand("balance", function(source)
