    local money = Open77.database.scalar.await("SELECT money FROM players WHERE identifier = ?", { Open77.players.identifier(source) })
    Open77.chat.send(source, ("Balance: %d eddies"):format(money or 0))
end, false)

name: single
summary: Runs a SQL query and returns its first row.
description: Requires `database.access`. Same callback and `.await` forms as `query`; answers `nil` when nothing matched, which is the difference from `query` returning an empty table.
example:
-- One row, or nil when the player is unknown
AddEventHandler("onPlayerReady", function(playerId)
    local identifier = Open77.players.identifier(playerId)
    local row = Open77.database.single.await("SELECT * FROM players WHERE identifier = ?", { identifier })
    if not row then createPlayer(identifier) end
end)

name: transaction
summary: Runs several statements as one transaction.
description: Requires `database.access`. `statements` is an array of `{ query, values }` entries; all of them commit or none do. Same callback and `.await` forms as `query`.

name: update
summary: Runs a statement and returns the affected-row result.
description: Requires `database.access`. Use it for UPDATE and DELETE. `rawExecute` is an alias for the same method. Same callback and `.await` forms as `query`.
example:
-- Save the balance with the callback form
Open77.database.update("UPDATE players SET money = ? WHERE identifier = ?", { money, identifier }, function(affected)
    print("rows affected", affected)
end)

name: all
summary: Every looping effect, optionally filtered to one routing bucket.
description: Requires `world.effects`. Returns the whole registry, not just this resource's effects; the snapshot's `resource` field is provenance and cleanup scope, not an authorization boundary.
example:
-- Count the fires still burning in the arena instance
local burning = 0
for _, effect in ipairs(Open77.effects.all(ARENA_BUCKET)) do
    if effect.effect:sub(1, 5) == "fire." then burning = burning + 1 end
end

name: attach
summary: Create a replicated effect bound to a typed target and native slot.
description: Requires world.effects. target={kind="player"|"npc"|"vehicle"|"prop",id=decimalStringOrInteger}; effect is an installed preset. options requires slot; optional localAnchor=body|weaponRight, localSlot, ttlMs, streamingRadius=90, streamingHysteresis=20, localEvent, soundEvent, soundOnOwner=true. Uses exact target incarnation, streaming reattachment and resource-owned cleanup. localEvent selects an owner entity graph (not a sound); soundEvent is separate. Target disappearance/body/bucket change invalidates the effect. The ID proves registry admission, not visible/audible playback. Attachment TTL defaults60000 ms and is bounded to1..600000 ms; slot/localSlot are at most64 bytes. Limits are2048 effects globally and512 per resource. weaponRight/localEvent are player-only.
example:
local id, err = Open77.effects.attach({kind="player",id=tostring(playerId)},
 "electric.industrial_arm", {slot="RightHand",ttlMs=1500})
if not id then print(err); return end
-- Retain id and remove it when your action ends.

name: catalog
summary: Always an empty table on the server.
description: The dedicated server keeps no curated effect catalogue: the aliases live on the client, next to the records they resolve. It answers an empty list rather than `nil` so the shipped console command stays honest instead of failing on a nil call. Use the client `Open77.vfx` catalogue for alias names.
example:
-- Always empty on the server; the alias list lives on the client (Open77.vfx.catalog)
print(#Open77.effects.catalog()) -- 0

name: clearScreen
summary: Clears every server-driven screen effect on one player.
description: Requires `players.screenfx`. The same thing as `Open77.effects.screen(playerId, false)`, spelled out. Only the effects this relay owns are cleared: a client resource's own screen effects belong to that resource. See the Effects guide.
returns: true, or false and a reason
example:
-- Sobering up: clear every screen effect this resource put on the player
RegisterNetEvent("items:coffee", function()
    Open77.effects.clearScreen(source)
end)

name: create
summary: Creates a looping world effect owned by this resource.
description: Requires `world.effects`. The field is `effect`, not `name`, and the lifetime is `ttlMs`: a looping VFX has no duration because the registry retires it, not the engine. Definitions accept `effect`, `position`, `orientation`, `bucket`, `visible`, `streamingRadius` (10 to 2000, default 90), `streamingHysteresis` (default 20) and `ttlMs`. The registry holds 2,048 looping effects, of which one resource may own 512.

params.name: def
params.type: table { effect, position, orientation?, bucket?, visible?, streamingRadius?, streamingHysteresis?, ttlMs? }

example:
-- A burning barrel that stays lit for ten minutes
local fire, reason = Open77.effects.create({
    effect = "fire.small",
    position = { x = -1460.2, y = 99.9, z = 14.8 },
    ttlMs = 10 * 60 * 1000,
})
if not fire then print("no fire: " .. reason) end

name: explosion
summary: Detonates a blast at a point: VFX, area damage, and optionally the cars in it.
description: Native-parity E6, FiveM's `AddExplosion`. It composes three authorities that already exist and adds none: the picture is the same one-shot as `Open77.effects.play`, the player damage goes through the stats authority exactly as `Open77.players.damage` does (so god mode, the life-phase interlocks, the `explosion` damage multiplier and kill attribution all apply), and vehicles go through `Open77.vehicles.explode` unchanged -- occupants stay occupants, and a wreck already blown up is quietly skipped. **Three grants, because the halves differ in reach.** `world.effects` is always required and on its own buys a blast that is only a picture. `world.explosions` is required the moment `damage` is positive: unlike `players.stats.apply`, which hurts a player the resource has already named, this one hurts everyone in a circle, including players it never enumerated. `vehicles = true` requires `world.vehicles`, and without that opt-in no car is touched. Damage falls off linearly to zero at the rim. `force` scales the ragdoll impulse on a **lethal** hit only -- there is no server-side push for a survivor. A player whose last snapshot is stale is skipped rather than damaged at a position the server is unsure of, and everything is scoped to one routing bucket. Publishes `onExplosion` host-wide, with counts rather than names. See the [effects guide](effects.md).

params.name: options
params.type: table { radius?, damage?, force?, vfx?, sound?, bucket?, vehicles?, attacker? }

returns: table { players = { ids }, vehicles = { ids } }, or nil

reason: permission_denied:world.effects, permission_denied:world.explosions, permission_denied:world.vehicles, invalid_position, invalid_radius, invalid_damage, invalid_force, invalid_bucket, invalid_effect, invalid_sound, invalid_player_id, damage_unavailable, vehicles_unavailable, world_unavailable
example:
-- /boom: an explosion at the caller's feet that hurts players and wrecks cars
RegisterCommand("boom", function(source)
    local me = Open77.players.position(source)
    if not me then return end
    local blast = Open77.effects.explosion(me, { radius = 8, damage = 60, vehicles = true, attacker = source })
    if blast then print(#blast.players, "players hit,", #blast.vehicles, "vehicles wrecked") end
end, true)

name: get
summary: Reads one looping effect's canonical snapshot.
description: Requires `world.effects`. Reads are not restricted to the owning resource, so a spectator or admin tool can inspect an effect it did not create. Answers `nil` for an unknown id.
example:
-- Is the campfire still burning?
local fire = Open77.effects.get(campfireId)
if not fire then relight() end

name: play
summary: Plays a one-shot world effect at a point.
description: Requires `world.effects`. Broadcast to the players in range and never stored, so there is no handle and nothing to remove. Options are `position` (required, or the options table itself), `orientation` (quaternion, default identity), `bucket`, `range` (1 to 500, default 150) and `sound`.

params.name: opts
params.type: table { position, orientation?, bucket?, range?, sound? }

example:
-- Sparks where the player's lockpick failed
RegisterNetEvent("lockpick:failed", function()
    local me = Open77.players.position(source)
    if me then Open77.effects.play("sparks.burst.small", { position = me, range = 50 }) end
end)

name: playOn
summary: Play an ephemeral native effect on a typed target.
description: Requires world.effects. A bare target ID explicitly means player; typed targets avoid collisions between registries. name is a native entity effect event. options supports duration(default0),loop(defaultfalse),slot. Snapshot lifetime guards reject replaced targets; this one-shot is not replayed after streaming. Use attach for a durable owned effect.
example:
local ok, err = Open77.effects.playOn({kind="player",id=tostring(playerId)}, nativeEvent, {duration=1})
if not ok then print(err) end

name: remove
summary: Removes a looping effect this resource owns.
description: Requires `world.effects`. Another resource's effect answers `owned_by_another_resource`; a resource may read every effect but mutate only its own.
example:
-- The firefighters put the fire out
Open77.effects.remove(fireId)

name: screen
summary: Plays a full-screen post-process effect on one player's own view.
description: Requires `players.screenfx`. Deliberately NOT replicated -- a drunk screen belongs to the person who drank -- which is why it takes a playerId rather than a position, and why it reaches that client whether or not it runs any resource. `name` false or nil clears every effect this relay owns on that client. `options.strength` (0..1) picks among the authored tiers of the `drunk`, `drugged` and `health` families; `options.duration` is seconds, 0..600, 0 holding until cleared. The alias is checked against a mirror of the client table and refused as `unsupported_screen_effect`; the client's table stays the authority. See the Effects guide.
returns: true, or false and a reason
example:
-- Drinking makes the screen wobble for 30 seconds
RegisterNetEvent("items:drink", function()
    Open77.effects.screen(source, "drunk", { strength = 0.5, duration = 30 })
end)

name: screenCatalog
summary: The screen-effect aliases this server will accept, ascending.
description: A mirror of the client's curated table, so a typo is refused by the call that made it rather than by a log line on one player's machine. Includes the tiered family names (`drunk`, `drugged`, `health`) as well as their tiers. See the Effects guide.
example:
-- Validate an item's screen effect at startup
local known = {}
for _, alias in ipairs(Open77.effects.screenCatalog()) do known[alias] = true end
assert(known["drunk"], "this server does not support the drunk effect")

name: sound
summary: Play spatial sound on a typed target with optional action deduplication.
description: Requires world.effects. A bare target means player. options={unique=false,duration=5,actionId?,excludePlayers?}; duration is seconds and bounded by the backend. actionId is an opaque resource-scoped identity: repeated delivery of one contact does not replay sound. excludePlayers omits selected listeners, useful when native contact already supplies their audio. Sound targets carry current lifetime identity; no stale-body playback or durable late-stream replay is implied. duration is0.05..60 seconds; actionId is at most192 bytes and deduplication retains it for60 seconds without TTL renewal. excludePlayers accepts at most32 positive IDs; action identities are limited to8192 globally/4096 per resource.

name: update
summary: Patches a looping effect this resource owns.
description: Requires `world.effects`. Sparse: only the fields present are taken. The effect name is deliberately not patchable -- changing it is a remove and a create, because the running VFX instance is built from it.

params.name: patch
params.type: table { position?, orientation?, bucket?, visible?, streamingRadius?, streamingHysteresis?, ttlMs? }

example:
-- The fire moves with the burning car
Open77.effects.update(fireId, { position = Open77.vehicles.getPosition(carId) })

name: adopt
summary: Takes a native lift under authoritative control.
description: Requires `world.elevators`. The definition accepts `engineEntity`, `position`, `bucket`, `initialFloor`, `flags` (default powered plus interaction allowed) and a required `floorCount`. Adoption is what turns a scenery lift into a replicated object every client agrees about; before it, each client's lift is its own.

params.name: def
params.type: table { engineEntity, position, bucket?, initialFloor?, flags?, floorCount }

example:
-- Take the apartment lift under server control so everyone sees the same cab
local lift, reason = Open77.elevators.adopt({
    engineEntity = engineEntity,     -- from a client's Open77.elevators.nearby()
    position = { x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.0 },
    floorCount = 12,
    initialFloor = 0,
})
if not lift then print("adopt failed: " .. reason) end

name: all
summary: Every managed elevator, optionally filtered to one routing bucket.
description: Requires `world.elevators`. Returns the whole registry, adopted by whichever resource.
example:
-- Send every lift back to the ground floor at server start
for _, lift in ipairs(Open77.elevators.all()) do
    Open77.elevators.goTo(lift.id, 0)
end

name: call
summary: Alias of `Open77.elevators.goTo`.
description: Requires `world.elevators`. The same function under the name a call button would use; there is no separate queuing behaviour behind it.
example:
-- A call button on floor 5
RegisterNetEvent("lift:button", function(elevatorId, floor)
    Open77.elevators.call(elevatorId, floor)
end)

name: get
summary: Reads one elevator's canonical snapshot.
description: Requires `world.elevators`. Answers `nil` for an id the registry does not know.
example:
-- Only accept a new request when the lift is idle
local lift = Open77.elevators.get(elevatorId)
if lift and lift.phase == "idle" then Open77.elevators.goTo(elevatorId, 7) end

name: goTo
summary: Starts authoritative travel to a floor.
description: Requires `world.elevators`. Options are `travelMs` (default 8000) and `force`, which starts travel even when the lift is not idle. The travel time is the server's contract with every viewer, so all clients animate the same journey.
example:
-- A slow freight lift: 15 seconds to the top floor
Open77.elevators.goTo(elevatorId, 11, { travelMs = 15000 })

name: pause
summary: Pauses authoritative movement.
description: Requires `world.elevators`. The lift holds where it is and keeps its destination; `resume` continues the same journey.
example:
-- Power cut: every lift stops where it is
for _, lift in ipairs(Open77.elevators.all()) do Open77.elevators.pause(lift.id) end

name: remove
summary: Releases a managed elevator.
description: Requires `world.elevators`. The native lift stays in the world; only Open77's authority over it ends, so it reverts to ordinary client-local scenery.
example:
-- Hand the lift back to the engine when the resource no longer needs it
Open77.elevators.remove(elevatorId)

name: resume
summary: Continues a paused journey.
description: Requires `world.elevators`. Resuming a lift that is not paused is accepted and changes nothing.
example:
-- Power is back
for _, lift in ipairs(Open77.elevators.all()) do Open77.elevators.resume(lift.id) end

name: setFlags
summary: Sets the power, lock, interaction and door policy bits.
description: Requires `world.elevators`. The constants are in `Open77.elevators.flags`: `powered` (1), `locked` (2), `interactionAllowed` (4) and `doorsClosed` (8). This replaces the mask rather than merging it, so read the snapshot first when only one bit should change.
example:
-- Lock the lift for the heist: keep it powered but not usable
local f = Open77.elevators.flags
Open77.elevators.setFlags(elevatorId, f.powered | f.locked)

name: teleport
summary: Moves a lift to a floor with no travel.
description: Requires `world.elevators`. Administrative recovery: it skips the journey entirely, so it is the way out of a lift stuck mid-shaft, not a normal call.
example:
-- Admin recovery for a lift stuck between floors
RegisterCommand("liftfix", function(source, args)
    Open77.elevators.teleport(tonumber(args[1]), 0)
end, true)

name: clearBucket
summary: Retires one routing bucket's environment override.
description: Requires `world.environment`. The players still standing in that bucket are re-synced onto the default environment with a revision newer than the one they last applied, so nobody is left on the sky of a world that no longer exists. Once the last override is gone the authority returns to a single broadcast per mutation instead of one send per connected player.
example:
-- The arena match is over: the instance goes back to the default sky
Open77.environment.clearBucket(ARENA_BUCKET)

name: getState
summary: The canonical clock and weather state, right now.
description: Requires `world.environment`. Carries `scope` and `bucket`, the clock as both `secondsOfDay` and `hour`/`minute`/`second`, `rate`, `frozen`/`timeFrozen`, `weather`/`weatherPreset`/`weatherPriority`, `transitionSeconds` and `weatherTransitionRemainingMs`, `weatherFrozen`/`randomWeather`/`nextWeatherInMs`, the `revision`/`weatherRevision`/`authorityEpoch` triple clients use to reject a stale snapshot, and `buckets` — every routing bucket currently holding an override. It is the same table every setter returns and the same payload `onEnvironmentChanged` carries.
example:
-- /time: tell the player the in-game time
RegisterCommand("time", function(source)
    local env = Open77.environment.getState()
    if env then Open77.chat.send(source, ("It is %02d:%02d, %s"):format(env.hour, env.minute, env.weather)) end
end, false)

name: publishChange
summary: Publishes the reserved `onEnvironmentChanged` event host-wide.
description: Requires `world.environment`. The authority's own door: `onEnvironmentChanged` is a platform name reserved on the event bus, so `TriggerEvent` refuses it with `reserved_event` and this is the only way it can be published. Same queue, same by-value marshalling and same tick boundary as `TriggerEvent`. No resource other than the one holding the environment state needs to call it.
returns: reason: permission_denied:world.environment, resource_stopping, resource_preparing, event_payload_not_serializable, event_queue_limit
example:
-- Only the environment authority calls this; a gamemode listens instead
AddEventHandler("onEnvironmentChanged", function(state)
    print("weather is now", state.weather)
end)

name: setTime
summary: Sets the authoritative time of day every player projects.
description: Requires `world.environment`. The host installs this facade in every VM; the authority itself is the bundled `open77_weather` resource, reached through a synchronous export call, because the only code able to move a sky is that resource's CLIENT projection. `bucket` is optional: omitted it moves the default environment, given it creates or updates that routing bucket's override, seeded from the default as it reads at that moment. Answers `environment_unavailable` when the authority is not running — which `resources.load` can cause silently. See [the guide](weather.md).
returns: reason: permission_denied:world.environment, environment_unavailable, invalid_time, invalid_bucket, too_many_environment_overrides
example:
-- /settime <hour> <minute> for admins
RegisterCommand("settime", function(source, args)
    Open77.environment.setTime(tonumber(args[1]) or 12, tonumber(args[2]) or 0, 0)
end, true)

name: setTimeFrozen
summary: Stops or resumes the authoritative clock where it stands.
description: Requires `world.environment`. Freezing rebases first, so the clock stops at the reading it had rather than at its last anchor, and resuming continues from there. This is the server-side clock only: the client projection never holds REDengine's `SetPausedState`, which two-client runtime testing showed also slows gameplay and vehicle physics. `bucket` scopes the change to one routing bucket.
example:
-- Freeze the clock at night for the horror event
Open77.environment.setTime(2, 0, 0)
Open77.environment.setTimeFrozen(true)

name: setTimeRate
summary: Sets how many game seconds pass per real second.
description: Requires `world.environment`. Accepts `0` to `120`; the shipped default is `8.0`, which MUST match the engine's own rate or the projection has to correct the clock continuously — and every correction is a `SetGameTimeByHMS` world time jump that makes the streamer re-resolve nodes and resurrect destroyed props (measured 25 Aug). Changing day length properly needs a native rate control, not this.
example:
-- Slow days: one game hour per 15 real minutes
Open77.environment.setTimeRate(4)

name: setWeather
summary: Applies a synchronized weather preset over a transition.
description: Requires `world.environment`. `preset` is an Open77 name (`sunny`, `lightclouds`, `cloudy`, `rain`, `heavyclouds`, `fog`, `pollution`, `sandstorm`), one of the configured aliases, or the REDengine `24h_weather_*` value. `transitionSeconds` defaults to the preset's own and must be `0` to `300`. A player who joins mid-transition picks it up at its current point rather than restarting it. `bucket` scopes the change to one routing bucket.
returns: reason: permission_denied:world.environment, environment_unavailable, unknown_weather, invalid_transition, transition_must_be_between_0_and_300, invalid_bucket
example:
-- Rain in the arena instance only, over 20 seconds
Open77.environment.setWeather("rain", 20, ARENA_BUCKET)

name: setWeatherFrozen
summary: Pins the current preset by stopping the random scheduler.
description: Requires `world.environment`. The name means something different on each runtime, deliberately: on the CLIENT it is an unconditional lock against a vanilla controller submitting its own preset, and is not an operator choice; on the SERVER it means pin the preset — the weighted random draw stops, so the sky stays where it was put. It is the same switch `weather.random off` throws, and it is the half a competitive gamemode wants, because lighting is a fairness variable.
example:
-- Competitive mode: pin the weather so lighting is fair
Open77.environment.setWeather("sunny", 0)
Open77.environment.setWeatherFrozen(true)

name: cancel
summary: Server only. Vetoes the cancellable event this handler is running under.
description: Alias of CancelEvent.
example:
-- Veto a chat message from a muted player (alias of CancelEvent)
Open77.events.on("chatMessage", function(playerId, name, text)
    if muted[playerId] then Open77.events.cancel() end
end)

name: emit
summary: Publishes an event host-wide; the same function as TriggerEvent.
description: No permission. Since the host-wide bus exists, this reaches every running resource that handles the name, not only this VM: the fan-out is queued and drained at the next tick boundary, in resource-name order. Open77.events.emitLocal is the one that stays inside this VM. Host events (onPlayerReady, onPlayerDisconnected, the resource lifecycle events) arrive through the same handler list a resource uses for its own, so it listens for both the same way.
example:
-- Announce a robbery to every resource on the server
Open77.events.emit("bank:robbed", source, amount)

name: emitCancellable
summary: Server only. Publishes a host-wide cancellable event and returns its verdict handle.
description: Alias of TriggerCancellableEvent.
example:
-- Let other resources veto a purchase (alias of TriggerCancellableEvent)
RegisterNetEvent("shop:buy", function(itemId)
    local verdict = Open77.events.emitCancellable("shop:beforeBuy", source, itemId)
    if verdict and verdict:await() then return end -- somebody said no
    sell(source, itemId)
end)

name: emitLocal
summary: Server only. Fires an event in this resource's VM only.
description: Alias of TriggerLocalEvent.
example:
-- Internal signalling that stays inside this resource
Open77.events.emitLocal("shop:restocked", "ammo", 200)

name: off
summary: Removes a local or network handler; the same function as `RemoveEventHandler`.
description: No permission. Takes the id `Open77.events.on` or `Open77.net.on` returned.
example:
-- Stop listening after the first player is ready
local handler
handler = Open77.events.on("onPlayerReady", function(playerId)
    print("first player:", playerId)
    Open77.events.off(handler)
end)

name: on
summary: Registers an event handler; the same function as AddEventHandler.
description: No permission. One handler list receives three sources: this VM's Open77.events.emitLocal, the host-wide bus every resource publishes on, and the platform's own lifecycle events. Cross-resource *calls* with a return value are still Open77.exports; the bus carries announcements, not answers. Returns a handler id for Open77.events.off. The limit is 2,048 handlers per resource.
example:
-- Listen for another resource's announcement
Open77.events.on("bank:robbed", function(robberId, amount)
    Open77.players.setWanted(robberId, 3)
end)

name: wasCanceled
summary: Server only. Whether the cancellable event being dispatched has already been vetoed.
description: Alias of WasEventCanceled.
example:
-- Log messages an earlier filter already vetoed
Open77.events.on("chatMessage", function(playerId, name, text)
    if Open77.events.wasCanceled() then print("filtered:", text) end
end)

name: call
summary: Calls another server resource's export and returns a promise.
description: Asynchronous and cross-resource, unlike `TriggerEvent`, which never leaves this VM. Returns an `Open77.Promise`: `promise:await()` yields the copied return values, `promise:status()` reports pending, resolved, rejected or cancelled. Awaiting a pending call requires a managed coroutine. Call it from a running resource, not during preparation. The provider keeps its own permissions and identity: arguments never supply caller identity, and the exported coroutine does not inherit the player `source`. See [Cross-resource server exports](server-exports.md).
example:
-- Call the bank resource's export and await the answer
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, reason = Open77.exports.call("bank", "withdraw", playerId, 100)
    if not pending then return print(reason) end
    local ok, err = pending:await()
    if not ok then Open77.chat.send(playerId, "Withdrawal failed: " .. tostring(err)) end
end)

name: callSync
summary: Calls another server resource's export inline on this thread.
description: The non-sugar form of exports.resource:name(...). Runs the callee in its own VM before returning and yields its values directly. It RAISES on failure instead of returning nil, reason -- the one place Open77 departs from its own convention, so that ported FiveM code behaves the same; use pcall to handle failure. The callee must not yield (export_yielded), gets its own instruction budget (export_budget_exhausted fails only that call), and chains are capped at 8 frames (export_recursion_limit). Arguments and results are copied, never shared, so no Lua value is held across the boundary. Prefer Open77.exports.call when the callee can be slow, because a synchronous call holds the tick.
example:
-- Synchronous export call: the bank answers inline (raises on failure)
local ok, balance = pcall(Open77.exports.callSync, "bank", "balance", source)
if ok then Open77.chat.send(source, ("Balance: %d"):format(balance)) end

name: action
summary: Reads one hacking action by id: the current upload or its bounded terminal receipt.
description: Requires `players.hacking.read`. A completed, blocked or cancelled action is kept for a bounded time so a resource that only holds the id can still learn how it ended; after that the answer is `nil`.
returns: action table, or nil when unknown or expired
example:
-- Report how the upload ended, from the id kept when it started
local action = Open77.hacking.action(actionId)
if action then print("upload status:", action.status) end

name: cancel
summary: Cancels this provider's active upload.
description: Requires `players.hacking.cancel`. Only an upload this resource started can be cancelled; the victim is released and the actor keeps whatever the acceptance already cost.
example:
-- The victim entered a safe zone: cancel our upload on them
RegisterNetEvent("safezone:entered", function()
    if activeUploads[source] then Open77.hacking.cancel(activeUploads[source]) end
end)

name: capabilities
summary: Reports the hacking schema, profiles, authority model and hard limits.
description: Requires `players.hacking.read`. The grade schema each `define*` accepts, the six hack kinds, the evidence model (clients submit intent and visibility only; the server decides) and the bounds -- read it instead of copying the tables out of [Hacking and counterplay](hacking.md).
example:
-- Print the hack kinds this server supports at startup
local caps = Open77.hacking.capabilities()
if caps then for _, kind in ipairs(caps.kinds or {}) do print(kind) end end

name: clearProtection
summary: Clears only this provider's protection scope on a player.
description: Requires `players.hacking.policy`. Another provider's safe-area or resistance scope on the same player is untouched.
example:
-- Leaving the safe zone lifts our protection scope
RegisterNetEvent("safezone:left", function()
    Open77.hacking.clearProtection(source)
end)

name: configureProtection
summary: Owns a safe-area or electrical-resistance scope on a player's current body.
description: Requires `players.hacking.policy`. `options.safeArea = true` refuses every upload against the player; `options.resistance` (0..1) scales electrical damage. The scope belongs to this provider and to the current body: a new body needs a new call.
example:
-- Nobody can be hacked inside the safe zone
RegisterNetEvent("safezone:entered", function()
    Open77.hacking.configureProtection(source, { safeArea = true })
end)

name: define
summary: Registers this resource's hack definition and its grades.
description: Requires `players.hacking.define`. `definition` is `{ id, version, grades = { { id, range, uploadMs, staminaCost, cooldownMs, damage, statusMs, recoveryMs, lockHacking, nonlethal, kind? } } }`; `kind` selects Short Circuit, Overheat, Cyberware Malfunction, Cripple Movement, Reboot Optics or Weapon Glitch, six kinds of one warned, interruptible upload. Register the matching implant through `Open77.cyberware.define` with the same provider, id, version and grade ids, in the `operating_system` slot. See [Hacking and counterplay](hacking.md).

name: defineIce
summary: Registers this resource's Self-ICE definition and its grades.
description: Requires `players.hacking.define`. Grades carry `charges` and `rechargeMs`; a victim whose Self-ICE has a charge blocks an incoming upload and spends it. The matching implant lives in the `self_ice` slot, profile `self_ice`.

name: definePurge
summary: Registers this resource's active-purge definition and its grades.
description: Requires `players.hacking.define`. Grades carry `staminaCost`, `cooldownMs`, `allowSelf`, `allowAlly`, `range`, `cancelUploads` and `removeStatuses`. The matching implant lives in the `purge` slot, profile `active_purge`.

name: purge
summary: Purges uploads and statuses on a target through the actor's active-purge implant.
description: Requires `players.hacking.activate`. Goes through the same defence authority as a player's own purge input: the actor must own the grade, the target must be self or an ally the grade allows, and stamina and cooldown are spent. `options.operationId` is required, as for `start`.
example:
-- A medic purges a team-mate's statuses from a command
RegisterCommand("purge", function(source, args)
    local target = tonumber(args[1]) or source
    local result, reason = Open77.hacking.purge(source, target, "myserver.purge", "training",
        { operationId = ("purge:%d:%d"):format(source, GetGameTimer()) })
    if not result then Open77.chat.send(source, "Purge refused: " .. reason) end
end, false)

name: start
summary: Starts an entitled hack upload from one player against a target.
description: Requires `players.hacking.activate`. The actor must own the matching installed implant grade; the server checks range, visibility evidence, stamina, cooldown, Self-ICE and protection scopes, then runs the warned upload. `options.operationId` is REQUIRED and must be stable across retries of the same operation -- the same id with different arguments is rejected. Progress arrives on `onHackingTransition`.
example:
-- A scripted hack from the player against the target they aimed at
RegisterNetEvent("hack:request", function(targetId)
    local result, reason = Open77.hacking.start(source, targetId, "myserver.short_circuit", "training",
        { operationId = ("hack:%d:%d"):format(source, GetGameTimer()) })
    if not result then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Hack refused: " .. reason) end
    activeUploads[source] = result.actionId
end)

name: state
summary: Reads a player's authoritative hacking state.
description: Requires `players.hacking.read`. Includes the active upload if any and the remaining status windows: `cyberwareSuspendedMs`, `frozenMs`, `malfunctionMs`, `malfunctionBlocks`, `crippledMs`, `crippleHeavy`, `blindedMs` and `weaponGlitchedMs`. This is the server's ledger, not the victim's rendering.
example:
-- Is the player still blinded?
local state = Open77.hacking.state(playerId)
if state and state.blindedMs > 0 then print("blind for another", state.blindedMs, "ms") end

name: statuses
summary: Lists the owned statuses currently affecting a player.
description: Requires `players.hacking.read`. Same answer as `Open77.statuses.list`: every status any provider applied to this player, with its kind, provider, action id and deadline.
example:
-- List every status currently on a player
for _, status in ipairs(Open77.hacking.statuses(playerId) or {}) do
    print(status.kind, status.provider, status.deadline)
end

name: hold
summary: Puts an item record into one of a player's ten equipment slots, so it is genuinely held.
description: The other half of the attachment surface, and deliberately a different call from `Open77.props.attach`: that one makes a prop **follow**, this one makes a body **hold**. The item goes in through the engine's own transaction system, so it moves with the animation instead of hovering near the body. The price is that it is not arbitrary. The thing held must be an item **record** (`Items.something`), not an `.ent`, and the slot is one of the ten `AttachmentSlots.*` records the client compiles in `client/src/game/Slot.hpp`: `Head`, `Face`, `InnerChest`, `OuterChest`, `Legs`, `Feet`, `Outfit`, `UnderwearTop`, `UnderwearBottom`, `WeaponRight`. `WeaponRight` is the right hand and the default; there is no `back` and no `hip`. Held equipment is client-owned REDengine state, so this is a relay with the same contract as `Open77.clothing` and `Open77.weapons`: it returns a request id immediately and the verified outcome arrives on `open77:helditem:completed`. The bundled `open77_helditems` resource owns the client half; without it the request times out after ten seconds. It writes the same slot as `Open77.weapons`, so pick one per gamemode.
example:
-- Put a briefcase in the courier's hand
Open77.heldItems.hold(courierId, "Items.GenericCraftingMaterial1", { slot = "WeaponRight" })

name: release
summary: Empties one of a player's equipment slots of the item this API put there.
description: Requests the slot be emptied and reports the verified outcome on `open77:helditem:completed`, like `Open77.heldItems.hold`. `options.slot` defaults to `WeaponRight`. The body keeps whatever the server's equipment record says it wears; only the named slot is stated.
example:
-- The courier delivered: empty the hand
Open77.heldItems.release(courierId, { slot = "WeaponRight" })

name: requestSnapshot
summary: Asks a player's client what its ten equipment slots currently hold.
description: Asynchronous. The completion event's `result` is a table keyed by slot name, each entry carrying `record`, `empty` and `held` (whether this API is what put it there). Read from the body's own equipment registry rather than from anything the server remembers, which is the honest answer after a write has settled.
example:
-- What is the player holding right now?
Open77.heldItems.requestSnapshot(playerId)
AddEventHandler("open77:helditem:completed", function(playerId, requestId, operation, accepted, reason, result)
    if operation == "snapshot" and accepted then print(json.encode(result)) end
end)

name: slots
summary: The ten equipment slot names Open77.heldItems accepts.
description: Sorted. These are the `AttachmentSlots.*` TweakDB records, the only closed and validated slot vocabulary in the tree -- `entSlotComponent` slot names are authored per entity and cannot be enumerated ahead of time, which is why the effects surface (`Open77.effects.attach`) takes a free string and validates it against the target instead.
example:
-- Print the slot names this API accepts
for _, slot in ipairs(Open77.heldItems.slots()) do print(slot) end

name: request
summary: Makes an outbound HTTP request; the same function as `PerformHttpRequest`.
description: Requires `http.request` **and** a server that enabled the bridge with an allow-list -- an empty list reaches nothing and redirects are never followed, so the list is the whole reachable surface. The request leaves the tick thread at once, the exchange runs on the thread pool, and the callback runs on the owning resource's own tick. The callback is `(status, body, headers, err)`, with `status = 0` when the exchange did not complete. A refused request still invokes the callback, so a script never waits on one.

params.name: url
params.type: string (absolute http/https, host on the allow-list)

params.name: method
params.type: string (GET default, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD)

returns: reason: permission_denied:http.request, http_unavailable, invalid_url, host_not_allowed, invalid_method, body_too_large, too_many_headers, invalid_header, too_many_requests
example:
-- Post to a Discord webhook when the server starts
Open77.http.request("https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...", function(status, body, headers, err)
    if status == 0 then print("webhook failed: " .. tostring(err)) end
end, "POST", { content = "Server is up!" })

name: append
summary: Appends text to a file in this resource's data directory.
description: Requires `filesystem.write`. Creates the file when it does not exist. The 4 MiB ceiling applies to the resulting file, so an append-only log needs its own rotation.
example:
-- An audit log line per admin command
Open77.io.append("admin.log", ("%s %s /%s\n"):format(Open77.time.utc(), Open77.players.name(source), command))

name: copy
summary: Copies a file inside this resource's data directory.
description: Requires `filesystem.read` for the source **and** `filesystem.write` for the destination -- both, because the operation reads and writes. Without `overwrite`, an existing destination answers `already_exists`.
example:
-- Keep a backup before rewriting the config
Open77.io.copy("config.json", "config.backup.json", true)

name: exists
summary: Whether a path exists inside this resource's data directory.
description: Requires `filesystem.read`. Returns `nil, reason` rather than `false` when the path itself is refused, so a rejected path is never mistaken for an absent file.
example:
-- First run: write a default config if there is none
if not Open77.io.exists("config.json") then
    Open77.io.writeJson("config.json", { startingMoney = 500 })
end

name: list
summary: Lists one directory inside this resource's data directory.
description: Requires `filesystem.read`. Non-recursive and sorted, at most 2,048 entries. Each entry is `{ name, type, size? }`. Omitting the argument lists the data directory itself.
returns: array of { name, type, size? }, or nil
example:
-- Load every house file in data/houses/
for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.io.list("houses") or {}) do
    if entry.type == "file" then loadHouse(json.decode(Open77.io.read("houses/" .. entry.name))) end
end

name: makeDirectory
summary: Creates a directory and any missing parents.
description: Requires `filesystem.write`. Creating a directory that already exists succeeds: the caller asked for it to be there, and it is.
example:
-- Make sure the folder exists before the first save
Open77.io.makeDirectory("houses")

name: move
summary: Moves or renames a file inside this resource's data directory.
description: Requires `filesystem.write`. Both ends are checked against the same path rules. Without `overwrite`, an existing destination answers `already_exists` rather than being replaced.
example:
-- Rotate the log when it gets big
local info = Open77.io.stat("admin.log")
if info and info.size > 1024 * 1024 then
    Open77.io.move("admin.log", "admin.old.log", true)
end

name: read
summary: Reads a UTF-8 text file from this resource's data directory.
description: Requires `filesystem.read`. Paths are relative to the calling resource's `data/` directory; absolute paths, `..` escapes and reparse-point traversal are rejected. A file is limited to 4 MiB and a relative path to 512 UTF-8 bytes. This cannot read another resource, the server configuration, or the resource's own manifest and scripts.
returns: reason: invalid_path, path_outside_resource, reparse_point_denied, not_found, not_a_file, file_too_large, io_error

name: readJson
summary: Reads a file and decodes it with the bounded Open77 JSON codec.
description: Requires `filesystem.read`. Inherits the codec's 48 KiB and depth limits on top of the file limits, so it is for configuration and small records, not a database. A decode failure is reported as a reason rather than raising.
returns: reason: invalid_json among the read reasons
example:
-- Load the race course from data/courses/
local course, reason = Open77.io.readJson("courses/watson-loop.json")
if not course then print("no course: " .. reason) end

name: remove
summary: Removes one file.
description: Requires `filesystem.write`. Never removes a directory tree -- that is deliberate, so a path bug cannot take a resource's whole data directory with it.
example:
-- The house was demolished: delete its file
Open77.io.remove("houses/" .. houseId .. ".json")

name: stat
summary: Reads one entry's metadata.
description: Requires `filesystem.read`. Returns `{ name, type, size?, modifiedUtc }`. `modifiedUtc` is the honest way to tell whether a file changed since the resource last read it.
returns: table { name, type, size?, modifiedUtc }, or nil
example:
-- Reload the prices only if the file changed
local info = Open77.io.stat("prices.json")
if info and info.modifiedUtc ~= lastLoaded then
    prices = json.decode(Open77.io.read("prices.json"))
    lastLoaded = info.modifiedUtc
end

name: write
summary: Atomically replaces a UTF-8 text file in this resource's data directory.
description: Requires `filesystem.write`. The replacement is atomic, so a crash mid-write leaves the previous contents rather than a truncated file. Same path rules and 4 MiB limit as `read`.
example:
-- Save a plain text MOTD
Open77.io.write("motd.txt", "Welcome to Night City RP. Be nice.")

name: writeJson
summary: Encodes a value and writes it atomically.
description: Requires `filesystem.write`. Encodes with the bounded Open77 JSON codec, then writes through `Open77.io.write`, so the replacement is atomic. A value the codec refuses answers a reason instead of writing a partial file.
example:
-- Persist the house owners without a database
Open77.io.writeJson("houses.json", houses)

name: clear
summary: Clears this resource's keys matching a prefix.
description: Server-side; no capability. The store is one JSON file under this resource's own `data/` directory, and no caller-supplied path reaches it, so a resource cannot address another's store -- isolation is structural, which is why this needs no permission where `Open77.io` needs `filesystem.*`. An empty or omitted prefix clears the whole store.
example:
-- Wipe this resource's saved state for a fresh season
RegisterCommand("season-reset", function()
    print("removed", Open77.kvp.clear("season:"), "keys")
end, true)

name: compareAndSet
summary: Atomically changes a key when its typed value matches.
description: Server-side; no capability. The store is one JSON file under this resource's own `data/` directory, and no caller-supplied path reaches it, so a resource cannot address another's store -- isolation is structural, which is why this needs no permission where `Open77.io` needs `filesystem.*`. `expected = nil` means "must be absent"; `replacement = nil` deletes. The comparison is TYPED: an integer 1 does not satisfy an expectation written as 1.0, because the store keeps the two apart and a later read would answer differently.
example:
-- Claim the daily bonus only once, atomically
if Open77.kvp.compareAndSet("bonus:" .. identifier, nil, today) then
    giveBonus(playerId)
end

name: delete
summary: Deletes one persistent key.
description: Server-side; no capability. The store is one JSON file under this resource's own `data/` directory, and no caller-supplied path reaches it, so a resource cannot address another's store -- isolation is structural, which is why this needs no permission where `Open77.io` needs `filesystem.*`. Deleting an absent key is `false`, not an error.
returns: true when removed, false when absent
example:
-- The player sold their house: forget the saved key
Open77.kvp.delete("house:" .. identifier)

name: find
summary: Finds typed entries by sorted key prefix.
description: Server-side; no capability. The store is one JSON file under this resource's own `data/` directory, and no caller-supplied path reaches it, so a resource cannot address another's store -- isolation is structural, which is why this needs no permission where `Open77.io` needs `filesystem.*`. Keys are ordinal-sorted. `limit` must be 1..4096; anything else is `invalid_limit` rather than a silent clamp.
returns: array of { key, value, type }, or nil
example:
-- A leaderboard from the stored scores
for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.kvp.find("score:", 100) or {}) do
    print(entry.key:sub(7), entry.value)
end

name: get
summary: Reads one typed persistent value.
description: Server-side; no capability. The store is one JSON file under this resource's own `data/` directory, and no caller-supplied path reaches it, so a resource cannot address another's store -- isolation is structural, which is why this needs no permission where `Open77.io` needs `filesystem.*`. A missing key answers with the caller's default, or nil, and NO reason -- a reason there would be indistinguishable from a storage failure at the call site.
example:
-- Money persisted without a database
local balance = Open77.kvp.get("money:" .. identifier, 500)

name: has
summary: Checks whether a persistent key exists.
description: Server-side; no capability. The store is one JSON file under this resource's own `data/` directory, and no caller-supplied path reaches it, so a resource cannot address another's store -- isolation is structural, which is why this needs no permission where `Open77.io` needs `filesystem.*`.
example:
-- First join on this server?
if not Open77.kvp.has("seen:" .. identifier) then
    Open77.kvp.set("seen:" .. identifier, true)
    Open77.chat.send(playerId, "Welcome to the city, first-timer!")
end

name: increment
summary: Atomically increments a numeric key.
description: Server-side; no capability. The store is one JSON file under this resource's own `data/` directory, and no caller-supplied path reaches it, so a resource cannot address another's store -- isolation is structural, which is why this needs no permission where `Open77.io` needs `filesystem.*`. Atomic in the sense that matters: the server Lua runtime is one thread, so a read-modify-write cannot interleave with another resource's. An absent key starts at zero. Integer plus integer stays an integer, so a counter never drifts into float territory. `integer_overflow`, `number_overflow`, `value_not_numeric` and `delta_not_numeric` are named rather than wrapped.
example:
-- One kill counter per player, persisted
AddEventHandler("onPlayerLifeStateChanged", function(playerId, revision, phase, reason)
    if phase ~= "dead" then return end
    local killer = Open77.players.getLifeState(playerId).killer
    if killer then Open77.kvp.increment("kills:" .. Open77.players.identifier(killer), 1) end
end)

name: keys
summary: Lists sorted keys matching a prefix.
description: Server-side; no capability. The store is one JSON file under this resource's own `data/` directory, and no caller-supplied path reaches it, so a resource cannot address another's store -- isolation is structural, which is why this needs no permission where `Open77.io` needs `filesystem.*`.
example:
-- Every player who has a saved balance
for _, key in ipairs(Open77.kvp.keys("money:") or {}) do print(key) end

name: set
summary: Persists one typed value for this resource.
description: Server-side; no capability. The store is one JSON file under this resource's own `data/` directory, and no caller-supplied path reaches it, so a resource cannot address another's store -- isolation is structural, which is why this needs no permission where `Open77.io` needs `filesystem.*`. Quotas are the client store's numbers exactly: 256-byte keys, 64 KiB values, 4096 entries, 1 MiB of payload, same reason tokens. Values are string, integer, number or boolean; integer and number stay apart, so a counter read back from disk is still an integer. A refused write leaves the store exactly as it was. Writes are coalesced onto the tick and flushed again when the resource stops, so an orderly stop, reload or restart loses nothing and a hard kill loses at most one tick. A store that cannot be parsed reports `storage_corrupt` and is never overwritten with a fresh one.
example:
-- Save the player's money when they leave
AddEventHandler("onPlayerDisconnected", function(playerId)
    Open77.kvp.set("money:" .. Open77.players.identifier(playerId), wallet[playerId] or 0)
end)

name: setIfAbsent
summary: Stores a value only when its key is missing.
description: Server-side; no capability. The store is one JSON file under this resource's own `data/` directory, and no caller-supplied path reaches it, so a resource cannot address another's store -- isolation is structural, which is why this needs no permission where `Open77.io` needs `filesystem.*`. The cheap way to claim a lock without a database.
example:
-- A lock without a database: only one heist at a time
if not Open77.kvp.setIfAbsent("heist:lock", true) then
    return Open77.chat.send(source, "A heist is already running.")
end

name: stats
summary: Returns this resource store's usage and quotas.
description: Server-side; no capability. The store is one JSON file under this resource's own `data/` directory, and no caller-supplied path reaches it, so a resource cannot address another's store -- isolation is structural, which is why this needs no permission where `Open77.io` needs `filesystem.*`.
returns: table { entries, bytes, maximumEntries, maximumBytes, maximumKeyBytes, maximumValueBytes, resource }, or nil
example:
-- Log the store usage at startup
local stats = Open77.kvp.stats()
if stats then print(("kvp: %d entries, %d bytes"):format(stats.entries, stats.bytes)) end

name: debug
summary: Writes a resource-prefixed debug line to the server log.
description: No permission. On the server these four levels currently forward to the same resource-prefixed logger as `print`, so the level is documentation for the reader rather than a filter. The identically named **client** function does route by level. Signature is `(...)`; there is no return value.
example:
-- Verbose line in the server log
Open77.log.debug("purchase", source, itemId, price)

name: error
summary: Writes a resource-prefixed error line to the server log.
description: No permission. Forwards to the same resource-prefixed logger as `print`; it does not raise, abort the handler or mark the resource unhealthy. See `Open77.log.debug` for why the level does not yet filter on the server.
example:
-- Log a refused call without raising
local ok, reason = Open77.vehicles.create(definition)
if not ok then Open77.log.error("spawn refused:", reason) end

name: info
summary: Writes a resource-prefixed informational line to the server log.
description: No permission. Forwards to the same resource-prefixed logger as `print`. See `Open77.log.debug` for why the level does not yet filter on the server.
example:
-- Lifecycle line
Open77.log.info("shop resource started with", #items, "items")

name: warn
summary: Writes a resource-prefixed warning line to the server log.
description: No permission. Forwards to the same resource-prefixed logger as `print`. See `Open77.log.debug` for why the level does not yet filter on the server.
example:
-- Survivable but worth a look
Open77.log.warn("no database configured, prices will not persist")

name: all
summary: Every loot drop, optionally filtered to one routing bucket.
description: Requires `world.loot`. Returns the whole registry, whichever resource created each drop.
example:
-- Count the drops still lying in the arena
print(#Open77.loot.all(ARENA_BUCKET), "drops on the ground")

name: create
summary: Creates an authoritative ground loot drop.
description: Requires `world.loot`. The definition accepts `item`, `quantity` (default 1), `position`, `bucket`, `radius` (default 2), `label`, `visualItem`/`model` and `ttlMs`. Drops are replicated and owned by the creating resource, so they survive a player walking away and are cleaned up when the resource stops. See [loot](loot.md) for pickup validation and client projection.

params.name: def
params.type: table { item, quantity?, position, bucket?, radius?, label?, visualItem?, ttlMs? }

example:
-- A dead player drops 200 eddies where they fell, gone after five minutes
AddEventHandler("onPlayerLifeStateChanged", function(playerId, revision, phase)
    if phase ~= "dead" then return end
    local pos = Open77.players.position(playerId)
    if pos then
        Open77.loot.create({ item = "Items.money", quantity = 200, position = pos, label = "Eddies", ttlMs = 300000 })
    end
end)

name: get
summary: Reads one loot drop's snapshot.
description: Requires `world.loot`. Answers `nil` for an unknown or already collected id.
example:
-- Is the drop still there before paying out?
local drop = Open77.loot.get(lootId)
if not drop then print("already picked up") end

name: remove
summary: Removes a loot drop.
description: Requires `world.loot`. Use it when a mode ends a round rather than waiting for `ttlMs`.
example:
-- Round over: clear the leftover drops
for _, drop in ipairs(Open77.loot.all(ARENA_BUCKET)) do Open77.loot.remove(drop.id) end

name: update
summary: Patches an existing loot drop.
description: Requires `world.loot`. Reads the current drop first and keeps every field the patch omits, so moving a drop does not silently reset its quantity or label. An unknown id answers `false`.
example:
-- The wind blows the crate two metres; quantity and label stay
Open77.loot.update(lootId, { position = { x = -1444.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.0 } })

name: cancel
summary: Cancel this resource's authoritative motion lease.
description: Requires players.motion.control. Requires the exact player and motion ID owned by the calling resource. Ends network ownership and requests native cleanup; collision/braking and get-up remain native, so cancellation need not instantly stop velocity or animation.
example:
local result, err = Open77.motion.cancel(playerId, motionId)
if not result then print(err) end

name: current
summary: Read an authoritative living-motion lease.
description: Requires players.motion.read. Returns {id,player,incarnation,bucket,directionX,directionY,distance,createdAt,expiresAt,phase,reason}, or nil. Times are server-monotonic milliseconds. pending awaits owner native ACK; active is not server-observed rendering. Acknowledged ownership lasts6s, including recovery; no generic teleport or map collision solution is provided.
example:
local motion = Open77.motion.current(playerId)
if motion then print(motion.id, motion.phase) end

name: knockdown
summary: Request bounded native living-player motion.
description: Requires players.motion.control. options={x,y,distance}; direction nonzero and normalized, distance0..6 m. Requires ready/alive/unmounted exact body and no existing lease; native owner additionally refuses unsuitable states. Returns admission, not damage or physical completion. onPlayerMotionChanged reports pending/active/ended; server pending expires after2s. Active snapshot checks are ACK-rooted, not exact native launch-origin enforcement.
example:
local result, err = Open77.motion.knockdown(playerId, {x=0,y=1,distance=0})
if not result then print(err) else print(result.id) end

name: callClient
summary: Asks one client a question and returns a promise for the answer.
description: Requires network.events. Targets the handler that resource registered on that client; the table form { resource = "other", name = "x", timeout = ms } names another resource or sets a deadline (default 10,000 ms, range 100..120,000). There is no broadcast: callClient(-1, ...) answers callback_broadcast_unsupported, because one question cannot have many answers. Up to 29 arguments and 48 KiB per frame, 256 questions open per resource. Rejects with callback_not_found, callback_timeout, callback_target_stopped and the rest of the callback reason list. Aliased as Open77.callbacks.callClient.
example:
-- Ask one client to confirm before selling
CreateThread(function()
    local pending, reason = Open77.net.callClient(source, "confirmPurchase", "ammo_box", 50)
    if not pending then return print(reason) end
    local confirmed = pending:await()
    if confirmed then sell(source, "ammo_box") end
end)

name: callClientAwait
summary: Asks one client a question and waits for the answer.
description: Requires network.events. Open77.net.callClient followed by :await(), so it must run inside a CreateThread, a command handler or another managed task. A client that refuses, times out or disconnects yields nil, reason -- never a partial answer. Aliased as Open77.callbacks.callClientAwait.
returns: the client handler's return values, or nil, reason
example:
local accepted = Open77.net.callClientAwait(source, "confirmPurchase", item, price)
if accepted ~= true then return end

name: emitClient
summary: Sends an event to one client or every client; the same function as `TriggerClientEvent`.
description: Requires `network.events`. A `playerId` of `-1` broadcasts. Same 32-argument, 48 KiB envelope as the inbound direction.
example:
-- Namespaced spelling of TriggerClientEvent: tell one player, or everyone with -1
Open77.net.emitClient("bank:deposit", playerId, 250)
Open77.net.emitClient("server:announce", -1, "Restart in 5 minutes")

name: on
summary: Registers an authenticated client event; the same function as `RegisterNetEvent`.
description: Requires `network.events`. During a network handler the global `source` is set from the authenticated connection, never from the client's payload -- that is the whole point of the distinction from `Open77.events.on`. Events accept at most 32 arguments in a 48 KiB JSON envelope.
example:
-- Namespaced spelling of RegisterNetEvent; source is the authenticated player
Open77.net.on("shop:buy", function(itemId)
    print("player", source, "wants", itemId)
end)

name: register
summary: Answers a callback a client sends with Open77.net.call.
description: Requires network.events. The handler is called as handler(source, ...): `source` is the authenticated player id, taken from the transport and never from the payload, exactly as a RegisterNetEvent handler sets it -- and that is the only thing the caller cannot choose, so re-validate every argument. Use the source argument rather than the global in a handler that yields, because another task can overwrite the global across a Wait. Return values become the answer; raising rejects the caller's promise with the error text. Names are per resource: a client reaches this handler by naming this resource. Up to 256 names and 256 questions being served at once per resource; stopping the resource answers what it was still serving with callback_target_stopped. Aliased as Open77.callbacks.register. See the Network callbacks guide.
example:
Open77.net.register("getStock", function(source, item)
    if type(item) ~= "string" then return nil, "invalid_item" end
    return stock[item] or 0
end)

name: unregister
summary: Stops answering a callback name registered with Open77.net.register.
description: Requires network.events. A later request for that name is refused with callback_not_found on the next frame rather than waiting out the asker's deadline. Aliased as Open77.callbacks.unregister.
example:
-- Stop answering a callback when the shop closes
Open77.net.unregister("getStock")

name: broadcast
summary: Sends one notification to every player.
description: `send` with a player id of `-1`. The returned id addresses the whole broadcast, so one `update` or `dismiss` reaches everyone who received it.
example:
-- Everybody sees the storm warning for ten seconds
Open77.notifications.broadcast({
    type = "warning",
    title = "Weather",
    message = "A sandstorm is rolling in.",
    durationMs = 10000,
})

name: clear
summary: Clears this resource's notifications for one player or for everyone.
description: Omitting the player clears this owner's notifications everywhere. It never touches another resource's notifications, so a gamemode clearing its own HUD does not wipe a chat or admin toast.
example:
-- The heist is over: drop every toast this resource still shows
Open77.notifications.clear()

name: dismiss
summary: Dismisses one notification this resource sent.
description: Only the owning resource may dismiss it. Dismissing one that has already expired succeeds.
example:
-- Remove the "waiting for players" toast once the round starts
local waiting = Open77.notifications.send(playerId, { message = "Waiting for players...", durationMs = 0 })
AddEventHandler("arena:roundStarted", function()
    Open77.notifications.dismiss(waiting)
end)

name: send
summary: Sends a notification to one player.
description: Routes to the official `open77_notifications` client package. Ids and mutation rights are isolated per calling server resource, so one resource cannot dismiss another's notification. See [notifications](notifications.md) for every definition field and the queue limits.

name: update
summary: Patches a notification this resource sent.
description: Sparse patch. Use it for a live counter or a progress line rather than dismissing and resending, which would restart the entry's animation and its place in the queue.
example:
-- A live progress counter, patched in place instead of re-sent
CreateThread(function()
    local id = Open77.notifications.send(playerId, { message = "Loading 0 %", durationMs = 0 })
    for percent = 10, 100, 10 do
        Wait(500)
        Open77.notifications.update(id, { message = ("Loading %d %%"):format(percent) })
    end
    Open77.notifications.dismiss(id)
end)

name: all
summary: Every authoritative NPC, optionally filtered to one routing bucket.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Returns the whole registry, whichever resource created each NPC.
example:
-- /npcs: how many server NPCs are alive right now
RegisterCommand("npcs", function(source)
    local alive = 0
    for _, npc in ipairs(Open77.npcs.all()) do
        if npc.health > 0 then alive = alive + 1 end
    end
    Open77.chat.send(source, ("%d NPCs alive"):format(alive))
end, true)

name: applyDamage
summary: Applies authoritative damage to an NPC.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. `source` and `cause` are recorded with the hit so a kill can be attributed. The damage still passes the NPC's damage policy, so an `invulnerable` NPC takes nothing.
example:
-- A trap deals 30 damage to the guard who stepped on it
Open77.npcs.applyDamage(guardId, 30, nil, "trap")

name: create
summary: Creates an authoritative NPC.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Build one from `record = "Character.*"` directly -- no catalogue entry is needed -- or from the legacy `template` alias. Definition fields are `record`, `template`, `position`, `yaw`, `bucket`, `appearance`, `loadout`, `behavior`, `aiMode`, `damagePolicy`, `health`, `maxHealth`, `streamingRadius`, `streamingHysteresis`, `despawnWhenUnobserved` and `persistent`. The id comes back at once, but engine readiness is asynchronous: a freshly created NPC is not yet a body in the world. See [NPCs](npcs.md).
example:
-- A shopkeeper standing behind the counter, who never fights back
local shopkeeper, reason = Open77.npcs.create({
    record = "Character.Judy",
    position = { x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.0 },
    yaw = 180.0,
    damagePolicy = "invulnerable",
    persistent = true,
})
if not shopkeeper then print("could not spawn the shopkeeper: " .. reason) end

name: get
summary: Reads one NPC's canonical snapshot.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Answers `nil` for an unknown id. The snapshot is the server's record, so it is available before the body has streamed to anyone.
example:
-- Is the boss still alive?
local boss = Open77.npcs.get(bossId)
if boss and boss.health <= 0 then
    Open77.chat.broadcast("The boss is down!")
end

name: getAttitude
summary: Reads back every attitude row an NPC states.
description: Requires `world.npcs`, and only for an NPC this resource created. Returns a table with `default`, `players`, `npcs`, `groups` and `relations`; `relations` is the row projected by `setRelationship` and is written by the platform, not by `setAttitude`.
example:
-- Debug: print how the guard regards everyone
local attitude = Open77.npcs.getAttitude(guardId)
if attitude then print("default attitude:", attitude.default) end

name: getBehavior
summary: Reads the canonical behavior policy of an owned NPC.
description: Requires world.npcs. Returns a detached table with aiEnabled, combatEnabled, perceptionEnabled, voiceEnabled. Client inspection uses Open77.npcs.get(id).behavior with npcs.read.
example:
-- Only re-enable combat if it was actually off
local behavior = Open77.npcs.getBehavior(guardId)
if behavior and not behavior.combatEnabled then
    Open77.npcs.setCombatEnabled(guardId, true)
end

name: getGroup
summary: The relationship group an NPC belongs to.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Returns the `combat.group` string, or nil when the NPC has none.
example:
-- Gang members share loot with their own group only
if Open77.npcs.getGroup(npcId) == "maelstrom" then
    dropGangLoot(npcId)
end

name: getRelationship
summary: Reads back a declared group relationship.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Returns the attitude token, or nil when this resource has declared nothing for the pair.
example:
-- Check before declaring: are the two gangs already at war?
if Open77.npcs.getRelationship("maelstrom", "valentinos") ~= "hostile" then
    Open77.npcs.setRelationship("maelstrom", "valentinos", "hostile")
end

name: kill
summary: Kills an NPC authoritatively.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Goes through the NPC life authority rather than setting health to zero, so the death is replicated once and consistently.
example:
-- /killnpc <id>
RegisterCommand("killnpc", function(source, args)
    local npcId = tonumber(args[1])
    if npcId then Open77.npcs.kill(npcId) end
end, true)

name: remove
summary: Removes an authoritative NPC.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Despawns the body for every viewer and drops the registry entry, including its queued tasks.

name: revive
summary: Revives an NPC, at full health by default.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. `health` defaults to 100. Reviving an NPC that is alive is accepted and simply sets its health.
example:
-- The medic revives the fallen bodyguard at half health
Open77.npcs.revive(bodyguardId, 50)

name: setAIEnabled
summary: Pauses or resumes a server-owned NPC's native AI and Open77 tasks.
description: Requires world.npcs and ownership. Does not change aiMode or the other behavior options. Disabling revokes the simulation lease; enabling resumes according to the selected mode.
example:
-- Pause every NPC while the round is paused, resume after
for _, npc in ipairs(Open77.npcs.all(ARENA_BUCKET)) do
    Open77.npcs.setAIEnabled(npc.id, false)
end

name: setAiMode
summary: Chooses who drives an NPC.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Modes are in `Open77.npcs.ai`: `tasks` (0, the Open77 task queue), `frozen` (1) and `native` (2, vanilla AI). This is a different axis from `setAIEnabled`, which pauses whichever driver is selected without changing the mode.
example:
-- Let the engine's own AI drive this civilian instead of the task queue
Open77.npcs.setAiMode(npcId, "native")

name: setAppearance
summary: Convenience patch for an NPC's appearance.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Exactly `update(id, { appearance = appearance })`.
example:
-- Swap the bartender's outfit for the night shift
Open77.npcs.setAppearance(bartenderId, "judy_night")

name: setAttitude
summary: Makes an NPC hostile, neutral or friendly toward a target.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Attitude is **per NPC and per target**, because that is the only shape the engine expresses per incarnation: `gameAttitudeAgent.SetAttitudeTowards(agent, attitude)` is a pair override. `options.towards` selects the row -- a player id, `{ npcId = n }` (which must belong to this resource) or `{ group = "name" }` -- and omitting it sets the default that covers everyone without a row. Resolution order is the per-entity row, then the per-group row, then the resource relationship row, then the default. Passing `nil` for `attitude` removes the row. An NPC that states nothing behaves exactly as it did before this call existed. Eligibility is a hard cap on players: a dead player, or one in another routing bucket, is never made a target by a directive. See the [NPC guide](npcs.md#attitude-and-relationship-groups).
example:
-- The guard becomes hostile toward the one player who broke in
Open77.npcs.setAttitude(guardId, "hostile", { towards = intruderId })

name: setBehavior
summary: Changes a server-owned NPC's native AI, combat, perception and voice policy.
description: Requires world.npcs and ownership. Partial boolean options aiEnabled, combatEnabled, perceptionEnabled, voiceEnabled; all default true. Replicated to observers and late joiners. See npc-behavior.md for engine semantics and boundaries.
example:
-- A passive quest giver: no combat, no barks, still walks
Open77.npcs.setBehavior(questGiverId, { combatEnabled = false, voiceEnabled = false })

name: setBucket
summary: Moves an NPC to another routing bucket.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Changes who can see it: only players in the same bucket stream the NPC.
example:
-- Move the arena boss into the arena instance
Open77.npcs.setBucket(bossId, ARENA_BUCKET)

name: setCombatEnabled
summary: Allows or suppresses a server-owned NPC's combat behavior.
description: Requires world.npcs and ownership. False clears threats, disables hostile acquisition/reactions and blocks outgoing hit processing without disabling scripted locomotion.
example:
-- Truce: the gang stops fighting during the negotiation
for _, npcId in ipairs(gang) do
    Open77.npcs.setCombatEnabled(npcId, false)
end

name: setDamagePolicy
summary: Sets whether an NPC can be hurt or killed.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Policies are in `Open77.npcs.damage`: `mortal` (0), `immortal` (1, can be hurt but not killed) and `invulnerable` (2, takes nothing).
example:
-- The quest giver can be hurt but never killed
Open77.npcs.setDamagePolicy(questGiverId, "immortal")

name: setGroup
summary: Puts an NPC in a relationship group.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Writes the pre-existing `combat.group` loadout field, so it keeps its existing meaning -- two NPCs sharing a non-empty group are allies -- and additionally picks up whatever `setRelationship` has declared for that group. Group names are at most 64 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - .`; `nil` removes the group. Unlike the attitude rows, a group does **not** survive a wholesale `setLoadout`, because it is an ordinary loadout field.
example:
-- Two spawned gang members become allies through a shared group
Open77.npcs.setGroup(firstId, "maelstrom")
Open77.npcs.setGroup(secondId, "maelstrom")

name: setHealth
summary: Convenience patch for an NPC's health and maximum.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Passing `maxHealth` raises or lowers the canonical maximum at the same time; omitting it leaves the maximum alone.
example:
-- The boss has 500 health, out of 500
Open77.npcs.setHealth(bossId, 500, 500)

name: setLoadout
summary: Convenience patch for an NPC's loadout.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Exactly `update(id, { loadout = loadout })`.
example:
-- Arm the guard with a Lexington
Open77.npcs.setLoadout(guardId, { weapon = "Items.Preset_Lexington_Default" })

name: setPerceptionEnabled
summary: Controls autonomous sensory acquisition for a server-owned NPC.
description: Requires world.npcs and ownership. False disables senses, reactions and automatic threat seeding; does not cancel an existing explicit target. Combat or AI disabled takes precedence.
example:
-- A stealth mission: the guard only fights if a script tells it to
Open77.npcs.setPerceptionEnabled(guardId, false)

name: setRagdoll
summary: Sets an NPC's canonical ragdoll state.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Exactly `update(id, { ragdoll = enabled == true })`; the state is replicated, so every viewer agrees.
example:
-- Knocked out by a punch: the body goes limp for three seconds
Open77.npcs.setRagdoll(npcId, true)
SetTimeout(3000, function() Open77.npcs.setRagdoll(npcId, false) end)

name: setRelationship
summary: Declares how two of this resource's groups regard each other.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. The matrix is **per resource** -- one resource's groups never reach another's bodies, exactly as its NPC reads and writes never do -- and it is symmetric: declaring `a` against `b` also declares `b` against `a`. The resulting row is projected onto every owned NPC in either group and replicated, so observers resolve it without asking the server; an NPC that joins the group later picks up the standing row. `nil` for `attitude` removes the declaration. The matrix dies with the resource that declared it. This is NOT the engine's global attitude matrix: `gameCAttitudeManager.SetAttitudeRelation` is process-wide and shared with vanilla content, and is deliberately not used -- see `docs/research/npc-behavior-control.md`.
example:
-- Gang war: every Maelstrom NPC this resource owns hates every Valentino
Open77.npcs.setRelationship("maelstrom", "valentinos", "hostile")

name: setTransform
summary: Sets an NPC's canonical position and yaw.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. A teleport, not a walk: for movement that the AI performs, enqueue a `moveTo` task instead.
example:
-- Teleport the shopkeeper back behind the counter
Open77.npcs.setTransform(shopkeeperId, { position = counter, yaw = 180.0 })

name: setVoiceEnabled
summary: Controls voice lines and barks of a server-owned NPC.
description: Requires world.npcs and ownership. Controls native voiceset lines/grunts (including combat/search barks), suppresses scripted voiceovers and filters native dialogue routed through subtitles. Replicated per NPC, not a global sound/SFX mute or a guarantee to stop audio already playing.
example:
-- Silence the bartender's barks during the cutscene
Open77.npcs.setVoiceEnabled(bartenderId, false)

name: target
summary: Who an NPC is currently fighting.
description: Requires `world.npcs`, and only for an NPC this resource created. Returns `{ kind = "none"|"player"|"npc", id = n }`, mirroring the last reading its lease holder reported. It is the engine's own target tracker, not a record of what a script asked for, so an NPC that acquires a target by perception shows up here too. `onNpcTargetChanged` fires on every change to this value.
example:
-- Is the guard fighting a player right now?
local target = Open77.npcs.target(guardId)
if target and target.kind == "player" then
    Open77.chat.send(target.id, "The guard is after you!")
end

name: templates
summary: The legacy alias catalogue of NPC templates.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. It is a convenience list, **not** a limit: `create` accepts any `Character.*` record whether or not it appears here.
example:
-- Print the legacy alias list once at startup
for _, template in ipairs(Open77.npcs.templates()) do
    print(template.name, template.record)
end

name: update
summary: Patches an NPC's canonical state.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Sparse: appearance, loadout, behavior, AI mode, damage policy, health and ragdoll can all be patched in one call, and everything omitted is left alone. The convenience setters below are thin wrappers over this.

name: all
summary: Every task currently queued or running on an NPC.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Ordered by channel and priority, which is the order the scheduler will take them in.
example:
-- Debug: what is the NPC doing?
for _, task in ipairs(Open77.npcs.tasks.all(npcId)) do
    print(task.id, task.type, task.status)
end

name: attack
summary: Orders an NPC to engage a target.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. **Action channel**, so it composes with a standing movement task instead of replacing one: the engine suspends `ignoreInCombat` movement for the fight and resumes it afterwards. The target is a player id or `{ npcId = n }`, and an NPC target must belong to this resource. The task forces the pair hostile and seeds the target into the puppet's own target tracker, re-seeding every `reacquireMs` (default 4,000; 500-60,000); the engine's combat AI drives the body from there, so Open77 never issues a shoot command and never cancels the behaviour tree. It reports `success` when the target dies, streams out or is removed, and `failure` with `attack_target_unavailable` when the target cannot be resolved at all. Cancelling drops the seeded threat; the attitude is left to whatever `setAttitude` states.

params.name: target
params.type: player id, or table { playerId } | { npcId }

example:
-- The bodyguard engages whoever attacked the client
AddEventHandler("vip:attacked", function(attackerId)
    Open77.npcs.tasks.attack(bodyguardId, attackerId)
end)

name: cancel
summary: Cancels one queued or running task.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Leaves the rest of the queue in place; `clear` is the way to empty a channel.
example:
-- The player paid: the guard stops attacking
local task = Open77.npcs.tasks.attack(guardId, playerId)
AddEventHandler("debt:paid", function()
    Open77.npcs.tasks.cancel(guardId, task)
end)

name: chase
summary: Drives an NPC's vehicle after a target.
description:
Requires `world.npcs` and `world.vehicles`. This is a ped-addressed view of `Open77.vehicles.ai`, which owns the vanilla `AIVehicleDriveToPointAutonomousCommand` pipeline -- there is no second driving stack and no second set of limits. The NPC must already be the attached driver of a vehicle (`Open77.vehicles.ai.attachDriver(vehicleId, { npcId = id })`), otherwise every one of these returns `nil, "npc_not_driving"`. The return value is the driving state the vehicle API returns.
