The target is a player id, or a table naming `playerId`, `vehicleId` or `npcId`. The destination is refreshed twice a second from the target's position for as long as it stays in the same bucket.

params.name: target
params.type: player id | table { playerId | vehicleId | npcId }

example:
-- A police NPC already driving a cruiser chases the suspect
Open77.npcs.tasks.chase(copId, suspectId, { distance = 8 })

name: clear
summary: Clears queued and current tasks, optionally on one channel.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Omitting the channel clears them all. Clearing the movement channel stops the NPC where it is rather than returning it anywhere.
example:
-- Stop everything the NPC was doing
Open77.npcs.tasks.clear(npcId)

name: driveTo
summary: Drives an NPC's vehicle to a position.
description:
Requires `world.npcs` and `world.vehicles`. This is a ped-addressed view of `Open77.vehicles.ai`, which owns the vanilla `AIVehicleDriveToPointAutonomousCommand` pipeline -- there is no second driving stack and no second set of limits. The NPC must already be the attached driver of a vehicle (`Open77.vehicles.ai.attachDriver(vehicleId, { npcId = id })`), otherwise every one of these returns `nil, "npc_not_driving"`. The return value is the driving state the vehicle API returns.

`options.style` is the driving behaviour (`normal`, `cautious`, `aggressive`) and is the same field `Open77.vehicles.ai.setBehavior` writes.
example:
-- The taxi driver takes the car to the drop-off point
Open77.npcs.tasks.driveTo(driverId, vector3(-1442.2, 127.4, 18.0), { speed = 15 })

name: driveWander
summary: Drives an NPC's vehicle along the road network indefinitely.
description:
Requires `world.npcs` and `world.vehicles`. This is a ped-addressed view of `Open77.vehicles.ai`, which owns the vanilla `AIVehicleDriveToPointAutonomousCommand` pipeline -- there is no second driving stack and no second set of limits. The NPC must already be the attached driver of a vehicle (`Open77.vehicles.ai.attachDriver(vehicleId, { npcId = id })`), otherwise every one of these returns `nil, "npc_not_driving"`. The return value is the driving state the vehicle API returns.

This is `joinTraffic`, the engine's own lane-following mode. It is **not** a random-destination wander: Cyberpunk traffic AI drives authored lanes and there is no free-roam equivalent to GTA's `TaskVehicleDriveWander`.
example:
-- Ambient traffic: this driver just cruises the city
Open77.npcs.tasks.driveWander(driverId, { speed = 12 })

name: driving
summary: The driving job an NPC is the attached driver of.
description: Requires `world.npcs` and `world.vehicles`. This is a ped-addressed view of `Open77.vehicles.ai`, which owns the vanilla `AIVehicleDriveToPointAutonomousCommand` pipeline -- there is no second driving stack and no second set of limits. The NPC must already be the attached driver of a vehicle (`Open77.vehicles.ai.attachDriver(vehicleId, { npcId = id })`), otherwise every one of these returns `nil, "npc_not_driving"`. The return value is the driving state the vehicle API returns.
example:
-- Is the taxi still on its way?
local state = Open77.npcs.tasks.driving(driverId)
if state then print("driving job:", state.status) end

name: enqueue
summary: Enqueues any supported task on an NPC.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. The escape hatch under the typed helpers: `taskType` names the task, `parameters` is JSON-encoded for the host, and `options` carries `channel` (default 0), `priority` (default 0) and `timeoutMs` (default 0, meaning no timeout). Channels are in `Open77.npcs.channels`: `movement` (0), `look` (1), `action` (2) and `fullBody` (3) -- tasks on different channels run at the same time.

name: enterVehicle
summary: Sends an NPC to a vehicle seat.
description:
Requires `world.npcs`. Movement channel -- walking to a car is locomotion, so it replaces a standing `moveTo` rather than composing with it.

Seats use `Open77.vehicles.seats` numbering (`-1` driver, `0` front passenger, `1` rear left, `2` rear right) and also accept the names `driver`, `frontPassenger`, `rearLeft`, `rearRight`. The body walks to the car and mounts when it is within `approachDistance`; `warp = true` skips the walk and mounts on the spot.

The task reports `Executing` while walking and succeeds only once the mounting relation is readable back off the body, because that is the only honest proof it is seated. It fails with `vehicle_not_streamed` when no client has the car streamed in, and `vehicle_mount_refused` when the engine refuses the seat.

params.name: options
params.type: table { warp?, approachDistance?, speed?, priority?, timeoutMs? }

example:
-- The getaway driver walks to the car and takes the wheel
Open77.npcs.tasks.enterVehicle(driverId, getawayCarId, Open77.vehicles.seats.driver)

name: exitVehicle
summary: Takes an NPC out of whatever seat it is in.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Movement channel. Idempotent on purpose: a body already out of the car has done what was asked, and the task succeeds with reason `not_in_vehicle` rather than failing. `options.vehicleId` narrows the task to one vehicle, in which case a body sitting in a different one fails with `vehicle_mismatch` instead of being pulled out of it.
example:
-- The passenger gets out at the destination
Open77.npcs.tasks.exitVehicle(passengerId, { vehicleId = taxiId })

name: face
summary: Rotates an NPC's body toward a world point.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Look channel, so it runs alongside movement. Options are `tolerance` (default 3 degrees), `speed` (rotation, default 180 degrees per second), `priority` and `timeoutMs` (default 5,000).
example:
-- The shopkeeper turns to face the customer
local customer = Open77.players.position(playerId)
if customer then Open77.npcs.tasks.face(shopkeeperId, customer) end

name: flee
summary: Sends an NPC running away from something.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Movement channel. `from` is a player id, `{ npcId = n }` or a fixed `{ x, y, z }`; a live body is re-measured every cycle, so the NPC keeps breaking contact as the thing it flees moves. It reports `success` once `distance` metres separate them (5-200, default 50) or the target is gone, and each leg is capped so the body asks for a destination it can path to. The tracked threat on the fled body is dropped once at task start; this is best-effort, because the attitude is untouched and a still-hostile body may re-acquire the same target by perception -- `setAttitude(id, "neutral", { towards = ... })` is the composable answer. Options are `speed` (default `sprint`), `distance`, `priority` and `timeoutMs` (default 30,000).

params.name: from
params.type: player id, or table { playerId } | { npcId } | { x, y, z }

example:
-- The civilian runs 60 m away from the shooter
Open77.npcs.tasks.flee(civilianId, shooterId, { distance = 60, speed = "sprint" })

name: follow
summary: Makes an NPC follow a player, another NPC, or a point.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Movement channel. `target` is a player id (a number), `{ type = "npc", id = ... }`, or a position table. Options are `distance` (default 2 metres), `speed` (default `walk`) and `onTargetLost` (default `wait`), plus `priority` and `timeoutMs`.

params.name: options
params.type: table { distance?, speed?, onTargetLost?, priority?, timeoutMs? }

example:
-- The bodyguard follows the client two metres behind
Open77.npcs.tasks.follow(bodyguardId, clientId, { distance = 2, speed = "walk" })

name: get
summary: Reads one task's state.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. The task state machine is described in [NPCs](npcs.md); a task that has finished stops being readable.
example:
-- Wait until the walk is finished
CreateThread(function()
    local task = Open77.npcs.tasks.moveTo(npcId, door)
    while Open77.npcs.tasks.get(npcId, task) do Wait(250) end
    print("the NPC has arrived (or gave up)")
end)

name: guard
summary: Anchors an NPC to a position and lets it fight from there.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Movement channel. A standing order with no natural end: it runs until cancelled or timed out. Whenever the body is further than `radius` metres (2-100, default 10) from the anchor **and is not already in a fight**, it walks back; while it holds a hostile threat it is left entirely alone, so the engine can take cover and manoeuvre. Guarding does not by itself make anything hostile -- pair it with `setAttitude` or a relationship group. Options are `speed` (default `run`), `priority` and `timeoutMs`.
example:
-- Two guards hold the gate and fight from there
for _, guardId in ipairs(guards) do
    Open77.npcs.tasks.guard(guardId, gate, 8)
end

name: hold
summary: Holds an NPC's movement until cancelled or timed out.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Movement channel, no default timeout: it holds indefinitely until `cancel`, `clear`, or an explicit `timeoutMs`.
example:
-- Freeze the NPC in place while the dialogue runs
local hold = Open77.npcs.tasks.hold(npcId)
AddEventHandler("dialogue:closed", function() Open77.npcs.tasks.cancel(npcId, hold) end)

name: lookAt
summary: Drives an NPC's look channel toward a player, NPC or point.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Look channel. `target` is a player id (a number), `{ type = "player"|"npc", id = ... }`, or a position table. Unlike `face`, this turns the head rather than the body.
example:
-- The receptionist watches the player who walked in
Open77.npcs.tasks.lookAt(receptionistId, playerId)

name: moveTo
summary: Walks or runs an NPC to a world point.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Movement channel. Options are `speed` (default `walk`), `acceptanceRadius` (default 1 metre), `priority` and `timeoutMs` (default 30,000 -- unlike most tasks, this one gives up rather than pathing forever).
example:
-- Send the courier running to the drop point
Open77.npcs.tasks.moveTo(courierId, { x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.0 }, { speed = "run" })

name: patrol
summary: Sends an NPC round a list of points.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Movement channel. `loop` defaults to true and `backAndForth` to false, so the default is a closed circuit. Options also take `speed`, `priority` and `timeoutMs`.

params.name: options
params.type: table { loop?, backAndForth?, speed?, priority?, timeoutMs? }

name: playAnimation
summary: Runs a full-body animation on an NPC.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Full-body channel, so it takes over movement and look for its duration. `options.loop` defaults to false.
example:
-- The bouncer smokes by the door
Open77.npcs.tasks.playAnimation(bouncerId, "emote_smoke", { loop = true })

name: setDriverAbility
summary: Maps a 0..1 driver ability onto the two levers the engine exposes.
description:
Requires `world.npcs` and `world.vehicles`. This is a ped-addressed view of `Open77.vehicles.ai`, which owns the vanilla `AIVehicleDriveToPointAutonomousCommand` pipeline -- there is no second driving stack and no second set of limits. The NPC must already be the attached driver of a vehicle (`Open77.vehicles.ai.attachDriver(vehicleId, { npcId = id })`), otherwise every one of these returns `nil, "npc_not_driving"`. The return value is the driving state the vehicle API returns.

FiveM's `SetDriverAbility` is an engine skill parameter and 2.31 has none. This is an explicit **mapping**, documented so nobody has to guess it: below 0.34 is `cautious`, above 0.67 is `aggressive`, and in between is `normal`; the speed cap is `8 + ability * 24` metres per second. It returns the resulting driving state so a caller can read exactly what was applied instead of assuming.
example:
-- A nervous rookie driver
Open77.npcs.tasks.setDriverAbility(driverId, 0.3)

name: stopDriving
summary: Stops whatever an NPC's vehicle was doing.
description: Requires `world.npcs` and `world.vehicles`. This is a ped-addressed view of `Open77.vehicles.ai`, which owns the vanilla `AIVehicleDriveToPointAutonomousCommand` pipeline -- there is no second driving stack and no second set of limits. The NPC must already be the attached driver of a vehicle (`Open77.vehicles.ai.attachDriver(vehicleId, { npcId = id })`), otherwise every one of these returns `nil, "npc_not_driving"`. The return value is the driving state the vehicle API returns.
example:
-- Pull over: the chase is called off
Open77.npcs.tasks.stopDriving(copId)

name: wait
summary: Makes an NPC wait for a fixed time.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Action channel by default. `timeoutMs` defaults to the duration plus one second, so a wait cannot outlive itself.
example:
-- Walk to the counter, wait two seconds, then walk back
CreateThread(function()
    Open77.npcs.tasks.moveTo(npcId, counter)
    Open77.npcs.tasks.wait(npcId, 2000, { channel = Open77.npcs.channels.movement })
    Open77.npcs.tasks.moveTo(npcId, home)
end)

name: wander
summary: Lets an NPC wander with the supplied movement parameters.
description: Requires `world.npcs`. Movement channel. The whole options table is passed to the host as the task parameters, so it carries the wander radius and speed as well as `priority` and `timeoutMs`.

name: workspot
summary: Puts an NPC into an authored workspot scenario.
description:
Requires `world.npcs`. FullBody channel, the same one `playAnimation` uses, so a workspot and an animation cannot run on one body at once.

`reference` is either a **catalogue profile id** (`smoke`, `sit`, `phone`, `dance`, `meditate`, ... -- see `Open77.npcs.tasks.workspots`), which brings its own shipped device entity and its own validated clip set, or a **raw clip name** played through the generic device. The catalogue profile is the supported form; a raw clip is an escape hatch whose animset the generic device may not carry.

`durationMs` ends the scenario by **succeeding**, not by timing out: a scenario that ran its course is not a failure, and `timeoutMs` stays free to mean "no client ever picked the command up". `loop = true` has no end and runs until cancelled.

params.name: reference
params.type: catalogue profile id or clip name

params.name: options
params.type: table { durationMs?, loop?, clip?, priority?, timeoutMs? }

example:
-- The mechanic leans on the car for a minute
Open77.npcs.tasks.workspot(mechanicId, "smoke", { durationMs = 60000 })

name: workspots
summary: The vanilla scenario catalogue a workspot task can name.
description: Ungated. The same twelve shipped RP workspot profiles `Open77.animations.list()` offers for players -- one catalogue, two callers, never two lists that could disagree. Each entry gives `id`, `label`, `category`, the default `clip`, the vanilla `workspot` resource it plays, and the full clip set. `query` filters on id, label or category.
example:
-- List the workspot profiles a task can name
for _, profile in ipairs(Open77.npcs.tasks.workspots()) do
    print(profile.id, profile.label)
end

name: policy
summary: The perspective policy **this** resource set.
description: Requires `network.events`. Returns `policy, perspective, declared` for the calling VM only -- it is not a read of the server's effective policy, which is whatever was written last by any resource.
example:
-- What did this resource set?
local policy, perspective, declared = Open77.perspective.policy()
if declared then print("we set", policy, perspective) end

name: setPolicy
summary: Sets whether players on this server may use third person.
description: Requires `network.events`. `policy` is `disabled`, `allowed`, `default` or `forced`; `perspective` is `fpp` or `tps` and is required for `forced`, because a pin with nothing pinned would quietly become first person. The policy is broadcast to every client and answered again to anyone who joins later. Call it from the resource's **start path**: a reload replaces the VM, and the policy lives in it. If two resources declare a policy the last write wins, so one owner -- normally the gamemode -- is the remedy.
example:
-- A hardcore server: first person only, set on the resource's start path
Open77.perspective.setPolicy("forced", "fpp")

name: cancel
summary: Cancel an interaction owned by this resource.
description: Requires players.interactions.read (inspection) or players.interactions.control (creation/cancellation). Uses canonical player IDs. The coordinator reserves both players and cancels on death, disconnect, vehicle entry, bucket change, resource stop, timeout or presentation failure. Gameplay effects remain the resource's responsibility. See player-interactions.md. Custom reason accepts 1–64 ASCII alphanumeric/underscore characters; invalid reasons normalize to cancelled. Delayed callbacks should retain the interaction ID, never cancel whatever action happens to occupy the player later.
example:
-- The item vanished mid-handover: cancel the interaction with a reason
Open77.playerInteractions.cancel(interactionId, "item_removed")

name: current
summary: Read the interaction reserving a player, including an unanswered invitation.
description: Requires players.interactions.read (inspection) or players.interactions.control (creation/cancellation). Uses canonical player IDs. The coordinator reserves both players and cancels on death, disconnect, vehicle entry, bucket change, resource stop, timeout or presentation failure. Gameplay effects remain the resource's responsibility. See player-interactions.md. Terminal states are removed from the active registry. Read access never grants cancellation of another resource's action.
returns: active state or nil; nil, reason on rejection
example:
-- Refuse a trade while the player is already in an interaction
local busy = Open77.playerInteractions.current(playerId)
if busy then return Open77.chat.send(playerId, "Finish what you are doing first.") end

name: get
summary: Read a copied active state by opaque interaction ID.
description: Requires players.interactions.read (inspection) or players.interactions.control (creation/cancellation). Uses canonical player IDs. The coordinator reserves both players and cancels on death, disconnect, vehicle entry, bucket change, resource stop, timeout or presentation failure. Gameplay effects remain the resource's responsibility. See player-interactions.md. Terminal states are removed from the active registry. Read access never grants cancellation of another resource's action.
returns: active state or nil; nil, reason on rejection
example:
-- Read the state of the interaction we started
local state = Open77.playerInteractions.get(interactionId)
if state then print(state.kind, state.phase) end

name: isReserved
summary: Check whether a player is exclusively reserved by this service.
description: Requires players.interactions.read (inspection) or players.interactions.control (creation/cancellation). Uses canonical player IDs. The coordinator reserves both players and cancels on death, disconnect, vehicle entry, bucket change, resource stop, timeout or presentation failure. Gameplay effects remain the resource's responsibility. See player-interactions.md. Terminal states are removed from the active registry. Read access never grants cancellation of another resource's action.
example:
-- A reserved player cannot be teleported by the event script
if Open77.playerInteractions.isReserved(playerId) then return end

name: list
summary: List active interactions owned by this resource only.
description: Requires players.interactions.read (inspection) or players.interactions.control (creation/cancellation). Uses canonical player IDs. The coordinator reserves both players and cancels on death, disconnect, vehicle entry, bucket change, resource stop, timeout or presentation failure. Gameplay effects remain the resource's responsibility. See player-interactions.md. Terminal states are removed from the active registry. Read access never grants cancellation of another resource's action.
example:
-- /interactions: what is this resource coordinating right now?
RegisterCommand("interactions", function(source)
    for _, state in ipairs(Open77.playerInteractions.list() or {}) do
        Open77.chat.send(source, ("%s: %d -> %d (%s)"):format(state.kind, state.actorId, state.targetId, state.phase))
    end
end, true)

name: request
summary: Reserve and coordinate a two-player interaction.
description: Requires players.interactions.read (inspection) or players.interactions.control (creation/cancellation). Uses canonical player IDs. The coordinator reserves both players and cancels on death, disconnect, vehicle entry, bucket change, resource stop, timeout or presentation failure. Gameplay effects remain the resource's responsibility. See player-interactions.md. Kinds: give, heal, carry, escort, custom. Options: durationMs (500–600000, default4000), startDistance (.25–10, default3), breakDistance (startDistance–20, default5), inviteTimeoutMs (1000–60000, default15000), consent (defaulttrue), optional actorAnimation/targetAnimation RP profiles for stationary kinds. Carry/escort reject profile overrides. Both players must be alive, on foot, near and in the same bucket. Acceptance is not proof of native playback; observe lifecycle events.
example:
-- /give <id>: hand an item over with a four-second synchronized animation
RegisterCommand("give", function(source, args)
    local target = tonumber(args[1])
    if not target then return end
    local state, reason = Open77.playerInteractions.request(source, target, "give", { durationMs = 4000 })
    if not state then Open77.chat.send(source, "Cannot give: " .. reason) end
end, false)

name: all
summary: Every authenticated player id, ascending.
description: No permission. `GetPlayers` is the same function. This is the host's roster, so a gamemode no longer needs its own copy assembled from join and leave events.
example:
-- Announce a restart to everyone currently connected
RegisterCommand("announce", function(source, args)
    local text = table.concat(args, " ")
    for _, playerId in ipairs(Open77.players.all()) do
        Open77.notifications.send(playerId, { type = "warning", message = text })
    end
end, true)

name: ban
summary: Bans a player's device identity through the master and disconnects them now.
description: Requires `players.ban`. `BanPlayer` is the same function. Resolves the authenticated device identity and submits a **server-scoped** ban to the master -- different from `Open77.access.ban`, which writes the server's own local list. `durationSeconds` must be strictly positive; omitting it bans permanently. Reasons accept up to 512 UTF-8 bytes. Central publication is best-effort and asynchronous while the local kick is queued immediately.
returns: reason: permission_denied:players.ban, invalid_player_id, invalid_reason, invalid_duration, server_unavailable, ban_failed
example:
-- /ban <id> <days> <reason>: a temporary ban published through the master
RegisterCommand("ban", function(source, args)
    local target, days = tonumber(args[1]), tonumber(args[2])
    if not target or not days then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Usage: /ban <id> <days> <reason>") end
    local reason = table.concat(args, " ", 3)
    local ok, err = Open77.players.ban(target, reason, days * 86400)
    if not ok then Open77.chat.send(source, "Ban failed: " .. err) end
end, true)

name: closest
summary: The nearest player to a point or to another player.
description: No permission. The first entry `Open77.players.nearby` would return, with the same anchor rules and the same options plus `radius`, which it takes in the options table because it has no positional radius. It answers a **bare nil** -- no second value -- when the search worked and nobody matched, and `nil, reason` when it failed: that is what separates an empty street from a bad argument.

params.name: anchor
params.type: integer (player id) | table { x, y, z }

params.name: options
params.type: table { radius?, bucket?, includeSelf?, limit?, maxAgeMs? }

returns: nearest entry, or nil when nobody matched
example:
-- /rob: rob the closest player within 3 metres
RegisterCommand("rob", function(source)
    local victim = Open77.players.closest(source, { radius = 3 })
    if not victim then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Nobody close enough.") end
    Open77.chat.send(victim.playerId, Open77.players.name(source) .. " is robbing you!")
end, false)

name: damage
summary: Applies authoritative damage to a player.
description: Requires `players.damage.apply`. Options are `attacker`, `cause` (or its alias `kind`) and `weapon`. The damage still passes the combat multipliers, team and scope rules, and every installed `Open77.combat.onDamage` arbiter.
example:
-- Fall damage reported by a zone trigger: 20 points, no attacker
RegisterNetEvent("parkour:badLanding", function()
    Open77.players.damage(source, 20, { cause = "fall" })
end)

name: disconnect
summary: Disconnects a player with a reason they see.
description: Requires `players.disconnect`. `DropPlayer` is the same function. The reason is trimmed, must contain no control characters and is limited to 127 UTF-8 bytes so the transport can deliver it without truncation; omitting it uses `Disconnected by server.`. The closure is deferred until the current Lua callback returns, and repeated calls for the same player in one tick are idempotent -- the first reason wins.
returns: reason: permission_denied:players.disconnect, invalid_player_id, invalid_reason, player_not_found, server_unavailable
example:
-- /kick <id> <reason>
RegisterCommand("kick", function(source, args)
    local target = tonumber(args[1])
    if not target then return end
    local reason = table.concat(args, " ", 2)
    Open77.players.disconnect(target, reason ~= "" and reason or "Kicked by an admin.")
end, true)

name: distance
summary: The distance in metres between two players, two points, or one of each.
description: No permission. Each argument is a player id (an integer) or a point (a table with numeric `x`, `y`, `z`); an Open77 `vector3` is a point, because the shared vector type is a plain table with real `x`/`y`/`z` fields. Three-dimensional. A player's position comes from their last accepted snapshot whatever its age -- call `Open77.players.get` first if the age matters to the decision you are about to make. `position_unknown` means the player exists but has never reported a transform.

params.name: a
params.type: integer (player id) | table { x, y, z }

params.name: b
params.type: integer (player id) | table { x, y, z }

returns: reason: invalid_argument, invalid_position, player_not_found, position_unknown, sessions_unavailable
example:
-- Handcuffs only work at arm's length
RegisterCommand("cuff", function(source, args)
    local target = tonumber(args[1])
    if not target then return end
    local metres = Open77.players.distance(source, target)
    if not metres or metres > 2.0 then
        return Open77.chat.send(source, "Get closer.")
    end
    Open77.players.setFrozen(target, true)
end, false)

name: endpoint
summary: The address a player is connecting from, as `ip:port`.
description: Requires `players.identity.sensitive` -- the only function in this API behind that capability, and the reason it exists. An endpoint is an IP address: it identifies a person outside the game, it is the one field here that can follow someone home, and in most of the world it is regulated personal data. A resource that wants it says so in its manifest, where the operator installing that resource sees it before running it. Folding it into the ungated `Open77.players.identity` would have handed every resource on the server an address list it never asked for. IPv4 renders `203.0.113.9:31337`, IPv6 `[2001:db8::1]:31337`. `endpoint_unavailable` when the transport cannot name an address it is sure of -- it never guesses one.
example:
-- Anti-alt check: log the address a suspicious account joined from
-- (the manifest must declare players.identity.sensitive)
AddEventHandler("onPlayerConnected", function(playerId)
    local endpoint, reason = Open77.players.endpoint(playerId)
    print(("player %d connected from %s"):format(playerId, endpoint or reason))
end)

name: fade
summary: Cover or uncover one player's screen from the server.
description: Requires `players.screen`. `out` true fades that player to black and HOLDS; `out` false gives the image back. The client consumes the relay frame itself and drives the same guarded native quest fade `Open77.screen` uses, so the target needs no client resource of its own, and a fade a client resource already owns is never stolen -- the request is refused instead. `durationMs` is 0..10000 (default 500); `options.timeoutMs` is 1000..60000 (default 15000) and is a ceiling the CLIENT enforces on real time, so forgetting the second call costs a pause, never a player stuck looking at black. Bracket a teleport with it: fade, move, fade back.
example:
-- Bracket a teleport with a fade so the player never sees the streaming
CreateThread(function()
    Open77.players.fade(playerId, true, 400)
    Wait(400)
    Open77.players.teleport(playerId, { x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.0 }, { fade = false })
    Open77.players.fade(playerId, false, 400)
end)

name: fadeIn
summary: Give one player's image back.
description: Requires `players.screen`. `Open77.players.fade(playerId, false, durationMs)`.
example:
-- The cutscene is over: give the image back
Open77.players.fadeIn(playerId, 800)

name: fadeOut
summary: Fade one player's screen to black and hold it.
description: Requires `players.screen`. `Open77.players.fade(playerId, true, durationMs, options)` under the name a spawn or teleport reads better with.
example:
-- Knocked out: black screen for five seconds, then back
CreateThread(function()
    Open77.players.fadeOut(playerId, 300)
    Wait(5000)
    Open77.players.fadeIn(playerId, 1000)
end)

name: forceOutOfVehicle
summary: Forces a player out of a vehicle, overriding the exit lock.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Alias of `Open77.vehicles.forcePlayerOutOfVehicle`. Omitting the vehicle ejects them from whatever they are in. The forced exit overrides `setVehicleExitLocked` and keeps the seat reserved until native confirmation or the bounded transition timeout.
example:
-- The car was sold while someone was sitting in it
Open77.players.forceOutOfVehicle(playerId)

name: get
summary: Everything the host can answer about one player synchronously, with a dated transform.
description: No permission. The one read a job script makes before it acts. Unlike `Open77.players.position` it never goes quiet on a stale snapshot: it reports `ageMs` and `fresh` and lets the caller pick its own threshold -- `fresh` is true precisely when `position` would have answered, so the old semantics are still reachable from one reading. Always present: `playerId`, `bucket`, `fresh`, `ready`. Present once the player has reported: `ageMs`, `position` `{ x, y, z }`, `heading` (alias `yaw`), `velocity` `{ x, y, z }`, `speed`, `stateFlags`, `flags`, and `supportKind`/`supportId` on a moving support. Present when the host can resolve them: `name`, `identifier`, `userId`. A player who has never sent an accepted snapshot has no `position` and no `ageMs` at all, which is distinguishable from a reading that is merely old. Health (`players.stats.read`), life (`players.life.read`) and vehicle seat (`world.vehicles`) fields are **absent rather than false** without the permission that already guards `getHealth`, `getLifeState` and `getVehicleSeat`. See [the rich read](server-api.md#the-rich-read-and-the-freshness-decision).
example:
local read = Open77.players.get(playerId)
if read and read.position and (read.ageMs or 0) < 5000 then
  -- your freshness threshold, not ours
end

name: getHealth
summary: A player's health, armor and god-mode snapshot.
description: Requires `players.damage.read`. `GetPlayerHealth` is the same function. New resources should prefer `Open77.stats.getHealth`, which returns the richer nested pool the client also exposes.
example:
-- /hp <id>: an admin reads a player's health
RegisterCommand("hp", function(source, args)
    local hp = Open77.players.getHealth(tonumber(args[1]) or source)
    if hp then Open77.chat.send(source, ("Health %d / %d"):format(hp.health, hp.maxHealth)) end
end, true)

name: getHoloCallEyes
summary: Read whether any server resource holds a player's holocall eye-glow lease.
description: Requires players.holocall.read and an explicit connected network player ID. This reads authoritative cosmetic intent, not a native render acknowledgement. False means no lease; nil, reason means the query failed. See holocall-eyes.md.
example:
-- Is the player already on a call before starting a new one?
local enabled = Open77.players.getHoloCallEyes(playerId)
if not enabled then Open77.players.setHoloCallEyes(playerId, true, { durationMs = 30000 }) end

name: getLifeState
summary: A player's canonical life snapshot.
description: Requires `players.life.read`. `GetPlayerLifeState` is the same function. `phase` is `alive`, `dead`, `revivepending`, `respawnpending` or `recovering` -- **no underscore**, unlike the client spelling. Prefer `isDead` over comparing the string.
example:
-- Only a living player can accept a job
RegisterCommand("job", function(source)
    local life = Open77.players.getLifeState(source)
    if not life or life.phase ~= "alive" then
        return Open77.chat.send(source, "Come back when you are on your feet.")
    end
    startJob(source)
end, false)

name: getStats
summary: A player's combined health and stamina snapshot.
description: Requires `players.stats.read`. `GetPlayerStats` is the same function, and `Open77.stats.get` is the preferred spelling for new resources.
example:
-- Show health and stamina together on request
RegisterCommand("stats", function(source)
    local stats = Open77.players.getStats(source)
    if stats then
        Open77.chat.send(source, ("HP %d / %d  Stamina %d / %d"):format(
            stats.health, stats.maxHealth, stats.stamina, stats.maxStamina))
    end
end, false)

name: getVehicleSeat
summary: A player's canonical vehicle seat assignment.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Alias of `Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat`. Canonical means the server's reservation, which exists before the client has mounted and survives a stream-out.
example:
-- Passengers cannot pay the toll: find the driver of the same car
local seat = Open77.players.getVehicleSeat(playerId)
if seat and seat.seat ~= "seat_front_left" then
    local driver = Open77.vehicles.getDriver(seat.vehicleId)
    if driver then chargeToll(driver) end
end

name: getWanted
summary: The wanted policy this server has decided for a player.
description: Returns `{ level, maxLevel, enabled }`, where `enabled` is the dispatch switch of the bucket the player is in. It is what the SERVER decided and pushed, never a reading of the game: the server has no way to learn the engine's real heat stage. A player the server has never set answers the defaults - level 0, ceiling 5, and their bucket's dispatch setting. Requires `players.wanted.read`, which is separate from `players.wanted` because what a server has decided about a player is state a resource has no business enumerating just because it can call a function.
returns: table { level, maxLevel, enabled }, or nil
example:
-- /wanted: show a player their current heat
RegisterCommand("wanted", function(source)
    local wanted = Open77.players.getWanted(source)
    if wanted then
        Open77.chat.send(source, ("Wanted level %d of %d"):format(wanted.level, wanted.maxLevel))
    end
end, false)

name: heal
summary: Heals a player by an amount.
description: Requires `players.damage.apply`. `HealPlayer` is the same function. Clamped at the canonical maximum; it does not revive a dead player.
example:
-- A medkit pickup heals 50 points
RegisterNetEvent("shop:useMedkit", function()
    Open77.players.heal(source, 50)
end)

name: identifier
summary: A player's durable authenticated identifier.
description: No permission. `GetPlayerIdentifier` is the same function. Durable across sessions, unlike the player id, which is only valid for this connection -- key persistent data on this.
example:
-- Key the player's money on the durable identifier, never on the session id
AddEventHandler("onPlayerReady", function(playerId)
    local key = "money:" .. Open77.players.identifier(playerId)
    local balance = Open77.kvp.get(key, 500)
    Open77.chat.send(playerId, ("Welcome back. Balance: %d eddies"):format(balance))
end)

name: identifiers
summary: Every identifier Open77 holds for a player, as a table.
description: The table companion to the FiveM `GetPlayerIdentifiers` array. Carries `open77` and `userId` (the same account GUID under both spellings), `name`, `fingerprint` (the SHA-256 of the identity public key) and `joinedAt`. `endpoint` is present **only** when the resource holds `players.identity.sensitive` -- absent, not nil-filled, so a caller can tell "you may not ask" from "there is nothing there". There is deliberately no `discord`, `steam`, `license` or `xbl`: Open77 has exactly one durable identifier and does not invent the others.
example:
-- Log what Open77 knows about a player when they join
AddEventHandler("onPlayerConnected", function(playerId)
    local ids = Open77.players.identifiers(playerId)
    if ids then print(("%s joined (account %s)"):format(ids.name, ids.userId)) end
end)

name: identity
summary: An admitted player's authenticated identity.
description: No permission. `GetPlayerIdentity` is the same function. Returns `{ userId, name, publicKey, fingerprint, joinedAt }`; the fingerprint matches the one the client's `identity.dump` prints, which is what makes an out-of-band verification possible.
example:
-- Look up the account behind a session
RegisterCommand("whois", function(source, args)
    local identity = Open77.players.identity(tonumber(args[1]))
    if not identity then return Open77.chat.send(source, "No such player.") end
    Open77.chat.send(source, ("%s, account %s, joined %s"):format(identity.name, identity.userId, identity.joinedAt))
end, true)

name: inBucket
summary: The authenticated players in one routing bucket, ascending.
description: No permission. `GetPlayersInBucket` is the same function. Answers `false, invalid_bucket` for a negative or oversized bucket.
returns: array of player ids, or false
example:
-- Start the race only when the lobby instance has at least two players
local racers = Open77.players.inBucket(RACE_BUCKET)
if #racers >= 2 then
    startRace(racers)
end

name: isDead
summary: Whether a player is dead, revive-pending or respawn-pending.
description: Requires `players.life.read`. `IsPlayerDead` is the same function. Resolved from the enum rather than the string, so it is immune to the client/server spelling split -- this is the safe way to ask.
example:
-- A dead player cannot use the shop
RegisterCommand("shop", function(source)
    if Open77.players.isDead(source) then
        return Open77.chat.send(source, "You are in no state to shop.")
    end
    openShop(source)
end, false)

name: isFrozen
summary: Whether a player is currently held still.
description: Requires `players.life.read`. `IsPlayerFrozen` is the same function. Reads the canonical life state rather than a resource's own bookkeeping, so it answers true while ANY resource holds the player -- not only this one. `Open77.players.getLifeState(id).frozen` carries the same bit.
example:
-- Refuse a second /cuff on a player somebody already holds
if Open77.players.isFrozen(target) then
    return Open77.chat.send(source, "They are already restrained.")
end

name: isGhosted
summary: Whether a player is currently non-solid.
description: Requires `players.life.read`. `IsPlayerGhosted` is the same function. Reads the canonical life state rather than a resource's own bookkeeping.
example:
-- Spawn protection is still on: skip the damage report
if Open77.players.isGhosted(victimId) then return end

name: isVisible
summary: Whether a player's body is rendered by other clients.
description: Requires `players.life.read`. `IsPlayerVisible` is the same function. **Answered from the server-owned life bit and never probed from a client**: Cyberpunk 2.31 exposes no readable hidden flag on `entIVisualComponent`, so there is nothing in the engine to ask. Unknown players answer `true` -- absence of a life state is not invisibility. The same bit is on the life snapshot as `getLifeState(id).visible`.
example:
-- A hidden admin is skipped by the scoreboard
for _, playerId in ipairs(Open77.players.all()) do
    if Open77.players.isVisible(playerId) then
        table.insert(board, Open77.players.name(playerId))
    end
end

name: kick
summary: Alias of `Open77.players.disconnect`.
description: Requires `players.disconnect`. The same function under the name an admin command would use; it is not a separate, harsher action.
example:
-- Kick anyone who is AFK for more than 15 minutes
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        Wait(60000)
        for _, playerId in ipairs(Open77.players.all()) do
            local read = Open77.players.get(playerId)
            if read and read.speed == 0 and (idleSince[playerId] or 0) > 15 * 60 then
                Open77.players.kick(playerId, "Kicked for inactivity.")
            end
        end
    end
end)

name: kill
summary: Kills a player authoritatively.
description: Requires `players.life.kill`. Options are `killer`, `cause` (default `script`), `weapon` and `impulse = { x, y, z }`. Do not call it on a player whose readiness gate has not opened -- see `Open77.ready`.
example:
-- /slay <id>: an admin kills a player
RegisterCommand("slay", function(source, args)
    local target = tonumber(args[1])
    if not target then return end
    local ok, reason = Open77.players.kill(target, { killer = source, cause = "admin" })
    if not ok then Open77.chat.send(source, "Refused: " .. reason) end
end, true)

name: name
summary: A player's display name.
description: No permission. `GetPlayerName` is the same function. Answers `nil` for an unknown or departed session.
example:
-- Greet the player by name in chat when they are ready
AddEventHandler("onPlayerReady", function(playerId)
    Open77.chat.send(-1, ("%s joined the city."):format(Open77.players.name(playerId)))
end)

name: nearby
summary: The players within a radius of a point or of another player, nearest first.
description: No permission. `anchor` is a player id (an integer) or a point (a table with numeric `x`, `y`, `z`) -- never ambiguous, and a `vector3` is a point. An omitted or nil `radius` means no radius limit. Options: `bucket` (an integer narrows to it; `false` means every bucket; the default is the anchor player's own bucket, or every bucket for a point anchor), `includeSelf` (default false, ignored for a point anchor), `limit`, and `maxAgeMs`. The default keeps stale readings, because a player whose snapshots stalled is still somewhere; `maxAgeMs` is how you ask for a threshold. Entries carry `playerId`, `distance`, `bucket`, `fresh`, and `ageMs`/`name`/`position`/`heading`/`speed` where available -- deliberately not the whole of `get`, which would ask three services once per player per call. Sorted nearest first, ties broken by player id so two identical calls answer in the same order.

params.name: anchor
params.type: integer (player id) | table { x, y, z }

returns: array of entries sorted by distance, or nil
reason: invalid_argument, invalid_position, invalid_radius, invalid_options, invalid_bucket, invalid_limit, invalid_max_age, player_not_found, position_unknown, sessions_unavailable
example:
for _, witness in ipairs(Open77.players.nearby(robber, 40)) do
  Open77.notifications.send(witness.playerId, { text = ("%.0f m away"):format(witness.distance) })
end

name: ping
summary: The transport's measured round-trip time for one player, in milliseconds.
description: No capability: this is latency, not identity. Every scoreboard in the genre shows it, the player already sees their own, and a resource that could not read it would measure it with a round trip of its own. GameNetworkingSockets' smoothed estimate, refreshed roughly twice a second. Three failures, deliberately distinct: `player_not_found` for a player who is not connected, `ping_unavailable` when the transport cannot measure at all (the phantom transport that drives bots never can) or has not sampled yet, and `invalid_player_id`. A bare nil would collapse all three into "no".
example:
-- /ping: show your own latency
RegisterCommand("ping", function(source)
    local ms, reason = Open77.players.ping(source)
    Open77.chat.send(source, ms and ("Ping: %d ms"):format(ms) or ("Ping unavailable: " .. reason))
end, false)

name: position
summary: A player's last known position and routing bucket.
description: No permission. `GetPlayerPosition` is the same function. Returns `{ x, y, z, bucket }` from the server's snapshot, so it can lag a fast-moving player by a tick.
returns: table { x, y, z, bucket }, or nil
example:
-- /where: print where a player is standing
RegisterCommand("where", function(source, args)
    local pos = Open77.players.position(tonumber(args[1]) or source)
    if not pos then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Unknown position.") end
    Open77.chat.send(source, ("%.1f, %.1f, %.1f (bucket %d)"):format(pos.x, pos.y, pos.z, pos.bucket))
end, true)

name: positions
summary: Every player's position in one call.
description: No permission. `GetPlayersPositions` is the same function. Returns `{ [playerId] = { x, y, z, bucket } }` for every player with a snapshot younger than two seconds; a player without one is **absent** rather than a `nil` entry. One call replaces a loop of `position` over the roster.
example:
-- Count who is inside the event zone, in one pass
local inside = 0
for playerId, pos in pairs(Open77.players.positions()) do
    if #(vector3(pos.x, pos.y, pos.z) - zoneCenter) < zoneRadius then
        inside = inside + 1
    end
end

name: requestLifeResync
summary: Asks a client to re-apply the canonical life state.
description: Requires `players.life.resync`. `RequestPlayerLifeResync` is the same function. The repair path for a client whose local view has drifted from the server's record; it does not change the record itself.
example:
-- A player reports "I look dead but I am alive": push the canonical state again
RegisterCommand("resync", function(source)
    Open77.players.requestLifeResync(source)
end, false)

name: respawn
summary: Brings a DEAD player back to life at a chosen point.
description: Requires `players.life.respawn`. **Not a general move**: it refuses with `invalid_state` unless the player's phase is already `Dead`, so it cannot relocate a living player at all -- use `Open77.players.teleport` for that. `options.position` is required; `heading` (default 0), `bucket` (default 0), `health` (a fraction, default 1.0) and `graceMs` (default 5000) are optional. Wait for the readiness gate before calling it on a joining player.

params.name: options
params.type: table { position, heading?, bucket?, health?, graceMs? }

name: restoreHealth
summary: Fills a player's health pool.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `RestorePlayerHealth` is the same function, and `Open77.stats.restore(playerId, "health")` is the pool-generic spelling. Fills to the canonical maximum without reviving a dead player.
example:
-- Round start: everyone at full health
for _, playerId in ipairs(Open77.players.inBucket(ARENA_BUCKET)) do
    Open77.players.restoreHealth(playerId)
end

name: restoreStamina
summary: Fills a player's stamina pool.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `RestorePlayerStamina` is the same function. Useful at a round start, where waiting for regeneration would be visible.
example:
-- Round start: full stamina so nobody starts the sprint tired
for _, playerId in ipairs(Open77.players.inBucket(ARENA_BUCKET)) do
    Open77.players.restoreStamina(playerId)
end

name: revive
summary: Revives a player where they fell.
description: Requires `players.life.revive`. Options are `health` (a fraction, default 0.20) and `graceMs` (default 3000), the window during which the revived player cannot be damaged again.
example:
-- A medic revives a downed player nearby
RegisterCommand("revive", function(source)
    local patient = Open77.players.closest(source, { radius = 3 })
    if not patient or not Open77.players.isDead(patient.playerId) then
        return Open77.chat.send(source, "Nobody to revive here.")
    end
    Open77.players.revive(patient.playerId, { health = 0.3, graceMs = 5000 })
end, false)

name: setArmor
summary: Sets a player's canonical armor.
description: Requires `players.damage.apply`. `SetPlayerArmor` is the same function. Armor is a separate pool from health and is consumed first by incoming damage.
example:
-- Buying a vest at the shop
RegisterNetEvent("shop:buyArmor", function()
    Open77.players.setArmor(source, 100)
end)

name: setDownedDamageable
summary: Whether a downed player can still be damaged.
description: Requires `players.damage.apply`. `SetPlayerDownedDamageable` is the same function. Turn it on for a mode with finishing blows, off for one where a downed player is safe until revived.
example:
-- Battle-royale rule: a downed player can still be finished
AddEventHandler("onPlayerReady", function(playerId)
    Open77.players.setDownedDamageable(playerId, true)
end)

name: setFrozen
summary: Holds a player's body still, server-authoritative.
description:
Requires `players.life.freeze`. `SetPlayerFrozen` is the lower-level spelling. The body is held where it stands with the engine's own `GameplayRestriction.NoMovement` -- the same record vanilla death applies -- so nothing fights the hold and nothing slides on an observer's screen.

**What it stops:** walking, running, sprinting, crouch-moving, jumping, dodging, sliding and vaulting. Every locomotion input, pressed or held.

**What it does NOT stop, deliberately:** looking around, chat, voice, menus and the inventory, interaction prompts, and damage -- a frozen player can still be shot and still dies. It does not holster a weapon, block firing, or eject anyone from a vehicle. A freeze is a primitive, not a policy: combine it with the control-blocking surface if you want more.

The claim is keyed by the calling resource. Two resources may hold the same player, and `setFrozen(id, false)` drops only your own claim -- he stays frozen while anybody else still holds him. A resource's claims are dropped for it when it stops, reloads or crashes, and a freeze is also lifted by death, respawn, a bucket change and disconnect, so a script that went away can never strand a player. Re-apply after a respawn if the gamemode still wants him held. Refused with `transition_in_progress` while a revive or respawn is in flight, exactly like `setGhosted`.
example:
-- /freeze <id> toggles a hold on a player
RegisterCommand("freeze", function(source, args)
    local target = tonumber(args[1])
    if not target then return end
    local frozen = Open77.players.isFrozen(target)
    Open77.players.setFrozen(target, not frozen)
end, true)

name: setGhosted
summary: Makes a player non-solid, with an optional automatic clear.
description: Requires `players.life.ghost`. `SetPlayerGhosted` is the lower-level spelling. `options.autoClear` defaults to **true**, with `clearDistance` and `clearMs` deciding when the ghost lifts -- that is what stops a spawn-protected player staying non-solid indefinitely. The server owns the state, so every observer agrees about it.
example:
-- Spawn protection: non-solid for 10 seconds or until they walk 15 m away
AddEventHandler("onPlayerReady", function(playerId)
    Open77.players.setGhosted(playerId, true, { clearMs = 10000, clearDistance = 15.0 })
end)

name: setGodMode
summary: Toggles a player's canonical damage immunity.
description: Requires `players.damage.apply`. `SetPlayerGodMode` is the same function. God mode is checked by the server, not the client, so it also refuses damage a Lua arbiter would have allowed.
example:
-- /god toggles invulnerability for an admin
RegisterCommand("god", function(source)
    godMode[source] = not godMode[source]
    Open77.players.setGodMode(source, godMode[source])
    Open77.chat.send(source, godMode[source] and "God mode on." or "God mode off.")
end, true)

name: setHeading
summary: Turns a living player to face a yaw.
description: Requires `players.teleport`. The cheap half of the placement pair: a heading streams nothing and cannot fall through a floor, so this dispatches and returns instead of confirming. `Open77.players.teleport` is the one that confirms. Refuses with `player_not_ready`, `player_not_alive` or `invalid_heading`.
example:
-- After the teleport, face the player toward the shop counter
Open77.players.setHeading(playerId, 270.0)

name: setHealth
summary: Sets a player's health.
description: Requires `players.damage.apply`. `SetPlayerHealth` is the same function. Setting zero passes through life authority rather than leaving a player alive at no health, so it is a real death with the usual replication.
example:
-- /sethp <id> <value>
RegisterCommand("sethp", function(source, args)
    local target, value = tonumber(args[1]), tonumber(args[2])
    if not target or not value then return end
    Open77.players.setHealth(target, value)
end, true)

name: setHoloCallEyes
summary: Synchronize a player's native blue holocall eye glow.
description: Requires players.holocall.control. Uses a network player ID, not an entity handle. Enabled must be a boolean; options may only contain durationMs (integer 0..600000, default 0). True acquires/renews this resource VM's lease; false releases only its lease. The glow remains enabled while any resource holds a lease. It clears on death, disconnect, resource stop/reload/failure or expiry. Reliable bucket snapshots cover late joins and re-stream; clients project onto native and F7 bodies. Does not open the phone UI or start a call. See holocall-eyes.md.
example:
-- Blue eyes for 30 seconds while the holocall runs
RegisterNetEvent("phone:callStarted", function()
    Open77.players.setHoloCallEyes(source, true, { durationMs = 30000 })
end)

name: setMaxHealth
summary: Sets a player's canonical maximum health.
description: Requires `players.damage.apply`. `SetPlayerMaxHealth` is the same function. Lowering the maximum clamps the current value.
example:
-- A perk raises the maximum health to 150
Open77.players.setMaxHealth(playerId, 150)

name: setMaxStamina
summary: Sets a player's canonical maximum stamina.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerMaxStamina` is the same function. Lowering the maximum clamps the current value.
example:
-- A "runner" job class gets more stamina
Open77.players.setMaxStamina(playerId, 150)

name: setMaxWanted
summary: Sets the ceiling one player's wanted level may reach, 0 to 5.
description: **The engine has no per-player wanted level.** `PreventionSystem` holds ONE heat stage, for the one player its client is running: `ChangeHeatStage(stage, reason)`, `GetHeatStage()` and `SetMinMaxResetHeatLevels(min, max, isDefault)` take no target, the state is scalar on a singleton, and every consumer reads one global `UI_WantedBar`. A per-player number works only because every Open77 player has their own game and the server tells each client its own value. The police that follow are LOCAL to that client - not Open77 entities, not replicated - so two wanted players standing together are two private pursuits, each invisible to the other. Do not build a shared chase on this. The value is pushed to the client immediately and re-pushed on a bucket change and on world entry; the server never learns the engine's real heat, because there is no value channel back from REDscript. Requires `players.wanted`. The engine call behind it is `SetMinMaxResetHeatLevels(0, level, false)`; the floor stays 0 because a nonzero minimum would strand a session at a heat it could never clear. Lowering the ceiling below a standing level lowers the level with it and reports that through `onPlayerWantedChanged` - leaving a player above their own ceiling is a state the engine's reset rules would undo at the next opportunity anyway.
example:
-- A VIP zone where the police never go past two stars
AddEventHandler("onPlayerBucketChange", function(playerId, bucket, previous)
    Open77.players.setMaxWanted(playerId, bucket == VIP_BUCKET and 2 or 5)
end)

name: setRegen
summary: Sets a player's health regeneration rate.
description: Requires `players.damage.apply`. `SetPlayerRegen` is the same function, and `Open77.stats.setRegenRate(playerId, "health", rate)` is the pool-generic spelling. Zero disables regeneration.
example:
-- Hardcore mode: no passive health regeneration
AddEventHandler("onPlayerReady", function(playerId)
    Open77.players.setRegen(playerId, 0)
end)

name: setRegenEnabled
summary: Turns a player's health regeneration on or off.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerRegenEnabled` is the same function. Distinct from setting the rate to zero: the configured rate is remembered and comes back when regeneration is re-enabled.
example:
-- Regeneration pauses while the player is bleeding, without losing the configured rate
Open77.players.setRegenEnabled(playerId, false)
SetTimeout(30000, function() Open77.players.setRegenEnabled(playerId, true) end)

name: setStamina
summary: Sets a player's stamina.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerStamina` is the same function, and `Open77.stats.set(playerId, "stamina", value)` is the pool-generic spelling. Stamina is authoritative on the server: the client reads it and never sets it.
example:
-- An energy drink refills stamina to 80
RegisterNetEvent("shop:useEnergyDrink", function()
    Open77.players.setStamina(source, 80)
end)

name: setStaminaRegen
summary: Sets a player's stamina regeneration rate.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerStaminaRegen` is the same function. Zero disables regeneration; use `setStaminaRegenEnabled` to pause it while keeping the configured rate.
example:
-- Athletic perk: stamina comes back twice as fast
Open77.players.setStaminaRegen(playerId, 20)

name: setStaminaRegenEnabled
summary: Turns a player's stamina regeneration on or off.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerStaminaRegenEnabled` is the same function. Turning it off is how a mode makes a sprint budget matter without rewriting the rate.
example:
-- Exhaustion effect: no stamina regeneration for 20 seconds
Open77.players.setStaminaRegenEnabled(playerId, false)
SetTimeout(20000, function() Open77.players.setStaminaRegenEnabled(playerId, true) end)

name: setVehicleExitLocked
summary: Sets or clears a player's durable no-exit policy.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Alias of `Open77.vehicles.setPlayerExitLocked`. Blocks ordinary unmount and manual seat switching; a server-forced exit still overrides it. Distinct from the vehicle's own `locked` entry flag, which governs getting *in*.
example:
-- The prisoner transport: nobody leaves the van until it arrives
Open77.players.warpIntoVehicle(prisonerId, vanId, Open77.vehicles.seats.rearLeft)
Open77.players.setVehicleExitLocked(prisonerId, true, vanId)

name: setVisible
summary: Hides a player's body from every other client, or shows it again.
description: Requires `players.life.visibility`. `SetPlayerVisible` is the lower-level spelling. **Presentation only, and deliberately orthogonal to `setGhosted`**: an invisible player is still solid, still shootable, still heard in proximity voice and still listed in `Open77.players.all()` -- which is what makes "invisible but still simulated" the default rather than a special mode. His nameplate is withheld with his body, because a plate over empty air would leak the exact position the hide exists to conceal, and a resource cannot opt out of that. The state is server-owned and rides the reliable life state, so it survives a proxy re-stream; clients re-assert the hide on a 1 Hz beat because 2.31 exposes no readable hidden flag to detect a render-proxy rebuild dropping it. On a remote body that is simultaneously being dressed, the body stays hidden while either owner holds it and appears only when both release, in either order. Released automatically on death, respawn, bucket change, disconnect, reconnect, and when the calling resource stops or reloads -- invisibility has no proximity auto-clear the way a ghost does, so nothing else would ever recover a stranded body.
example:
-- /vanish toggles an invisible admin
RegisterCommand("vanish", function(source)
    hidden[source] = not hidden[source]
    Open77.players.setVisible(source, not hidden[source])
end, true)

name: setWanted
summary: Sets one player's NCPD wanted level, 0 to 5.
description: **The engine has no per-player wanted level.** `PreventionSystem` holds ONE heat stage, for the one player its client is running: `ChangeHeatStage(stage, reason)`, `GetHeatStage()` and `SetMinMaxResetHeatLevels(min, max, isDefault)` take no target, the state is scalar on a singleton, and every consumer reads one global `UI_WantedBar`. A per-player number works only because every Open77 player has their own game and the server tells each client its own value. The police that follow are LOCAL to that client - not Open77 entities, not replicated - so two wanted players standing together are two private pursuits, each invisible to the other. Do not build a shared chase on this. The value is pushed to the client immediately and re-pushed on a bucket change and on world entry; the server never learns the engine's real heat, because there is no value channel back from REDscript. Requires `players.wanted`. `setWanted(id, 0)` is `ClearPlayerWantedLevel`. The player's ceiling is applied here, not on the client: asking for 5 under a ceiling of 2 succeeds and reports `level = 2` beside the `requested` value, so a caller is told about the clamp instead of discovering it. Fires the host event `onPlayerWantedChanged(playerId, level, previous)` when the value actually changes - a decision this server made, never an observation of the game.
returns: table { level, requested, maxLevel }, or nil
example:
-- Robbing the store puts three stars on the robber
RegisterNetEvent("store:robbed", function()
    local result = Open77.players.setWanted(source, 3)
    if result then print("wanted level now", result.level) end
end)

name: spectate
summary: Puts one player behind another player's shoulder, body and all.
description: Requires `players.spectate`. Ghosts the spectator, hides his body and puts a follow camera on the target, as one transaction: if the body cannot be taken away nothing is applied and nothing is sent. `targetId` false or nil ends the session. `options`: `blendMs` (0..10000, default 400), `distance` (0..100, default 4.0), `height` (-50..50, default 1.5). Both halves come back on every way it can end -- either side dying, disconnecting, reconnecting or changing bucket, and this resource stopping -- and the body is restored to what it was, so a ghost another script owns survives. Refusals: `cannot_spectate_self`, `target_not_found`, `spectator_not_alive`, `target_not_alive`, `different_bucket`, `target_is_spectating`, `not_spectating`. The world streams around the SPECTATOR's body, so teleport him to the target for anything further than a couple of hundred metres. See the Scripted cameras guide.
returns: true, or false and a reason
example:
-- /spectate <id>, and /spectate alone to stop
RegisterCommand("spectate", function(source, args)
    local target = tonumber(args[1])
    local ok, reason = Open77.players.spectate(source, target, { distance = 5.0 })
    if not ok then Open77.chat.send(source, "Cannot spectate: " .. reason) end
end, true)

name: spectating
summary: Who this player is watching, or 0.
description: Requires `players.life.read`. Answered from the server-owned session roster, never probed from a client. See the Scripted cameras guide.
example:
-- A spectator cannot be damaged by what they are watching
local watching = Open77.players.spectating(playerId)
if watching ~= 0 then return end

name: spectators
summary: Everyone watching this player, ascending.
description: Requires `players.life.read`. Returns an array of player ids. See the Scripted cameras guide.
example:
-- Tell a streamer how many admins are watching them
local count = #Open77.players.spectators(playerId)
if count > 0 then
    Open77.chat.send(playerId, ("%d admin(s) are spectating you."):format(count))
end

name: taskEnterVehicle
summary: Seats a player through the vanilla entry animation.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Alias of `Open77.vehicles.taskPlayerEnter`, with the same `options` as `warpIntoVehicle`: `moveBucket` (default true) and `exitLocked`/`lockExit` (default false). The reservation, the bucket move and every refusal reason are the warp's; only the way the affected client reaches the seat changes, and it falls back to the warp when the animation does not land within three seconds.
example:
-- The taxi arrived: the customer climbs in with the animation
Open77.players.taskEnterVehicle(customerId, taxiId, Open77.vehicles.seats.rearRight)

name: taskLeaveVehicle
summary: Ejects a player from their current vehicle.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Alias of `Open77.vehicles.taskPlayerLeave`, which is the same durable forced exit as `forceOutOfVehicle`. The leaving player's own exit is instant on this build -- the local authored exit workspot crashed the engine's release dispatch when it was measured, so the client does not attempt it -- while every observer still sees the exit animated on this player's proxy.
example:
-- The taxi reached its destination
Open77.players.taskLeaveVehicle(customerId, taxiId)

name: teleport
summary: Moves a living player, with no life transition.
description: Requires `players.teleport`. Returns a **Promise** that resolves when the client reports the body settled at the destination, or `nil, reason` when the request was refused outright. Health, inventory, weapons and vehicle occupancy are untouched -- this is not `respawn`, which refuses unless the player is already dead and costs a death to work around. `options`: `heading`, `bucket` (changed before the move, so no observer left in the origin bucket ever sees the destination; restored if the move fails), `fade` (default true, with `fadeOutMs`/`fadeInMs` default 400), `dismount` (default false) and `timeoutMs` (1000..30000, default 12000). Resolves with `{ x, y, z, state }` where `state` is `settled` or `near`. Rejects with `player_not_ready` (no life record -- the continue screen, where acting on a client crashes it), `player_not_alive`, `player_in_vehicle`, `invalid_position` or `settle_timeout`. A player in a vehicle is refused rather than ejected: pass `dismount = true` to accept losing the vehicle, which unmounts behind the fade and refuses with `dismount_failed` if the body is still seated after 750 ms.

params.name: options
params.type: table { heading?, bucket?, fade?, fadeOutMs?, fadeInMs?, dismount?, timeoutMs? }

example:
-- /tp <x> <y> <z>, waiting until the body has really landed
RegisterCommand("tp", function(source, args)
    local x, y, z = tonumber(args[1]), tonumber(args[2]), tonumber(args[3])
    if not x or not y or not z then return end
    local pending, reason = Open77.players.teleport(source, { x = x, y = y, z = z }, { dismount = true })
    if not pending then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Teleport refused: " .. reason) end
    local landed, err = pending:await()
    Open77.chat.send(source, landed and ("Arrived (%s)"):format(landed.state) or ("Failed: " .. err))
end, true)

name: warpIntoVehicle
summary: Puts a player in a vehicle seat authoritatively.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Alias of `Open77.vehicles.warpPlayerIntoVehicle`, with the same options: `moveBucket` (default true; false makes a bucket mismatch answer `wrong_bucket`) and `exitLocked`/`lockExit` (default false). Seats accept `-1..2`, the `Open77.vehicles.seats` constants, aliases like `driver`, and canonical `seat_*` names.
example:
-- /seat <vehicleId>: put the caller in the driver seat instantly
RegisterCommand("seat", function(source, args)
    local vehicleId = tonumber(args[1])
    if not vehicleId then return end
    local ok, reason = Open77.players.warpIntoVehicle(source, vehicleId, "driver")
    if not ok then Open77.chat.send(source, "Refused: " .. reason) end
end, true)

name: all
summary: Every authoritative prop, optionally filtered to one routing bucket.
description: Requires `world.props`. Returns the whole registry, whichever resource owns each prop.
example:
-- Count the props in the event instance
print(#Open77.props.all(EVENT_BUCKET), "props in the event")

name: attach
summary: Set a synchronized prop binding.
description: Binding fields: parentType ('player' or 'vehicle'), parentId (canonical network ID, not an engine handle), bone (named slot, empty for root), offset {x,y,z} in metres (each ±20), rotation {x,y,z} in degrees (each ±360, local Z-Y-X composition). Unknown fields and non-finite numbers reject. Missing streamed parents are hidden, then rebound when available. See attachments.md. Requires world.props and ownership of the prop. Parent must be alive/valid in the same bucket. Up to 32 bindings per parent. Optional expectedRevision enables compare-and-swap; stale updates reject. Idempotent identical attachment does not create a new revision.
returns: true on success; nil, reason on rejection
example:
-- The courier picks the crate up: it follows their right hand
Open77.props.attach(crateId, { parentType = "player", parentId = courierId, bone = "RightHand" })

name: attachedTo
summary: List replicated props attached to one parent.
description: Requires world.props. Uses a canonical player/vehicle ID and returns copied prop records, including bindings and revisions. Inspection can include other resources' props, but mutation still checks ownership.
example:
-- Every replicated prop currently attached to the player
for _, prop in ipairs(Open77.props.attachedTo("player", playerId) or {}) do
    print(prop.id, prop.model)
end

name: catalog
summary: Always an empty table on the server.
description: The dedicated server keeps no curated model catalogue -- the aliases live on the client, next to the records they resolve. It answers an empty list rather than `nil` so the shipped `prop.catalog` console command stays honest instead of failing on a nil call.
example:
-- Always empty on the server; the alias list lives on the client
print(#Open77.props.catalog()) -- 0

name: clear
summary: Removes every prop this resource owns and returns how many.
description: Requires `world.props`. Called for you when the resource stops, so a reloading gamemode never leaves orphaned scenery behind. It never touches another resource's props.
example:
-- The event is over: remove every prop this resource placed
AddEventHandler("event:ended", function()
    print("removed", Open77.props.clear(), "props")
end)

name: create
summary: Creates an authoritative, replicated world prop.
description: Requires `world.props`. This is the **server** meaning of the name: the prop is owned by the creating resource, streamed per player rather than broadcast to a bucket, and visible to everyone in range. The identically named *client* function makes a local, unreplicated decoration instead. Definitions accept `model`, `position`, `yaw`, `scale` (a number or `{ x, y, z }`), `appearance`, `bucket`, `physics` (`static`, `kinematic`, `dynamic`, `none`), `collision`, `visible`, `kind` (`prop`, `light`, `effect`), `light`, `streamingRadius` (10 to 2000, default 120), `streamingHysteresis` (default 30) and `ttlMs` (0 for no expiry, seven days maximum). The registry holds 8,192 props, of which one resource may own 2,048. Ids are decimal strings; do not pass them through `tonumber`.
returns: reason: permission_denied:world.props, quota_exceeded, invalid_position, invalid_model, unknown_alias, record_provisioning_failed, entity_spawn_failed, world_unavailable
example:
-- A replicated crate at the drop point, gone after an hour
local crate, reason = Open77.props.create({
    model = "crate.small",
    position = { x = -1442.2, y = 127.4, z = 18.0 },
    yaw = 45.0,
    ttlMs = 60 * 60 * 1000,
})
if not crate then print("no crate: " .. reason) end

name: detach
summary: Release a synchronized prop binding.
description: Requires world.props and prop ownership. Optional expectedRevision prevents detaching a newer binding. Leaves the prop at the server's last coarse parent anchor, which is not an exact client-side animated bone transform. Already detached is idempotent. Death, disconnect, parent removal and bucket changes also detach automatically.
returns: true on success; nil, reason on rejection
example:
-- The courier put the crate down: it stays where the body last carried it
Open77.props.detach(crateId)

name: get
summary: Reads one prop's canonical snapshot.
description: Requires `world.props`. Reads are not restricted to the owner; the snapshot's `resource` field is provenance and cleanup scope, not an authorization boundary.
example:
-- Is the crate still there before paying for its pickup?
local crate = Open77.props.get(crateId)
if not crate then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Somebody already took it.") end

name: getAttachment
summary: Read a prop's current replicated binding.
description: Binding fields: parentType ('player' or 'vehicle'), parentId (canonical network ID, not an engine handle), bone (named slot, empty for root), offset {x,y,z} in metres (each ±20), rotation {x,y,z} in degrees (each ±360, local Z-Y-X composition). Unknown fields and non-finite numbers reject. Missing streamed parents are hidden, then rebound when available. See attachments.md. Requires world.props. Returns a copy, not a mutable reference. Nil can mean detached or absent; inspect the second result for a capability/validation failure.
returns: binding table or nil; nil, reason on rejection
example:
local binding, err = Open77.props.getAttachment(propId)
if binding then print(binding.parentType, binding.parentId, binding.bone) end

name: isAttached
summary: Check whether a prop has a binding.
description: Requires world.props. Returns false when no binding exists, and nil plus reason for a rejected query. This tests authoritative state, not whether a particular client has streamed or rendered its parent.
example:
-- Is the crate still being carried?
if Open77.props.isAttached(crateId) then print("someone is carrying the crate") end

name: remove
summary: Removes a prop this resource owns.
description: Requires `world.props`. Another resource's prop answers `owned_by_another_resource`.
example:
-- The player picked up the crate
RegisterNetEvent("crates:pickup", function(crateId)
    if Open77.props.remove(crateId) then giveReward(source) end
end)

name: setAttachmentTransform
summary: Change a binding's local offset and rotation.
description: Binding fields: parentType ('player' or 'vehicle'), parentId (canonical network ID, not an engine handle), bone (named slot, empty for root), offset {x,y,z} in metres (each ±20), rotation {x,y,z} in degrees (each ±360, local Z-Y-X composition). Unknown fields and non-finite numbers reject. Missing streamed parents are hidden, then rebound when available. See attachments.md. Requires world.props and prop ownership. Omitted vectors retain their previous values. The current revision is used if expectedRevision is omitted; stale explicit revisions reject. A detached prop rejects with not_attached.
example:
-- Nudge the carried crate ten centimetres up and turn it sideways
Open77.props.setAttachmentTransform(crateId, { x = 0, y = 0, z = 0.1 }, { x = 0, y = 0, z = 90 })

name: setBucket
summary: Moves a prop to another routing bucket.
description: Requires `world.props`. Changes which players stream it.
example:
-- Move the stage props into the concert instance
for _, propId in ipairs(stageProps) do Open77.props.setBucket(propId, CONCERT_BUCKET) end

name: setTransform
summary: Moves and optionally rescales a prop this resource owns.
description: Requires `world.props`. Takes `position`, `yaw` and `scale` (a number or `{ x, y, z }`). Unlike the client prop API, scale belongs here rather than in `update`.
example:
-- The crane lifts the container two metres
local snapshot = Open77.props.get(containerId)
Open77.props.setTransform(containerId, { position = { x = snapshot.x, y = snapshot.y, z = snapshot.z + 2.0 } })

name: update
summary: Patches a prop this resource owns.
description: Requires `world.props`. Sparse, and it deliberately does **not** accept `model` or `kind`: changing either is a remove and a create, because the render proxy is built from them. A resource may read every prop but mutate only its own.

params.name: patch
params.type: table { appearance?, physics?, collision?, visible?, bucket?, light?, streamingRadius?, streamingHysteresis?, ttlMs? }

example:
-- Hide the barrier while the road is open, keep it registered
Open77.props.update(barrierId, { visible = false, collision = false })

name: hold
summary: Takes or refreshes this resource's hold on a player.
description: No permission. Returns the player's `session`, which later identifies the hold being released. Refreshing an existing hold restarts its deadline.
example:
-- Hold a joining player until their character is loaded from the database
AddEventHandler("onPlayerConnected", function(playerId)
    local session = Open77.ready.hold(playerId, "loading character")
    loadCharacter(playerId, function() Open77.ready.release(playerId, session) end)
end)

name: isReady
summary: Whether anything is still holding a player.
description: No permission. A player the host does not know is reported ready, so an unknown id never blocks a mode forever. The rule the gate exists for: do not teleport, spawn, kill or force a respawn on a player until this is true. Reading state, rosters and HUD payloads is unaffected.
example:
-- Never teleport a player the gate still holds
if not Open77.ready.isReady(playerId) then return end
Open77.players.teleport(playerId, spawnPoint)

name: participate
summary: Declares that this resource holds joining players until it is finished with them.
description: No permission. Call it **once, at load**: every player who connects from then on arrives with one hold in this resource's name, which is what stops another resource teleporting or spawning them mid-setup. Options are `timeoutMs` and `reason`. Every hold carries a deadline, so a resource that never releases costs one degraded join and one `WRN` naming it, never a stuck server.
example:
-- Declare at load that this resource holds every joining player
Open77.ready.participate({ timeoutMs = 15000, reason = "character load" })

name: release
summary: Clears this resource's hold on a player.
description: No permission. A `session` that no longer matches is dropped rather than releasing a newer hold -- that is what keeps a late release from opening the gate for the player who reconnected in the meantime. `onPlayerReady(playerId, detail)` is emitted into **every** running resource when the last hold clears.
example:
-- Character loaded: release the hold taken at connect
Open77.ready.release(playerId, session, "character loaded")

name: status
summary: Who is holding a player, and for how long.
description: No permission. Returns `{ known, ready, session, ageMs, holds = { { resource, reason, ageMs, remainingMs } } }`. The `ready` console command prints the same thing, which is the quickest way to find the resource that is not releasing.
example:
-- /whoholds <id>: which resource is not releasing a player?
RegisterCommand("whoholds", function(source, args)
    local status = Open77.ready.status(tonumber(args[1]))
    for _, hold in ipairs(status.holds or {}) do
