        Open77.chat.send(source, ("%s: %s (%d ms left)"):format(hold.resource, hold.reason, hold.remainingMs))
    end
end, true)

name: generation
summary: A running server resource's opaque VM generation.
description: No permission. Omitting the name answers this VM's own generation; naming another running server resource answers its generation, or `0` when it is unavailable. The value changes on every restart and reload, which is how a cached handle or a deferred callback can tell it is talking to the same VM it started with.
example:
-- Ignore a timer that fired after this resource was reloaded
local generation = Open77.resource.generation()
SetTimeout(60000, function()
    if Open77.resource.generation() ~= generation then return end
    save()
end)

name: list
summary: Every discovered resource and its runtime state.
description: No capability. Entries are `{ name, version, state, generation, memoryBytes }` plus `error` when the resource failed. `state` is the lowercased runtime state: discovered, starting, running, stopping, stopped, failed or blocked.
example:
-- /resources: state of every resource
RegisterCommand("resources", function(source)
    for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.resource.list() or {}) do
        Open77.chat.send(source, ("%s %s (%s)"):format(entry.name, entry.version, entry.state))
    end
end, true)

name: metadata
summary: One resource's parsed manifest, or one field of it.
description: No capability. With no `key`, returns the whole manifest as `{ name, version, open77Version, autoStart, reloadPolicy, dependencies, permissions, sharedScripts, serverScripts, clientScripts, preloadMods, clientFiles }`. With a key, returns just that field; both the camelCase and the manifest's own snake_case spelling are accepted. `author` and `description` answer `unknown_metadata_key` rather than an empty string: the manifest parser does not read them, so claiming a value would be a claim this server cannot make.
returns: table or field value, or nil
example:
-- Read another resource's version from its manifest
print("chat version", Open77.resource.metadata("open77_chat", "version"))

name: name
summary: This resource's name, as its manifest declares it.
description: No permission. `GetCurrentResourceName` is the same function.
example:
-- Prefix log lines with the resource name
print(("[%s] started"):format(Open77.resource.name()))

name: restart
summary: Queues a resource restart for the next tick boundary.
description: Requires `resources.control`. See `Open77.resource.start` for why it is queued.
example:
-- /restart-shop from an admin (needs resources.control)
RegisterCommand("restart-shop", function(source)
    local ok, reason = Open77.resource.restart("shop")
    if not ok then Open77.chat.send(source, reason) end
end, true)

name: start
summary: Queues a resource start for the next tick boundary.
description: Requires `resources.control`. Queued, never inline: a resource stopping or restarting another while a Lua state is on the stack would free memory that is still executing, so the verb is applied where a console line is applied -- on the game-loop thread, outside every VM. Reports acceptance, not completion; read `Open77.resource.list()` on a later tick for the outcome. An unknown name answers `unknown_resource` immediately rather than as a line in a log nobody is reading.
example:
-- Start the event resource when an admin opens the event
RegisterCommand("event-open", function()
    Open77.resource.start("summer_event")
end, true)

name: state
summary: The current server-side state of a resource.
description: No permission. `GetResourceState` is the same function. Worth asking after a lifecycle event: a queued `open77:resource:started` describes a transition that happened, and a stop or start can have followed before the next tick.
example:
-- Wait for a dependency to be running before using its export
CreateThread(function()
    while Open77.resource.state("bank") ~= "running" do Wait(500) end
    print("bank is up")
end)

name: stop
summary: Queues a resource stop for the next tick boundary.
description: Requires `resources.control`. See `Open77.resource.start` for why it is queued.
example:
-- Stop the event resource when the event closes
RegisterCommand("event-close", function()
    Open77.resource.stop("summer_event")
end, true)

name: getEntity
summary: An entity's routing bucket.
description: No permission. `GetEntityRoutingBucket` is the same function. The default is `0`.
example:
-- Which instance is this vehicle in?
print("vehicle bucket", Open77.routingBuckets.getEntity(vehicleEntityId))

name: getPlayer
summary: A player's routing bucket.
description: No permission. `GetPlayerRoutingBucket` is the same function. The default is `0`. A bucket is a visibility scope: players and entities only see others in the same one.
example:
-- Only players in the same bucket can trade
if Open77.routingBuckets.getPlayer(a) ~= Open77.routingBuckets.getPlayer(b) then
    return Open77.chat.send(a, "You are not in the same instance.")
end

name: setEntity
summary: Moves an entity to another routing bucket.
description: No permission. `SetEntityRoutingBucket` is the same function. The per-kind helpers (`Open77.vehicles.update`, `Open77.npcs.setBucket`, `Open77.props.setBucket`) do the same thing with validation.
example:
-- Move the entity into the arena instance
Open77.routingBuckets.setEntity(entityId, ARENA_BUCKET)

name: setLockdownMode
summary: Sets a bucket's entity lockdown mode.
description: No permission. `SetRoutingBucketEntityLockdownMode` is the same function. Modes are `inactive`, `relaxed`, `strict` and `full`, tightening what clients in that bucket may create.
example:
-- Nothing client-created may exist in the competitive arena
Open77.routingBuckets.setLockdownMode(ARENA_BUCKET, "strict")

name: setPlayer
summary: Moves a player to another routing bucket.
description: No permission. `SetPlayerRoutingBucket` is the same function. This moves their authoritative visibility scope, so it is how a lobby, an instanced arena or a private apartment is built.
example:
-- Each apartment is its own instance: bucket 1000 + house id
RegisterNetEvent("house:enter", function(houseId)
    Open77.routingBuckets.setPlayer(source, 1000 + houseId)
end)

name: setPopulationEnabled
summary: Turns ambient population on or off for one bucket.
description: No permission. `SetRoutingBucketPopulationEnabled` is the same function. Switching it off empties a bucket of vanilla pedestrians and traffic, which is what an arena or a staged scene usually wants.
example:
-- No traffic or crowd in the arena instance
Open77.routingBuckets.setPopulationEnabled(ARENA_BUCKET, false)

name: cancelRestart
summary: Disarms a pending server restart.
description: Requires `runtime.restart`. The reason `open77:admin:scheduledRestart` is a plain notification rather than a cancellable event: stopping a shutdown is an authority, not a veto every listener gets for free. Broadcasts the cancellation to players and raises `open77:admin:restartCancelled` when a restart was actually armed; a no-op otherwise. Refusals: `permission_denied:runtime.restart`, `restart_control_unavailable`.
example:
-- /cancelrestart for admins
RegisterCommand("cancelrestart", function(source)
    Open77.runtime.cancelRestart()
end, true)

name: commands
summary: Every command registered across every running resource, plus the built-in verbs.
description: No capability; it is a read of the operator's own installation. Entries are `{ name, resource, restricted, source }`, `source` being `resource` for a Lua registration and `console` for a built-in verb. The built-ins listed are the resource-lifecycle set the coordinator owns; the ACL, ban, routing-bucket and phantom verbs are **not** listed, because they live in a hand-written dispatcher with no registry to read. The `source` field is what tells a reader this list has two origins.
example:
-- /commands lists everything, built-ins included
RegisterCommand("commands", function(source)
    for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.runtime.commands() or {}) do
        Open77.chat.send(source, ("/%s (%s)"):format(entry.name, entry.source))
    end
end, true)

name: executeCommand
summary: Queues one console line to run at the next tick boundary.
description: Requires `runtime.commands`, which grants a PLAIN resource's authority: it may invoke another resource's ordinary command and nothing else. A command declared `restricted` and every resource-lifecycle verb are refused. A resource that also declares `resources.control` runs the line with the authority the in-game operator escalation uses. FiveM's `ExecuteCommand` runs as the console with no declaration anywhere that a resource holds rcon; here the manifest says it. **Queued, never inline**: Lua runs inside the host's tick, so dispatching a line synchronously would re-enter a VM and reset an instruction budget mid-flight. The call reports acceptance, not completion, and the reply goes to the server log naming the resource that asked. Refusals: `permission_denied:runtime.commands`, `empty_command`, `command_line_too_long`, `command_queue_full`, `invalid_command_line`.
example:
-- Run another resource's ordinary command from a script (needs runtime.commands)
Open77.runtime.executeCommand("weather rain")

name: luaVersion
summary: The Lua version this server VM runs.
description: No permission. Returns the interpreter's `_VERSION` string, for a resource that wants to record what it ran on.
example:
-- Record the interpreter in the startup log
print("running on", Open77.runtime.luaVersion())

name: restartStatus
summary: Whether a restart is armed, and how long is left.
description: Requires `runtime.restart`. The read `open77:admin:scheduledRestart` cannot replace: an event announces a CHANGE, and a resource that started after the restart was scheduled never saw one. Ask this once at start, then subscribe. `secondsRemaining` is measured at the moment of the read and is 0 when nothing is armed. Refusals: `permission_denied:runtime.restart`, `restart_control_unavailable`.
example:
-- Warn a joining player about a pending restart
AddEventHandler("onPlayerReady", function(playerId)
    local status = Open77.runtime.restartStatus()
    if status and status.scheduled then
        Open77.chat.send(playerId, ("Server restart in %d s"):format(status.secondsRemaining))
    end
end)

name: scheduleRestart
summary: Schedules a server restart, with the same warnings an operator's would raise.
description: Requires `runtime.restart` -- its own capability, not `resources.control`: stopping one resource and stopping the whole server are different powers. Takes exactly the path a Warden-scheduled restart takes, so players get the same broadcast now and the same warning ladder (30m, 15m, 10m, 5m, 2m, 60s, 30s, 10s) as the deadline approaches, and every running resource gets `open77:admin:scheduledRestart(secondsRemaining, reason)` on each rung. Calling it again re-arms the schedule rather than adding a second one. `seconds` must be an integer in [1, 604800] and is clamped by the scheduler to at least 5 s; `reason` is broadcast to every player, so it is capped at 200 bytes and must hold no control characters. Refusals: `permission_denied:runtime.restart`, `invalid_delay`, `invalid_reason`, `restart_control_unavailable` (a host with no game loop).
example:
-- /restart <minutes> <reason> with the standard warning ladder
RegisterCommand("restart", function(source, args)
    local minutes = tonumber(args[1]) or 15
    Open77.runtime.scheduleRestart(minutes * 60, table.concat(args, " ", 2))
end, true)

name: broadcast
summary: Plays a file for every player on the server.
description: `play` with a target of `-1`, which leaves as ONE event rather than one per player. Use the `{ near = ..., radius = ... }` target instead for anything positional: a district's shop jingle broadcast to the whole server is on every player's wire in every bucket.
example:
-- Curfew siren for everyone, quietly
Open77.sound.broadcast("sfx/curfew.ogg", { volume = 0.4 })

name: play
summary: Plays an audio file this resource ships, for one player, for everyone, or for everyone in range.
description: The server never touches audio: it names a file and an audience, and the bundled `open77_sound` client resource decodes and mixes it. `target` takes three shapes: a player id; `-1` for everyone; or a table `{ near = playerId | {x,y,z}, radius = n, bucket = n | false, limit = n }`, which is resolved HERE through `Open77.players.nearby` and sent to each player found. `radius` is required in that form -- a `near` without one would silently reach the whole bucket. The bucket rule is the one every proximity read uses: the anchor player's own bucket by default, so two players in different routing buckets never hear each other. The file must be declared in THIS resource's `files` manifest entry and must reach the client, so the resource needs a client script too -- a server-only resource is never downloaded and its audio is unreachable, which the client reports on the local `open77:soundFailed` event. `options` is the client option table (`volume`, `loop`, `pitch`, `position`, `entity`, `maxDistance`, `refDistance`, `offset`) plus an optional `id`, which defaults to the file path. See [sound](sound.md) for the spatial model and for the honest list of what this is not.
returns: reason: invalid_sound_target, invalid_sound_radius, invalid_sound_file, invalid_sound_id, invalid_options, no_audience, permission_denied:network.events, network_unavailable, sound_payload_too_large
example:
-- A gunshot everyone within 40 m of the shooter hears
Open77.sound.play({ near = source, radius = 40.0 }, "sfx/shot.ogg")

name: setPosition
summary: Moves one of this resource's spatial sounds to a new world point.
description: Refused client-side with `sound_not_spatial` on a sound started without `position` or `entity`. Sending a position at, say, 5 Hz is how a siren follows a car the server owns; for a body the client can see, start the sound with `entity` instead and let the client track it.
example:
-- The siren follows the server-owned cruiser, five times a second
CreateThread(function()
    while chasing do
        Open77.sound.setPosition(-1, "siren", Open77.vehicles.getPosition(cruiserId))
        Wait(200)
    end
end)

name: setVolume
summary: Changes a live sound's volume on an audience.
description: 0..1, ramped client-side so it does not click. On a spatial sound it multiplies the distance falloff. It is NOT the player's in-game audio slider, which this system cannot read.
example:
-- Turn the boombox down for everyone
Open77.sound.setVolume(-1, "boombox", 0.2)

name: stop
summary: Stops one of this resource's sounds on an audience.
description: Same target shapes as `play`. A client only stops a sound this resource started there: the owner is stamped by the host from the calling resource's name and `open77:sound:` is a reserved client-event prefix, so one resource can never stop another's audio.
example:
-- Hang up: stop the ringing on that one player
Open77.sound.stop(source, "phone")

name: stopAll
summary: Stops every sound this resource started, for an audience or for everyone.
description: The target defaults to `-1`. It is also sent automatically when this resource stops, so a looping siren cannot outlive the resource that started it.
example:
-- The event ends: silence everything this resource started
Open77.sound.stopAll()

name: allowRequest
summary: Opts one bag key in to client write requests, behind a validator.
description: Requires `state.write`. The client never writes a bag: it submits through `Open77.state.request` and this validator decides. `validator(source, value)` answers `accepted [, normalisedValue]`, and the value the bag stores is the one the validator returned -- clamp or rewrite here. Anything but true refuses. The selector may be a kind string to cover every bag of that kind, or one bag. The validator is retired when the resource stops.

name: clear
summary: Drops the stored state.
description: No permission. `save(nil)` under a clearer name: the next VM to start sees nothing and initialises from scratch.
example:
-- A season reset: the next reload starts from scratch
RegisterCommand("season-reset", function()
    Open77.state.clear()
end, true)

name: denyRequest
summary: Withdraws a client-writable bag key.
description: Requires `state.write`. Later client requests for that key are refused with `not_requestable`.
example:
-- The radio feature is switched off: clients may no longer request the key
Open77.state.denyRequest("player", "radioFrequency")

name: entity
summary: The replicated state bag of one vehicle, NPC or prop.
description: Requires `state.write` to write, nothing to read. Accepts `(kind, id)` or `{ kind = , id = }`, where kind is `vehicle`, `npc` or `prop`. The audience is the owning registry's own viewer set, so the bag follows the entity through stream-in, stream-out and bucket changes, and it dies with the entity.
example:
-- Replicate a car's fuel level to everyone who can see the car
Open77.state.entity("vehicle", vehicleId):set("fuel", 61.5)

name: load
summary: Reads back the value the previous VM stored.
description: No permission. Answers `nil` on a fresh start -- which is the signal to initialise rather than resume -- and `nil, reason` when the stored value cannot be decoded.
example:
-- Resume the round state after a hot reload
local saved = Open77.state.load()
round = saved and saved.round or 1

name: offChange
summary: Stops a state-bag change subscription.
description: No permission. Takes the id `Open77.state.onChange` returned.
example:
-- Stop watching once the match ends
local sub = Open77.state.onChange("global", "round", function(_, _, value) print("round", value) end)
AddEventHandler("arena:matchOver", function() Open77.state.offChange(sub) end)

name: onChange
summary: Watches state-bag changes matching a selector and a key.
description: No permission. The selector is a bag handle, a `{ kind = , id = }` table, a bare kind string for every bag of that kind, or nil for every bag; the key is a key name or nil for every key. The handler runs at a tick boundary as `fn(selector, key, value, previous)` and may Wait. Only subscribed resources are touched, and subscriptions are retired when the resource stops.
example:
-- Log every job change on any player
Open77.state.onChange("player", "job", function(selector, key, value, previous)
    print(("player %s job: %s -> %s"):format(tostring(selector.id), tostring(previous and previous.name), tostring(value and value.name)))
end)

name: player
summary: The replicated state bag of one player.
description: Requires `state.write` to write, nothing to read. Replicated to every player in that player's routing bucket, including the subject; a player in another bucket never receives it. The bag dies with the player's session.
example:
-- Replicate the player's job so every client in the bucket can read it
Open77.state.player(source):set("job", { name = "police", grade = 3 })

name: save
summary: Stores this resource's state so it survives a reload.
description: No permission. **Not a key-value store**: it holds one value per resource, round-tripped through JSON by the host, so store plain data -- functions, coroutines and metatables do not survive, and cycles are rejected. Passing `nil` clears it. Call it **when the state changes, not on stop**: a reload prepares the successor VM *before* stopping this one, so a write from a stopping resource is refused and returns false. It deliberately does not survive the resource going down: `stop`, `restart` and `refresh` drop it, which keeps an operator's way of saying "come up as you would at boot".

params.name: value
params.type: any JSON-encodable value, or nil to clear

example:
-- Save the round state every time it changes, so a reload resumes it
local function setRound(n)
    round = n
    Open77.state.save({ round = round })
end

name: get
summary: A player's combined health and stamina snapshot.
description: Requires `players.stats.read`. `GetPlayerStats` is the same function. The client exposes the same read names and the same nested pool shape, but no setters -- the server owns both pools. See [Player health and stamina](player-stats.md).
example:
-- /stats: both pools in one read
RegisterCommand("stats", function(source)
    local stats = Open77.stats.get(source)
    if stats then
        Open77.chat.send(source, ("HP %d / %d, stamina %d / %d"):format(
            stats.health.value, stats.health.maximum, stats.stamina.value, stats.stamina.maximum))
    end
end, false)

name: getHealth
summary: A player's health pool.
description: Requires `players.stats.read`. Returns `{ value, current, maximum, max, fraction, percentage, regenEnabled, regenPerSecond, regenerating }`, or `nil` for an unknown player. The duplicate spellings are deliberate: they let resources written against either convention read the same table.
example:
-- A medic sees the patient's health before treating
local hp = Open77.stats.getHealth(patientId)
if hp and hp.fraction < 0.5 then
    Open77.chat.send(medicId, ("Patient at %d %%"):format(hp.percentage))
end

name: getStamina
summary: A player's stamina pool.
description: Requires `players.stats.read`. Same shape as the health pool.
example:
-- Refuse the sprint-heavy job to an exhausted player
local stamina = Open77.stats.getStamina(source)
if stamina and stamina.fraction < 0.3 then
    return Open77.chat.send(source, "Catch your breath first.")
end

name: health
summary: Alias of `Open77.stats.getHealth`.
description: Requires `players.stats.read`. The shorter spelling of the same read, matching the client's.
example:
-- Short spelling, same read
local hp = Open77.stats.health(playerId)
print(hp and hp.value)

name: restore
summary: Fills one pool.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `pool` is `health` or `stamina`. Filling health does not revive a dead player.
example:
-- A pool name from the item definition: "health" or "stamina"
RegisterNetEvent("items:use", function(item)
    if consumables[item] then Open77.stats.restore(source, consumables[item].pool) end
end)

name: restoreHealth
summary: Fills the health pool.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `RestorePlayerHealth` is the same function; `restore(playerId, "health")` is the pool-generic spelling.
example:
-- Round start: full health for everyone in the arena
for _, playerId in ipairs(Open77.players.inBucket(ARENA_BUCKET)) do
    Open77.stats.restoreHealth(playerId)
end

name: restoreStamina
summary: Fills the stamina pool.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `RestorePlayerStamina` is the same function; `restore(playerId, "stamina")` is the pool-generic spelling.
example:
-- An energy drink
RegisterNetEvent("items:energyDrink", function()
    Open77.stats.restoreStamina(source)
end)

name: set
summary: Sets one pool's current value, in points.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `pool` is `health` or `stamina`; anything else answers `false, invalid_stat_pool`. Setting health to zero routes through life authority, so it is a real death.
example:
-- Everyone starts the hardcore round at 50 health
for _, playerId in ipairs(Open77.players.inBucket(ARENA_BUCKET)) do
    Open77.stats.set(playerId, "health", 50)
end

name: setHealth
summary: Explicit health setter.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerHealth` is the same function; `set(playerId, "health", value)` is the pool-generic spelling. Zero routes through life authority.
example:
-- /sethp <id> <value>
RegisterCommand("sethp", function(source, args)
    local target, value = tonumber(args[1]), tonumber(args[2])
    if target and value then Open77.stats.setHealth(target, value) end
end, true)

name: setHealthMax
summary: Explicit health maximum setter.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerMaxHealth` is the same function; `setMax(playerId, "health", maximum)` is the pool-generic spelling.
example:
-- A perk: 150 maximum health
Open77.stats.setHealthMax(playerId, 150)

name: setHealthRegenEnabled
summary: Turns health regeneration on or off.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerRegenEnabled` is the same function.
example:
-- Bleeding: no regeneration until bandaged
Open77.stats.setHealthRegenEnabled(playerId, false)
RegisterNetEvent("items:bandage", function()
    Open77.stats.setHealthRegenEnabled(source, true)
end)

name: setHealthRegenRate
summary: Sets the health regeneration rate.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerRegen` is the same function. Zero disables it.
example:
-- Hardcore server: health never comes back on its own
AddEventHandler("onPlayerReady", function(playerId)
    Open77.stats.setHealthRegenRate(playerId, 0)
end)

name: setMax
summary: Sets one pool's canonical maximum and clamps its current value.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `pool` is `health` or `stamina`. Lowering the maximum below the current value clamps it rather than leaving an impossible reading.
example:
-- The pool name comes from the perk definition
Open77.stats.setMax(playerId, perk.pool, perk.maximum)

name: setRegenEnabled
summary: Turns one pool's regeneration on or off.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `enabled` must be a boolean; anything else answers `false, invalid_argument`. Distinct from a rate of zero: the configured rate is remembered.
example:
-- Pause stamina regeneration while the player is carrying a body
Open77.stats.setRegenEnabled(playerId, "stamina", false)

name: setRegenRate
summary: Sets one pool's regeneration rate, in points per second.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. Zero disables regeneration for that pool.
example:
-- Athletic perk: stamina regenerates twice as fast
Open77.stats.setRegenRate(playerId, "stamina", 20)

name: setStamina
summary: Explicit stamina setter.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerStamina` is the same function; `set(playerId, "stamina", value)` is the pool-generic spelling.
example:
-- The player just ran a marathon: stamina to 10
Open77.stats.setStamina(playerId, 10)

name: setStaminaMax
summary: Explicit stamina maximum setter.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerMaxStamina` is the same function; `setMax(playerId, "stamina", maximum)` is the pool-generic spelling.
example:
-- A "runner" class gets a bigger stamina pool
Open77.stats.setStaminaMax(playerId, 150)

name: setStaminaRegenEnabled
summary: Turns stamina regeneration on or off.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerStaminaRegenEnabled` is the same function.
example:
-- Exhaustion: no stamina regeneration for 20 seconds
Open77.stats.setStaminaRegenEnabled(playerId, false)
SetTimeout(20000, function() Open77.stats.setStaminaRegenEnabled(playerId, true) end)

name: setStaminaRegenRate
summary: Sets the stamina regeneration rate.
description: Requires `players.stats.apply`. `SetPlayerStaminaRegen` is the same function. Zero disables it.
example:
-- A heavy backpack halves stamina regeneration
Open77.stats.setStaminaRegenRate(playerId, 5)

name: stamina
summary: Alias of `Open77.stats.getStamina`.
description: Requires `players.stats.read`. The shorter spelling of the same read, matching the client's.
example:
-- Short spelling, same read
local stamina = Open77.stats.stamina(playerId)
print(stamina and stamina.percentage)

name: apply
summary: Applies a configured, bounded status to a target using a registered grade.
description: Requires `players.statuses.apply`. The grade's `kind`, duration and effect come from the definition; canonical eligibility (alive, ready, not protected) is checked the same way an upload's impact is. No upload runs and no damage is dealt: this is the status half of a hack on its own, for a scripted consequence such as a story beat or a penalty.
example:
-- A story beat blinds the player for the grade's duration, no upload, no damage
Open77.statuses.apply(narratorId, playerId, "myserver.short_circuit", "training")

name: list
summary: Lists the owned statuses currently affecting a player.
description: Requires `players.hacking.read`. Every status any provider applied -- kind, provider, action id, deadline -- the same answer as `Open77.hacking.statuses`.
example:
-- Show a player their active statuses
for _, status in ipairs(Open77.statuses.list(playerId) or {}) do
    Open77.chat.send(playerId, ("%s until %d"):format(status.kind, status.deadline))
end

name: remove
summary: Removes this provider's status without reversing the damage it did.
description: Requires `players.statuses.purge`. Only a status this resource applied can be removed; the victim's client is told to end its native presentation.
example:
-- The medic cures the status this resource applied
Open77.statuses.remove(actionId)

name: monotonic
summary: Server-monotonic seconds since the process started.
description: No permission. The same unit and meaning as the client `Open77.time.monotonic`. Use it for durations: it never jumps backwards, unlike wall-clock time.
example:
-- Measure how long a round lasted
local startedAt = Open77.time.monotonic()
AddEventHandler("arena:roundOver", function()
    print(("round lasted %.0f s"):format(Open77.time.monotonic() - startedAt))
end)

name: unix
summary: Wall-clock seconds since 1970 UTC, fractional.
description: No permission. `GetUnixTime` is the same function. The sandbox has no `os` library, so this is how an expiring ban or a scheduled event gets the real date.
example:
-- A ban that expires in 24 hours
bans[userId] = { until_ = Open77.time.unix() + 86400 }

name: utc
summary: The current instant as an ISO 8601 string.
description: No permission. `GetUtcTimestamp` is the same function. The same instant as `unix`, formatted for a log line or a stored record.
example:
-- Timestamp a log line
print(Open77.time.utc(), "player", source, "bought", itemId)

name: capture
summary: A frozen plain table of every current value.
description: No permission. Unlike the `declare` proxy, this does not read through: it is a snapshot to pin onto one match, which is the only correct form for a mode running several rounds at once.
example:
-- Pin the rules for this match so a mid-match panel write cannot change them
local rules = Open77.tunables.capture()
startMatch(rules)

name: declare
summary: Declares this resource's operator-tunable settings and returns a live proxy.
description: No permission. Declaration fields are `value` (the required default), `type` (`number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `string`, `enum`), `min`, `max`, `step`, `choices`, `unit`, `apply` (`live`, `next_round`, `next_match`), `label`, `description`, `group` and `order`. `min`, `max`, `type` and `choices` are enforced on every write; `step` and `unit` are presentation only. Limits: 128 tunables per resource, 64 KiB of declaration, 32 choices, 256-character strings. **The proxy reads through to the host on every access** -- read it at the point of use, because a value hoisted into a file-scope local is captured at load time and never updates while the admin panel goes on reporting the new number. A malformed declaration raises; an undeclared key read through the proxy raises rather than answering nil.

name: get
summary: The current value of one tunable.
description: No permission. Answers `nil, reason` for an undeclared key. A key declared `next_round` or `next_match` does not reach this until the resource calls `promote()`.
example:
-- Read one value at the point of use
local seconds = Open77.tunables.get("roundSeconds")

name: pending
summary: The changes waiting on a round or match boundary.
description: No permission. Key to value for everything an operator has written that `promote()` has not yet adopted.
example:
-- Tell the admin what will change at the next round
for key, value in pairs(Open77.tunables.pending()) do
    print(("next round: %s = %s"):format(key, tostring(value)))
end

name: promote
summary: Adopts every pending change and returns the keys that moved.
description: No permission. Call it at the boundary the resource declared -- the start of a round or a match -- so a mid-match write cannot change the rules under the players.
example:
-- Adopt operator changes at the round boundary
AddEventHandler("arena:roundStarting", function()
    for _, key in ipairs(Open77.tunables.promote()) do print("applied", key) end
end)

name: set
summary: Writes one tunable, with the same validation as the admin panel.
description: No permission. Returns `ok, message, pending`; `pending` is true when the key's `apply` policy holds the value at a boundary. Values are owned by the host, so they survive a reload **and** a stop and come back after a restart from `tunables.json`. The owning resource -- and no other -- receives `onTunableChanged(key, value, pending)` after every accepted write.
example:
-- /roundtime <seconds> writes the tunable with the same validation as the panel
RegisterCommand("roundtime", function(source, args)
    local ok, message, pending = Open77.tunables.set("roundSeconds", tonumber(args[1]))
    if not ok then Open77.chat.send(source, message) elseif pending then Open77.chat.send(source, "Applies next round.") end
end, true)

name: adopt
summary: Turns a client's description of a vanilla car into a canonical vehicle.
description:
Requires `world.vehicles` **and** `world.vehicles.adopt`, which is its own string because this is the one vehicle call that creates world state from something a client wrote. `playerId` must be the player the server believes sent the description — inside a net event handler that is `source`, and it must never be read out of the payload, because the placement checks are the entire defence. The description is what the client's `Open77.vehicles.adoptable()` hands back: `engineEntity`, `record`, `position`, and optionally `orientation`, `health`, `flags`, `primaryColor`, `secondaryColor`, `doors`, `windows`, `tires`, `brokenGlass`, `brokenLights` and `detachedParts`.

**Adoption takes the car's identity, not the engine's entity.** A traffic car is spawned, owned and despawned by REDengine population on one client, and the plugin has no notification it can rely on for a despawn it did not start — a canonical vehicle bound to such an entity would quietly become a ghost. So nothing is bound: the server creates an ordinary canonical vehicle from the description, with the same lifetime, the same reaper and the same projection path as one a garage spawned, and the client then hands its vanilla chassis back with `Open77.vehicles.releaseAdopted`.

Refusals are `adopt_policy_closed` (the player's bucket is not open), `too_far`, `player_unavailable` (no position for them), `duplicate_adoption` (a car of the same record is already adopted within three metres of that spot, because traffic is spawned per client and two players on one corner each describe their own), `vehicle_limit`, and the `invalid_*` family. `already_adopted` is not a failure: it answers with the id of the vehicle the first proposal created, because a retry after a dropped acknowledgement is the ordinary way a client proposes the same chassis twice.
example:
RegisterNetEvent("garage:adopt", function(description)
  local id, reason = Open77.vehicles.adopt(source, description)
  if not id then return print(reason) end
  -- Tell the proposing client to hand its vanilla chassis back.
  TriggerClientEvent("garage:adopted", source, description.engineEntity, id)
end)

name: all
summary: Lists authoritative server vehicles.
description: Returns snapshots ordered by Open77 ID. An optional routing bucket filters the result; omitting it returns every vehicle visible to the resource.
example:
-- /cars: how many server vehicles exist, and how many in the caller's bucket
RegisterCommand("cars", function(source)
    local everywhere = Open77.vehicles.all()
    local here = Open77.vehicles.all(Open77.players.get(source).bucket)
    Open77.chat.send(source, ("%d vehicles on the server, %d in your instance"):format(#everywhere, #here))
end, true)

name: applyProperties
summary: Alias for `setProperties`.
description: Identical contract. Useful to a codebase that reserves `set` for single-field writes.
example:
-- Restore a garage car exactly as it was stored
local stored = json.decode(row.props)
local id = Open77.vehicles.create({ record = stored.record, position = spot })
local ok, reason = Open77.vehicles.applyProperties(id, stored)
if not ok then print("garage restore failed: " .. reason) end

name: areLightsOn
summary: Whether a vehicle's headlights are lit at all.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. True for both `"on"` and `"high"`; `getLights` tells them apart.
example:
-- A traffic cop script: fine anyone driving at night with the lights off
for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.vehicles.all()) do
    local lit = Open77.vehicles.areLightsOn(entry.id)
    local driver = Open77.vehicles.getDriver(entry.id)
    if lit == false and driver then
        Open77.chat.send(driver, "Turn your headlights on!")
    end
end

name: breakAllGlass
summary: Breaks a range of vehicle glass elements.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Breaks the first `count` destructible-glass bits. The optional count defaults to all 32 and must be in 0..32.
example:
-- /wreck-glass <vehicleId>: shatter every window of a car
RegisterCommand("wreck-glass", function(source, args)
    local vehicleId = tonumber(args[1])
    if not vehicleId then return end
    Open77.vehicles.breakAllGlass(vehicleId)
end, true)

name: breakGlass
summary: Breaks one vehicle glass element.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setGlassBroken(id, glass, true)`; the canonical bit is replicated and retained for late joiners.
example:
-- The thief smashes the driver's window to get in
Open77.vehicles.breakGlass(vehicleId, 1)

name: breakLight
summary: Breaks one vehicle light.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setLightBroken(id, index, true)`.
example:
-- A hit on the front of the car breaks the first two lights
Open77.vehicles.breakLight(vehicleId, 0)
Open77.vehicles.breakLight(vehicleId, 1)

name: breakTire
summary: Breaks one vehicle tire.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setTireBroken(id, index, true)`. Tire indexes are 0..3.
example:
-- Spike strip: burst the two front tires
Open77.vehicles.breakTire(vehicleId, 0)
Open77.vehicles.breakTire(vehicleId, 1)

name: clearLightsHue
summary: Hands the lights back the record's own colour.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Exactly `setLightsHue(id, nil)`.
example:
-- The tuning shop's "stock lights" option
RegisterCommand("lights-stock", function(source)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if not seat then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Sit in the car first.") end
    Open77.vehicles.clearLightsHue(seat.vehicleId)
end, false)

name: clearLockedForPlayer
summary: Drops one player's lock exception.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Identical to `Open77.vehicles.setLockedForPlayer(id, playerId, nil)`: the player goes back to whatever the canonical bit says, and is re-sent that answer immediately.
example:
-- Taking the keys back: the player sees the car's real lock state again
RegisterCommand("keys-revoke", function(source, args)
    local vehicleId, target = tonumber(args[1]), tonumber(args[2])
    if not vehicleId or not target then return end
    Open77.vehicles.clearLockedForPlayer(vehicleId, target)
    Open77.chat.send(target, "Your keys were taken back.")
end, true)

name: clearPerformance
summary: Hands a vehicle back its record's rated performance.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Identical to `Open77.vehicles.setPerformance(id, nil)`. The withdrawal is replicated like the ceiling was, so every projection stops clamping rather than keeping the last value until it streams out.
example:
-- The race ended: hand every car back its real top speed
for _, vehicleId in ipairs(raceCars) do
    Open77.vehicles.clearPerformance(vehicleId)
end

name: closeDoor
summary: Closes a door, trunk, or hood.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setDoorOpen(id, door, false)`.
example:
-- Close the trunk once the delivery has been loaded
Open77.vehicles.closeDoor(vehicleId, Open77.vehicles.doors.trunk)

name: closeWindow
summary: Closes one side window.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setWindowOpen(id, window, false)`.
example:
-- Roll up the driver's window when it starts raining
AddEventHandler("onEnvironmentChanged", function(env)
    if env.weather ~= "rain" then return end
    for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.vehicles.all()) do
        Open77.vehicles.closeWindow(entry.id, Open77.vehicles.windows.frontLeft)
    end
end)

name: closest
summary: The nearest registered vehicle to a point or a player.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `Open77.vehicles.nearby` with a limit of one, and the same options. Nobody in range is a plain `nil` with NO reason, which is how a caller tells 'the search worked and the street is empty' from 'the search failed'. **Only server-spawned vehicles are in the registry.** A player standing next to a vanilla traffic car is standing next to something REDengine population spawned on their own client: it has no canonical id and this call cannot see it. Adopting vanilla traffic is a separate capability that does not exist yet.
example:
-- /lock: lock the nearest server vehicle to the caller
RegisterCommand("lock", function(source)
    local nearest = Open77.vehicles.closest(source, { radius = 8 })
    if not nearest then return Open77.chat.send(source, "No vehicle nearby.") end
    Open77.vehicles.lock(nearest.id)
    Open77.chat.send(source, ("Locked %s (%.1f m away)"):format(nearest.record, nearest.distance))
end, false)

name: create
summary: Creates a server-authoritative network vehicle.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The definition selects the record, transform, routing bucket, appearance, optional authoritative paint, flags, health, and initial damage. The server allocates the Open77 ID and replicates the canonical vehicle to interested clients. The creator name is retained as provenance and cleanup scope, never as an exclusive mutation lock. The definition also takes the three lifetime keys `ttlMs`, `persistent` and `despawnWhenUnobserved`, so a garage does not need a second call; a definition without them behaves exactly as it did before, and a lifetime that cannot be applied undoes the creation rather than half-honouring it -- the same rule the initial-damage path already follows.
example:
-- /car: spawn a Quadra a few metres in front of the caller and put them in the driver seat
RegisterCommand("car", function(source)
    local me = Open77.players.get(source)
    if not me or not me.position then return end
    local id, reason = Open77.vehicles.create({
        record = "Vehicle.v_sport2_quadra_turbo_r",
        position = { x = me.position.x + 4.0, y = me.position.y, z = me.position.z },
        yaw = me.heading,
        ttlMs = 30 * 60 * 1000, -- gone after 30 minutes if nobody removes it
    })
    if not id then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Spawn failed: " .. reason) end
    Open77.vehicles.warpPlayerIntoVehicle(source, id, Open77.vehicles.seats.driver)
end, false)

name: damageBodyCell
summary: Adds damage to one body cell.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Adds the amount to the current normalized cell and clamps the result to 0..1.
example:
-- A minor collision: add 25 % damage to body cell 12
Open77.vehicles.damageBodyCell(vehicleId, 12, 0.25)

name: damageBodyZone
summary: Adds damage across a body zone.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Adds the amount to each selected body cell and clamps every result to 0..1.
example:
-- Rear-ended: damage the whole back zone by half
Open77.vehicles.damageBodyZone(vehicleId, "back", 0.5)

name: detachPart
summary: Detaches one vehicle panel authoritatively.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setPartDetached(id, part, true)`. The state is replicated and retained for late join.
example:
-- Bring the wreck to life visually: tear off the front bumper and the hood
Open77.vehicles.detachPart(vehicleId, "bumperFront")
Open77.vehicles.detachPart(vehicleId, "hood")

name: detachedParts
summary: Maps stable detached-part names to network bit indexes.
description: Read-only constants for trunk, hood variants, door variants and front/back bumpers. Indexes are append-only protocol values in the range 0..15.
example:
-- List every panel name you can pass to detachPart
for name, bit in pairs(Open77.vehicles.detachedParts) do
    print(name, bit)
end

name: explode
summary: Detonates a vehicle through every viewer's own engine.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Writes the canonical ledger -- health to zero, `destroyed` and `exploded` raised, one revision -- and every client that has the vehicle streamed then reconciles its projection through the damage path that already replays a wreck to a late joiner, which ends in REDengine's own explosion on that machine. **Occupants stay occupants**: nobody is ejected, no seat is freed, no life state changes, and the server sends no damage to any player, inside the car or standing next to it. What the blast does to a body is the engine's own damage model running on each client, reaching the server the ordinary way through the player damage report -- a resource that wants the occupants dead has to say so itself. **Terminal and not repeatable**: a second call is refused with `already_exploded` rather than re-detonating a wreck, while a vehicle that is merely `destroyed` -- written off by collisions, never blown up -- is still a legitimate target. An owner report taken before the explosion and claiming a pristine car cannot undo it: health merges by minimum and the destruction bits by OR, both monotone. **Only server-spawned vehicles are in the registry.** A player standing next to a vanilla traffic car is standing next to something REDengine population spawned on their own client: it has no canonical id and this call cannot see it. Adopting vanilla traffic is a separate capability that does not exist yet.
example:
-- A car bomb: the fuse runs ten seconds after the player is warned
RegisterCommand("carbomb", function(source, args)
    local vehicleId = tonumber(args[1])
    if not vehicleId then return end
    local driver = Open77.vehicles.getDriver(vehicleId)
    if driver then Open77.chat.send(driver, "Something is beeping under your seat...") end
    SetTimeout(10000, function()
        local ok, reason = Open77.vehicles.explode(vehicleId)
        if not ok then print("explode refused: " .. reason) end
    end)
end, true)

name: forcePlayerOutOfVehicle
summary: Forces a player out of a network vehicle.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Publishes a durable forced-exit order and keeps the canonical seat reserved until the client confirms native unmount or the bounded transition timeout expires. This operation overrides an active exit lock. Supplying `vehicleId` protects against ejecting the player from a newer assignment by mistake.
example:
-- Police stop: pull the driver out of whatever they are driving
RegisterCommand("pullout", function(source, args)
    local target = tonumber(args[1])
    if not target then return end
    local ok, reason = Open77.vehicles.forcePlayerOutOfVehicle(target)
    if not ok then Open77.chat.send(source, "Could not eject: " .. reason) end
end, true)

name: freeSeats
summary: Every free seat of a vehicle, in seat order.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Canonical `seat_*` names in `driver, frontPassenger, rearLeft, rearRight` order, so picking `[1]` gives a deterministic 'put them anywhere' seat. Every seat of the four-seat model is considered; a two-seat record still reports its rear seats free, because the registry does not know the model's seat count.
returns: array of seat names, or nil
example:
-- Taxi: put the customer in the first free seat, whatever it is
local seats = Open77.vehicles.freeSeats(taxiId)
if seats and seats[1] then
    Open77.vehicles.warpPlayerIntoVehicle(customerId, taxiId, seats[1])
else
    Open77.chat.send(customerId, "The taxi is full.")
end

name: get
summary: Returns one authoritative server vehicle snapshot.
description: Reads canonical identity, transform, motion, flags, colors, all damage channels including detached parts, openings, occupants, lifetime, any performance ceiling, and authority state. Returns `nil` for an unknown ID. The transform half is `position` (a vector3), `heading` and `yaw` (one value, both names), `orientation` as `{ x, y, z, w }`, and the unchanged `x`/`y`/`z`. The motion half is `velocity`, `angularVelocity`, `speed` (m/s), `speedKph`, `onGround`, `reversing`, `moving` and `driverPlayerId` -- all of it the last thing the physics owner reported, and all of it zeroed when the vehicle has no owner, because nobody is simulating it then. `exploded` and `destroyed` are derived booleans over the same flags; `persistent`, `despawnWhenUnobserved` and `ttlMs` report the lifetime policy, `ttlMs` counted from now and absent when there is no deadline.
example:
-- Speed camera: check every car's speed once a second
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        Wait(1000)
        for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.vehicles.all()) do
            local car = Open77.vehicles.get(entry.id)
            if car and car.speedKph > 120 and car.driverPlayerId then
                Open77.chat.send(car.driverPlayerId, ("Slow down! %.0f km/h"):format(car.speedKph))
            end
        end
    end
end)

name: getAdoptPolicy
summary: One routing bucket's adoption policy.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Deliberately **not** gated by `world.vehicles.adopt`: a resource may see that a bucket is closed without being allowed to open it. Answers `"none"`, `"driver"` or `"any"`.
example:
-- Tell a joining player whether they may steal street cars in this instance
AddEventHandler("onPlayerReady", function(playerId)
    local bucket = Open77.players.get(playerId).bucket
    if Open77.vehicles.getAdoptPolicy(bucket) ~= "none" then
        Open77.chat.send(playerId, "Street cars can be taken here.")
    end
end)

name: getAppearance
summary: The entity appearance variant this car wears.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Answers the variant name, or `""` for the record's own default. The appearance variant is Cyberpunk's equivalent of a livery: a name defined by the vehicle's entity template, which is how the game ships one model in several trims.
example:
-- /livery: show which trim the caller's car wears
RegisterCommand("livery", function(source)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if not seat then return end
    local variant = Open77.vehicles.getAppearance(seat.vehicleId)
    Open77.chat.send(source, variant == "" and "Stock trim" or ("Trim: " .. variant))
end, false)

name: getDamage
summary: Returns the canonical damage snapshot.
description: Reads the server-owned body grid plus broken glass, light, tire, and detached-part masks. It returns `nil` when the vehicle ID is unknown.
example:
-- Mechanic's quote: count broken tires and detached panels
local damage = Open77.vehicles.getDamage(vehicleId)
if damage then
    print("tires mask:", damage.tires, "detached parts mask:", damage.detachedParts)
end

name: getDamageProfile
summary: Returns a resource-local vehicle damage profile.
description: Reads the profile registered by the current server resource for the specified vehicle record. Profiles are not shared implicitly between resources.
example:
-- Confirm the profile this resource registered for the Hella is in place
local profile = Open77.vehicles.getDamageProfile("Vehicle.v_standard2_archer_hella_player")
if not profile then
    print("no damage profile registered for the Hella yet")
end

name: getDriver
summary: The player driving this vehicle, or nil when nobody is.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The front-left occupant from the canonical seat ledger. Absent rather than zero when the seat is empty, and absent while an entry animation is still running, because a reserved seat is not yet a driver. Also on the read as `Open77.vehicles.get(id).driverPlayerId`, which is the field the occupants list is scanned for nine times out of ten.
example:
-- Charge the driver, not the passengers, when a car passes the toll gate
local driver = Open77.vehicles.getDriver(vehicleId)
if driver then
    Open77.chat.send(driver, "Toll: 50 eddies were taken from your account.")
end

name: getEngineHealth
summary: Vehicle health under its FiveM name.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `Open77.vehicles.getHealth`; there is no separate engine pool on this build.
example:
-- Ported FiveM code: the engine "health" is the car's single health pool, 0..1
local health = Open77.vehicles.getEngineHealth(vehicleId)
if health and health < 0.3 then
    Open77.chat.send(driverId, "Your car is about to give up. Find a mechanic.")
end

name: getHeading
summary: The vehicle's heading in degrees.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Extracted from the full orientation quaternion rather than from `qz`/`qw` alone, because a replicated vehicle carries roll and pitch too and a car on a slope would otherwise report a heading it is not facing. Identical to the client snapshot's `heading`, and in the same degrees as `Open77.players.get(...).heading` and the `yaw` that `create` and `setTransform` take. `Open77.vehicles.getYaw` is the same function under the other name.
example:
-- Spawn a second car parked right behind the first, facing the same way
local car = Open77.vehicles.get(vehicleId)
local heading = Open77.vehicles.getHeading(vehicleId)
Open77.vehicles.create({
    record = car.record,
    position = { x = car.position.x, y = car.position.y - 6.0, z = car.position.z },
    yaw = heading,
})

name: getHeadlightHue
summary: Alias for `getLightsHue`.
description: Identical contract, under the name a creator looking for headlights will try first.
example:
-- Save the headlight tint with the rest of the garage record
local hue = Open77.vehicles.getHeadlightHue(vehicleId)
saved.lightsHue = hue -- nil means stock lights

name: getHealth
summary: A vehicle's health, 0 to 1.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Canonical, and merged by MIN from the physics owner's report: an observer cannot heal a car by claiming it is fine.
example:
-- Refuse the race entry with a damaged car
RegisterCommand("race-join", function(source)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if not seat then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Sit in your race car first.") end
    local health = Open77.vehicles.getHealth(seat.vehicleId)
    if health < 0.9 then
        return Open77.chat.send(source, "Repair your car before joining.")
    end
    enterRace(source, seat.vehicleId)
end, false)

name: getLights
summary: A vehicle's headlight mode as a word.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Answers `"off"`, `"on"` or `"high"` -- the same three words `setLights` accepts, so a read feeds straight back into a write.
example:
-- Flash the high beams twice, then put the lights back as they were
CreateThread(function()
    local before = Open77.vehicles.getLights(vehicleId)
    for _ = 1, 2 do
        Open77.vehicles.setLights(vehicleId, "high"); Wait(300)
        Open77.vehicles.setLights(vehicleId, "off"); Wait(300)
    end
    Open77.vehicles.setLights(vehicleId, before)
end)

name: getLightsHue
summary: The CrystalCoat headlight hue in force, or nil.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Answers a number in `0..1`, or `nil` when the car uses its record's own light colour. `nil` rather than zero, because zero is a real hue -- red -- and the engine struct this mirrors carries its own `lightsColorDefined` boolean for exactly that reason. `getHeadlightHue` is the same function.
example:
-- Tuning shop: show the current tint before offering a new one
local hue = Open77.vehicles.getLightsHue(vehicleId)
if hue == nil then
    Open77.chat.send(source, "Stock headlights.")
else
    Open77.chat.send(source, ("Current tint: %.2f"):format(hue))
end

name: getPaint
summary: Reads authoritative vehicle paint.
description: Returns `applied` plus keyed primary and secondary RGB tables. Pure black remains distinguishable from reset because `applied` is a separate canonical flag. Returns `nil` for an unknown vehicle ID.
example:
-- Save the paint job so the garage can restore it later
local paint = Open77.vehicles.getPaint(vehicleId)
if paint and paint.applied then
    saveGarage(ownerId, { primary = paint.primary, secondary = paint.secondary })
end

name: getPerformance
summary: The performance ceiling in force, or nil.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `{ topSpeedKph, accelerationScale, taperKph }`, or `nil` when the vehicle runs at its record's rated performance. Also on the read as `Open77.vehicles.get(id).performance`.
example:
-- Show the active speed cap to the driver
local cap = Open77.vehicles.getPerformance(vehicleId)
if cap then
    Open77.chat.send(driverId, ("This car is limited to %d km/h"):format(cap.topSpeedKph))
end

name: getPlayerSeat
summary: Reads one player's canonical vehicle-seat assignment.
description: Returns the server ledger entry with vehicle ID, canonical seat name, numeric flags, and transition/policy booleans. It returns `nil` when the player is not assigned to a vehicle.
example:
-- Only the driver may pay for fuel
RegisterCommand("refuel", function(source)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if not seat then return Open77.chat.send(source, "You are not in a vehicle.") end
    if seat.seat ~= "seat_front_left" then
        return Open77.chat.send(source, "Only the driver can refuel.")
    end
    Open77.vehicles.repair(seat.vehicleId, "mechanical")
end, false)

name: getPosition
summary: The vehicle's canonical position as a vector3.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. A plain `{ x, y, z }` table, which is what an Open77 vector3 is, so `#(a - b)` works on it without a conversion. The same point `Open77.vehicles.get(id).position` carries, and the same one `x`/`y`/`z` have always carried. **Only server-spawned vehicles are in the registry.** A player standing next to a vanilla traffic car is standing next to something REDengine population spawned on their own client: it has no canonical id and this call cannot see it. Adopting vanilla traffic is a separate capability that does not exist yet.
example:
-- Tow truck job: is the caller close enough to hook the car?
local car = Open77.vehicles.getPosition(vehicleId)
local me = Open77.players.position(source)
if car and me and #(vector3(car.x, car.y, car.z) - vector3(me.x, me.y, me.z)) < 5.0 then
    startTow(source, vehicleId)
end

name: getProperties
summary: Everything a garage has to store to put this exact car back.
description:
Requires `world.vehicles`. Answers one plain table -- strings, numbers, booleans and tables, so it survives `json.encode` and a database column unchanged -- or `nil, "vehicle_not_found"`. This is the Cyberpunk counterpart of the `GetVehicleProperties` helper every FiveM framework ships, and `setProperties` is its other half: **`setProperties(id, getProperties(id))` leaves the vehicle observably unchanged**, and the same table applied to a fresh vehicle of the same record reproduces it.

The shape is `{ version = 1, record, appearance, paint = { applied, primary = {r,g,b}, secondary = {r,g,b}, lightsHue? }, health, engineOn, lights = "off"|"on"|"high", siren, locked, drivable, invulnerable, immortal, doors, windows, damage = { body = {30 cells}, glass, lights, tires, detachedParts, destroyed, exploded }, performance? }`.

**Deliberately not where the car was standing.** Position, heading, velocity, occupants, routing bucket and revision are not properties of the car, and a table that carried them would tempt a caller into teleporting by accident; `setTransform` and `setBucket` still own those.

**What Cyberpunk does not have is the real story here.** Vehicle visual customisation on build 2.31 is one struct, `GenericTemplatePersistentData` -- primary RGB, secondary RGB and a lights hue -- plus the entity appearance variant. There are no mod slots, no wheel types, no neon, no window tint and no numbered extras: not unimplemented, absent, with no RTTI type for any of them. `Open77.vehicles.unsupportedProperties` names every FiveM property that therefore has no counterpart, and `setProperties` refuses such a key by name rather than dropping it.
example:
-- /park: store the caller's car so it can be brought back after a restart
RegisterCommand("park", function(source)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if not seat then return end
    local props = Open77.vehicles.getProperties(seat.vehicleId)
    Open77.kvp.set("garage:" .. Open77.players.identifier(source), json.encode(props))
    Open77.vehicles.remove(seat.vehicleId)
    Open77.chat.send(source, "Car stored.")
end, false)

name: getSpeed
summary: Scalar speed in metres per second.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The physics owner's own drivetrain reading, in the unit every other Open77 read uses. **Motion is the last thing the owner reported**: a vehicle with no physics owner is not being simulated by anyone, so losing the lease -- a driver stepping out, disconnecting, or the lease expiring -- zeroes this rather than leaving a parked car claiming the speed it had when its driver got out. A server `setTransform` clears it for the same reason.
example:
-- Rear-end insurance: only pay out if the car was actually moving
local speed = Open77.vehicles.getSpeed(vehicleId)
if speed and speed > 5.0 then
    payInsurance(driverId)
end

name: getSpeedKph
summary: Scalar speed in kilometres per hour.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The same reading as `Open77.vehicles.getSpeed` converted once, because speed limits and performance ceilings are authored in km/h and every caller converting it themselves is a rounding bug waiting to happen.
example:
-- Radar: report who is over the limit on this road
for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.vehicles.nearby(radarPosition, 60)) do
    local kph = Open77.vehicles.getSpeedKph(entry.id)
    if kph and kph > 80 then
        print(("vehicle %d flashed at %.0f km/h"):format(entry.id, kph))
    end
end

name: getVehicleProperties
summary: The FiveM-shaped name for `getProperties`.
description: Identical contract. The name exists so a resource ported from a FiveM framework, where the helper is spelled `GetVehicleProperties`, does not have to be renamed to be read.
example:
-- FiveM-style garage code works unchanged
RegisterCommand("park", function(source)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if not seat then return end
    local props = Open77.vehicles.getVehicleProperties(seat.vehicleId)
    MySQL.update.await("UPDATE owned_vehicles SET props = ? WHERE owner = ?", { json.encode(props), Open77.players.identifier(source) })
end, false)

name: getVelocity
summary: The vehicle's linear velocity as a vector3, in metres per second.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. A plain `{ x, y, z }` table. Like `getSpeed`, it is the last accepted owner report and is zeroed when the physics lease is lost or the server teleports the vehicle. `Open77.vehicles.get(id).angularVelocity` carries the rotational half.
example:
-- Is the car sliding sideways? Compare velocity with the heading
local v = Open77.vehicles.getVelocity(vehicleId)
if v and math.abs(v.x) + math.abs(v.y) > 20 then
    print("fast lateral movement on vehicle", vehicleId)
end

name: getYaw
summary: Alias of `Open77.vehicles.getHeading`.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `heading` is the name the player read and `respawn` use; `yaw` is the name `create` and `setTransform` use. One value, both names, so nobody has to remember which surface they are on.
example:
-- Respawn the player's car at the same spot after a repair, facing the same way
local pos = Open77.vehicles.getPosition(vehicleId)
local yaw = Open77.vehicles.getYaw(vehicleId)
Open77.vehicles.remove(vehicleId)
Open77.vehicles.create({ record = record, position = pos, yaw = yaw })

name: honk
summary: Alias of `Open77.vehicles.triggerHorn`.
description: Requires `world.vehicles` and uses the same current-owner routing, duration bounds, and transient synchronization contract as `triggerHorn`.
example:
-- The taxi has arrived: honk twice
CreateThread(function()
    Open77.vehicles.honk(taxiId, 300)
    Wait(500)
    Open77.vehicles.honk(taxiId, 300)
end)

name: isDoorOpen
summary: Reads one canonical door opening state.
description: Server-side authoritative query covering four doors, trunk, and hood. Returns `nil` for an unknown vehicle ID.
example:
-- Refuse to drive off with the trunk open
if Open77.vehicles.isDoorOpen(vehicleId, Open77.vehicles.doors.trunk) then
    Open77.chat.send(driverId, "Close the trunk first.")
end

name: isDrivable
summary: Whether a vehicle is in service.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. False once `setDrivable(id, false)` has been applied. Independent of health: a wreck with a live engine is still 'drivable' by this flag.
example:
-- Impound: a car that was taken out of service cannot be sold
if not Open77.vehicles.isDrivable(vehicleId) then
    return Open77.chat.send(source, "This car is impounded.")
end

name: isEngineOn
summary: Whether a vehicle's engine is running.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Reads the canonical `engineOn` flag, which is what every client applies -- not a local guess. A read answers `nil` plus a reason where a write answers `false`.
example:
-- Fuel drains only while the engine runs
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        Wait(5000)
        for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.vehicles.all()) do
            if Open77.vehicles.isEngineOn(entry.id) then
                fuel[entry.id] = math.max(0, (fuel[entry.id] or 100) - 1)
            end
        end
    end
end)

name: isLocked
summary: Reads a vehicle's canonical entry-lock state.
description: Returns the derived durable lock boolean without requiring callers to decode the complete flags mask. Unknown vehicles return `nil`.
example:
-- /lock toggles the lock of the caller's car
RegisterCommand("lock", function(source)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if not seat then return end
    local locked = Open77.vehicles.isLocked(seat.vehicleId)
    Open77.vehicles.setLocked(seat.vehicleId, not locked)
    Open77.chat.send(source, locked and "Unlocked." or "Locked.")
end, false)

name: isLockedForPlayer
summary: Is this vehicle locked as far as this one player is concerned?
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The player's exception if they hold one, otherwise the canonical bit -- the single function that decides what a client is told, so a caller can never disagree with the fan-out. `Open77.vehicles.isLocked` still answers the canonical question, which is what a late joiner with no exception will be told.
example:
-- Tell the player whether their own keys open this car
RegisterCommand("trykeys", function(source, args)
    local vehicleId = tonumber(args[1])
    if not vehicleId then return end
    local locked = Open77.vehicles.isLockedForPlayer(vehicleId, source)
    Open77.chat.send(source, locked and "Your keys do not fit." or "The door opens.")
end, false)

name: isPartDetached
summary: Reads one canonical detached-part bit.
description: Returns whether a named/indexed panel is detached, or `nil` when the vehicle ID is unknown.
example:
-- The scrapyard pays less for a car missing its hood
local price = 1000
if Open77.vehicles.isPartDetached(vehicleId, "hood") then
    price = price - 200
end

name: isPlayerExitLocked
summary: Reports whether a player's canonical seat has exit lock enabled.
description: Returns true only when the player currently has a seat assignment carrying the durable `exitLocked` policy. An unseated or unknown player returns false.
example:
-- The arrested player stays in the police car until released
if Open77.vehicles.isPlayerExitLocked(suspectId) then
    Open77.chat.send(suspectId, "You cannot leave the vehicle.")
end

name: isSirenOn
summary: Whether a vehicle's siren is on.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Canonical: no client can report this bit, so the server's value is the only value.
example:
-- Only a cruiser with its siren on may run a red light
if Open77.vehicles.isSirenOn(vehicleId) then
    return -- no fine
end

name: isWindowOpen
summary: Reads one canonical side-window opening state.
description: Server-side authoritative query for indexes 0..3. It does not report broken glass and returns `nil` for an unknown vehicle.
example:
-- Drive-through: the customer must have the window down
if not Open77.vehicles.isWindowOpen(vehicleId, Open77.vehicles.windows.frontLeft) then
    Open77.chat.send(driverId, "Roll down your window to order.")
end

name: lock
summary: Locks a vehicle against ordinary entry.
description: Convenience alias for `setLocked(id, true)`. Requires `world.vehicles` and updates durable canonical state.
example:
-- The rental is over: lock the car so nobody else drives it away
Open77.vehicles.lock(rentalId)
Open77.chat.send(renterId, "Your rental has ended.")

name: lockForAll
summary: Locks a vehicle for everyone, revoking every exception.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `Open77.vehicles.setLockedForAll(id, true)` under a name that reads as an action.
example:
-- Impound a car: everyone loses access, including previous key holders
RegisterCommand("impound", function(source, args)
    local vehicleId = tonumber(args[1])
    if not vehicleId then return end
    Open77.vehicles.lockForAll(vehicleId)
    Open77.vehicles.setDrivable(vehicleId, false)
end, true)

name: nearby
summary: Every registered vehicle within a radius of a point or a player, nearest first.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Deliberately the same anchor, bucket and limit conventions as `Open77.players.nearby`: the anchor is a position table (a vector3 is one) or a player id, a player anchor defaults to that player's own routing bucket, `bucket = false` opts back out to every bucket, and ties are broken by vehicle id so the order does not reshuffle between calls. `occupied = true` keeps only cars with someone in them and `occupied = false` only empty ones. Each entry is `{ id, record, resource, bucket, distance, occupants, locked, position }` -- the placement, not the whole snapshot; call `Open77.vehicles.get` on the one you picked. **Only server-spawned vehicles are in the registry.** A player standing next to a vanilla traffic car is standing next to something REDengine population spawned on their own client: it has no canonical id and this call cannot see it. Adopting vanilla traffic is a separate capability that does not exist yet.
returns: reason: invalid_argument, invalid_position, invalid_radius, invalid_bucket, invalid_limit, invalid_options, player_not_found, position_unknown
example:
-- /nearcars: list the server vehicles within 30 m of the caller
RegisterCommand("nearcars", function(source)
    local list = Open77.vehicles.nearby(source, 30, { limit = 5 })
    if not list or #list == 0 then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Nothing nearby.") end
    for _, entry in ipairs(list) do
        Open77.chat.send(source, ("#%d %s at %.1f m"):format(entry.id, entry.record, entry.distance))
    end
end, false)

name: occupantInSeat
summary: Who is in one seat of a vehicle.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The `GetPedInVehicleSeat` of FiveM. Answers the player id and, as a second value, the full occupant record with its transition flags; a plain `nil` means the seat is free.
returns: playerId and occupant record, or nil
example:
-- The passenger seat decides who pays the taxi fare
local passenger = Open77.vehicles.occupantInSeat(taxiId, Open77.vehicles.seats.frontPassenger)
if passenger then
    chargeFare(passenger, 120)
end

name: openDoor
summary: Opens a door, trunk, or hood.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setDoorOpen(id, door, true)`.
example:
-- Pop the trunk when the delivery is loaded
Open77.vehicles.openDoor(vehicleId, Open77.vehicles.doors.trunk)

name: openWindow
summary: Opens one side window.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setWindowOpen(id, window, true)`.
example:
-- The driver stops at the ticket booth: roll down the window
Open77.vehicles.openWindow(vehicleId, Open77.vehicles.windows.frontLeft)

name: registerDamageProfile
summary: Registers resource-local named damage zones and glass parts.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Profiles are scoped to the calling server resource VM and can extend or override the default body-zone mapping for one vehicle record.
example:
-- Name the body cells so later calls can say "rear" instead of listing indexes
Open77.vehicles.registerDamageProfile("Vehicle.v_standard2_archer_hella_player", {
    bodyZones = { hood = { 13, 14, 15 }, trunkLid = { 1, 2, 3 } },
    glass = { windscreen = 0, rearWindow = 1 },
})
Open77.vehicles.damageBodyZone(vehicleId, "hood", 0.5)
Open77.vehicles.breakGlass(vehicleId, "windscreen")

name: remove
summary: Removes a server-authoritative network vehicle.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Any authorized resource may remove any canonical vehicle, regardless of which resource created it. Removal clears occupancy and authority before notifying streamed clients.
example:
-- /dv: delete the vehicle the caller is sitting in
RegisterCommand("dv", function(source)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if not seat then return Open77.chat.send(source, "You are not in a vehicle.") end
    Open77.vehicles.remove(seat.vehicleId)
end, true)

name: removePlayerFromVehicle
summary: Alias for forced authoritative vehicle exit.
description: Same contract as `forcePlayerOutOfVehicle`, including the optional expected vehicle ID, exit-lock override, client confirmation, and timeout cleanup.
example:
-- Car-jacking mini-game: the victim is thrown out when the thief wins
Open77.vehicles.removePlayerFromVehicle(victimId, vehicleId)
Open77.vehicles.warpPlayerIntoVehicle(thiefId, vehicleId, Open77.vehicles.seats.driver)

name: repair
summary: Repairs a selected vehicle damage scope.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Supported scopes are `glass`, `body`, `lights`, `tires`, `visual`, `mechanical`, and `full`. The default is `full`.
example:
-- The body shop fixes the paintwork only; the mechanic does the rest
RegisterCommand("bodyshop", function(source)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if seat then Open77.vehicles.repair(seat.vehicleId, "visual") end
end, false)

name: repairAllGlass
summary: Repairs all vehicle glass.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Clears the complete canonical broken-glass mask.
example:
-- The glass shop fixes every window for 200 eddies
if takeMoney(source, 200) then
    Open77.vehicles.repairAllGlass(vehicleId)
end

name: repairAllLights
summary: Repairs every vehicle light.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Clears the complete canonical broken-light mask.
example:
-- Part of the "full service" menu at the mechanic
Open77.vehicles.repairAllLights(vehicleId)

name: repairAllTires
summary: Repairs all four vehicle tires.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Clears the complete canonical broken-tire mask.
example:
-- Tire shop: four new tires
Open77.vehicles.repairAllTires(vehicleId)
Open77.chat.send(source, "New tires fitted.")

name: repairBodyCell
summary: Repairs one body cell.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Sets the selected 1-based body cell to zero damage and replicates the repaired state.
example:
-- Repair the single cell the player pointed at with the body-shop tool
Open77.vehicles.repairBodyCell(vehicleId, cellIndex)

name: repairBodyZone
summary: Repairs every body cell in a zone.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Clears all cells selected by a registered zone name or explicit index array.
example:
-- The body shop repairs one side of the car at a time
Open77.vehicles.repairBodyZone(vehicleId, "left")

name: repairGlass
summary: Repairs one vehicle glass element.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setGlassBroken(id, glass, false)`.
example:
-- Replace just the windscreen
Open77.vehicles.repairGlass(vehicleId, 0)

name: repairLight
summary: Repairs one vehicle light.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setLightBroken(id, index, false)`.
example:
-- Replace the left headlight
Open77.vehicles.repairLight(vehicleId, 0)

name: repairTire
summary: Repairs one vehicle tire.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Convenience wrapper over `setTireBroken(id, index, false)`.
example:
-- Change the front-left tire
Open77.vehicles.repairTire(vehicleId, 0)

name: resetPaint
summary: Restores a vehicle's authored paint.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Clears the canonical custom-paint flag without treating stored RGB bytes as a sentinel, then reliably publishes the reset to all current and future viewers.
example:
-- The player sold the car: back to factory paint for the next owner
Open77.vehicles.resetPaint(vehicleId)

name: seatFree
summary: Whether one seat of a vehicle is free.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. A seat held by an occupant whose entry animation is still running counts as TAKEN: the seat is reserved and a second warp into it is refused, so reporting it free would be a lie the caller then trips over. Seats accept `-1..2`, the `Open77.vehicles.seats` constants, aliases like `driver`, and canonical `seat_*` names.
example:
-- Let a passenger in only if the seat is really empty
if Open77.vehicles.seatFree(vehicleId, "frontPassenger") then
    Open77.vehicles.warpPlayerIntoVehicle(playerId, vehicleId, "frontPassenger")
else
    Open77.chat.send(playerId, "That seat is taken.")
end

name: seatName
summary: The canonical spelling of a seat name or index.
description: No permission. Turns `-1`, `"driver"`, `"frontLeft"` or `"seat_front_left"` into `"seat_front_left"`, which is the spelling every occupant record and every seat event uses. `nil` for anything that names no seat.
example:
-- Whatever the player typed, store the canonical seat name
RegisterCommand("sit", function(source, args)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.seatName(args[1] or "driver")
    if not seat then return Open77.chat.send(source, "Unknown seat.") end
    print(seat) -- seat_front_left, seat_front_right, ...
end, false)

name: setAdoptPolicy
summary: Opens or closes one routing bucket to vehicle adoption.
description: Requires `world.vehicles` and `world.vehicles.adopt`. `"none"` is the default and every bucket starts there: nothing is adoptable until a resource says so. `"driver"` accepts only a car the proposing player is standing at, within six metres — the car-theft shape, where you make canonical the car you are about to take and nothing else. `"any"` widens that to sixty metres; it does not remove the check. `options.bucket` selects the routing bucket (default `0`). The policy is server-side only: a client never learns it, and a proposal into a closed bucket is simply refused.
example:
-- Street cars may be stolen in the free-roam bucket, but only the one you stand at
Open77.vehicles.setAdoptPolicy("driver", { bucket = 0 })

name: setAppearance
summary: Swaps the appearance variant on a live car, on every viewer.
description:
Requires `world.vehicles` **and** `world.vehicles.appearance`.
