The second string exists because this is the one vehicle write that changes what the world LOOKS like rather than what a car does: it reaches a native entity-appearance reschedule on every viewer at once, for every car a resource can name, and a resource that wants to repaint the city should have to say so -- the same argument that gave adoption its own string. **It gates a CHANGE, never a restatement**: writing the variant a car already wears is accepted without it, which is what makes `setProperties(id, getProperties(id))` work for a resource that never changes a look.

`nil` or `""` restores the record's default variant. The name is not validated here, because only the client holds the entity template: a variant the model does not define is a no-op on each projection and the canonical value stays as written. `Open77.data.vehicle(record)` looks a record up but does not enumerate variants -- the shipped 2.31 catalogue does not carry them.

**No intent window, and that is structural rather than lucky.** The physics owner's durable report has no appearance field and no colour field of any kind, so the twice-a-second merge that used to undo server writes cannot reach this one. On the client the variant is applied through `entEntity::ScheduleAppearanceChange` and held on the replica until the projection attaches -- measured at up to about 3.7 s after the create -- then re-applied if the entity is torn down and streamed back.
example:
-- Livery shop: switch the caller's car to a different factory trim
RegisterCommand("livery", function(source, args)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if not seat or not args[1] then return end
    local ok, reason = Open77.vehicles.setAppearance(seat.vehicleId, args[1])
    if not ok then Open77.chat.send(source, "Livery refused: " .. reason) end
end, false)

name: setBodyCell
summary: Sets one body-damage cell.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Lua body-cell indexes are 1..30 and the value is clamped or validated in the normalized 0..1 range.
example:
-- Restore one body cell from a stored damage record
Open77.vehicles.setBodyCell(vehicleId, 7, 0.4)

name: setBodyDamage
summary: Replaces the complete body-damage grid.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The table must contain exactly 30 normalized finite values in the range 0..1.
example:
-- A freshly spawned car with a fully repaired body
local pristine = {}
for i = 1, 30 do pristine[i] = 0.0 end
Open77.vehicles.setBodyDamage(vehicleId, pristine)

name: setBodyZone
summary: Sets all body cells in a zone.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The zone may be a registered zone name or an explicit array of cell indexes. Every selected cell receives the normalized value.
example:
-- Crash scene prop: a car with a crushed front
Open77.vehicles.setBodyZone(vehicleId, "front", 0.9)

name: setDamage
summary: Replaces multiple canonical damage components at once.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Accepts a combined damage table and validates body cells and bit masks before publishing one authoritative update.

name: setDespawnWhenUnobserved
summary: Removes a vehicle once nobody has had it streamed for thirty seconds.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The window is not zero because interest is recomputed against the last received player snapshot, and a loading screen or a bucket change briefly empties a viewer set that is about to refill; thirty seconds rides that out. The clock runs for a vehicle nobody has **ever** seen too, which is what a garage wants -- a car spawned for a player who never turns up still goes. A viewer coming back resets the clock rather than pausing it, and turning the flag off forgets it entirely so that turning it back on later does not inherit a deadline from a window nobody was counting. A persistent vehicle is exempt. Read back as `Open77.vehicles.get(id).despawnWhenUnobserved`.
example:
-- Rental cars vanish once everybody has driven away from them
local id = Open77.vehicles.create({ record = "Vehicle.v_standard2_archer_hella_player", position = spot })
Open77.vehicles.setDespawnWhenUnobserved(id, true)

name: setDetachedPartMask
summary: Adds a canonical detached-part mask.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The 16-bit mask is monotonic on a live projection. Removing a previously detached bit is rejected because REDengine 2.31 has no validated safe reattachment primitive.
example:
-- Reproduce a stored wreck: bits are one-way, so apply the whole mask at once
Open77.vehicles.setDetachedPartMask(vehicleId, storedWreck.detachedParts)

name: setDoorMask
summary: Replaces the vehicle opening mask.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The six-bit mask covers four doors, trunk, and hood. Valid values are 0..63.
example:
-- Close everything at once (doors, trunk and hood)
Open77.vehicles.setDoorMask(vehicleId, 0)

name: setDoorOpen
summary: Sets one door, trunk, or hood opening state.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `door` is an index 0..5 or one of the constants in `Open77.vehicles.doors`.
example:
-- Pop the hood for the mechanic
Open77.vehicles.setDoorOpen(vehicleId, Open77.vehicles.doors.hood, true)

name: setDrivable
summary: Puts a vehicle in or out of service.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Out of service cuts the engine in the SAME canonical revision and locks the simulated driver's throttle and brake on every projection, so the car cannot be pushed along by its own inputs; a car whose throttle is dead while its engine idles is a bug report waiting to happen. Putting it back in service does NOT restart the engine -- that is `setEngine`. This is the `SetVehicleUndriveable` of FiveM, and like the entry lock it is server-authored: no owner report can clear it.
example:
-- Wheel clamp: the car stays intact but will not move
RegisterCommand("clamp", function(source, args)
    local vehicleId = tonumber(args[1])
    if not vehicleId then return end
    Open77.vehicles.setDrivable(vehicleId, false)
    Open77.chat.send(source, "Clamped.")
end, true)

name: setEngine
summary: Starts or stops a vehicle's engine.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Writes only the `engineOn` bit and leaves every other durable flag exactly as it was, which `Open77.vehicles.update` cannot do without a read-modify-write of the whole bitfield. The write also records a ten-second intent that outranks the physics owner's durable report, because that report is published every 500 ms and would otherwise clear a bit set while one was already in flight. The intent is released as soon as the owner reports the same value, so a driver who then starts the car themselves is obeyed immediately. An authority release or revoke -- a driver stepping out -- switches every electrical bit off by platform design; re-assert on `onVehicleAuthorityChanged` if that matters.
example:
-- Remote engine kill from the dispatcher
RegisterCommand("killengine", function(source, args)
    local vehicleId = tonumber(args[1])
    if not vehicleId then return end
    local ok, reason = Open77.vehicles.setEngine(vehicleId, false)
    if not ok then Open77.chat.send(source, reason) end
end, true)

name: setEngineHealth
summary: Sets vehicle health under its FiveM name.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. **Cyberpunk models one vehicle health pool.** There is no separate engine pool to damage, so this is `Open77.vehicles.setHealth` under the name a FiveM port reaches for, and at 0 the car is a wreck rather than a running car with a dead engine. If you want the car to stay whole but refuse to move, that is `setDrivable(id, false)`.
example:
-- FiveM port: remember the scale is 0..1 here, not 0..1000
Open77.vehicles.setEngineHealth(vehicleId, 0.5)

name: setGlassBroken
summary: Sets or clears one broken-glass bit.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `glass` may be a numeric 0..31 index or a name supplied by the resource's registered damage profile.
example:
-- The thief smashes the driver's window to get in
Open77.vehicles.setGlassBroken(vehicleId, 1, true)

name: setGlassMask
summary: Replaces the broken-glass bit mask.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The 32-bit mask describes destructible glass records, not the four reversible side-window opening states.
example:
-- Restore a stored broken-glass pattern on respawn
Open77.vehicles.setGlassMask(vehicleId, stored.glass)

name: setHeadlightColor
summary: The same tint, from an RGB colour.
description:
Requires `world.vehicles`. Accepts the same colour forms as `setPaint` -- `"#RRGGBB"`, `{ r, g, b }` or a positional table -- converts it to a hue and applies that. `nil` clears the tint.

**Only the hue survives.** The engine stores one float, so `#800000` and `#FF0000` light the car identically, and a grey has no hue at all and reads as red. The function exists because a porting creator has a colour in hand and not a hue; `setLightsHue` is the honest form. `setHeadlightColour` is the same function.
example:
-- The tuning shop sells a cyan headlight tint
RegisterCommand("lights", function(source, args)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if seat then Open77.vehicles.setHeadlightColor(seat.vehicleId, args[1] or "#00D8FF") end
end, false)

name: setHeadlightColour
summary: Alias for `setHeadlightColor`.
description: Identical contract, in the other spelling.
example:
-- British spelling, same tint
Open77.vehicles.setHeadlightColour(vehicleId, "#FF00AA")

name: setHealth
summary: Sets a vehicle's health, 0 to 1.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The same normalized pool `get(id).health` reads and `setDamage{ health = }` writes, under a name that does one thing. Out-of-range values are refused rather than clamped, so a caller passing FiveM's 0..1000 scale finds out.
example:
-- /fix restores the caller's car completely
RegisterCommand("fix", function(source)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if not seat then return end
    Open77.vehicles.setHealth(seat.vehicleId, 1.0)
    Open77.vehicles.repair(seat.vehicleId, "full")
end, true)

name: setHighBeams
summary: Raises or drops the high beams without going dark.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Turning them off leaves the side lights on if they were on, rather than switching the car dark -- which is what a naive `setLights("on"/"off")` pair gets wrong. Turning them on implies side lights, because the native mode cannot express one without the other.
example:
-- Flash the high beams at the car in front
CreateThread(function()
    Open77.vehicles.setHighBeams(vehicleId, true)
    Wait(400)
    Open77.vehicles.setHighBeams(vehicleId, false) -- side lights stay on
end)

name: setLightBroken
summary: Sets or clears one broken-light bit.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The light index must be in 0..31.
example:
-- Repair the right headlight only
Open77.vehicles.setLightBroken(vehicleId, 1, false)

name: setLightMask
summary: Replaces the broken-light bit mask.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Replaces the complete 32-bit canonical broken-light mask.
example:
-- Restore the stored broken-light pattern
Open77.vehicles.setLightMask(vehicleId, stored.lights)

name: setLights
summary: Sets a vehicle's headlight mode.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. One call for the whole mode, because `lightsOn` and `highBeams` are NOT independent on this build: the client maps the pair to a single native LightMode and 'high beams with no side lights' is not a state REDengine can express. Accepts `"off"`, `"on"`, `"high"` (aliases `highBeams`, `high_beams`, `full`) or a boolean. Carries the same ten-second intent as `setEngine`.
example:
-- Street lights on: every parked car turns its lights on at 20:00
AddEventHandler("onEnvironmentChanged", function(env)
    if env.hour ~= 20 then return end
    for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.vehicles.all()) do
        Open77.vehicles.setLights(entry.id, "on")
    end
end)

name: setLightsHue
summary: Tints the car's own lights.
description:
Requires `world.vehicles`. `hue` is `0..1` -- the H of the HSB triple the engine's visual template carries -- and `nil` hands the lights back the record's colour.

**This is the closest build 2.31 has to `SetVehicleNeonLights` or `SetVehicleHeadlightsColour`, and it is not the same thing.** There is no underglow and no xenon palette in this game; what exists is the vehicle's own emissive colour, continuous rather than indexed, in the same `GenericTemplatePersistentData` struct as the two paint colours. Because it is the same struct, the hue and the paint reach the engine in one event -- which is why the hue is carried inside `paint` in a property table, and why it is unaffected by `paintApplied`: a car can wear a tinted headlight over its stock body paint.

Replicated to every viewer and replayed on stream-in. It is not in the physics owner's durable report, so it needs no intent window.
example:
-- A tint slider from 0 to 1, and a "stock" button that clears it
RegisterNetEvent("tuning:lightsHue", function(hue)
    if hue then Open77.vehicles.setLightsHue(vehicleId, hue) else Open77.vehicles.clearLightsHue(vehicleId) end
end)

name: setLocked
summary: Sets or clears a vehicle's durable entry lock.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Atomically changes only `VehicleStateFlags.Locked`, publishes the canonical result to current viewers and late joiners, and does not overwrite unrelated flags. This blocks ordinary entry, not exit by an existing occupant; forced server seat assignment may deliberately bypass it.
example:
-- Personal vehicles spawn locked; the owner unlocks with /unlock
local id = Open77.vehicles.create({ record = record, position = spot })
Open77.vehicles.setLocked(id, true)
Open77.vehicles.setLockedForPlayer(id, ownerId, false)

name: setLockedForAll
summary: Sets the canonical entry lock and revokes every per-player exception.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Wiping the exceptions is the point, not a side effect: "lock this for everyone" has to mean everyone, including the key holders excepted a minute ago. `Open77.vehicles.setLocked` is unchanged and moves only the canonical bit, leaving exceptions standing -- use that one when the exceptions should survive. When the canonical bit was already at the requested value but exceptions were dropped, the whole audience is re-stated explicitly, because nothing else would tell the excepted players their exception is gone.
example:
-- Lock the car for the street but keep it open for the two key holders
Open77.vehicles.setLockedForAll(vehicleId, true)
for _, holder in ipairs({ ownerId, partnerId }) do
    Open77.vehicles.setLockedForPlayer(vehicleId, holder, false)
end

name: setLockedForPlayer
summary: Decides one player's view of a vehicle's entry lock.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `true` or `false` pins that player's view regardless of the canonical bit; `nil` drops the exception and puts them back on it. This is the shape a keys resource needs: `setLockedForAll(id, true)` for the street, then `setLockedForPlayer(id, holder, false)` for each key holder. The canonical bit stays `locked`, so a late joiner is told the right thing with no bookkeeping, and a key holder who disconnects takes their exception with them. The substitution happens at the single point where state reaches a socket, so no fan-out path can disagree with `isLockedForPlayer`. Per-player state is never written to the canonical flags, which is also why no owner report can disturb it -- `Locked` is outside the set an owner report is allowed to carry.
returns: reason: invalid_argument, invalid_player_id, vehicle_not_found, vehicles_unavailable, permission_denied:world.vehicles
example:
Open77.vehicles.setLockedForAll(id, true)
for _, holder in ipairs(keyHolders) do
  Open77.vehicles.setLockedForPlayer(id, holder, false)
end

name: setPaint
summary: Sets authoritative paint on a canonical vehicle.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Accepts primary and optional secondary RGB colors as `#RRGGBB`, keyed `{ r, g, b }`, or positional tables. Omitting secondary mirrors primary. Paint is cross-resource and replicated to current viewers, stream-in projections, reconnects, and late joiners.

name: setPartDetached
summary: Detaches one standard vehicle part.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The part may be an index 0..15 or a name from `Open77.vehicles.detachedParts`. Only `true` is accepted; respawn the vehicle to restore panels.
example:
-- The crash tore off the trunk lid
Open77.vehicles.setPartDetached(vehicleId, "trunk", true)

name: setPerformance
summary: Caps one vehicle's top speed and pickup, from the server.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The profile is `{ topSpeedKph, accelerationScale, taperKph }`: a speed ceiling in km/h in `0..1000` (zero means none), throttle authority at every speed in `(0, 1]`, and how many km/h below the ceiling the throttle starts easing off, `3..200` with a default of `12`. **The taper is never zero**: below about 3 km/h the roll-off is short enough that the limiter hunts around the ceiling and it reads as stutter, which is why the client-local governor has refused that band since it shipped -- the server form enforces the identical envelope on the Lua boundary, in the registry and on both sides of the wire, so a server cap cannot be a way around a rule somebody measured. `nil` clears the ceiling, and so does a profile that asks for nothing -- no ceiling and full throttle authority. The taper is not part of that test: a roll-off width around a ceiling that does not exist changes nothing, which is how the native profile decides it too. This is the server-authoritative form of the client-local governor -- the same three numbers, decided by the server instead, which is what a tuning shop or a speed limit inside an instance needs. The ceiling is replicated to **every viewer**, not only to the client that currently owns the physics: ownership changes on every driver entry and exit, and a ceiling chased across those transitions would be missing for exactly the first second of every drive. It survives the physics owner's twice-a-second durable report by construction -- that report carries no performance field, so the merge has nothing to overwrite -- and it survives a projection that has not attached yet, because the client holds the intent on the replica and applies it when the entity appears. **Only server-spawned vehicles are in the registry.** A player standing next to a vanilla traffic car is standing next to something REDengine population spawned on their own client: it has no canonical id and this call cannot see it. Adopting vanilla traffic is a separate capability that does not exist yet.
returns: reason: invalid_argument, invalid_top_speed, invalid_acceleration, invalid_taper, vehicle_not_found, vehicles_unavailable, permission_denied:world.vehicles

name: setPersistent
summary: Exempts a vehicle from every automatic removal.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. One meaning, deliberately: no time-to-live takes it, the unobserved sweep does not take it, and it survives the stop of the resource that created it. An explicit `Open77.vehicles.remove` still takes it -- persistence is protection from the reapers, not from the owner. Taking persistence away hands the vehicle back to any deadline it still carries. Read back as `Open77.vehicles.get(id).persistent`.
example:
-- The faction's tank stays in the world across resource restarts and reaper sweeps
local id = Open77.vehicles.create({ record = "Vehicle.v_militech_basilisk", position = base })
Open77.vehicles.setPersistent(id, true)

name: setPlayerExitLocked
summary: Prevents or permits a player-controlled vehicle exit.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. While locked, native unmount and manual seat-switch attempts are rejected and reconciliation remounts any divergent local state. Seat policy is cross-resource, so an authorized gamemode or utility resource may coordinate vehicles created elsewhere. A server forced exit still overrides the lock. The optional vehicle ID is an optimistic guard against stale assignments.
example:
-- Arrest: the suspect cannot leave the cruiser until released
Open77.vehicles.warpPlayerIntoVehicle(suspectId, cruiserId, Open77.vehicles.seats.rearLeft)
Open77.vehicles.setPlayerExitLocked(suspectId, true, cruiserId)

name: setPlayerIntoVehicle
summary: Alias for authoritative player seat assignment.
description: Same contract as `warpPlayerIntoVehicle`. This name is useful to codebases that reserve `warp` for client presentation, while both server names create the same canonical seat assignment.
example:
-- FiveM-style helper name for the same seat assignment
Open77.vehicles.setPlayerIntoVehicle(playerId, vehicleId, "driver")

name: setProperties
summary: Applies a stored property table to a vehicle.
description:
Requires `world.vehicles`, plus `world.vehicles.appearance` if -- and only if -- the table CHANGES the appearance variant. Restating the variant a car already wears is free, which is what keeps the round trip working for a resource that never changes a look.

**`version` decides how absence is read, and it is the only thing that does.** A table carrying `version = 1` -- which is every table `getProperties` hands back -- is a COMPLETE description, so an absent optional field means "this car has none": no lights hue, no performance ceiling. A table without `version` is a PATCH, so an absent field is left exactly as it was, and `setProperties(id, { paint = { primary = "#FF0000" } })` is a repaint and nothing else.

**A property with no Cyberpunk counterpart is refused by name**, as `unsupported_property:modEngine` or `unsupported_property:paint.neonColor` -- the offending key alphabetically first, so the refusal is reproducible whatever `pairs` decides that run. Pass `{ ignoreUnsupported = true }` to skip them instead, in which case the third return value lists what was skipped. Refusing is deliberate: a garage that silently loses two thirds of its table is worse than one that fails loudly on day one. `Open77.vehicles.unsupportedProperties` maps every such name to the reason.

`record` is checked, never applied: REDengine cannot change a spawned entity's record, so a Quadra table handed to a Thorton answers `record_mismatch` rather than half-restoring. Detached parts are one-way on a live projection, so a table asking for fewer than the car has already lost answers `detached_parts_not_reattachable`; respawn and apply the table to the new car.

**The order of application is deliberate.** Health, paint, doors, windows and the durable damage go in ONE `update`, so no viewer ever sees a half-restored car. The electrical bits then go through `setEngine`, `setLights`, `setSiren` and `setDrivable`, because those are what record the server intent that stops the physics owner's next durable report from undoing them -- writing them as raw flags would look like it worked and quietly revert about half a second later. The visual template and the performance ceiling follow on their own durable channels.
returns: reason: unsupported_property:<name>, unsupported_version, record_mismatch, detached_parts_not_reattachable, invalid_argument, invalid_paint, invalid_damage, invalid_health, invalid_appearance, invalid_lights_hue, vehicle_not_found, permission_denied:world.vehicles, permission_denied:world.vehicles.appearance
skipped: the list of unsupported names, only with ignoreUnsupported
example:
local stored = json.decode(row.props)
local id = Open77.vehicles.create({ record = stored.record, position = spot })
local ok, reason = Open77.vehicles.setProperties(id, stored)
if not ok then print("garage restore failed: " .. reason) end

name: setSiren
summary: Turns a vehicle's siren on or off.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. **The light bar and the sound are one bit and cannot be separated.** The only native this build exposes is `vehicleBaseObject.ToggleSiren(Bool)`, which takes no channel argument, so there is no `setSirenLights` that would not also make noise. The siren is also the one electrical bit no owner snapshot can read back, which is why the client echoes the canonical value instead of reporting it -- without that echo a cop car's bar went dark about five seconds after it was set.
example:
-- /siren toggles the caller's cruiser
RegisterCommand("siren", function(source)
    local seat = Open77.vehicles.getPlayerSeat(source)
    if not seat then return end
    local on = Open77.vehicles.isSirenOn(seat.vehicleId)
    Open77.vehicles.setSiren(seat.vehicleId, not on)
end, false)

name: setTimeToLive
summary: Gives a vehicle a deadline, in milliseconds from now.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `0` or `nil` cancels a deadline the vehicle already had, so a caller does not have to recreate it. Capped at seven days, mirroring the prop registry. The reaper runs once per tick, before interest is reconciled, so a vehicle whose lifetime ends leaves as a real removal the client tears down rather than quietly dropping out of the next interest pass. Read back as `Open77.vehicles.get(id).ttlMs`, counted from now and absent rather than zero once cancelled. A vehicle marked persistent ignores its deadline while it stays persistent. A deadline takes an **occupied** vehicle too, deliberately: a time-to-live silently declined because someone happened to be sitting in the car is a worse surprise than the removal, and the seat ledger is closed out properly either way. Clear the deadline on `onPlayerEnteredVehicle`, or mark the vehicle persistent, if that matters.
example:
-- A job car is removed one hour after it was handed out
Open77.vehicles.setTimeToLive(vehicleId, 60 * 60 * 1000)

name: setTireBroken
summary: Sets or clears one broken tire.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Mutates one tire index in 0..3 and replicates the canonical state to streamed observers.
example:
-- Spike strip: burst the two front tires
Open77.vehicles.setTireBroken(vehicleId, 0, true)
Open77.vehicles.setTireBroken(vehicleId, 1, true)

name: setTireMask
summary: Replaces the broken-tire bit mask.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Only the lower four bits are valid and correspond to tire indexes 0..3.
example:
-- All four tires burst at once (bits 0..3)
Open77.vehicles.setTireMask(vehicleId, 15)

name: setTransform
summary: Moves a vehicle authoritatively.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Updates position and yaw, revokes any active physics lease, and publishes the new canonical transform to current viewers.

name: setTtl
summary: Alias of `Open77.vehicles.setTimeToLive`.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The short spelling, matching the `ttlMs` key on `Open77.vehicles.create`.
example:
-- Same as setTimeToLive: this rental disappears after 15 minutes
Open77.vehicles.setTtl(vehicleId, 15 * 60 * 1000)

name: setUndriveable
summary: Takes a vehicle out of service, or puts it back.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The inverted spelling of `Open77.vehicles.setDrivable`, for callers porting `SetVehicleUndriveable`.
example:
-- FiveM port: SetVehicleUndriveable(veh, true) becomes
Open77.vehicles.setUndriveable(vehicleId, true)

name: setVehicleProperties
summary: The FiveM-shaped name for `setProperties`.
description: Identical contract, for a resource ported from a framework that spells it `SetVehicleProperties`. `applyProperties` is a third name for the same function.
example:
-- FiveM-style garage restore works unchanged
local ok, reason = Open77.vehicles.setVehicleProperties(vehicleId, json.decode(row.props))
if not ok then print(reason) end

name: setWindowOpen
summary: Sets one reversible side-window opening state.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. This controls the four openable side windows and is separate from destructible broken-glass state.
example:
-- Open the rear-right window for the passenger
Open77.vehicles.setWindowOpen(vehicleId, Open77.vehicles.windows.backRight, true)

name: startEngine
summary: Starts a vehicle's engine.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `Open77.vehicles.setEngine(id, true)` under a name that reads as an action.
example:
-- Remote start from the key fob
RegisterCommand("remotestart", function(source)
    local nearest = Open77.vehicles.closest(source, { radius = 20 })
    if nearest then Open77.vehicles.startEngine(nearest.id) end
end, false)

name: stopEngine
summary: Stops a vehicle's engine.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `Open77.vehicles.setEngine(id, false)` under a name that reads as an action.
example:
-- Cut the engine when the driver is arrested
Open77.vehicles.stopEngine(vehicleId)

name: taskPlayerEnter
summary: Seats a player through the vanilla entry animation.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The same authoritative reservation as `warpPlayerIntoVehicle`, taking the same `options` and answering with the same refusal reasons; the only difference is that the affected client is asked to reach the seat by mounting through the mounting facility and playing the authored entry, instead of being placed in the seat in one frame. It does **not** walk the player to the door: the approach is an NPC behaviour, and driving a network puppet through it crashed the observing client when it was measured, so the player is mounted where they stand and slides in. The animation is bounded — a client whose mounting relation does not become readable within three seconds warps instead — so the seat is always reached and `warpPlayerIntoVehicle` remains the path that never depends on an animation.
example:
local ok, reason = Open77.vehicles.taskPlayerEnter(playerId, vehicleId, Open77.vehicles.seats.driver)
if not ok then
  -- every refusal is the warp's refusal, verbatim
  print(reason)
end

name: taskPlayerEnterVehicle
summary: Alias for the animated authoritative seat assignment.
description: Same contract as `Open77.vehicles.taskPlayerEnter`. The longer spelling mirrors the client-side `Open77.vehicles.taskPlayerEnterVehicle`, which presents an already-authorised **remote** occupant; this server name creates the canonical assignment that such a presentation would be showing.
example:
-- The player walks up and climbs in with the animation
Open77.vehicles.taskPlayerEnterVehicle(playerId, vehicleId, Open77.vehicles.seats.frontPassenger)

name: taskPlayerLeave
summary: Ejects a player from a network vehicle.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The FiveM-shaped name for the same durable forced exit as `forcePlayerOutOfVehicle`, and it is honest about not being the mirror image of `taskPlayerEnter`: **the leaving player's own exit is instant on this build.** That is a measurement, not an omission — driving the local player's authored exit workspot inside the mount release window faulted on the engine's release-dispatch thread and the workspot never started once, so the client does not attempt it. Every other player still sees this occupant's exit animated, because a remote proxy's exit has always been; only the ejected player's own screen skips it.
example:
-- The taxi reached its destination: the customer gets out
Open77.vehicles.taskPlayerLeave(customerId, taxiId)

name: taskPlayerLeaveVehicle
summary: Alias for the authoritative vehicle exit.
description: Same contract as `Open77.vehicles.taskPlayerLeave`, spelled to match `taskPlayerEnterVehicle`.
example:
-- The ride is over: the passenger gets out
Open77.vehicles.taskPlayerLeaveVehicle(passengerId, taxiId)

name: triggerHorn
summary: Sounds a synchronized vehicle horn.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Sends a reliable, authority-epoch-bound one-shot command to the client currently simulating the vehicle. An unoccupied parked vehicle intentionally has no physics owner, so the server addresses all current viewers directly without granting a lease. Duration is 100..2000 ms and defaults to 250 ms. The event is transient and is not late-join state.
example:
-- Honk when the player's rental is unlocked remotely
Open77.vehicles.unlock(vehicleId)
Open77.vehicles.triggerHorn(vehicleId, 200)

name: unlock
summary: Unlocks a vehicle for ordinary entry.
description: Convenience alias for `setLocked(id, false)`. Requires `world.vehicles` and updates durable canonical state.
example:
-- The renter paid: unlock their car
Open77.vehicles.unlock(rentalId)

name: unlockForAll
summary: Unlocks a vehicle for everyone, revoking every exception.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. `Open77.vehicles.setLockedForAll(id, false)` under a name that reads as an action.
example:
-- Event: every car in the lot is free to take
for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.vehicles.all()) do
    Open77.vehicles.unlockForAll(entry.id)
end

name: unsupportedProperties
summary: The FiveM vehicle-property names with no Cyberpunk counterpart, and why.
description:
A table, not a function: each key is a FiveM `GetVehicleProperties` field this engine cannot express, and each value says what is missing. `setProperties` refuses every one of them by name. Read it to decide, before writing, what a ported script has to drop -- and read it instead of guessing, because several of the absences are surprising: there are no colour INDICES (Cyberpunk paint is RGB), no livery index (the appearance variant is a name, not a number), and no plate at all.

The list covers `modKit`, `mods`, `modEngine`, `modBrakes`, `modTransmission`, `modSuspension`, `modArmour`, `modTurbo`, `wheels`, `wheelType`, `wheelColor`, `windowTint`, `neonEnabled`, `neonColor`, `xenonColor`, `livery`, `roofLivery`, `extras`, `color1`, `color2`, `pearlescentColor`, `interiorColor`, `dashboardColor`, `dirtLevel`, `tyreSmokeColor`, `plateText`, `plateIndex` and `fuelLevel`.
returns: table mapping property name to the reason it has no counterpart
example:
for name, why in pairs(Open77.vehicles.unsupportedProperties) do
  print(("%s: %s"):format(name, why))
end

name: update
summary: Updates canonical durable vehicle fields.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. Applies only supplied fields, such as health, flags, colors, openings, tires, body damage, broken glass/lights, or detached parts. Any authorized resource may update any canonical vehicle; the authoritative result is replicated to current viewers and late joiners.

name: warpPlayerIntoVehicle
summary: Assigns a player to an authoritative vehicle seat.
description: Requires `world.vehicles`. The server reserves the seat immediately, optionally moves the player into the vehicle routing bucket, and keeps a durable forced-entry order until the target streams and the client confirms the native mount. Seat coordination is intentionally cross-resource: any resource with the permission may target any canonical vehicle. Proximity and the vehicle locked flag are bypassed; destroyed/exploded vehicles and occupied seats are rejected.

name: attachDriver
summary: Attaches a server-owned vehicle AI controller.
description: options.npcId optionally mounts an existing NPC owned by this resource; omission means driverless operation. Reserves the driver seat. Requires world.vehicles. Refuses occupied driver seats, destroyed vehicles, unsupported AV/Basilisk records and conflicting controllers. The NPC must be alive, in the same bucket and without active tasks. No NPC is created automatically.
example:
-- Put a spawned NPC at the wheel of the taxi
local state, reason = Open77.vehicles.ai.attachDriver(taxiId, { npcId = driverId })
if not state then print("no driver: " .. reason) end

name: chase
summary: Pursues a canonical entity using native autonomous pathing.
description: Same targetKind, targetId, speed, distance, behavior and timeout options as follow. Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. It does not enable weapon use, teleport catch-up, scripted ramming or police pursuit logic. Targets and simulator must remain in the same routing bucket.
example:
-- A police car chases the suspect's vehicle
Open77.vehicles.ai.chase(cruiserId, { targetKind = "vehicle", targetId = suspectCarId, speed = 25, behavior = "aggressive" })

name: driveTo
summary: Starts native autonomous driving to a world position.
description: Requires world.vehicles and this resource's attached controller. options.position={x,y,z} is required. Optional speed (0.5..55 m/s), arrivalRadius (1..20 m), timeoutMilliseconds (1000..3600000) and behavior. Returns a task state, or nil, reason. Acceptance is not arrival: subscribe to arrived, blocked or failed.

name: follow
summary: Continuously follows a canonical player, vehicle or NPC.
description: Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. options.targetKind is player, vehicle or npc and targetId is the canonical ID. Optional distance (3..80 m), speed, behavior and timeoutMilliseconds. Uses the native autonomous path follower with server-updated target coordinates, at most twice per second. Stops with target_unavailable if the target leaves the bucket or disappears.
example:
-- The bodyguard's car follows the client's car at 10 m
Open77.vehicles.ai.follow(escortId, { targetKind = "player", targetId = clientId, distance = 10 })

name: followRoute
summary: Drives an ordered route of world points.
description: Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. options.points is an array of 1..64 {x,y,z} positions. Supports loop, speed, behavior, arrivalRadius and timeoutMilliseconds. Emits waypointReached at each point and arrived once at a non-looping route's end. This is a destination sequence, not an exact authored racing spline.

name: joinTraffic
summary: Starts indefinite native road-following.
description: Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. Uses the autonomous command's driveDownTheRoadIndefinitely mode; it does not spawn ambient traffic or use the solo Delamain taxi system. Supports speed, behavior and timeoutMilliseconds. No arrival event is expected; stop explicitly or handle failure/timeout.
example:
-- Ambient: the car just drives around the city
Open77.vehicles.ai.joinTraffic(carId, { speed = 12 })

name: on
summary: Subscribes to this resource's vehicle AI lifecycle events.
description: Requires a function callback. Events: waypointReached, arrived, cancelled, failed, blocked and resumed. The handler receives a decoded state table, not JSON text. Events are routed only to the controller's resource. blocked with reason=no_progress is a stall detector, not proof of an obstacle collision. No events are replayed; query state first.
example:
-- Charge the fare when the taxi arrives
Open77.vehicles.ai.on("arrived", function(state)
    local fare = fares[state.vehicleId]
    if fare then chargeFare(fare.playerId, fare.price) end
end)

name: removeDriver
summary: Stops AI control and releases its driver seat.
description: Requires world.vehicles and ownership of this AI controller. Cancels an active task and unmounts (but does not delete) the optional NPC, restoring its previous AI mode. Returns the detached state, or nil, reason.
example:
-- The ride is over: the NPC lets go of the wheel
Open77.vehicles.ai.removeDriver(taxiId)

name: setBehavior
summary: Selects normal, cautious or aggressive AI behavior.
description: Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. normal keeps native avoidance; cautious uses a 75% speed ceiling; aggressive enables native clearTrafficOnPath. These are bounded presets, not a promise of police AI or traffic-law compliance.
example:
-- The getaway driver stops caring about traffic
Open77.vehicles.ai.setBehavior(getawayId, "aggressive")

name: setSpeed
summary: Updates the native driving speed limit.
description: Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. speed is finite, 0.5..55 m/s; default 12. Changes the active command without restarting it each frame. Actual speed remains subject to road geometry, obstacles and the vehicle. Cautious behavior applies 75% of the configured ceiling.
example:
-- Slow the bus down in the school zone
Open77.vehicles.ai.setSpeed(busId, 6)

name: state
summary: Reads authoritative vehicle AI state.
description: Requires world.vehicles. Returns the controller state or nil when no driver is attached. Contains vehicleId, npcId, taskId (strings), revision, mode, status, reason, speed, behavior, destination x/y/z, routeIndex/count, targetKind/id, distance, owner and epoch. Motion is still subject to the ordinary vehicle authority lease.
example:
-- Where is the taxi in its job?
local state = Open77.vehicles.ai.state(taxiId)
if state then print(state.status, state.mode, state.speed) end

name: stop
summary: Cancels the active task and stops the vehicle.
description: Requires world.vehicles and controller ownership. Idempotent. Keeps the AI controller and driver seat reserved for the next task. Emits cancelled once for an active task. Use removeDriver to release the seat.
example:
-- Red light: stop, then continue two seconds later
CreateThread(function()
    Open77.vehicles.ai.stop(busId)
    Wait(2000)
    Open77.vehicles.ai.joinTraffic(busId)
end)

name: addPlayer
summary: Adds a player to a voice channel.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. `options.canSpeak` and `options.canListen` both default to **true**; pass `false` explicitly for a listen-only or speak-only membership. This is the function name -- `addChannelPlayer` does not exist, and calling it inside a `pcall` is how a squad channel silently ends up with no members.
example:
-- An officer joins the dispatch channel when they clock in
RegisterNetEvent("police:onDuty", function()
    Open77.voice.addPlayer(dispatchChannel.id, source, { canSpeak = true, canListen = true })
end)

name: channels
summary: Every canonical voice channel.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. Covers radio, phone, party, admin and spatial channels alike -- they differ by configuration, not by kind.
example:
-- /voicechannels: list every channel for an admin
RegisterCommand("voicechannels", function(source)
    for _, channel in ipairs(Open77.voice.channels() or {}) do
        Open77.chat.send(source, ("%s (%s)"):format(channel.name, channel.mode))
    end
end, true)

name: createChannel
summary: Creates a resource-owned voice channel.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. `options` is required and must be a table. Effects include `gain`, `lowPassHz`, `highPassHz`, `distortion`, `radioNoise`, `spatialBlend` and the reverb controls `reverbWet`, `reverbRoomSize`, `reverbDecay`, `reverbDamping` and `reverbPreDelayMs`. A non-persistent channel is released automatically with its owning resource. See [Integrated voice chat](voice.md).
example:
-- A police radio channel with a radio-style effect
local dispatch, reason = Open77.voice.createChannel({
    name = "NCPD dispatch",
    mode = "radio",
    effect = { highPassHz = 220.0, lowPassHz = 4800.0, radioNoise = 0.04 },
})
if not dispatch then print("no radio: " .. reason) end

name: getChannel
summary: Reads one voice channel.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. Answers `nil` for an unknown channel id.
example:
-- Is the party channel still there after a reload?
local party = Open77.voice.getChannel(partyChannelId)
if not party then party = Open77.voice.createChannel({ name = "Party", mode = "party" }) end

name: getParticipant
summary: Reads one player's voice participation.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. Carries proximity settings, server mute and deaf policy, and the channels they belong to.
example:
-- Tell an admin what a player's voice state is
RegisterCommand("voiceinfo", function(source, args)
    local participant = Open77.voice.getParticipant(tonumber(args[1]))
    if participant then Open77.chat.send(source, ("muted=%s deaf=%s"):format(tostring(participant.muted), tostring(participant.deaf))) end
end, true)

name: participants
summary: Every voice participant, with proximity, mute/deaf and memberships.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. The server's own view, so it answers for a player whose client has not reported anything.
example:
-- Count how many players are server-muted
local muted = 0
for _, participant in ipairs(Open77.voice.participants() or {}) do
    if participant.muted then muted = muted + 1 end
end

name: removeChannel
summary: Removes a voice channel.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. Members are dropped with it; they are not moved to another channel.
example:
-- The heist crew disbands: drop its channel
Open77.voice.removeChannel(crewChannelId)

name: removePlayer
summary: Removes a player from a voice channel.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. Their other channel memberships and their proximity setting are untouched.
example:
-- Clocking off leaves the dispatch channel
RegisterNetEvent("police:offDuty", function()
    Open77.voice.removePlayer(dispatchChannel.id, source)
end)

name: setChannelPlayerMuted
summary: Mutes one player in one channel.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. `muted` defaults to true when omitted. Scoped to that channel: the player still speaks everywhere else, unlike `setPlayerMuted`.
example:
-- The dispatcher silences one officer on the radio only
Open77.voice.setChannelPlayerMuted(dispatchChannel.id, officerId, true)

name: setChannelPlayerPermissions
summary: Sets a member's speak and listen rights independently.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. Both `canSpeak` and `canListen` default to true when omitted, so passing an empty table restores full membership rights.
example:
-- A trainee may listen to dispatch but not speak
Open77.voice.setChannelPlayerPermissions(dispatchChannel.id, traineeId, { canSpeak = false, canListen = true })

name: setDefaultProximityDistance
summary: Changes the default proximity reach.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. `applyToExisting` defaults to **false**, so by default this only affects participants who join afterwards; pass true to retune everyone who is already connected.
example:
-- A quieter RP server: 15 m reach for everyone, including those already online
Open77.voice.setDefaultProximityDistance(15, true)

name: setEnabled
summary: Turns voice on or off for the whole server.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. `enabled` defaults to true when omitted. Disabling stops relaying without removing channels or memberships, so re-enabling restores the topology.
example:
-- /voice off during the event briefing, /voice on after
RegisterCommand("voice", function(source, args)
    Open77.voice.setEnabled(args[1] ~= "off")
end, true)

name: setPlayerDeaf
summary: Stops a player hearing anyone on the server.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. `deaf` defaults to true. The receive-side counterpart of `setPlayerMuted`, enforced at the relay.
example:
-- A "deafened" status effect for 30 seconds
Open77.voice.setPlayerDeaf(playerId, true)
SetTimeout(30000, function() Open77.voice.setPlayerDeaf(playerId, false) end)

name: setPlayerMuted
summary: Stops a player being heard anywhere on the server.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. `muted` defaults to true. Server-wide send policy, enforced at the relay -- the client cannot talk its way past it.
example:
-- /vmute <id> for admins
RegisterCommand("vmute", function(source, args)
    local target = tonumber(args[1])
    if target then Open77.voice.setPlayerMuted(target, true) end
end, true)

name: setProximity
summary: Enables, disables or tunes one player's proximity reach.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. `options.enabled` defaults to true; `options.distance` overrides the server default for that player alone. Turning proximity off leaves their channel memberships working.
example:
-- A megaphone item: 80 m reach for one player
RegisterNetEvent("items:megaphone", function(on)
    Open77.voice.setProximity(source, { enabled = true, distance = on and 80 or 20 })
end)

name: setQuality
summary: Sets the global codec quality profile.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. A server-wide policy, not a per-player one: it trades bandwidth against fidelity for everybody.
example:
-- Save bandwidth on a full server
Open77.voice.setQuality("standard")

name: status
summary: Global voice quality, default proximity and relay counters.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. The dedicated server owns reachability: a client's requested scope never bypasses routing buckets, proximity, membership, mute/deaf, rate or quality checks, and the rejection counters here are where that shows.
example:
-- Log the relay counters once a minute
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        Wait(60000)
        local status = Open77.voice.status()
        if status then print("voice quality", status.quality, "default reach", status.proximityDistance) end
    end
end)

name: updateChannel
summary: Patches a voice channel.
description: Requires `voice.manage`. Sparse: the patch is merged with the channel id and only the fields present are applied, so one effect can be retuned without restating the rest.
example:
-- Add more static to the radio without restating the rest
Open77.voice.updateChannel(dispatchChannel.id, { effect = { radioNoise = 0.1 } })

name: activate
summary: Alias of `Open77.weapons.setActive`.
description: Asynchronous. The same function under a second name; it accepts both the slot and the record form.
example:
-- Draw the player's slot 1 when the round starts
Open77.weapons.activate(playerId, 1)

name: assign
summary: Assigns a weapon record to one of a player's three slots.
description: Asynchronous. The calling resource declares `network.events` and depends on `open77_weapons >=0.1.0`; the request is relayed to the official `open77_weapons` client package. `slot` is an integer 1 to 3 and `record` is at most 160 characters. Listen for `open77:weapons:completed` with `playerId, requestId, operation, accepted, reason, result`; replies are matched to the authenticated target and the calling resource, and an unanswered request completes with `request_timeout` after ten seconds. See [Weapon Lua API](weapons-api.md).
example:
-- Give the new officer a pistol in slot 1 and draw it
RegisterNetEvent("police:onDuty", function()
    Open77.weapons.assign(source, "Items.Preset_Lexington_Default", 1, { active = true })
end)

name: clear
summary: Empties all three of a player's weapon slots in one request.
description: Asynchronous, like every other weapon mutation; the FiveM `RemoveAllPedWeapons` equivalent. One relay message rather than three `remove` calls: the owner runs the three native removals itself and answers once, so there is one request id to correlate instead of three and no way to end up half-cleared because one leg was refused. A slot that was already empty is **not** a failure and does not make `accepted` false. The completion's `result` carries `cleared` and a `slots` array of `{ slot, accepted, reason }`. Requires `network.events` and a dependency on `open77_weapons >=0.1.0`. See [Weapon Lua API](weapons-api.md).
example:
-- Arrested: every weapon slot emptied in one request
RegisterCommand("disarm", function(source, args)
    local target = tonumber(args[1])
    if target then Open77.weapons.clear(target) end
end, true)

name: get
summary: The server's cached view of a player's weapons, answered synchronously.
description: Requires `player.weapons.read`. **This is a cache, not authority.** Weapons live in the client's REDengine equipment system; the server has no copy of that state and no way to verify one, so every field is as true as the owner's last report -- read it to decide (anticheat, inventory sync, a shop refusing a sale), never to assert. The answer carries **two** ages because its halves refresh at different rates. `reportedAgeMs` dates `active`, `drawn` and `magazine`, which ride the ordinary 20 Hz player snapshot, and `fresh` applies the same two-second rule as `Open77.players.get`. `loadoutAgeMs` dates `slots`, which is pushed only when the loadout changes, so minutes there is normal and means nothing is wrong. `source` is `report` once the owner has described its slots and `snapshot` when only the packet's weapon block has arrived; the call fails with `weapons_unreported` when nothing at all has been heard, which is different from a player carrying nothing. The `onPlayerWeaponChanged` event fires once per change. See [Weapon Lua API](weapons-api.md).
returns: { playerId, slots, active, activeRecord, activeTweakDbId, drawn, magazine, reportedAgeMs, loadoutAgeMs, fresh, source }, or nil
example:
-- The shop refuses a sale to a player who already carries a Lexington (cached view)
local weapons = Open77.weapons.get(source)
if weapons and weapons.activeRecord == "Items.Preset_Lexington_Default" then
    return Open77.chat.send(source, "You already have one.")
end

name: holster
summary: Puts away whatever a player is holding.
description: Asynchronous, same relay and completion contract as `assign`. It holsters rather than removing: the slots keep their weapons.
example:
-- Entering the hospital holsters the weapon
AddEventHandler("hospital:entered", function(playerId)
    Open77.weapons.holster(playerId)
end)

name: remove
summary: Empties one of a player's three weapon slots.
description: Asynchronous, same relay and completion contract as `assign`. `slot` is an integer 1 to 3.
example:
-- Confiscate slot 2
Open77.weapons.remove(playerId, 2)

name: requestSnapshot
summary: Asks a player's client for its current weapon state.
description: Asynchronous. The completion event's `result` carries the slot contents and ammunition the client actually holds, which is the honest answer after a write has settled.
example:
-- Ask the client what it really holds, and read the answer from the completion event
Open77.weapons.requestSnapshot(playerId)
AddEventHandler("open77:weapons:completed", function(playerId, requestId, operation, accepted, reason, result)
    if operation == "snapshot" and accepted then print(json.encode(result)) end
end)

name: setActive
summary: Draws a weapon, by slot or by record.
description: Asynchronous, same relay and completion contract as `assign`. Two forms: a slot number 1 to 3, which takes no options, or a record string with optional options. Passing options with a slot is refused, because the two forms mean different things.
example:
-- Force the katana out for the melee round
Open77.weapons.setActive(playerId, "Items.Preset_Katana_Default", { slot = 3 })

name: setAmmo
summary: Sets a slot's magazine and reserve ammunition.
description: Asynchronous, same relay and completion contract as `assign`. `amounts` takes `reserve` and `magazine` -- at least one is required, each a non-negative integer up to 1,000,000 -- plus an optional boolean `activate`.
example:
-- An ammo box refills slot 1
RegisterNetEvent("items:ammoBox", function()
    Open77.weapons.setAmmo(source, 1, { magazine = 12, reserve = 120 })
end)

name: unequip
summary: Alias of `Open77.weapons.remove`.
description: Asynchronous. The same function under the name the clothing API uses for the same idea.
example:
-- Same as remove: take the weapon out of slot 1
Open77.weapons.unequip(playerId, 1)

name: clearArea
summary: Removes the server-owned entities inside a radius and can suppress vanilla population there.
description: The server half of `Open77.world`, and the only function in it: the client's `world` table (raycast, groundZ, nearby, nearest, district) needs a physics world and a streamed player, and a dedicated server has neither. **Ownership is the contract.** It removes what the CALLING resource owns and nothing else; entities inside the radius belonging to another resource are counted in `refused` and left standing. Without that rule a gamemode clearing a street would delete the parked cars a roleplay resource spawned and still holds ids for, and that resource would discover it only when its own ids began answering `not_found`. `foreign = true` lifts the rule, and only for VEHICLES, and only for a resource whose manifest carries `world.clearArea.foreign`; without the permission the WHOLE call is refused rather than quietly downgraded, because a silent downgrade would report success on a street that still has somebody else's cars in it. The restriction to vehicles is structural, not a policy choice: NPC and prop removal is owner-checked inside the authority services themselves, and the server's NPC read is owner-scoped, so a foreign NPC is never even a candidate. Options: `npcs`, `vehicles`, `props` (booleans, all default true), `population` (default false), `bucket`, `foreign` (default false), `grace` (metres of outward slack). A `nil` bucket means every bucket, the same reading `Open77.zones.playersIn` takes, since a place is not a player and has no bucket of its own to borrow. `population = true` REQUIRES a bucket and drives `Open77.routingBuckets.setPopulationEnabled`; the suppression that follows is **bucket-wide, not confined to the radius**, because that is the only shape the switch has. There is no radius-scoped vanilla-population control on 2.31. The containment test is `Open77.zones.contains` from the shared zone module, so the radius cap and the geometry rules are the ones every other Open77 zone obeys. A missing `world.npcs`, `world.vehicles` or `world.props` skips that kind and still succeeds: a teardown that failed outright over one of three permissions would leave the other two kinds behind.

params.name: options
params.type: table { npcs?, vehicles?, props?, population?, bucket?, foreign?, grace? }

returns: table { npcs, vehicles, props, refused, foreignVehicles, population } where population is "unchanged", "suppressed" or "unavailable", or nil
reason: permission_denied:world.clearArea.foreign, invalid_radius, invalid_position, invalid_options, invalid_bucket, bucket_required_for_population, or a shared zone-module token (invalid_grace)

name: getPopulation
summary: Reads the ambient population policy of one routing bucket.
description: Ungated. `enabled` is derived (`crowd > 0 or traffic > 0 or police`), so it can never say "on" while every density is zero. `crowdGranularity` is `continuous` and `trafficGranularity` is `binary`, which is the honest statement of what 2.31 can apply.
returns: table { bucket, crowd, traffic, police, enabled, crowdGranularity, trafficGranularity }, or nil
example:
-- Is the arena instance empty of vanilla crowd?
local policy = Open77.world.getPopulation(ARENA_BUCKET)
if policy and policy.enabled then print("population still on in the arena") end

name: setPopulation
summary: Sets the ambient population density of one routing bucket.
description:
Requires `world.population`. Server-owned and replicated to every client in the bucket; the client half (`Open77.world.population`) is read-only, so there is nothing to race.

`crowd` is a fraction of the vanilla pedestrian density, 0..1, and is applied as one through the engine's community density modifier. `traffic` is accepted as 0..1 but 2.31 exposes no vehicle density modifier, so it is a **switch**: any value above zero means vanilla traffic. `getPopulation` reports that as `trafficGranularity = "binary"` rather than letting a caller assume the fraction was honoured. `police` allows or forbids vanilla prevention spawns outright.

A bucket nobody has configured is the vanilla world (`1, 1, true`), not an empty one. `Open77.routingBuckets.setPopulationEnabled` is the same state expressed as a switch: off sets all three off, on restores the vanilla figures.
example:
-- A quiet RP district: half the crowd, no traffic, no police
Open77.world.setPopulation(0, { crowd = 0.5, traffic = 0, police = false })

name: setPreventionEnabled
summary: Turns NCPD dispatch on or off for a whole routing bucket.
description: `TogglePreventionSystem` on every client currently in that bucket, and on any client that enters it afterwards. Per bucket rather than per player because it is a property of the world a set of players share, and because that is the only shape the engine's switch has - it takes no target. A bucket nobody has set runs dispatch, which is vanilla. Turning it off does not change anybody's wanted level: the two are separate, and a player left at level 3 in a bucket with dispatch off keeps the level and stops getting the police. Requires `world.prevention`, which is separate from `players.wanted` on purpose - a resource that should be able to make somebody a fugitive is not automatically one that should be able to abolish the police for everyone. Note that this is NOT the same switch as the police block `Open77.world.clearArea`'s population suppression drives on the client; while that suppression is active the client refuses a wanted-level raise with `population_suppressed`.
example:
-- No NCPD in the arena instance
Open77.world.setPreventionEnabled(ARENA_BUCKET, false)

name: bounds
summary: The zone's bounding volume: a planar centre and radius plus an optional height band.
description: Available in both runtimes, from the shared prelude scripting/lua/open77_zones.lua. Exactly the shape of the one squared comparison a poll loop wants per zone per tick, and of the radius a server roster scan wants. `minZ` and `maxZ` are nil when the zone is unbounded on that side, which only a polygon with no declared height range can be. This is what makes a polygon affordable: a zone the player is not standing in is rejected by its bounds for about the cost of a sphere (1.25 us against 1.2 us, measured in the client host), so cost tracks the zones that actually overlap the player rather than the number registered.

params.name: zone
params.type: table (a definition, or a value from Open77.zones.normalize)

returns: table { x, y, z, radius, minZ, maxZ } (minZ and maxZ may be nil), or nil, reason
reason: the same tokens as Open77.zones.contains
example:
local b = assert(Open77.zones.bounds(turf))
print(("turf spans %.1f m around %.1f, %.1f"):format(b.radius, b.x, b.y))

name: contains
summary: Is a point inside a zone? The one containment implementation both runtimes share.
description: Available in both runtimes, from the shared prelude scripting/lua/open77_zones.lua. The client poller and the server's Open77.zones.playersIn both call this, which is the point: a client and a server that disagreed at a boundary would leave a place a player can stand where the prompt appears but the grant is refused, or worse the other way round. Shapes: omit `shape` for the cylinder that shipped (planar `radius` around `position` plus a `maxHeight` band, default 6 m); `sphere` is a true 3-D ball and refuses `maxHeight`; `box` takes `position`, `size` (FULL extents) and `rotation` in degrees about the vertical axis; `poly` (alias `polygon`) takes `points` (3..512 planar vertices, concave allowed) with optional `minZ`/`maxZ` -- absent means unbounded on that side; `combo` takes `zones`, nested up to 4 deep. Every shape is CLOSED: a point on an edge, a face or a vertex is inside. `point` is a vector3 or any { x =, y =, z = } table. `options` may carry `grace` (metres to expand the zone outward, with rounded corners -- the server's tolerance for a replicated position, and the client's hysteresis band), `origin` ({ x, y, z } where the zone's anchor actually is right now, which is how an entity-attached zone is tested) and `rotation` (degrees, the zone's heading right now). A definition carrying `attach` REQUIRES `origin`, because resolving an entity is not something pure geometry may do. `false` always means outside and never 'could not tell'. Pure: it reads no world and holds no state. See the Proximity zones guide.

params.name: zone
params.type: table (a definition, or a value from Open77.zones.normalize)

returns: reason: invalid_definition, unknown_shape, invalid_position, invalid_radius, invalid_max_height, max_height_unsupported, invalid_size, invalid_rotation, invalid_points, too_many_points, degenerate_polygon, invalid_height_range, invalid_zones, too_many_zones, zone_nesting_too_deep, invalid_attach, invalid_point, invalid_options, invalid_grace, invalid_origin, origin_required

name: containsPlayer
summary: Server only. The single-player containment gate a grant should run before it acts.
description: Three answers, and they are genuinely different: true, false, and nil with a reason when the answer is not knowable. Refusing on nil is a policy decision the caller has to make, not one this call may make silently. A player in another routing bucket is `false` -- a different bucket is a different world, so they are not standing in this zone by any reading. A player who has never reported a position is nil/position_unknown, which is not 'outside'. Pass `maxAgeMs` when a stale reading must not grant: without it the last known position is used however old it is, matching Open77.players.get and Open77.players.nearby. `grace`, `origin` and `rotation` behave as they do on Open77.zones.playersIn. Use this for one player and playersIn for a sweep. See the Proximity zones guide.

params.name: definition
params.type: table (a zone definition, or a value from Open77.zones.normalize)

params.name: options
params.type: table { bucket?, maxAgeMs?, grace?, origin?, rotation? }

returns: reason: player_not_found, position_unknown, position_stale, invalid_options, invalid_max_age, or any Open77.zones.contains token including origin_required
example:
-- The shop only sells to a player really standing inside it
local shop = Open77.zones.normalize({ shape = "box", position = { x = -1460.2, y = 99.9, z = 14.8 }, size = { x = 12, y = 6, z = 4 } })
RegisterNetEvent("shop:buy", function(itemId)
    local inside = Open77.zones.containsPlayer(source, shop, { maxAgeMs = 2000 })
    if not inside then return Open77.chat.send(source, "You are not in the shop.") end
    sell(source, itemId)
end)

name: normalize
summary: Validates a zone definition once and precomputes everything a containment test needs.
description: Available in both runtimes, from the shared prelude scripting/lua/open77_zones.lua. Returns a prepared zone -- a plain table, so it still survives json.encode and pairs -- carrying the validated shape, its bounding volume and the derived values a test would otherwise recompute. Open77.zones.contains accepts either form, but on a raw definition it has to redo this work on every single call: measured in the client host, a 32-vertex polygon costs about 9.5 us prepared and roughly eight times that unprepared, because the vertex list is rebuilt and the shoelace area re-run before the test can start. Normalize once, keep the result, test many. Shapes: omit `shape` for the cylinder that shipped (planar `radius` around `position` plus a `maxHeight` band, default 6 m); `sphere` is a true 3-D ball and refuses `maxHeight`; `box` takes `position`, `size` (FULL extents) and `rotation` in degrees about the vertical axis; `poly` (alias `polygon`) takes `points` (3..512 planar vertices, concave allowed) with optional `minZ`/`maxZ` -- absent means unbounded on that side; `combo` takes `zones`, nested up to 4 deep. Every shape is CLOSED: a point on an edge, a face or a vertex is inside.
returns: reason: the same tokens as Open77.zones.contains
example:
local shop = assert(Open77.zones.normalize({ shape = "box",
    position = { x = -1460.2, y = 99.9, z = 14.8 },
    size = { x = 12.0, y = 6.0, z = 4.0 }, rotation = 37.0 }))
print(shop.shape, shop.bounds.radius)

name: playersIn
summary: Server only. Every player inside a zone, nearest to its anchor first, honouring routing buckets.
description: The authoritative half of zones. The client zone service (open77_zones) is PRESENTATION: it decides whether a prompt draws, it runs on a machine the player owns, and it can say anything. Anything that grants -- a shop selling, a job paying, a door opening, a safe zone suppressing damage -- must re-derive containment here first. The geometry is Open77.zones.contains, the same shared file the client embeds, so a definition means the same thing on both sides. Built on Open77.players.nearby and inheriting its conventions exactly: entries are { playerId, bucket, distance, fresh, ageMs, name, position, heading, speed }, ties break by player id so two calls with the same input answer in the same order, and `distance` is to the zone's ANCHOR, not to its boundary. `bucket` defaults to every bucket -- a zone is a place, not a player, and has no bucket of its own to borrow; pass a number to narrow, or false for every bucket explicitly. `limit` applies after containment, never to the bounding-sphere scan. `grace` is metres of slack, and a validation wants a few: Open77.players.position is a replicated snapshot and an honest player's latest position may not have landed yet, so the check exists to stop a client claiming to be somewhere else entirely, not to arbitrate centimetres. `origin` and `rotation` re-site the whole zone, which is how an entity-attached definition is validated server-side. See the Proximity zones guide.

params.name: definition
params.type: table (a zone definition, or a value from Open77.zones.normalize)

params.name: options
params.type: table { bucket?, maxAgeMs?, limit?, grace?, origin?, rotation? }

returns: table (array of nearby-style entries, possibly empty), or nil, reason
reason: invalid_options, invalid_limit, any Open77.zones.contains token including origin_required, or a reason from Open77.players.nearby
example:
-- Everyone inside the safe zone is healed every ten seconds
CreateThread(function()
    while true do
        Wait(10000)
        for _, entry in ipairs(Open77.zones.playersIn(safeZone) or {}) do
            Open77.players.heal(entry.playerId, 10)
        end
    end
end)

name: decode
summary: Decodes JSON into safe Lua values.
description: Produces only strings, numbers, booleans and tables of those, within the same depth and node bounds as the encoder. Malformed input answers nil rather than raising, so a caller can tell a bad payload from an empty one.
example:
-- Parse the props column of a garage row
local props = json.decode(row.props)
if not props then print("corrupt garage row", row.id) end

name: encode
summary: Serialises a bounded Lua value to JSON.
description: The same encoder the event and export marshallers use, so a value this accepts is a value that crosses a resource boundary. Functions, userdata, cyclic tables and non-finite numbers are refused rather than guessed at. `json` is a plain global on the server; the client spells it Open77.json.
example:
-- Store a table as JSON in the kvp store
Open77.kvp.set("garage:" .. identifier, json.encode(props))

name: new
summary: Creates a promise this resource settles itself.
description: The same Open77.Promise object Open77.exports.call and Open77.net.callClient return, so the runtime has one promise type rather than two. A promise created here keeps its value and can be awaited repeatedly, where the client's single-consumer export promise cannot; code that awaits once is portable across both. See the FiveM compatibility guide.
example:
local p = promise.new()
CreateThread(function() Wait(250) p:resolve("done") end)
print(p:await())
